## 2026-10-30 · #686 · The community node takes 250 pods at its next rebuild (kubelet maxPods 250 over the prefix delegation it already had)

**Why.** The attackme node (the community cluster's one t3.2xlarge) allocated 110 pods and had about 53 running,
so about 55 per-attendee Jokers (#685) fit at once. #685 keeps the Jokers tiny with a 5-minute scale-to-zero;
this is the insurance Michael asked for on 2026-10-29 in case the room outruns that, deferred to the next node
rebuild because the cap lives in node user data and changing it replaces the node.

**What was already there.** The issue asks for two things. The first, `ENABLE_PREFIX_DELEGATION=true` on the
vpc-cni addon, was already set for every cluster (`WARM_PREFIX_TARGET=1`, `before_compute = true`), so nothing
changed there. The second, the kubelet's max-pods, was the literal `maxPods: 110` in the nodeadm NodeConfig.

**What changed.**
- **Terraform** (`infra/terraform/aws/cluster/main.tf`): new `variable "max_pods"` (number, default 110, validated
  to 110..250), and the NodeConfig reads `maxPods: ${var.max_pods}`. Admin and attendee clusters are unchanged
  at 110. With prefix delegation a t3.2xlarge has 4 ENIs x 14 slots x 16 = 896 pod IPs, so the node has addresses for all 250 and
  kubelet sets the cap; at 250 pods the node holds about 17 /28 prefixes (~272 IPs) of the shared /18s.
- **fleet.sh**: new `max_pods_for_role` (community -> 250, everything else -> 110), a sibling of
  `imds_hop_limit_for_role` (#113) and role-derived for the same reason: the burn-cluster posture follows the
  role, and the roster carries no column for it. `up_one` passes `-var max_pods=<n>` on every apply and in the dry-run plan line.
- **docs/MASTER-RECREATION-SPEC.md**: the node-sizing and cluster-root paragraphs name `var.max_pods` and the 250.

**Trade-off, stated once.** AWS's max-pods calculator recommends at most 110 pods on an instance under 30 vCPUs
(a t3.2xlarge has 8). It is a recommendation about kubelet and container-runtime load that EKS does not enforce,
and the issue sets 250 on purpose; the community node runs mostly idle, scaled-to-zero Jokers. If the rebuilt node
shows kubelet or PLEG trouble under load, the lever is a larger community instance (roster `instance_type`); the
cap stays at 250.

**Tests.** `verify/test_public_pod_cap.py` (offline, new): `var.max_pods` exists, defaults to 110, is bounded,
and is what the NodeConfig reads (no literal maxPods left); prefix delegation is on in the vpc-cni addon before
compute; `max_pods_for_role` gives community 250 and everything else 110 and is wired into `up_one`'s vars and

## 2026-10-31 · #706 · `fleet.sh monitors --data`: every fleet monitor and fleet-dashboard query must answer for every named cluster

**Why.** #485's criterion is "apply the fleet monitors to the next event's instructor org and confirm every query
returns data". Nothing checked the second half. `--check` failed only on a monitor that was missing, drifted or
extra; for one that was present it printed the state and passed, No Data included, and it never ran a dashboard
query. So a monitor or column on a wrong metric, tag or log name passed every test, and its silence read as health.

**What changed.**
- `infra/datadog-fleet/fleet_monitors.py` has a new read-only mode, `--data --cluster NAME [--cluster NAME ...]`,
  which uses the secret's read-only key as `--check` does. It exits 1 on any blank and prints one line per query.
  - A monitor that fires on absence (`< 1`) is read by its own per-cluster state (`GET /api/v1/monitor` with
    `group_states=all`). Every named cluster needs a group in OK, Warn or Alert. No Data, Unknown, Skipped or no
    group at all is a blank.
  - A monitor that fires on a rising count (`> n`) has no series on a healthy cluster, so its state cannot tell
    a right name from a wrong one. node-not-ready reads `!status:true`, and kube-state-metrics core sends
    `by_condition` only for the status a node is in. guard-proxy-erroring counts error logs. Each now carries
    a `signal` in `monitors.yaml`: the same source without the bad-news filter (the Ready condition in every
    status, and every guard-proxy log line). `--data` sends it through `POST /api/v2/query/scalar` over the
    monitor's window. Validation refuses a rising-count monitor without a signal, a signal on another metric,
    on a tag or log term the monitor does not filter on, or ungrouped, and a signal on an absence monitor. A
    new bad-news monitor therefore cannot slip past the data check.
  - Every query on the fleet dashboard goes through the same scalar API over its widget's `live_span`. A widget
    with none (the spans timeseries) uses the time picker's opening hour. A grouped answer must hold every named
    cluster with a non-null value, and an ungrouped tile must hold a non-null value.
  - The leaderboard is left out (`DATA_DASHBOARDS`). Its cells count challenge outcomes, so they are blank
    until the room plays, and a setup check cannot require them.
  - `--data` without `--cluster`, `--cluster` without `--data`, and a cluster outside `kube_cluster_name:burritobot-*`
    are refused before any key is read.
- `fleet.sh` usage, `infra/datadog-fleet/README.md` and `docs/GO-LIVE-CHECKLIST.md` step d2 give the command.

**Tests.** `verify/test_fleet_monitors.py`'s fake org now answers `group_states=all` and `/api/v2/query/scalar`.
Two shipping clusters pass `--data`, and every fleet-dashboard query and both signals are sent, each over its
window, with the read-only key and no write. Each of these fails, naming the query and the cluster: one table
column blank for one cluster, a monitor group in No Data (which `--check` passes), a monitor with no group for a
cluster, a signal that answers nothing, a tile that answers null, a column that answers nothing at all, a
missing monitor, and a third named cluster that ships nothing. The validation cases above are each a check.
Weakening the loader to accept No Data, or to return 0 on a blank, or to skip the signals, fails the file.
`verify/test_fleet_monitors_live.py` runs `--data` after `--check` for `WIB_FLEET_CLUSTERS` (default
burritobot-public,burritobot-private, the two clusters in Whitney's sandbox org, #629).

**Not yet run on a cluster.** With both KubeCon clusters up and shipping, and one /chat on each within 5 minutes,
a session with the accen-dev profile runs `WIB_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT=accen-dev WIB_REGION=us-west-2 python3
verify/test_fleet_monitors_live.py` (in `bash verify/run-e2e.sh`). It needs #485's apply first. Two things only a
live org can settle: whether the read-only key may call `/api/v2/query/scalar` (`infra/ops-view/ops_view.py`
already sends it the same way), and whether kube-state-metrics core reports `condition:ready` with a
`status:true` series on a healthy node, as node-not-ready's signal assumes. If either is wrong, the live test
fails naming that query.

## 2026-10-31 · #707 · The workshop-agent Agent has an Application of its own, without RespectIgnoreDifferences

Decided in peopleforrester/talks-knowledge#110 (talks-knowledge decisions.md, 2026-10-30, d0e9958), the structural fix
#679 left open. In ai-layer the Agent's evil-mcp toolNames ignore sat inside its tools array, and ai-layer syncs with
RespectIgnoreDifferences=true. Argo CD v3.5.2 copied the ignored field back from live as a JSON merge patch holding the
whole live array, so on attendee, burn and full no git change to a tool entry reached a running cluster until
`fleet.sh converge` recreated the Agent. The recreate also reset the student's C7 state. Option (2), moving C7's
workshop control off the tools array, was not taken: `docs/MASTER-RECREATION-SPEC.md` row D14 keeps kagent `toolNames`
as the workshop cluster's C7 control (#516).

**What changed.**
- **The Agent moved** out of `gitops/ai-layer/resources.yaml` into `gitops/workshop-agent/agent.yaml`, a kustomize
  bundle of that one file in namespace `agent`. Its ModelConfigs, RemoteMCPServers, agent-sa and Role stay in ai-layer.
- **`gitops/bootstrap/apps/workshop-agent.yaml`** is the new Application, at sync wave 4, after ai-layer's 3, since
  the Agent names objects ai-layer creates. kagent makes the agent Deployment when the Agent appears, which is after
  ai-layer's otel-ordering-gate, so the pod is still instrumented. It keeps the evil-mcp toolNames ignore, rendered
  only when `c7Control` is not `gateway` as before, and the modelConfig ignore. Its sync options are
  `ServerSideApply=true` and `Force=true` (#349), with no `RespectIgnoreDifferences`. ai-layer lost both Agent
  ignores. Its RespectIgnoreDifferences comment now lists only the ignores it still has.
- **Every profile** (attendee, burn, admin, full and local-inference) lists `workshop-agent` beside `ai-layer`. The
  attendee count is 33 Applications, the instructor count 37: the run-of-show, the platform page and the design
  glance say so. platform-baseline.yaml's demo-agent entry is now `adopted` by `workshop-agent.yaml`. The build
  diagram's BurritoBot chip reads the new app.
- **Readers of the Agent** were repointed: fleet.sh `repair_agent_tools`, `verify/kubecon_probe.py`,
  `bedrock_profile_check.py` and `model_pin_check.py` (a `committed_manifests()` that reads both bundles), the C7
  toggle's and fallback's comments and hint, `tool_audit.py`, the Datadog monitor comment, lab-platform.yaml's
  instrumented note, the web terminal's toggle comment (both copies), and 30 offline tests that load the Agent.
  `test_bootstrap_chart.py` reads the Agent's inject annotation from the new bundle. It also checks that every
  profile listing ai-layer lists workshop-agent and that the c7Control guard is in workshop-agent.yaml alone.
  `test_bootstrap_chart_render.py` reads the rendered Agent ignore from workshop-agent and checks that ai-layer has
  none.
- **fleet.sh's comment** on `repair_agent_tools` says it is no longer the only route on the toolnames profiles. It
  stays in converge for a root pinned before this change, for an Agent whose list a field manager kept through a
  sync, and for a cluster Argo has not reconciled. It reads the committed list from the new bundle.
- **The spec** (`docs/MASTER-RECREATION-SPEC.md`) has workshop-agent at wave 4 in the components table, the Agent
  bundle in recreation steps 3 and 4, and the ignores bullet. The tier paragraph (#598) says how a tier lands now,
  and `docs/GO-LIVE-CHECKLIST.md` says the same.

**How the sync works now.** Without RespectIgnoreDifferences an ignore acts on the diff alone. A student's
guard-mcp-on narrows evil-mcp's toolNames live, the Agent still shows Synced, and selfHeal has nothing to do. A sync
applies the Agent as git has it. A git change to a workshop-mcp tool makes the Agent OutOfSync, and auto-sync lands
it on every profile with no converge. Because the Agent has its own Application, a change elsewhere in ai-layer
syncs ai-layer and leaves the Agent alone.

**Costs, accepted in #707.**
- A git change to evil-mcp's committed toolNames alone is ignored by the diff, so on the toolnames profiles it
  reaches new clusters only. #515 accepted the same cost for `agentgateway-c7-config`. On admin nothing ignores the
  list, so such a change lands there too.
- A sync after any other change to the Agent applies git's evil-mcp list and git's modelConfig. It resets a student's
  live guard-mcp-on, and a live modelConfig tier patch with it. #598 says no script applies a tier yet. A student
  whose guard-mcp-on is reset runs it again.

**Tests.** `verify/test_agent_tools_sync.py` keeps the v3.5.2 port. It shows the port still reproduces #679 under
ai-layer's old options, the check that keeps the port honest. It adds what a sync without the option applies, and
selfHeal, which syncs only an OutOfSync Agent. For each of attendee, burn, full and admin it then checks the rendered
workshop-agent Application: its path, its wave after ai-layer's, selfHeal and prune, ServerSideApply and Force, no
RespectIgnoreDifferences, and no Agent ignore left on ai-layer. It checks that git's twelve tools land on a stale
Agent and leave it Synced, and that a later workshop-mcp rename lands too. It checks that a fresh cluster gets the
committed Agent and that a live tier survives selfHeal with no git change. On the toolnames profiles it checks that
a student's guard-mcp-on survives a selfHeal with no git change, and it checks both costs above. On admin it checks
that a git change to evil-mcp's list lands. The check that no RespectIgnoreDifferences app ignores into a CRD array
now has no exception. `test_repair_agent_tools.sh` holds the new path and the comment. `test_agent_tools_exist.py`
and `test_recreation_spec_tier_swap.py` read the new Application.

**The previous attempt** (hecaton run on pool claude-performantpro-5) stopped before any work, because that pool's
podman store had a RunRoot under another worktree (1270196839-481-7103) and no `crun`. The fault was in the pool's
container setup. Nothing under `verify/` or `infra/` calls podman, and this run's pool answers `podman info` with
crun, so the repo had nothing to fix.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The structure is proven offline; Argo CD's real sync on a live Agent is not. Owed on a
burn or attendee cluster that is already up, in a session with AWS access: let the root move to a commit carrying
this change and confirm `workshop-agent` is Synced and Healthy. Then change a workshop-mcp tool in git and, with no
converge, run
`KUBECONFIG=<file> kubectl --context <ctx> -n agent get agent workshop-agent -o jsonpath='{.spec.declarative.tools[0].mcpServer.toolNames}'`.
It must print git's list. Then run guard-mcp-on in the web terminal, wait past a selfHeal (about a minute), and
confirm evil-mcp's toolNames still reads `["get_weather"]`. On a cluster that is already up, the first sync after
this change moves the Agent between Applications. If ai-layer's prune runs first, it deletes the Agent and
workshop-agent creates it again, so the pod cycles once and the student's C7 state resets. If workshop-agent applies
first, it rewrites the Agent's tracking annotation, and ai-layer no longer counts the Agent as its own to prune. The
live check above should note which one happened.

## 2026-10-31 · #715 · The five demo apps run lab-platform's web image by digest, set through kustomize.images at the root's registry

**What changed.** The demo-app-{hedgehog,mantis-shrimp,spider,unicorn,wombat} Deployments pulled
`docker.io/library/nginx:1.27-alpine` from Docker Hub. That was five anonymous pulls per cluster during an event,
and lab-platform's `deploy/mirror/pulled.tsv` (lab-platform#335, PR #337) lists them as a gap. They now run
`ghcr.io/peopleforrester/lab-platform/web@sha256:73cd15652cb8b8eb706bd43f8877541db7f7c9e5f810ef0739636a27fc34fbd9`. That is the
digest lab-platform's `deploy/watch-it-burn/images.tsv` pins, and on 2026-10-31 the `v1` tag on ghcr.io still served
it. The image is a Go static file server on base-static (`cmd/web`, `internal/webserve`) that reads one routes file,
`web.yaml`.

**Why through kustomize.images and not a literal reference.** `verify/test_image_registry.py` (#622) forbids a
literal `ghcr.io/peopleforrester/lab-platform` anywhere the root deploys. A root can pass an ECR pull-through cache
path as `imageRegistry`, and only an apps/ file is rendered with that value. So each demo-app directory is now a
kustomize bundle, with a `kustomization.yaml` over its three files. Its Deployment names the kustomize image `web`,
and its `gitops/bootstrap/apps/demo-app-*.yaml` sets
`web={{ .Values.imageRegistry }}/web@sha256:73cd…`. ai-layer.yaml sets llm-guard the same way (#652). The entry
carries the digest and no tag, so that the reference is the exact one images.tsv records.

**The routes file.** Each directory has a `web.yaml`, and the five copies are identical. It has the same shape as
lab-platform's `internal/webserve/testdata/demo-app.web.yaml`: `listen: ":8080"`, `root: /srv/www`, `/` serving
`index.html`, and `/healthz` answering `ok`. The kustomization generates it as `demo-app-<name>-web-<hash>`, mounted
at `/etc/web`, where the image reads it by default. Because the name carries a hash, a routes change rolls the pod.
The page ConfigMap is mounted read-only at `/srv/www`. `/index.html`, which nginx also served, is now a 404, and
nothing links to it.

**The port moved from 80 to 8080, and the Service did not.** The routes file listens on 8080 as lab-platform's
example does, so a non-root process with every capability dropped does not need to bind a privileged port. Each
Service keeps port 80, which console.conf proxies the `<app>-<cluster>` hostnames to, and now targets 8080.
`apps-allow-ingress` already admitted 8080 from the VPC CIDR and kube-system. Its port 80 rule stays, because
games/villain-apps still listens there. The comment now says so.

**The container.** `NETWORK_BOUNDARY=sandbox` is set. Without it the image refuses the all-interfaces bind and exits,
as a local run of the pinned binary showed. The root filesystem is read-only and nginx's cache, run and tmp
emptyDirs are gone. The probes ask `/healthz` on the named port.

**The allow-list.** restrict-image-registries already admits `ghcr.io/` and any ECR registry, and its comment already
named the web image. The new test checks the reference at the default registry and through a cache path. The image
is not added to verify-image-signatures. That policy adds a lab-platform image only once its signature has been
checked (#669). A `sha256-<digest>.sig` tag exists for this digest on ghcr.io, but it has not been verified against
the workshop key, so that is left as a follow-up.

**images.lock.** The `docker.io/library/nginx:1.27-alpine` row, which nothing references now, is replaced in its
position by `web ghcr.io/peopleforrester/lab-platform/web@sha256:73cd… repo:peopleforrester/lab-platform/cmd/web -`.
The `nginx:1.27-alpine` row stays, for the Dockerfile FROM lines.

**Tests.** `verify/test_demo_app_web_image.py` (offline) checks five things for each app. It checks the Application's
one images entry and how it parses. It checks the bundle and its generator. It checks web.yaml's routes, which must
be identical across the five. It checks the Deployment's image name, env, port, probes, mounts and securityContext,
and the Service's 80 to 8080. It also checks the allow-list at both registries and the images.lock row. Last, it
checks that no tracked file under gitops/ names Docker Hub nginx outside a comment, and that this sweep fires on the
old manifest. `verify/test_bootstrap_chart_render.py` (tools tier) renders the burn profile with and without
`imageRegistry`. It builds each bundle with the rendered entries as Argo CD does, and checks the Deployment's image
and that the web volume is the generated ConfigMap holding web.yaml as written. Outside the suites, this run ran the
pinned image's binary on its own against the wombat web.yaml, with only root and port changed for a non-root host.
`/` answered 200 text/html with the full page, `/healthz` answered `ok`, and without NETWORK_BOUNDARY it exited 1,
naming the bind.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** No E2E test fetches a party page. Owed on an attendee or full cluster in a session with
AWS access, after the root moves to a commit carrying this change:
`KUBECONFIG=<file> kubectl --context <ctx> -n apps get pods -l 'app in (demo-app-hedgehog,demo-app-mantis-shrimp,demo-app-spider,demo-app-unicorn,demo-app-wombat)' -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.containerStatuses[0].ready} {.status.containerStatuses[0].imageID}{"\n"}{end}'`
must show five Ready pods on the `web@sha256:73cd…` image. Then `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://hedgehog-<cluster>.agenticburn.com/`
must print 200, and the page must draw in a browser. The same holds for each of the other four hostnames.

## 2026-10-31 · #716 · Place the IMDS credential-theft beat in the KubeCon and DevOpsDays run-of-show

**Context.** #113 built the IMDS credential-theft challenge (`challenges/imds-node-creds/`: `FACILITATOR.md`
and `steal-node-creds.sh`) and the infra that makes it land on the community cluster alone (hop limit 2,
no `agent-deny-imds`). #113's decisions.md entry deferred the stage placement explicitly: "Final stage
placement in the run-of-show (which segment, how it flows in the 30-minute KubeCon demo vs the 2-hour
format) is the presenters' choreography call and is left as a follow-up." This issue, #716, is that
follow-up. The beat runs on the community cluster (`attackme`) as a watch-the-screen presenter beat. The
audience cannot do it from a phone, so it has the same shape as the C4 fork bomb "on our box only". That
same phone limit is why Challenge 8 (terminal RBAC) was cut from the KubeCon breakout.

**Decision.**
- **KubeCon 30-minute breakout** (`facilitation/kubecon-na-2026-run-of-show.md`, driven from `/kubecon`):
  the beat goes in **Segment 6, the OWASP/ASI close**, as the issue directed ("the natural slot is the
  OWASP/ASI close"). It is added after the OWASP Kubernetes Top 10 bullet and before "Burritos only", as an
  optional 1-minute watch-the-screen beat pegged to OWASP Agentic Security Initiative **ASI03, Identity and
  Privilege Abuse** (the same id the lab names in Challenge 8), run from a presenter checkout against the
  community kube-context, with the command and the owed caveats pointing at
  `challenges/imds-node-creds/FACILITATOR.md`. It is marked "the first thing to drop if the clock is behind"
  because segment 6 is already time-pressured and the break-it finale must win the remaining minutes. The
  same block is added to `gitops/ai-layer/web/kubecon.html` so the surface the presenters drive from carries
  it; the block is a `<div class="control">` prose block like the finale, because the beat is terminal-driven
  and has no copy-ready phone prompt, so it carries no `data-beat` article. A row was added to the "Challenges
  shown live, and challenges cut" table, internal id `ASI03`.
- **DevOpsDays 2-hour format.** DevOpsDays Portland 2026 is already delivered (conference-knowledge
  `devopsdays-portland-2026`, status delivered 2026-09-08 to 10), and the beat was built after it, so this
  is forward-looking for the next 2-hour run. The live 2-hour surface is `/brief`
  (`gitops/ai-layer/web/brief.html`), with `docs/RUN-OF-SHOW-2026-08.md` the retired-but-named artifact
  pointing at it. The beat is placed in both as the **watch-the-screen companion to Challenge 8** (ASI03):
  Challenge 8's own cloud-credential probe ends `IMDS: BLOCKED` on the student cluster (the control
  working); the presenters turn it inside out on the Community cluster where both IMDS controls are off.
  Framed as presenter-run, optional, and read-only, and kept off the numbered student challenge list
  (brief.html still says "no bonus challenges by design").

(`docs/CHALLENGE-ASSETS.md`, `verify/test_challenge_assets.py`'s `range(1,9)`, `docs/DESIGN-GLANCE.md`,
`lab.html`), exactly as #113 reasoned. Its id stays ASI03, which lives in the facilitator doc and the
terraform/values comments. No challenge-count file was touched.

**The deck is a separate follow-up (rounds-agenticburn).** Per the issue thread (rounds-agenticburn,
2026-10-31): the KubeCon deck (`peopleforrester/rounds-agenticburn`) has no IMDS beat, and its owner asked
that placing the beat in the deck's close be filed as an issue there with the slide wording. This repo
builds no slide HTML, so the deck change is handled by a follow-up on rounds-agenticburn.

## 2026-10-31T16:10:00Z · 2.3 · #643 · The standbys' gaps against the 10-28 call: zones, a watcher that cannot stay down, preflight, a teardown that finishes

An audit of 0061642 against #643's done-when and the 10-28 call ("12 public and 3 private, across zones and
regions ... no manual failover") found six gaps, each closed in code with an offline test:

- **Zones.** Every cluster is one node, and the node group used both lab subnets, so a standby's zone was the Auto
  Scaling group's pick. backups.tsv gains a `zone` column (a or b, the lab VPC's first or second private subnet); the
  cluster module takes `node_subnet_ids` (null keeps today's behavior for every other cluster, through the eks
  module's `coalesce(each.value.subnet_ids, var.subnet_ids)`); fleet.sh's `node_subnets_for` passes the one subnet
  and fails the build if the lab VPC lacks it. The standbys up at any moment cover both zones of every region.
- **The watcher could stay down.** Cron started it once; any exception, a reload that hung past its timeout
  (TimeoutExpired was uncaught), or a reboot ended automatic promotion until a person noticed. Now a tick's error is
  logged and retried, a hung reload is a failed attempt, and cron runs `watch --from --until` every 5 minutes; the
  lock keeps it to one, and a restart that finds it alive exits silently.
- **A region outage stalled the watcher.** Console-LB lookups ran one after another, each waiting out its own
  timeouts, so a us-west-2 outage could hold ticks off for minutes; a failed lookup also erased the known LB. Lookups
  now run concurrently and a failed one keeps the LB already known (the self-check decides health).
- **No preflight before spend.** A wave now runs `fleet.sh preflight` per region (the default account only, sized to
  that region's clusters) and skips a region that fails. `backups.py preflight` runs it alone.
- **The teardown refused everything after any promotion,** and its cron line removed the schedule anyway, leaving all
  15 standbys billing. It now keeps only the holder, destroys the rest, and exits 1 naming the holder.
- **Cron lines into a missing logs directory never ran** (the redirection fails before the command). Each line now
  makes the directory first; a test runs every line with sh on a checkout that has none.

The run of show gains the exact bring-up, rehearsal, schedule and teardown commands and a cost table: about $0.48
a standby-hour (EKS $0.10, t3.2xlarge $0.3328, 100 GiB gp3, the NLB and its two addresses), $0.07 an hour per new
lab VPC, roughly $95 for KubeCon and $22 for one rehearsal, from AWS list prices read 2026-10-31.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Everything above is offline. Owed, with Michael's go for the spend: the two lab VPC
applies, `backups.py preflight all`, both waves, `verify/test_backups_promotion_live.py` (which now also checks
each region's standbys landed in two distinct AZs, and that no scheduled watcher holds the lock), and the schedule.
`node_subnet_ids` has not been through `terraform plan`.

The view's spec asks for request count, tool calls by name, guard decisions, errors and cost. The 2026-10-29 build had
all but guard decisions and errors. Two widgets are added to `infra/datadog-room/room_view.yaml`:

- **What the guards stopped:** a logs count of guard-proxy's `input_blocklist_hit`, `input_classifier_block` and
  `output_scrub`, and workshop-mcp's `ticket_withheld`, grouped by `@event` only: the events the fleet leaderboard
  counts. Measured 2026-10-31 with the read-only key: the search parses, and over 30 days it found
  `input_classifier_block` and `ticket_withheld` on `burritobot-private` and nothing on `burritobot-public`, whose
  guards were off. So it reads zero until a presenter turns a guard on for attackme.
- **Chats that failed:** chat spans with `status.code:status_code_error` from the `span_metrics` connector. Measured
  the same day: Datadog stores the value lower-cased (`status_code_error`, `status_code_unset`); the upper-case
  OTel spelling matches nothing.

`room_view.py`'s fence now admits a logs query only as a count, grouped by `@event`, with
`kube_cluster_name:burritobot-public` as a top-level term and no top-level `OR`, naming or excluding no other
cluster. Every query, metrics or logs, is refused if it names a content attribute (`CONTENT_MARKERS`).
`verify/test_room_view.py` covers each refusal, and checks that every guard event is one the platform logs.

Public sharing in the sandbox org: Datadog's shared dashboards and permissions pages (read 2026-10-31) name no
sandbox or trial limit. An admin can turn sharing types off under Public Sharing settings, and
`dashboards_public_share` is a Standard-role permission. Whether sharing is on in Whitney's org shows only at the
apply. The read-only key named the org `Datadog` on 2026-10-31, so the prefix guard passes.

Not yet run on an org: `--apply`, `--check` and `verify/test_room_view_live.py`, which need a write key from
Whitney's user. Not measured: whether a logs-backed top list renders on a public share. The shared dashboards page
lists Top List as supported and says nothing about data sources.

## 2026-10-31 · #721 · The collector writes generate_content's input and output from kagent's ADK payloads

**What changed.** A new processor, `transform/adk_model_content` (gitops/otel-collector/values.yaml), runs after
`transform/adk_tool_content` on every profile (and before burn's `transform/scrub_pii`). On a `generate_content`
span it parses `gcp.vertex.agent.llm_request` / `llm_response` and writes `gen_ai.input.messages`,
`gen_ai.output.messages` and `gen_ai.system_instructions` in the GenAI semconv message shape (roles
user/assistant/tool; parts text, reasoning, tool_call, tool_call_response; finish_reason). Datadog's OpenTelemetry
instrumentation page, read 2026-10-31, names those three attributes as the first source of an LLM span's messages,
JSON strings, then the `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details` event. It copies, never moves, and leaves a span
that already has `gen_ai.input.messages` alone.

**Why the collector, not the runtime (option 1 on the issue).** kagent v0.10.1's Go runtime stamps the two ADK
attributes itself (`go/adk/pkg/telemetry/attributes.go`) on adk-go v2.1.0, which has no gen_ai message attributes.
adk-go main does (`internal/telemetry/genaimessages.go`, behind its content-capture switches), so a later kagent may
make this processor redundant; the `== nil` guards keep it from overwriting that.

**The 2048 cut.** kagent's own cap is 32 KiB, over which it writes `{"original_size","payload_prefix","truncated"}`.
2048 is Tempo's `max_attribute_bytes` default, so the cut read in Tempo is likely Tempo's and the collector sees the
whole payload. Not confirmed on a cluster. Whatever arrives cut: the HasPrefix/HasSuffix guard skips it, a cut that
ends in `}` fails ParseJSON (error_mode ignore, one warn line), and in every case nothing is written and the span
goes on unchanged. verify/test_adk_model_content_e2e.py drives each case through the pinned otelcol-contrib 0.160.0.

**The feature gate.** The statements use OTTL lambdas (MapEach, Filter, Any, When), alpha behind
`ottl.functions.enableLambda`, now in `command.extraArgs`. Without the gate the collector refuses the whole config,
so `collector_render.feature_gate_args()` reads that list and every E2E test that runs the traces processors passes
it. verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py's second model call now carries the Go runtime's ADK attributes instead of
gen_ai messages, as the issue noted.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** After rollout on a cluster with Datadog (collector pods restarted), send one /chat and
check: `kubectl -n monitoring logs ds/otel-collector-opentelemetry-collector-agent | grep -c adk_model_content`
(expect 0 or a rare ParseJSON warn), then in LLM Observability (or `/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/spans/events`, ml_app
burritobot) that the `generate_content` rows show input, output and the system prompt. Also read the length of
`gcp.vertex.agent.llm_request` on that span in Datadog: over 2048 confirms the Tempo reading above.

## 2026-10-31 · #486 · A Falco DaemonSet with no ready pod reads as falco:false, and the test pins it

Michael's 2026-10-27 probe of watch-it-burn-michael-admin (staging d2d75c5, guard-proxy 96f3203) found the
badges matching the cluster and the Community override gone, but the cluster's Falco pod was crash-looping
on kernel 6.18 (#626). The open question before closing #486: does `/controls` answer falco:true for a
DaemonSet that exists but has no ready pod?

**Answer: no.** The pinned proxy.py (submodule at 000f57e, which carries f1fbd46) reads
`security/falco` and sets `falco` to `status.numberReady > 0`, so a crash-looping DaemonSet (numberReady 0),
a DaemonSet that has not reported readiness, an empty status, a missing DaemonSet and a 403 all read false.
guard-proxy-agenticburn's conformance suite pins the same five shapes
(`conformance/test_admin_endpoints.py::test_controls_falco_reads_the_daemonset`); all eight Falco tests
pass against the pinned commit.

**What changes here:** `verify/test_falco_badge_measured.py` used to require only that the pinned proxy.py
read the DaemonSet path. A later pin bump that regressed to "the DaemonSet exists" would have passed it. It
now imports the pinned proxy.py, swaps its cluster read for a fake API and runs `read_controls()` for the
six shapes above, requiring true only with a ready pod. Replacing the readiness gate with `ds is not None`
fails three of them. The test stays in the offline gate: it needs the submodule, which
`verify/ensure-submodules.sh` already checks out, and no cluster.

**Not changed:** the Go rewrite's `/controls` still answers 501 (PRD #412, `internal/server/server.go`
`unbuiltGET`); it is a later milestone of that PRD, and the workshop runs proxy.py. The crash loop itself is
#626 (Falco 0.45.1 via chart 9.2.1, 89fce6a).

## 2026-10-31 · #583 · The live Bedrock check sends its model call over a port-forward to the gateway, not from inside workshop-agent

**Context.** The coordinator ran `verify/test_gateway_bedrock_tagged_live.py` on watch-it-burn-community on
2026-10-31 (accen-dev, us-west-2, main at 6ffb4df) and it exited 1 with 7 PASS and 3 FAIL. The pin is live:
agentgateway's `BEDROCK_NOVA_MODEL` is the cluster's application inference profile ARN, and every Ready gateway pod
carries it. The model call never ran, though. The test ran `python3 -c` in workshop-agent's default container,
`kagent`, and got `exec: "python3": executable file not found in $PATH`. The two checks after it failed because
there was no response to read.

**What the image has.** The published `ghcr.io/kagent-dev/kagent/app:0.10.1` (index sha256:d39d5c948386...,
linux/amd64 sha256:252f241eea11..., pulled and listed with podman on 2026-10-31, never run) puts
`/.kagent/.venv/bin` first on its PATH. Its `python3` there resolves through `python` and
`/python/cpython-3.13-linux-x86_64-gnu` to `/python/cpython-3.13.15-linux-x86_64-gnu/bin/python3.13`, which is a
real file. So the image alone does not explain the failure. The kagent 0.10.1 controller sets no PATH on the
container (go/core/internal/controller/translator/agent/manifest_builder.go, buildPodTemplate). Nothing in this repo
does either: not the Agent's `deployment.env`, not the watch-it-burn-python Instrumentation, and no KubeArmorPolicy
selects the pod. Why the live exec found no python3 is still open. The same listing shows the image has nothing in
`/bin` or `/usr/bin`, so there is no shell, curl, wget, env, grep or ls. No other command run inside that
container would have got round it.

**Decision.** The call is sent from the host the test runs on, by `verify/gateway_forward.py`. It starts a
`kubectl --context <ctx> -n agent port-forward --address 127.0.0.1 pod/<a Ready gateway pod> :3002`, reads the
local port from kubectl's `Forwarding from` line, POSTs the same 5-token chat to `/bedrock/v1/chat/completions`,
returns the status and Bedrock's whole reply, and stops the port-forward. The request goes through the same :3002
listener, the same `/bedrock` route and the same backend as the agent's call. The gateway signs it with its own Pod
Identity credentials whoever sends it, and the model in the path is its `BEDROCK_NOVA_MODEL`. So a 200 answers the
issue's question (does Bedrock take the %2F-escaped ARN through agentgateway) just as one sent from the agent pod
would. `verify/local-inference-live.py` had the same exec and now uses the same helper, with `deploy/agentgateway`
and the `/local` route.

**What it gives up.** The call no longer goes over the pod-to-pod hop from workshop-agent, so it no longer touches
chat-path-ingress (#552). A port-forward reaches the gateway pod's loopback through the kubelet, which no
NetworkPolicy judges. That ingress rule's live check is `verify/test_llm_bypass_live.py`, which reads off the live
policies that workshop-agent is admitted to :3002 and that other pods are not.

**REJECTED: an ephemeral debug container in the workshop-agent pod, or a short-lived pod with workshop-agent's
label.** Each would keep the agent-pod hop. But an ephemeral container stays in the running agent pod's spec until
that pod is replaced, and the clusters this runs on are the KubeCon breakout's, up through 2026-11-12. A pod with
`app.kubernetes.io/name: workshop-agent` falls under the workshop-agent Service's selector and would be handed
students' A2A traffic. Both also need an image the armed admin profile admits. The port-forward changes nothing on
the cluster.

**Tests.** `verify/test_gateway_forward.py` (offline, 17 checks) runs the helper against a stub kubectl. The stub
refuses any call without the expected `--context` and takes only a loopback port-forward to :3002. The test covers
the path, the model and `max_tokens` the request carries; a 200 reply longer than 400 characters still parsing as
JSON; a 403 coming back with Bedrock's message; a port-forward that never comes up (an error with kubectl's reason,
and no request); and no port-forward left running after any of them. It also holds both live checks to the helper,
with no exec into workshop-agent.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The coordinator re-runs `CONTEXT=<ctx> python3 verify/test_gateway_bedrock_tagged_live.py`
on watch-it-burn-community (kubeconfig from `aws eks update-kubeconfig --kubeconfig /tmp/community.kubeconfig --name
watch-it-burn-community --region us-west-2 --profile accen-dev`). A 200 through the port-forward closes #583. Any other
status prints Bedrock's reply, and that reply says what encoding the path needs on agentgateway v1.7.0.

## 2026-10-31 · #265 · ADK's merged tool span is not marked, so a block is one error in the trace list

**What the live check found.** The coordinator ran the check list the 2026-10-30 #265 entry left owed, on
watch-it-burn-private (host burritobot-private) at staging `0934f27`, and posted it on #265. `verify/c1-exfil-block.sh`
and `verify/one_root_probe.py` passed, `execute_tool run_shell` was red with `error.type:tool_error` and its arguments
and result on the span, and the generate_content after it was not red. But Agent Observability's trace list read
**2** errors. The second was `execute_tool (merged)` (LLM Observability name `(merged tools)`), the parent of
`execute_tool run_shell`.

**Why.** When the model asks for more than one tool in a turn, adk-go opens one span around them
(`internal/llminternal/base_flow.go` handleFunctionCalls, read on google/adk-go main 2026-10-31), and
`TraceMergedToolCallsResult` (`internal/telemetry/telemetry.go`) gives it `gen_ai.tool.name` "(merged tools)",
`tool_call_args` "N/A" and, as `gcp.vertex.agent.tool_response`, the whole merged function-response event: every
call's response, the failed run_shell's "command FAILED" included. Both of `transform/adk_tool_content`'s status
rules matched that text. The call that failed is the run_shell span under it, so by question 925's rule (status is left
unset on an operation that ended without an error) it stays unmarked. ADK still sets its status itself when the
merge returns a Go error (`RecordError`), which this does not touch.

**What changed.**
- `gitops/otel-collector/values.yaml`: the six status, message and `error.type` statements of
  `transform/adk_tool_content` now start `where name != "execute_tool (merged)" and`. The argument and result copies
  still run on the merged span, so its row shows every response.
- `verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py`: the two Challenge 1 tool calls now sit under a merged span shaped as adk-go writes
  it. The new checks are that the merged span is not red and that run_shell is the trace's only error span. The
  event is written with json.dumps' spaces so both rules, isError and the text, would match it; adk-go writes it
  compact, which only the text rule matches. Against `0934f27`'s config it fails 9 checks (3 per profile); with this
  change it passes.
- `verify/test_collector_config.py` (offline) pins the exclusion on all six statements.

**The check list, corrected.** The 2026-10-30 entry's list names `call_llm`. The Go runtime the clusters run emits
none (#713, above); its agent step is `invoke_agent workshop_agent`. The criterion is now: `invocation` and
`invoke_agent workshop_agent` carry `gen_ai.provider.name:aws.bedrock`, as every execute_tool and generate_content
span does. The live check found that already true. The fixture keeps a `call_llm` for the Python runtime.

**Not yet run on a cluster:** the trace list reading 1. On a cluster with this collector config rolled out and Datadog
on: `bash verify/c1-exfil-block.sh <host> <ctx> <profile>`, then open that interaction in Agent Observability and
check that the trace list shows 1 error and Span Errors in Trace is 1, and that `execute_tool (merged)` is not red.
`CONTEXT=<ctx> python3 verify/one_root_probe.py` should still pass. Whether Agent Observability's side panel shows
run_shell's arguments and result is still a look by eye. Offline: `python3 verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py`.

**Also seen, filed as a follow-up.** The live check found two root-level spans in Agent Observability: guard-proxy's
`POST` (kind llm, holding a `chat` on amazon.nova-pro-v1:0) and a `POST` (kind workflow) holding `invocation`. The
root row reads "No content" for input and output. Tempo and APM have one root, so the trace is whole and the two
rows come from how LLM Observability groups spans.

**Replayed on staging `ef66c77` (run 14714).** Run 14665's branch sat on staging `e5d0a7d`, and its tests gate failed
on `verify/test_fleet_wall_check.sh`. That commit renamed the run-of-show heading "Segment 1: Cold open" to "Segment 1:
Opening" while the test still looked for the old heading, and `ef66c77` (#742) moved the test to the new one. None of

## 2026-11-01 · #725 · The C1 stage-2b DNS-exfil path on the MCP side is the in-image Python name-lookup form

**What was built.** #725 is the MCP-side half of the C1 two-stage DNS beat whose design #723 landed at
`docs/research/2026-10-31-c1-dns-exfil-beat.md`. It is `challenges/c1-exfil-s3/dns-exfil.py`, the in-image
Python name-lookup form of the exfil hop, and `verify/test_c1_dns_exfil.py`, its offline cover. The hop is the
DNS twin of the HTTPS curl in `challenges/c1-exfil-s3/fallback.kubectl.sh`: it reads the demographics
`get_marketing_intel` returns (`gitops/ai-layer/workshop-mcp-server.py:190`), builds one query name
`<marker>.<demographics>.<collector-zone>`, and looks it up with `socket.getaddrinfo`. A short internal pointer
was added to `challenges/c1-exfil-s3/README.md`. No change was made to `workshop-mcp-server.py` or to the image.

**Why this shape, at the curl beat's altitude.** The curl beat has no dedicated exfil tool on the MCP server.
The agent is socially engineered to call `get_marketing_intel` and then POST the result through `run_shell`, and
the committed, deterministic representation of that hop is `fallback.kubectl.sh`. Stage 2b keeps the same shape.
The hop runs through `run_shell` and the in-image `python3`, so the image stays `curl` and `ca-certificates`
only, with no `dnsutils`, `dig` or `nslookup` added. It emits one representative lookup carrying the demographic
shares, the room-view payload, the way the curl beat POSTs the intel once. There is no encoder, no label
chunking and no tunnelling engine, which keeps it clear of weaponized tooling and at the defensive, educational
altitude of the design note and `docs/beacon-collector-spec.md`. The exfil is the query leaving the pod, so a
name the collector does not resolve (NXDOMAIN) still counts as sent, as a curl the beacon accepts does however
it answers.

**Why no server tool and no lab-text change.** Adding an MCP tool would be a higher altitude than the curl beat,
which exfiltrates through the general `run_shell`, and would show up on the agent's `toolNames` allowlist. The
design note is deferred to the next event and changes no lab text, slide, run of show or deploy config; the
attendee-facing `challenges/LAB-TEXT.md` was left untouched, and `dns-exfil.py` lives beside the C1 fallback as
build-time tooling inside the lab, which is where the note says the stage-2b tool behaviour is written.

**Tests.** `verify/test_c1_dns_exfil.py` loads the server with the same `tool_audit` stand-in
`verify/test_run_shell_failure.py` uses, loads the hop, and stubs `socket.getaddrinfo` so it makes no real DNS
query and needs no network. It proves the payload exists (`get_marketing_intel` returns demographic shares), the
shares ride out in one DNS-label-safe query name under the zone, `send()` looks that name up through the stdlib
resolver and a NXDOMAIN still counts as sent, the hop opens no HTTPS or curl path and imports stdlib only, and
the Dockerfile installs only `curl` and `ca-certificates` with no name-lookup binary. `bash verify/run-tests.sh`
and `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` are green.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The live check that the DNS lookups reach the collector with the
`agent-egress-allowlist` NetworkPolicy still enforced is owed under the `verify/run-e2e.sh` tier, parallel to
`verify/c1-exfil-block.sh` and taking `<host> <kube-context>`. It pipes `dns-exfil.py` into the `workshop-mcp`
pod and asserts the DNS collector's view records the query while the beacon count holds. It needs a fresh
attendee cluster, AWS, and the DNS collector and zone, so it is tracked by the live-validation child #728, after
the collector #726. The FQDN-aware control that closes the door is the open decision on #724 and is built by #727.
## 2026-11-01 · #742 · A /chat turn past guard-proxy's forward limit now stops the agent, and the Agent says runtime: go

**Where the time went.** Michael read the private Tempo trace f7fc16a5debc57b7240a11ccfdebef70 on 2026-10-31 (his
comment on #742). The time went into tool calls, in a loop. guard-proxy gave up at PROXY_TIMEOUT (120 s) and
answered the room's 502, and the agent ran on for 9,007 s. In that time it made 613 `deploy_app` calls sending 5
distinct manifests, none of which parsed, and it kept going after deploy_app began raising its refusals as errors. attackme had two more such loops left over from #644's load replay.
Deleting the workshop-agent pod on both clusters stopped them.

**Where the fix belongs, of the three the issue named.**
- *A cap on tool iterations in the Agent.* There is none to set. kagent v0.10.1's Agent CRD has no iteration, turn
  or LLM-call limit (read in the v0.10.1 source, `go/api/v1alpha2/agent_types.go`).
- *PROXY_TIMEOUT against TURN_TIMEOUT.* Unchanged, at 120 and 270. A runaway loop outlasts any timeout, so raising
  PROXY_TIMEOUT only delays the same 502. The forward's 120 s is under the turn's 270 s, so the forward is what ends
  a runaway turn, and the 270 s still fits under the console nginx's 285 s (verify/test_audience_path.py).
- *The agent's concurrency.* Not the cause: the time went into one turn's tool calls, not a wait in front of it.

The fix is the cancel. guard-proxy-agenticburn#27 (5fe5a7c) sends the /chat forward as a non-blocking A2A
message/send and polls it with tasks/get. When the forward fails or its time runs out while the task is still running,
it answers the 502 and then sends tasks/cancel for that task. ef66c77 pinned that build (fb6e2bf) here, and
`verify/guard-proxy-pin-on-main.sh` passes on it. guard-proxy-agenticburn#29 checked the agent's side live on
watch-it-burn-private on 2026-10-31: on the Go runtime, tasks/cancel through agentgateway's :3000 route stops the
running tool call, and nothing runs after it.

**The phone's sentence.** A turn that ends this way answers 502 with
`{"reply": "BurritoBot's kitchen isn't answering. Try again in a moment.", "guarded": false, ...}`, the /chat shape
the page shows whatever the status, so the phone reads that sentence and not "(502)".

**What this run adds.**
- `gitops/workshop-agent/agent.yaml` writes out `spec.declarative.runtime: go`. The v0.10.1 CRD already defaults
  the field to go, and both #697 and guard-proxy-agenticburn#29 read go live, so the sync changes nothing on a
  running cluster. It is written out because the cancel depends on it: kagent's Python runtime raises
  NotImplementedError from cancel and keeps running (guard-proxy-agenticburn#29). A default that changed, or a
  cluster created under an older CRD, would quietly bring back the 9,007 s loop.
- `verify/test_chat_turn_cancel.py`, offline. It checks that the pin contains 5fe5a7c, that the Agent says runtime
  go, and that PROXY_TIMEOUT is under TURN_TIMEOUT. Then it runs the pinned proxy.py with every value guard-proxy's
  Deployment sets, with the two timeouts scaled from 120 s and 270 s down to 1 s and 2.25 s. A fake agent accepts the
  turn as a task and never finishes it. The test checks that the room gets the 502 with the sentence above at
  PROXY_TIMEOUT, that the agent then gets one tasks/cancel naming the task, and that guard-proxy logs
  `forward_error` and `task_cancel`. With the submodule checked out at a022fa5, the build before the cancel, 6 of
  its checks fail: that build reads the agent's submitted task as the reply and answers 200, and sends no cancel.
- `verify/test_a2a_usage_key.py` checked that the runtime is python, reading an unset field as python, as kagent's
  `EffectiveDeclarativeRuntime` does. The API server fills in the CRD default (go) first, so that check passed on a
  value no cluster held. It now checks go, and that guard-proxy meters `adk_usage_metadata`, the Go runtime's key,
  through its fallback. `docs/MASTER-RECREATION-SPEC.md` no longer calls Python the default runtime.

**Not addressed here.** The issue's first sighting notes that the 14:45 trace never reached Datadog. The agent's
spans could not end while its turn ran on, and the cancel ends the turn. This run did not check whether that alone
gets such a trace to Datadog.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The proxy's own half, a `task_cancel` log line after a real runaway turn, needs the
re-pinned guard-proxy synced on a cluster. A session with AWS access, after the next bring-up of a cluster it
provisioned, replays load with `verify/load_replay.py` as in #644. Then it reads
`KUBECONFIG=/tmp/<cluster>.kubeconfig kubectl --context <ctx> -n agent logs deploy/guard-proxy -c proxy | grep -E
'"event": "(forward_error|task_cancel|task_cancel_failed)"'`. Every `forward_error` that had a task should be
followed by `task_cancel`, with no `task_cancel_failed`, and the workshop-mcp log should show no tool call a minute
later. guard-proxy-agenticburn#29's comment of 2026-10-31 records the agent-side check that already passed.

+call goes from kagent to Bedrock. Before M3 can be built, either guard-proxy or a second hop has to go
+between kagent and Bedrock. Estimating tokens from the A2A prompt text, or cancelling the agent's turn
+mid-flight, are rejected (guard-proxy-agenticburn decisions.md, 2026-10-31): neither bounds what a single
+model call spends. The embedded store (decision 2 below) does not depend on the hop. It holds the spent-so-far
+that guard-proxy already meters, so it can land on its own, before the hop is chosen.

## 2026-11-01 · #679 · guard-proxy's env froze in order, not content: converge reorders it, and verify reads the rollout from hashed names

The issue was reopened twice after 69ba6cf. guard-proxy's new `CONSOLE_ORIGIN` (a6af457) never reached either KubeCon
cluster, and guard-proxy stayed OutOfSync. Then, after ed8dbf8, every ai-layer sync reported Succeeded and applied
nothing new. The thread asked for four things: a fix covering any list with an ignored element, guard-proxy Synced
after an env change, the Agent Synced after a tools change, and a rollout check that reads the hashed ConfigMap
names, not the sync phase. #707 (813404e) already gives the Agent an Application of its own without
RespectIgnoreDifferences, so the Agent half is on staging. This entry covers the rest.

**Redone on #707's layout, not cherry-picked.** The previous run's draft (run 12949, 208557d, cut from staging at
eb57bae) was never merged, and `verify/draft-drift.sh` named 54 drifted paths. It moved the Agent into its own
`ai-layer-agent` Application. #707 had made the same move as `workshop-agent`, with the Agent at
`gitops/workshop-agent/agent.yaml`, so this run drops that half of the draft and its thirty reader edits. Run 14977 committed this on staging ef66c77 and failed on a stale base; run 15181 rebased it onto 4e86b30, where only this file overlapped (both sides append), and re-ran both suites. What is
kept and redone here: the real-code replay, the strategic-merge half of the port, `repair_env_order`,
`ai_layer_rollout` and the GOTCHAS section. The replay and the tests now read the Agent from #707's bundle and the
workshop-agent Application.

**Reproduced with Argo CD's own code.** `docs/research/2026-10-30-argo-sync-replay/replay.sh` runs v3.5.2's
`normalizeTargetResources` (copied verbatim) and `util/argo/diff.StateDiff` against envtest v1.34.1's kube-apiserver,
with server-side apply as argocd-controller. On 2026-11-01, on this layout, all 25 checks passed. What it shows:
- A built-in kind (guard-proxy) takes a strategic merge patch with merge keys, so its env list does not freeze in
  content. A `CONSOLE_ORIGIN` added in git lands in git's place on the first sync, a live `MODEL_TIER` toggle
  survives, and the Deployment reads Synced. The thread's guess that the whole env list was held is wrong in that
  form.
- The list does freeze in order. The patch carries `$setElementOrder/env` from live, so a sync applies the live
  order. The 2026-10-29 stopgap, `kubectl set env CONSOLE_ORIGIN=...`, appended the entry. From then on every sync
  kept it last, while the diff (and a server dry run of git's Deployment) puts it before `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`. So
  guard-proxy read OutOfSync for good, and selfHeal synced it alone every few seconds. Those are the partial syncs
  that held back ed8dbf8.
- New this run: a commit that only moves an entry freezes the same way, from git's side.
- After `repair_env_order`'s rewrite, one sync reads Synced, both after the stopgap and after a git-only reorder.
- The Agent before #707 (in ai-layer, respecting its ignores) never gets `read_support_ticket`. In the workshop-agent
  Application it gets git's twelve tools and reads Synced, and a student's guard-mcp-on still reads Synced.
- One question stays open: why a6af457's own sync did not land `CONSOLE_ORIGIN` before the stopgap. Through this code
  it lands. The live controller history is the only witness, and this run has no cluster.
- The replay now reads the live object with its managedFields, as Argo CD's live cache holds it. The first draft's
  `kubectl get` left them out.

**What changed.**
- `fleet.sh` `repair_env_order`, a converge step after `repair_agent_tools`. It has a row in `ENV_ORDER_LISTS` for
  each list ai-layer ignores an element of: guard-proxy/proxy and agentgateway/agentgateway. When the live env order
  differs from git's, it JSON-patches the live entries into git's order, values kept, as the Argo controller SA,
  with a `test` op on the container name. The pod rolls, so guard-proxy's runtime toggles and cost counter start
  again from its env.
- `fleet.sh` `ai_layer_rollout`, run by `verify_one`. It runs only when ai-layer's sync revision is this checkout's
  HEAD and gitops/ai-layer is clean. It then renders the bundle and checks two things: every hashed ConfigMap and
  Secret the commit generates exists live, and each Deployment mounts the commit's hashed names. A miss records
  `<name>:ai-layer-rollout`. A cluster at another revision is reported but not judged.
- `verify/test_agent_tools_sync.py` keeps #707's Agent checks. It adds apimachinery's strategic merge patch with
  `$setElementOrder` (mergePatchIntoOriginal, normalizeSliceOrder, mergeSortedSlice) beside the JSON merge patch. It
  runs guard-proxy's env through ai-layer's rendered ignores: a6af457 from git, the stopgap, a git-only reorder, and
  the repair. It now holds two rules over every profile. No Application that respects ignores may ignore inside a
  CRD's array. Every ignored element of a built-in list must be a row of `ENV_ORDER_LISTS`, and every row must be
  such a list.
- `verify/test_fleet_converge_repairs.sh` gains the 2026-10-29 env state, five rollout cases and the wiring.
- `docs/GOTCHAS-FLEET-AND-DELIVERY.md`'s guard-proxy section said the whole env was ignored and told operators to
  `kubectl set env`. It now says what git delivers and that an env entry is never added live. It names the repair,
  and it records the by-hand recovery from a stuck selfHeal operation that worked on 2026-10-29. ai-layer.yaml's
  ignore and RespectIgnoreDifferences comments say the same.

**Considered, not taken:** dropping RespectIgnoreDifferences from ai-layer, or moving guard-proxy into an Application
without it, as #707 did for the Agent. A sync would then apply git's env whole and correct the order, but every
guard-proxy commit would reset the Beat-2 toggles and the cost cap mid-workshop. On ai-layer it would also reset the
Bedrock ARN pin, the C7 gateway rule and the C8 Role. The freeze needs a live addition or a pure reorder, and the GOTCHAS
rule and the ai-layer comment forbid both. The converge repair covers the rest.

**Tests and mutations.** `bash verify/run-tests.sh` and `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` were run, with the results
in the run report. Each of these mutations fails a test: repair_env_order never patching (5 shim failures), the
agentgateway row dropped, the port ignoring `$setElementOrder`, and verify_one not running the rollout check (2).

**Tooling.** The replay is a by-hand research tool, not a gate test. It builds the argo-cd module (about 600 Go
modules) and runs an apiserver, about three minutes cold. Its pins are argo-cd v3.5.2 (VERSIONS.lock's), k8s.io/*
v0.36.1 (argo-cd's replaces) and envtest v1.34.1, checked against the SHA-512 in controller-tools'
envtest-releases.yaml (2026-10-30).

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Owed on each KubeCon cluster (watch-it-burn-community, watch-it-burn-private), in a
session with AWS access, once the root syncs this commit: run `./fleet.sh converge watch-it-burn-community
watch-it-burn-private` from infra/terraform/fleet. If `CONSOLE_ORIGIN` is still appended there, expect one "env is out
of git's order" line per cluster. Then guard-proxy should read Synced, and the run should print "ai-layer <sha> is
rolled out". Also confirm the workshop-agent Application is Synced with twelve workshop-mcp tools (#707's owed
check). On a fresh attendee cluster run `bash verify/run-e2e.sh` with CONTEXT set.
## 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z · build · Challenge 8 reads BurritoBot's env off the pod spec, not by exec (#743)

**The bug.** Challenge 8's "look inside BurritoBot's own container" beat told the student to run
`kubectl -n agent exec deploy/workshop-agent -c kagent -- sh -c 'env | grep ^AWS_; ls -a ~/.aws
/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount'` in `challenges/LAB-TEXT.md`, `gitops/ai-layer/web/lab.html`
and `verify/test_agent_cloud_credential_live.py`. The kagent app image the chart deploys,
`ghcr.io/kagent-dev/kagent/app:0.10.1`, has no shell and no `env`, `grep` or `ls` anywhere on its
filesystem (exported and listed with podman during #583); its only interpreter is
`/.kagent/.venv/bin/python3`. So the exec fails on every cluster and the beat shows the student nothing.

**The fix.** The beat now reads the same facts off the pod spec, which does not exec into the container:
`kubectl -n agent get pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=workshop-agent -o jsonpath='{range
.items[0].spec.containers[?(@.name=="kagent")].env[*]}{.name}={.value}{"\n"}{end}'`. The EKS Pod Identity
webhook injects `AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI` (the 169.254.170.23 agent) and
`AWS_CONTAINER_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN_FILE` into the kagent container's env at admission, so they are on the
pod spec and the jsonpath surfaces them, along with the absence of any static key. The prose no longer
claims "no ~/.aws directory" (a filesystem fact the read cannot show) and leans on the ServiceAccount
step just above it for the no-token point; the live test already asserts no container mounts the default
Kubernetes token off the same pod spec (`TOKEN_DIR not in mounts`).

**Files changed together.** `gitops/ai-layer/web/lab.html` (the beat's command and prose).
`verify/test_agent_cloud_credential_live.py` (the regex that lifts the beat's command out of the page now
matches the `get pod ... jsonpath` form; the output checks drop the two `No such file or directory` lines
and keep the pointer, token-file and no-static-key assertions). `challenges/LAB-TEXT.md` is a generated
export of `lab.html` (#419), so it was re-made with `bash verify/export-lab-text.sh` after `lab.html` was
committed, re-stamping its source blob and commit. One file the issue did not name had to change too:
`verify/test_agent_cloud_credential.py` (the offline render gate) pins the beat's commands verbatim in
`LAB_CMDS`, so its exec entry was replaced with the new read command to keep `verify/run-tests.sh` green.

**Tests.** `bash verify/run-tests.sh` is green, including the two render gates
(`test_agent_cloud_credential.py`, `test_lab_text_export.py`).

**Not yet run on a cluster.** This run has no cluster, so the live half was not exercised. The owed check
is `CONTEXT=<ctx> IAM_PIPELINE_PROFILE=<p> IAM_PIPELINE_REGION=<r> python3
verify/test_agent_cloud_credential_live.py` (driven by `bash verify/run-e2e.sh`) against a fresh attendee
cluster: it lifts the new command out of the live `lab.html`, runs it, and asserts the output carries the
Pod Identity pointer and token-file env and no static key. The issue also asked to first read the live
pod's image and try the command as written; on a cluster run `kubectl --context <ctx> -n agent get pod -l
app.kubernetes.io/name=workshop-agent -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.containers[0].image}'` to confirm the
deployed digest, which would also explain the separate `exec ... python3` "executable file not found"
seen on watch-it-burn-community in #583.

first replay, on 2026-10-31, had 4 such turns. This check is read during that re-run and does not ask for a

The run-of-show's Night Before step for #644 now ends with the two log reads and what they should show, before
attackme's reset. A `forward_error` reading `chat forward failed: timed out` should be followed by one
`task_cancel` and no `task_cancel_failed`. The workshop-mcp `shim` log should show no `tool_invocation` later

forward failed`), which does not. The room's turns take the first.

during #644's re-run. Those readings close #750.
## 2026-11-01 · #746 · Why Agent Observability draws one BurritoBot interaction as two roots, and why neither collector option joins them

**No code changed.** This entry records what was read, and the question it leaves for the coordinator.

**How Datadog builds the Agent Observability tree from OTLP spans.** Datadog's OTel instrumentation page
(docs.datadoghq.com/llm_observability/instrumentation/otel_instrumentation, read 2026-11-01) sets these rules:
- A trace is converted only if some span has `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.provider.name`,
  `openinference.span.kind`, `langfuse.observation.type` or `gen_ai.system`.
- In a trace that qualifies, "spans without any `gen_ai.*` attribute are also dropped individually". Their other,
  non-gen_ai attributes are dropped too.
- `parent_span_id` maps to `parent_id`. The page says nothing about moving a dropped span's children up to the
  nearest span that was kept. The two roots on #265's live check are consistent with the child of a dropped span
  becoming a root, which is the reading this entry takes.
- Span kind comes from `gen_ai.operation.name`: chat, generate_content, text_completion and completion are llm;
  execute_tool is tool; invoke_agent and create_agent are agent; anything else, or no operation at all, is workflow.
- An llm span takes its input and output from `gen_ai.input.messages` and `gen_ai.output.messages`, with
  `gen_ai.system_instructions` put in front of the input. Workflow and agent spans take theirs from the same two
  attributes. A tool span takes `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` and `gen_ai.tool.call.result`.
- `ml_app` is the service of the root span. When the APM trace's top-most span is not a gen_ai span, Datadog makes a
  separate Agent Observability trace for each top-level gen_ai span.

**What that does to one /chat.** The path from guard-proxy's `chat` to kagent's `invocation` is
`chat` → `agent.forward` → urllib `POST` → gateway `POST /` → gateway `Http` → kagent `POST /` → `invocation`.
- **Root 1, guard-proxy's `POST /chat`.** It is llm because proxy.py sets `gen_ai.operation.name` chat on it.
  proxy.py also writes the student's prompt and the final reply to it as `gen_ai.input.messages` and
  `gen_ai.output.messages`. The guard runs with `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=EVENT_ONLY`, and
  proxy.py counts that as capture on (proxy.py, pin fb6e2bf).
- **The dropped hops.** `agent.forward`, the urllib `POST` and the gateway's two spans carry no `gen_ai.*` attribute,
  so Datadog drops all four.
- **Root 2, kagent's `POST /`.** This is kagent's HTTP server span for the message/send. It has `gen_ai.*`
  attributes because kagent's Go executor calls `telemetry.SetKAgentSpanAttributes` before it opens `invocation`, and
  that call writes `gen_ai.task.id` and `gen_ai.conversation.id` onto whatever span is current. That span is the
  otelhttp server span (kagent v0.10.1, `go/adk/pkg/a2a/executor.go` Execute and
  `go/adk/pkg/telemetry/tracing.go`). It has no operation name, so it is a workflow, and it has no content
  attributes. Its parent, the gateway's `Http` span, was dropped, so it becomes a root. That matches #713's reading,
  "workflow POST, agent invocation, agent workshop_agent". The source reading makes this span the workflow root, but
  nobody has read which root row shows "No content". The issue's text says "the root row", and the live look below
  settles it.

Grouping by kind or by ml_app does not cause the split. Changing the guard span's kind does not move `invocation`
under it, and the guard root already carries the prompt and the reply. So neither option the issue named makes one
root.

**What would join them, and why the collector cannot do it cleanly.**
- **Bridge the hops.** This means putting a `gen_ai.*` attribute on the four hop spans so that Datadog keeps them.
  Since ef66c77 (guard-proxy fb6e2bf, #742), the forward is a non-blocking message/send polled by tasks/get, at 0.25 s
  doubling to 1 s. Every poll repeats the urllib `POST`, gateway `POST /` and gateway `Http` spans with the same
  attributes as the message/send's. The collector sees one span at a time, so it cannot stamp the message/send hops
  without stamping every poll's. A Challenge 1 turn held for 20 s by the blocked curl would gain about twenty polls of
  three spans each, an estimate from the 0.25 s to 1 s poll schedule and not measured. agentgateway records `a2a.method` only on the request span and only behind an `a2a` route policy (v1.7.0,
  `proxy/httpproxy.rs` and `telemetry/log.rs`), and never on the outbound `Http` span, whose id is the one forwarded
  to kagent.
- **Re-parent.** The collector can give guard-proxy's `chat` a span id derived from the trace id and point kagent's
  message/send server span at it. That makes one root, but every backend would then show the agent's request going
  around the gateway. That includes Datadog APM, and its service map would draw an edge from burritobot to
  burritobot-agent that PRD #27's three edges leave out. A message/send that did not come through guard-proxy would
  name a parent that does not exist.

Each of these trades away something the workshop shows elsewhere, so the choice goes to the coordinator as a
question in the run's report. The fixes are not built.

**Pinned now, in `verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py` (run 15236).** The fixture gives guard-proxy's `POST /chat` root
`gen_ai.operation.name` chat, the prompt and the reply, and gives kagent's `POST /` server span
`gen_ai.task.id` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`. The checks pin the shape Datadog receives, on all three profiles:
the guard root is kind llm with its content; `agent.forward`, the urllib `POST`, the gateway's `POST /` and `Http`
carry no `gen_ai.*` attribute, so Datadog drops them; kagent's `POST /` keeps its conversation id and has no
operation name, so it is a workflow row. Adding a `gen_ai.operation.name` to a hop span fails three checks, one per
profile, which I confirmed with a temporary copy of the test that was then removed. Whichever shape is chosen, these
checks change with it.

**Not yet run on a cluster:** the reading this diagnosis rests on. On a cluster with Datadog on, send one /chat. Read
that interaction's spans from the LLM Observability spans API, or open it in Agent Observability. Confirm that the
second root is kagent's `POST /` carrying `gen_ai.task.id` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`, and that its `parent_id`
names the gateway's `Http` span, which is absent from Agent Observability. Then record which root row shows "No
content" for input and output, and whether that row is the guard's `POST /chat` (which the source says carries the
prompt and reply) or kagent's workflow `POST /`. Offline: `python3 verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py`.

## 2026-11-01 · #746 · question 1034: keep the true parentage, so Agent Observability keeps two roots per interaction

**Question.** Should the collector re-parent kagent's request span onto guard-proxy's `chat` span, so that Agent
Observability shows one root per BurritoBot interaction, at the cost of Datadog APM showing the agent's request
skipping the agentgateway hop?

**Answer: keep the true parentage.** No re-parenting. APM, Tempo and the service map keep the path guard-proxy,
agentgateway, kagent, as the tracing is written today.

**Decided by** hecaton's research under Michael's standing rules, not by Michael. The ruling rests on
`docs/observability-priorities.md` (commit 05427b9, 2026-06-23, unrevised since): its Must-have 1 is the AI agent trace
chain in Datadog APM, `guard-proxy → agentgateway → kagent → Bedrock` as a connected waterfall, and its Must-have 3 is the
Service Map showing the same chain. One root per interaction in Agent Observability is not on that list. Re-parenting
would break Must-haves 1 and 3, since the waterfall would skip agentgateway. The answer was posted on
issue #746 as question 1034, with the same sources and the same decider.

**What it changes.**
- No collector processor re-parents kagent's span. `gitops/otel-collector/values.yaml` is unchanged by this entry.
- The Datadog-visible shape stays as pinned in `verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py` (commit 0b11a9c): guard-proxy's
  `POST /chat` is an llm row with the prompt and reply; the four hops carry no `gen_ai.*` attribute and are dropped;
  kagent's `POST /` keeps its conversation id and is a workflow row with no operation name.
- The copied `gen_ai.task.id` and `gen_ai.conversation.id` stay on kagent's server span. The 0b11a9c entry above
  planned to strip them as a tidy step. It is not built. With the ids stripped, Datadog would drop that span, and
  `invocation` would become the root: an agent row with no `gen_ai.input.messages` or `gen_ai.output.messages`, so the
  root row would still read "No content" and the trace would still show two roots. The strip would also remove the
  conversation id from the APM span. It does not meet the criterion, so it is a followup for the coordinator if wanted.
- Issue #746's acceptance criterion, "LLM Observability shows a BurritoBot interaction as two root-level rows, and the
  root row reads 'No content'", stays unmet under this answer. The criterion as worded describes the symptom, so
  whether the issue closes on this finding or its criterion is reworded is the coordinator's call. The #746 entry above
  is the record of the research.

**Live look still owed.** The "Not yet run on a cluster" reading in the #746 entry above stands unchanged: on a cluster
with Datadog on, send one /chat, confirm that the second root is kagent's `POST /` with `gen_ai.task.id` and
`gen_ai.conversation.id` and a `parent_id` naming the gateway's `Http` span, and record which root row shows "No content".

## 2026-11-01 · #749 · The persona answers the linked list when it notices the ask is unrelated; the probe stays 3 of 3

The community probe's off-topic beat asks "how do I reverse a linked list" three times in fresh conversations and
passes only on 3 of 3. On attackme it came back 2 of 3 on 2026-10-30, 2026-10-31 and 2026-11-01, the miss Nova
declining the ask as unrelated to the menu. The on-topic guard is off there, so the miss comes from the persona and
the model. The issue offered two ways out and left the choice to Michael. #535's entry above already settled it: the
gate moves to the Night Before run, and a missed off-topic beat makes that run red. Accepting 2 of 3 would
reverse that, so this run took the other way out, the persona. Michael can still choose to loosen the probe.

**What changed in the persona** (`gitops/workshop-agent/agent.yaml`, the one systemMessage every cluster runs):

- The first lines say the job includes helping with whatever else a guest asks, and they exempt help with something
  outside the cantina from "keep replies short".
- The paragraph #530 added now names the reasoning a miss writes in its scratchpad ("unrelated to the menu", the
  shape `COMMUNITY_OFF_TOPIC` records) and makes it the cue to answer in full.
- It says to answer in the same reply from what the model already knows, with no tool and no plan described in place
  of the answer. Those were the earlier misses' shapes: a narrated plan on 2026-10-29, and on 2026-10-30 a reply that
  was only the scratchpad, then a Bedrock ToolUse error.
- It gives the linked-list answer it wants (the prev, current and next walk, with a few lines of code), and then the
  nudge back to the order.

Every change widens what the bot answers (memory 'agent-graduated-resistance'), and the
persona still never says "off-topic" or "only talk burritos", which `verify/test_topic_guard.py` holds. On the admin
cluster the on-topic guard refuses in guard-proxy before the model is called, so the topic beat is unaffected.

**Tests.** `verify/test_kubecon_probe.py` holds the new wording, checks that the persona's own linked-list example
passes `judge_off_topic_answered`, and checks again that the persona never restricts topics. `bash verify/run-tests.sh`
and `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` were run; the results are in the run report.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Whether Nova now lands the beat every time is a live question. Once watch-it-burn-community
has synced this commit, a session with AWS access runs `python3 verify/kubecon_probe.py community attackme.burritobot.co
--context <community-context> --kubeconfig /tmp/community.kubeconfig --profile accen-dev`. The off-topic beat should
read "answered 3 of 3". If it misses again on several nights, loosening the probe is the remaining option, and that
is Michael's call.

## 2026-11-01 · #753 · sweep_orphan_sgs selects only the torn-down cluster's tagged groups

`sweep_orphan_sgs` in `infra/terraform/fleet/fleet.sh` took every `k8s-*` security group in the lab VPC whenever
`read_vpc_id_for` returned a VPC id. The lab VPC is shared with the roster clusters, so on 2026-11-01 `fleet.sh down
watch-it-burn-attendee-441` stripped the rules from the community and private clusters' agent-console and traffic
groups (#752, the parent). The sweep now selects with two `describe-security-groups` calls,
`Name=tag:elbv2.k8s.aws/cluster,Values=<name>` and `Name=tag:kubernetes.io/cluster/<name>,Values=owned`, each with
`Name=vpc-id,Values=<lab vpc>` when the VPC id is known and without it when it is not. AWS ANDs different filter
names, so the two tags cannot share one call; the results are merged and de-duplicated, because a group carrying
both tags would otherwise be deleted twice and its second, failing delete recorded as an `sg-leak`. The no-VPC
branch and its squashed-name filter (`k8s-traffic-<squashed>-*,k8s-<squashed>-*`) are gone. The load balancer
controller tags the service- and ingress-named groups (`k8s-agent-console-*`, `k8s-watchitburningres-*`) with
`elbv2.k8s.aws/cluster`, so those are still covered when they carry the cluster's tag. `owned` is required on the
`kubernetes.io/cluster/<name>` tag so a `shared` group is never taken.

**Untagged leftovers are no longer swept per cluster.** The Portland leftovers carried no tags (105 of 105), and the
VPC-wide `k8s-*` filter was what caught them. A tagless group is now left in place by `down`, and audit-zero's
`zero:<acct>:sg` line, which still counts every `k8s-*` group in the account, reports it as a failure, so it is not
silent. Removing such a group is a by-hand step until a later change decides how.

**Found while testing.** The merge pipeline first used `grep -v` to drop `None` and blank lines. Under fleet.sh's
`set -euo pipefail` that fails the assignment when no group matches, which would have ended the teardown on every
clean cluster. It uses `awk` instead, and `verify/test_sg_sweep.sh` now runs an empty sweep under errexit.

**Not changed here.** The revoke-then-delete ordering and the network-interface guard are as they were; a follow-up
child of #752 changes the ordering. `recheck_sg_leaks` stays: a cluster's own group can still be held by a sibling's
cross-reference during a parallel teardown. Its comment and the one in `sweep_orphan_sgs` no longer call the sweep
VPC-wide.

**Tests.** `verify/test_sg_sweep.sh` now pins the tag-scoped selection instead of the `k8s-*` name filter and the
absence of a `tag:kubernetes.io/cluster` filter. Its aws shim answers the tag filters only, and any other filter
returns a roster cluster's group and a tagless group; the checks assert that the tagged `k8s-agent-console-*` and
`k8s-watchitburningres-*` groups are deleted and the other two are never touched, with and without a VPC id. Against
the old fleet.sh, 17 of its checks fail.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The selection has only met the shim. The owed check is a `fleet.sh down` of one
attendee cluster in a lab VPC that also holds a roster cluster's load balancer, in a session with AWS access: the
torn-down cluster's `k8s-*` groups should go, the roster cluster's groups should keep their rules, and
`bash verify/run-e2e.sh` against the roster cluster should still pass afterwards.
