## 2026-11-01 · 2.2 · #754/#755 Delete orphan security groups first, revoke nothing on a survivor

`sweep_orphan_sgs` in `infra/terraform/fleet/fleet.sh` revoked a group's ingress and egress rules before it
tried to delete it. A group it then could not delete had already lost its rules, and on 2026-11-01 those were
the roster clusters' live agent-console and traffic groups in the shared lab VPC (#752).

Fix (#754): delete first, revoke nothing. Owning rules does not block a group's own deletion, so a genuine
orphan deletes directly; cross-references among this cluster's own orphans resolve across the three retry
passes as each sibling goes away. A group that still refuses to delete is in use or still referenced, so it
keeps its rules and is named as a survivor (its group ids in the log) and recorded as `sg-leak:<name>` for
`recheck_sg_leaks` and a human. The rule-stripping path, and the `describe` of a group's IpPermissions it
needed, are gone.

Rejected: keeping a revoke step as a last resort for groups that survive all three passes. A group that
cannot be deleted is in use or referenced, and revoking its rules is exactly the #752 harm; a true reference
cycle among orphans is rare and safe to leave for the re-check. Hecaton's split (2026-11-01) set this.

#755 is the regression: `verify/test_sg_sweep.sh` now checks that tearing down an attendee cluster whose lab
VPC also holds community/private never describes, revokes or deletes their groups, and that a survivor keeps
its rules (the #754 path). 44 offline checks.

Not yet run on a cluster: a real `fleet.sh down` of an attendee cluster in a lab VPC that also holds a roster
cluster's load balancer, in a session with AWS access. Expected: the attendee's own `k8s-*` groups go, the
roster cluster's groups keep their rules, a group still on a live LB's interface is left alone, and
`bash verify/run-e2e.sh` against the roster cluster still passes afterwards. Must not be tested against
anything live except a deliberate attendee teardown.

## 2026-11-01 · 2.2 · #762 The chat page assigns the witch name itself (in-repo parts; agent side owed)

The chat page gives every visitor a witch name on their first visit, as plain text with no link, and a very
small "Get a new witch name" button re-rolls it. Chosen mechanism: the page generates the name client-side
from the vocabulary mirrored into `gitops/ai-layer/web/burritbot.html` (WITCH_FIRST x WITCH_CREATURES) and
sets the `wib_witch` cookie on `.burritobot.co` itself (slug form, Max-Age 172800). The desk's `name_from_slug`
accepts it because it is the desk's own vocabulary, so the desk, `/me` and the wall find the person's Joker
under one name. `verify/test_witch_name_vocab.py` keeps the JS vocabulary exactly equal to ticket_site.py's
FIRST and CREATURES, so they cannot drift.

Rejected: a desk endpoint (e.g. GET /name or /vocab) the chat page calls. It would re-introduce a
`support-<cluster>.burritobot.co` reference on the chat page, which #763 removed on purpose, and add a
cross-origin credentialed call and a live-desk dependency for something the page can do alone. The cost is
that client-side generation cannot keep the desk's no-duplicates behaviour; with 768 names and ~50 phones a
collision is possible, the same best-effort the desk's per-process `_taken` set gives on one cluster. Names
are visible on the wall, so a visitor who collides or dislikes a name uses the re-roll button. Recorded per
the issue's latitude ("You choose how").

The name reaches the bot through the `/chat` POST body (`{prompt, session, witch}`); nothing is embedded in
the visible prompt, so the input guard still scans only what the visitor typed. guard-proxy does not yet read
`witch`: that is guard-proxy-agenticburn#34 (forward it into the agent context). Sending the field now is
harmless because the proxy ignores unknown body keys.

Not yet done, so #762 stays open: guard-proxy-agenticburn#34 (consume `witch`), then repin guard-proxy here,
then the live check (an HC-666 run on a cluster creating `joker-<the visitor's slug>`, the name shown on the
wall). Couples with #764, which removes the copied HC-666 prompt that used to carry the name.

## 2026-11-01 · #746 · Agent Observability gets its own copy of the traces, one root per turn, and APM keeps the true path

**Why this reopened.** Whitney's comment on #746 (2026-11-01, which also answers #756) keeps the issue open until five
things are true in her sandbox org's LLM Observability on live traces: one chat is one root row; that row shows the
prompt as input and the final reply as output; the tool calls sit under it; its duration covers the whole chat, not
14 ms; tokens and cost appear, where the guard row read `cost_estimate_status:skipped_tokens_missing`. Question 1034
above kept the true parentage because a re-parent in the one export path would have moved APM's waterfall and service
map too. That answer stands. This change re-parents only in a second copy that APM never receives.

**What Datadog documents (read 2026-11-01).**
- docs.datadoghq.com/opentelemetry/compatibility: OpenTelemetry traces with gen_ai attributes "are automatically
  converted into Agent Observability traces". That conversion is what turned APM's spans into the two roots.
- docs.datadoghq.com/llm_observability/instrument/otel_instrumentation: "An explicit `false` on any span prevents
  conversion of the entire trace" (`dd_llmobs_enabled`). The same page sends spans to Agent Observability through the
  OTLP traces endpoint with the header `dd-otlp-source=llmobs`, maps `parent_span_id` to `parent_id` unchanged, drops
  spans with no `gen_ai.*` attribute, and reads tokens from `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` and `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`.
- The endpoint per site is `otlp_trace_endpoint` in DataDog/documentation `shared/regions.yaml`:
  `https://otlp.datadoghq.com/v1/traces` for datadoghq.com, the same shape for the other sites.
- docs.datadoghq.com/llm_observability/investigate/cost: each llm span is priced on its own, and a trace with an llm
  span lacking a cost reads PARTIAL COST. The catalog it prices from (pydantic/genai-prices `prices/providers/aws.yml`)
  matches provider names containing `bedrock` and models containing `amazon.nova-pro`.
- adk-go v2.1.0 (kagent v0.10.1's pin) writes `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` and `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` on each
  `generate_content` span (`internal/telemetry/telemetry.go`, TraceGenerateContentResult).

**What changed** (`gitops/otel-collector/values.yaml`, `values-dual.yaml`, `values-burn.yaml`).
- `transform/llmobs_apm_off`, last in the traces processors (before burn's PII scrub), sets `dd_llmobs_enabled` false on
  every span, so the datadog exporter's copy makes no Agent Observability rows. Tempo receives the attribute too, which
  changes nothing there.
- `forward/llmobs`, a forward connector on the traces exporters, hands the processed spans to a new pipeline,
  `traces/llmobs`. It follows the lab pipelines' pattern: relay.yaml ends it at debug, and the Datadog overlay adds
  `otlp_http/llmobs` (the cluster's org) and, in datadog-dual.yaml, `otlp_http/llmobs_admin` (the instructor org,
  with datadog/admin's short retry). The copy leaves after every traces processor, so burn's PII scrub covers it.
- `transform/llmobs_one_root`, on the copy only. The guard span that holds the turn takes the trace id's low 64 bits
  as its span id, and kagent's `invocation` (when it has a parent) names that id as its parent. Both values come from
  the trace id alone, which matters because the collector is a DaemonSet and guard-proxy's and kagent's spans pass
  through different pods. The span that holds the turn is `POST /chat` on the storefront path (proxy.py at pin
  fb6e2bf, `_handle_chat`) or `sanitize` on the raw A2A pass-through (`_handle_post`), which the facilitator fallbacks
  and beat scripts send. That span becomes `invoke_agent`, Datadog's agent kind: guard-proxy makes no model call of its
  own, and as an llm row with no tokens it made the trace PARTIAL COST.
- `filter/llmobs_one_root`, on the copy only, removes guard-proxy's inner `chat` wrapper (the same prompt and reply as
  the root, an llm row with no tokens), kagent's server span (the 14 ms message/send row), and every span with no
  `gen_ai.*` attribute, which Datadog would drop anyway.

**How the five read offline.** `verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py` now runs both copies through each profile's real
pipelines (otelcol-contrib 0.160.0), for a storefront turn and a pass-through turn. APM's copy keeps every id and
parent as sent and carries the marker on every span. In the copy, each turn has one root, guard-proxy's span under its
derived id, kind agent, with the prompt and the reply. `invocation` hangs from it, so both tool calls sit under it. Its
duration is the guard span's own and contains every row. Every llm row carries its token counts. No span lacks a
`gen_ai.*` attribute, and none carries the marker. Removing the re-parent, the marker, the filter or the kind change
each fails its checks, which I confirmed on temporary edits of values.yaml that were then restored.
`verify/test_collector_no_datadog.py` holds the wiring offline: one intake per org APM ships to, on every profile,
each with its own org's key, `dd-otlp-source: llmobs` and `https://otlp.${env:DD_SITE}/v1/traces`.

**What differs from the earlier draft and its pins.** Runs 15236 and 15280 pinned the two-root shape: the guard root
as kind llm, kagent's `POST /` kept as a workflow row. Those checks are replaced by the five above. The fixture's
`sanitize` under `POST /chat` was not what proxy.py writes on that path; the storefront turn now has the `chat`
wrapper, and `sanitize` appears in the pass-through turn, where it is written. The re-parent that question 1034 turned
down moved APM's parentage. This one is on a copy only Agent Observability receives, so APM, Tempo and the service map
keep guard-proxy → agentgateway → kagent.

**Open edges.** An A2A message that did not come through guard-proxy names a parent that is not in the copy, and it
shows as its own root, as every kagent turn did before. The new pipeline adds no dependency.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Owed in a session that can read Whitney's sandbox org (#759 is the run-side access):
once a KubeCon cluster's root has synced this commit and the collector pods have rolled (the config checksum rolls
them), check the collector log for `otlp_http/llmobs` export errors with
`kubectl --context <ctx> -n monitoring logs ds/otel-collector-opentelemetry-collector-agent -c opentelemetry-collector | grep -i llmobs`.
A 403 there means the org's key is not accepted at the llmobs intake. Send one chat (the probe's HC-666 turn), then in
LLM Observability under `ml_app:burritobot` confirm Whitney's five: one root row; the prompt and the reply on it;
`read_support_ticket` and `deploy_app` under it; a duration matching guard-proxy's `POST /chat`; tokens and an
estimated cost, with no `skipped_tokens_missing`. In APM, open the same trace and confirm it still runs guard-proxy →
agentgateway → kagent with one `POST /chat` span. The overlap note on Datadog's page ("some data sent to Agent
Observability may also be written to the corresponding APM traces") is the one way the copy could reach APM, and that
look settles it. Offline: `python3 verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py` (in `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh`).

## 2026-11-01 · #756 · #746 stays open on Whitney's five live checks, and the gen_ai id strip is dropped

**Question.** Does #746 close on the finding that question 1034's entry records (Agent Observability keeps two roots
per BurritoBot interaction because the true parentage is kept), or is its criterion reworded?

**Answer: #746 stays open.** Whitney Lee, the talk's co-presenter, answered it in her comment on #746 on 2026-11-01,
which names #756: "#746 does not close on the finding recorded under question 1034." Her comment replaces the
issue's title-as-criterion with five checks, each read on live traces in her sandbox org's LLM Observability:
- One chat is one root row.
- That row shows the user's prompt as input and the bot's final reply as output, where today it reads "No content".
- The tool calls, `read_support_ticket` and `deploy_app` for example, sit under that root.
- The root row's duration covers the whole chat. Today kagent's row lasts 14 ms.
- Tokens and cost appear. Today the guard-proxy row carries `cost_estimate_status:skipped_tokens_missing`.

Her evidence is the probe's HC-666 chat (LLM Observability trace `c943363f5467508c8bfc14c6a40c4b59`) and the
linked-list probe chat, both showing the two roots, in `ml_app:burritobot` on cluster `burritobot-public`. The
presenters open these traces in front of the room for every challenge at KubeCon NA 2026.

**Decided by** Whitney, a collaborator on this repo, in writing on #746. This run only records the ruling, so no
question goes to the coordinator.

**What it changes.**
- #746's done-bar is her five checks. A partial outcome does not close it, and a run cannot meet the bar without
  read access to her sandbox org, which #759 is giving dispatched runs. Her comment asks that #746 not be re-labelled
  `agent-task` before #759 is done.
- Question 1034's answer still stands for APM, Tempo and the service map. Run 15333 on #746 (branch
  `agent/746-15333`, commits 241f8e6 and 7452788, not yet in staging when this entry was written) builds the one-root
  view in a second copy of the traces that only Agent Observability receives, and marks APM's copy
  `dd_llmobs_enabled` false. Its own decisions.md entry carries the design and the live look it owes.

## 2026-11-01 · 2.2 · #779 Join background threads before test_room_jokers.py exits (SIGABRT at shutdown)

Run 15361 of #745 failed the tests gate with test_room_jokers.py exit 134 after every check had passed. Exit
134 is SIGABRT. The file's last section points TICKET_SITE_URL at http://127.0.0.1:9 and deploys a room Joker,
so deploy_app starts two daemon threads in gitops/ai-layer/workshop-mcp-server.py: the _report sender, which
fails to connect and prints its failure, and a short scale-down threading.Timer. The test called
desk.shutdown() and exited without waiting for either. When a daemon thread held stdout's buffer lock as the
interpreter finalized, Python 3.13 aborted with "could not acquire lock for <_io.BufferedWriter ...> at
interpreter shutdown".

Fix, in verify/test_room_jokers.py only: after desk.shutdown(), join every thread other than the main thread
with a bounded timeout, then fail naming any still alive. workshop-mcp-server.py is unchanged; its five-minute
scale-down Timers are long-lived daemon threads by design, and the one test that covers what the desk is told
keeps the real _report (the #441 entry stubbed it in test_c6_villain_endpoint.py and test_deploy_app_limits.py).

Forced-race counts, from a scratch wrapper that was never committed. It replaces urllib.request.urlopen so a
port-9 send holds stdout's buffer lock with continuous unflushed writes for three seconds and then raises
URLError, and it runs the file through runpy as __main__. On origin/staging the pre-fix file exited 134 in 8 of
8 runs. The changed file exited 0 in 8 of 8. Without the forcing, 100 plain runs of the changed file exited 0.
Nothing is owed on a cluster.

## 2026-11-02 · #770 · The presenters' ttyd refuses a websocket with no, an empty or a wrong credential; the 101 tls-check saw opens nothing

**The question.** On 2026-11-01 lab-platform's tls-check on burritobot-private.agenticburn.com saw GET /terminal/ answer
401 but a websocket upgrade on /terminal/ with no credential answer 101. lab-platform#347 could not send the first
message on the presenters' cluster, because if the check were broken it would start a shell there.

**What ttyd 1.7.7 does with `-c user:password`.** This was measured on the binary the pod runs, with the entrypoint's
own flags, on loopback. The image gitops/ai-layer/resources.yaml pins (`web-terminal@sha256:68004fb5…`, amd64
manifest `9060bb0c…`) was read anonymously from ghcr.io. Its `/usr/local/bin/ttyd` has SHA-256 `8a217c96…7be4f55`,
the same as the 1.7.7 release's `ttyd.x86_64` in the release's SHA256SUMS. The pod's entrypoint comes from the
`web-terminal-entrypoint` ConfigMap, which is gitops/ai-layer/web-terminal/entrypoint.sh, so the flags are this repo's.

- **The 101 is not the shell.** An upgrade that asks for no subprotocol, as tls-check's curl probe sends it, or for
  `http-only`, gets 101 from anyone. libwebsockets binds that socket to ttyd's first protocol, the HTTP handler, which
  never spawns a command. No AuthToken starts a shell there, not even the right one with the right Basic credential.
- **The shell's protocol wants the credential at the upgrade.** On `tty`, the only protocol bound to the shell, a
  missing or wrong Basic credential means the connection is dropped and no 101 is sent, whatever the first message
  would have said.
- **With the Basic credential right, the AuthToken is checked as well.** An empty, wrong or missing AuthToken, or
  the password sent unencoded, is closed with 1008 and starts nothing. Keystrokes sent before the AuthToken drop the
  connection.
- **The positive control** is the right Basic credential and the right AuthToken. That starts exactly one shell,
  seen both in the spawned script's record and in ttyd's "started process" log line.

So the issue's question is answered for the binary and the flags. A socket whose first message carries an empty or
wrong AuthToken is closed without a shell, and an unauthenticated socket never gets that far. The terminal is not open
to anyone who knows the hostname.

**What changed.**
- `verify/test_ttyd_ws_auth.py`, tools tier, holds all of the above. It reads the credentialed `exec ttyd` line from
  the mounted entrypoint and fails if that line loses `-c`, `-b /terminal` or `-W`, or gains `--auth-header`. With
  `-c` removed it fails 37 checks. `verify/ttyd_ws.py` is the stdlib websocket client it uses. It sends one first
  message and never types into a shell.
- `verify/e2e-tools.lock` pins ttyd 1.7.7 by that SHA-256. run-e2e-tools.sh and run-e2e.sh point `$TTYD` at it.
  `test_e2e_tools_tier.py` holds the pin to the version images/web-terminal/Dockerfile downloads.
- `infra/terraform/fleet/check-tls.sh` gains a second upgrade probe with `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: tty` and no
  credential, and fails on a 101. Its existing probe's 101 shows the upgrade gets through, but it cannot tell an open
  terminal from a closed one. `verify/test_check_tls_shell_probe.sh` holds the new probe with curl stubbed. Run
  against the old script, it fails 4 of 7 checks.
- `verify/test_terminal_ws_auth_live.py`, the live half, runs through the public host, the router, nginx and the pod,
  and counts shell starts in ttyd's log.

**Not yet run on a cluster:** `CONTEXT=<a cluster you own> python3 verify/test_terminal_ws_auth_live.py` (it is in
`bash verify/run-e2e.sh`), and `./fleet.sh check-tls burritobot-private.agenticburn.com` with the new probe. This run
has no cluster. The live test starts one shell, its positive control, and closes it at once. Both have since run
green on burritobot-private, the live test on 2026-11-05 by hecaton run 17412; the #785 entry below holds both
outputs.

**Question 899:** Should the PR-gated apply path for the attendee fleet in #201 (a pull request runs a Terraform
plan, a human approves in a protected `fleet-prod` environment, and GitHub Actions applies with OIDC credentials,
with `fleet.sh` from a laptop kept as break-glass) be built now, held until a live event that needs the
shared-account fleet is confirmed, or closed?

**Answer:** Hold until a live fleet event is confirmed.

**Decided by:** hecaton's research under Michael's standing rules, not by Michael. The basis is Michael's own
pattern of 2026-09-07 on #112, #113, #116 and #117, recorded in this file's question 575 entry: post-Portland work
that is still wanted stays open on its labelled issue for a later event instead of being closed.

**What it changes:** nothing is built. No workflow, IAM role, Terraform backend block or state migration is added,
and `infra/terraform/fleet/fleet.sh` from a laptop, with one local state file per cluster across the five attendee
accounts in `WIB_ATTENDEE_ACCOUNTS`, stays the only apply path. #201 stays open, labelled post-portland, and waits
for the KubeCon Europe 2027 decisions on 2026-12-07 (talks-knowledge `talks/register.md`), which show whether a
Barcelona run needs the shared-account fleet. If one does, the next run asks the shape question this one left
open: the full gated pipeline or only the S3 state move with `use_lockfile = true`, and whether apply runs on merge
to `main`, as the issue says, or to `staging`, where CLAUDE.md routes every pull request. That run also starts from
these facts: there is no S3 backend or DynamoDB lock table to cut over, only local state, so the work is a full
state migration; `infra/README.md` does not exist, and the Terraform docs are in `infra/terraform/README.md`; and
the repo was created 2026-06-15, before the 2026-07-15 cut-off for the immutable OIDC `sub` claim, so the trust
policy matches the older repo-and-environment subject. If no live fleet event is confirmed, the next run asks
whether to close #201.

## 2026-11-02 · #207 · The IAM policy pipeline's structural check runs on every PR; the org half is not pursued

**What changed.** `.github/workflows/iam-policy.yml` runs on every PR, and every push to staging or main, that
touches `infra/terraform/**`, `infra/org/**`, `verify/iam_plan_render.py`, a `verify/test_iam_policy_*.py`, the
E2E tools lock or its fetch script, or the workflow itself. It fetches the pinned tools with
`verify/fetch-e2e-tools.sh` (conftest v0.71.1, terraform v1.15.6, each checked against its SHA-256) and runs
`test_iam_policy_pipeline.py`, `test_iam_policy_coverage.py` and `test_iam_policy_structural.py`. The structural
test plans the PR's own cluster and boundary roots with `verify/iam_plan_render.py`, so a PR that adds an Allow
with no Condition fails the job naming `Statement[N]`. Before this, check 3 ran only when someone ran the E2E tools
tier by hand, so a PR could merge without it.

**Choices made:**
- **Same runner and credentials as plan-policy.yml (question 592):** GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest, token
  `contents: read`, no secret, no OIDC role, actions pinned to the same commit SHAs. A fork PR is safe to check.
- **The tools come from `verify/e2e-tools.lock`, not a second pin list.** The job fetches the whole lock, including
  tools it does not use, rather than adding a name filter to `fetch-e2e-tools.sh`, which `test_e2e_tools_tier.py`
  exercises as it is. The extra downloads cost a hosted runner a few seconds.
- **Checks 1, 2 and 4 stay out of CI.** They call Access Analyzer and IAM simulate, which need an AWS credential,
  and question 592 keeps CI without one. They run by hand through `verify/test_iam_policy_aws.py`.
- `verify/test_iam_policy_ci.py` (offline) holds the workflow. Its paths must cover every root in `pipeline.ROOTS`,
  the pipeline's files and every IAM policy test. It must run the three tests and not the AWS one, hold no
  credential and pin its actions. The lock must carry the conftest version the structural test requires.

**The org half is not pursued.** On #202 on 2026-10-31, the owner wrote that we have no org-level access to those
accounts and will not pursue it. So the SCPs, RCPs, the org S3 Block Public Access policy, the console-deny SCP
(#207's acceptance 3), its break-glass and the instructor beat are not built. `infra/org/README.md` now says so,
and no longer says they wait on a provider grant.

**Seen working here:** with the lock's tools on PATH, all three tests pass. With the agent's Bedrock Condition
removed from `infra/terraform/aws/cluster/main.tf`, `test_iam_policy_structural.py` exits 1 on
`aws_iam_policy.bedrock_invoke: Statement[0] is an Allow with no Condition [allow-without-condition]`.

**Not yet run:** the workflow on GitHub, which runs at the first push to staging after promotion. Also not run is
`verify/test_iam_policy_aws.py`, #207's acceptance 2 (a widened identity policy fails check 2), with
`IAM_PIPELINE_PROFILE` and `IAM_PIPELINE_REGION` set. This run has no AWS profile.
## 2026-11-02 · #392 · A delivery is costed from member-account data, since the payer's tag activation is off the table

Michael's ruling on #392 (2026-11-01): nobody contacts Web Age or any lab-account support team, and nobody asks the
payer account (457247706586, the provider's Organization management account, #202) to activate anything. So
Cost Explorer's tag-filtered figure stays 0.00 and `teardown/activate-cost-tags.sh` stays unrun. The new
`teardown/delivery-cost-estimate.py` costs one delivery's window from what each member account reads itself, and
prints it as an estimate.

- **Sources, per account and region, all read-only.** EC2 instance hours by instance type, EKS cluster hours, EBS
  GiB-hours, NLB and ALB hours and NAT gateway hours from CloudTrail `lookup-events` (RunInstances/TerminateInstances,
  CreateCluster/DeleteCluster, CreateVolume/DeleteVolume, CreateLoadBalancer/DeleteLoadBalancer,
  CreateNatGateway/DeleteNatGateway). Resources made before the lookback that are still up come from describe calls.
  NAT data processed comes from the AWS/NATGateway `BytesInFromSource` and `BytesInFromDestination` sums. Bedrock
  input and output tokens per `ModelId` come from AWS/Bedrock in CloudWatch. guard-proxy's `/cost` counter is in
  memory and dies with the cluster, so it cannot cost a past window. Every rate comes from `pricing get-products`.
  Beside the estimate, each account's unfiltered `ce get-cost-and-usage` total is printed as the upper bound.
- **Attribution.** A resource counts when its own tags match `project=watch-it-burn` (and `event=<event>` with
  `--event`). It also counts when it carries a cluster-ownership tag (`elbv2.k8s.aws/cluster`, `eks:cluster-name`,
  `KubernetesCluster`, `kubernetes.io/cluster/<name>`) naming a fleet cluster that was up when the resource was
  made. That second rule reaches the LB controller's load balancers and the CSI volumes, which carry no fleet tags.
  The lifetime check matters because names are reused: a first draft matched on name alone and counted
  attendee-001's KubeCon rebuild into Portland. A resource whose own tag gives a different `event` never counts.
- **Bedrock is split in two.** Tokens on a tagged application inference profile (#513, from 2026-10-25) are counted
  in the estimate. Tokens on a system model id such as `us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0` belong to the whole account,
  which on accen-dev includes the Packt co-tenant. They are priced and printed beside the estimate, with a second
  total that adds them in. Portland predates #513, so its Bedrock appears only in that second total.
  `list-metrics` returns only metrics with data in the last two weeks, so the fleet's model ids are always queried
  from a table in the script (`BEDROCK_MODELS`). The test fails when the cluster root's `bedrock_tiers` or
  `tutor_model` names a model the table lacks.
- **Pricing selection.** Each lookup must match exactly one Price List product, or the run fails and names the
  candidates. The checks used are the usage-type regex (for example `^(USW2-)?BoxUsage:t3.2xlarge$`, which keeps
  out `TS-LoadBalancerUsage` and `RegionalNatGateway-Hours`) and, for Bedrock, the on-demand regional rate, which is
  what a `us.` geo profile pays (Global, batch, latency-optimized, cache and reserved variants are excluded).
  Anthropic models are under `AmazonBedrockFoundationModels`, not `AmazonBedrock`.
- **No partial answers.** A failed AWS call ends the run with exit 3, so a missing permission cannot print as a
  smaller total. A window that ends before CloudTrail's 90-day history begins is refused. The World's Fair week
  (2026-06-29) is already out of reach. Portland is readable until 2026-12-05.
- **Left out, and said on every report:** data transfer, LCUs, T3 Unlimited credits, gp3 above baseline, public
  IPv4, snapshots, CloudWatch, Logs, Secrets Manager, Route 53 and ECR. Partial hours are counted exactly. Node root
  disks are counted as `--root-volume-gib` (default 100, pinned by the test to `node_disk_size`) times instance
  hours, because RunInstances does not record the launch template's disk.
- **Also changed.** `teardown/cost-report.sh`, `teardown/activate-cost-tags.sh` and `cost/README.md` now say the
  payer is not asked and point at the estimator. `cost/estimates/` holds recorded runs; its README lists the owed
  Portland run.

**Tests.** `verify/test_delivery_cost_estimate.py` (offline suite) runs the script against an `aws` shim backed by
`verify/fixtures/delivery-cost/`. The pricing fixtures are recorded: products copied from the public Price List bulk
files for us-west-2 (`pricing.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/offers/v1.0/aws/<service>/current/us-west-2/index.json`,
fetched 2026-11-01), in `get-products` item shape, with the Windows/RHEL, gp2, Regional NAT, Outposts and Global
distractors left in. The shim applies the TERM_MATCH filters itself. The CloudTrail, describe, CloudWatch and Cost
Explorer fixtures are synthetic, in the documented response shapes, for a Portland-like week across two accounts.
They include Packt's resources, an ECS CreateCluster, a failed RunInstances, the reused attendee-001 name, a
lab NAT made before the lookback, a cluster-tag-only CSI volume and NLB, a tagged Haiku profile, untagged Nova Pro,
an unpriced model and a delete with no create. 46 checks: each line item against hand-computed figures, the
totals, the upper bounds, explicit profile and region on every call, read-only calls, the refusals, and the drift
guards against the cluster root. Run 15666 added four more for the untagged-node guard below, 50 in all.

**Not yet run on a cluster, and not yet run on AWS at all.** The owed check is the Portland run in
`cost/estimates/README.md`, from a session holding the five fleet profiles, saved as
`cost/estimates/devopsdays-portland-2026.txt`. It is owed before 2026-12-05. Three things only that run can show.
First, whether the member accounts allow `pricing:GetProducts`, `cloudtrail:LookupEvents` and the CloudWatch reads.
Second, whether RunInstances events carry the launch template's tags in `responseElements.instancesSet.items[].tagSet`
(if they do not, and the ownership tags are missing too, the node hours come out 0, and the report prints an
`INCOMPLETE, the total is too low` line under the total for each account whose fleet clusters ran with no node
attributed).
Third, under which `ModelId` CloudWatch reports calls made through an application profile.

**What differs from the draft.** One guard, and a duplicated test name fixed. The draft printed a cluster week whose
node instances could not be attributed as a quietly lower total, which is the 0.00 problem in a smaller form. Now,
when an account's fleet clusters have hours in the window and no node instance is attributed to them, the report
prints `INCOMPLETE, the total is too low` under the estimated total, naming the account and its cluster hours; the
test strips the tags from one account's node launches and checks the line appears for that account only. Run 15331 wrote this change (its commit b3d497b on
`agent/392-15331`) and ended `stale-authorization`, so it never reached staging. Run 15666 checked it with
`verify/draft-drift.sh origin/agent/392-15331 origin/staging`: the only drift is `decisions.md`, which is
append-only, and none of the paths the draft touches (`teardown/`, `cost/`, `verify/test_activate_cost_tags.sh`,
the new test and fixtures) was edited on staging since. The rest of the files are therefore the draft's, and this
entry is appended again at the current end of the file with today's date.

## 2026-11-02 · #205 · Drift on both planes: a documented self-heal window, a daily refresh-only plan that covers the standby regions, and a Config and CloudTrail record that joins the IAM pipeline

**What #205 asked.** Document and detect out-of-band change on both planes. Deleting a managed NetworkPolicy
returns within the documented window; a hand-made bucket via attendee keys shows in AWS Config and the next
drift plan; `docs/floor.md` gets an "unmanaged" register.

**The design.** Kubernetes plane: `docs/floor.md` documents two clocks. A deleted or hand-edited managed object comes
back within 30 s, provided its app has not self-healed in the previous 5 minutes. Repeated heals at one revision back
off 2/6/18/54/162 s, then 300 s. A push lands within 180 s on a `staging` cluster (no webhook is configured) and never
on a lab-platform cluster, which is pinned to one commit. This was read from the Argo CD v3.5.2 source
(`deploy-full-idp.sh`, chart 10.8.4) and the v3.5.6 source (lab-platform, chart 10.11.3, still its pin on
2026-11-02), and both behave the same. `verify/test_drift_floor.py` (offline) holds the doc to the chart.
`verify/test_drift_selfheal_live.py` (E2E) deletes `agent/platform-console-egress` and requires it back within
30 s. AWS plane: `infra/terraform/drift/drift-report.py` runs refresh-only plans and reads `resource_drift`, then
sweeps for unmanaged S3 buckets and EKS clusters, naming each creator from CloudTrail and saying whether Config
recorded it. `scheduled-drift.sh` is the daily cron wrapper, and driftctl is not added. `infra/terraform/aws/audit`
is the per-account Config recorder and multi-region trail, and it is the IAM policy pipeline's third root (suite
`audit`).

**What differs from the draft.** The previous draft was d7bb3ff on `origin/agent/205-12982` (2026-10-30), cut from the
staging of that day, and it never reached staging. `bash verify/draft-drift.sh origin/agent/205-12982 origin/staging`
named three drift lines (`VERSIONS.lock`, `decisions.md`, `verify/run-e2e.sh`), and staging had moved 125 commits.
Those three were only context changes, but the 125 commits also changed what the draft describes. Each claim was
checked against today's tree, and the draft's own gate, run here, found the first two of the changes below:

- **The standbys (#643) are in two more regions.** `infra/terraform/fleet/backups.tsv` builds standbys in us-east-1
  and us-east-2. Outside the home region each account keeps one lab VPC state per region,
  `aws/network/states/<profile>.<region>.tfstate` (`fleet.sh lab_vpc_state_for`). The draft would have planned a
  us-east-1 standby with us-west-2's `vpc_id`. It never planned the regional lab VPC states, and it listed clusters
  only in us-west-2, so a standby left running after its state went was never found. The report now keys lab VPCs
  by account and region and plans each regional state in its own region. Each cluster is planned against its own
  region's VPC. Clusters are listed in us-west-2, every region in `backups.tsv`, and every region a state is in.
  `verify/test_drift_report.py` adds a us-east-1 standby and an orphan in us-east-2, and the draft's report fails
  eight of the new checks.
- **The audit root stays one per account, in us-west-2.** Config is regional, so an unmanaged resource in a standby
  region is reported as "in <region>; the recorder is in us-west-2". The recorder's IAM role is global and named
  once per account, so a second regional apply would collide on it, and the standbys live for hours. The trail is
  multi-region, so CloudTrail still names the creator there. Applying it per region can be added later, if Config
  coverage there is wanted.
- **Two ignores added since the draft (#643).** The Bedrock ModelConfigs' `.spec.bedrock.region` and agentgateway's
  `BEDROCK_REGION` env now have register rows.
- **The Agent's ignores moved app (#707).** `workshop-agent` is its own Application now, without
  `RespectIgnoreDifferences`. The draft's row still named `ai-layer`, and its gate passed anyway because it only
  looked for the app's name anywhere in the row, where the Agent's own name matched. The gate now requires the
  row's App column to be exactly the owning app, and fails on the old row.
- **`deploy-full-idp.sh` now passes `--kube-context` to helm.** The gate's chart-pin pattern did not match the new
  line, so it now allows flags between `helm` and `upgrade`. The chart is still 10.8.4.
- **Unchanged, and rechecked.** The drill target `agent/platform-console-egress` is still in
  `gitops/ai-layer/resources.yaml`, and every profile still lists `ai-layer`. No Kyverno policy refuses its deletion.
  The attendee grant is still `aws_iam_user_policy.attendee_eks`, with the two EKS reads. The boundary still denies
  stopping the recorder and the trail. `mint_attendee_key` still writes `name,region,access_key,secret_key`.

**The schedule stays cron.** The question asked on #205 on 2026-10-24 (where the daily run lives) stands with its
default, and this run does not ask it again. `infra/terraform/drift/scheduled-drift.sh` runs from cron on the machine that holds the states. #201,
which would move state to a remote backend, is still open. `.github/workflows/plan-policy.yml` plans against a
moto mock, which is right for policy and useless for drift.

**Dependency.** The audit root's lock records hashicorp/aws 6.71.0, the newest 6.x when d7bb3ff was written (2026-10-30), under the
same `~> 6.0` constraint as the other roots; `terraform init` with the pinned Terraform v1.15.6 wrote it.

## 2026-11-02 · #629 · KubeArmor's KubeArmorConfig becomes a resource Argo CD tracks, so #662's log names reach a running cluster

**What was still failing.** The one run of `verify/test_datadog_sandbox_live.py` so far (2026-10-31, recorded under
#711 above) passed the span check on both clusters. It failed the log check, because logs from argocd, kubearmor and
aws-load-balancer-controller still carried their image names as service. #662 had given all three a `burritobot-`
service on 10-29, and its render test passes. The three have one thing in common: Argo CD never applies a git change
to them. There was no earlier draft of this to check against staging; the agent/629-* branches are all merged.

- **Argo CD and the AWS Load Balancer Controller** are Helm releases that `infra/deploy-full-idp.sh` installs once,
  outside Argo CD. `infra/argocd-values.yaml` and `infra/aws-load-balancer-controller-values.yaml` reach a cluster
  only when that script, or its two `helm upgrade` lines, runs again. watch-it-burn-private was built on 2026-10-28
  (PROJECT_STATE.md, "KubeCon platform up"), the day before #662. There is no code to change here. The upgrade is
  owed on a cluster, below.
- **KubeArmor is a real bug, fixed here.** `kubearmor-operator` 1.7.4 writes the `kubearmor-default` KubeArmorConfig,
  where #662's DD_SERVICE and DD_ENV live, from `templates/ka-config.yaml` as a `helm.sh/hook: post-install,post-upgrade`
  hook. Argo CD runs that as a PostSync hook. Three facts follow, each read 2026-11-02:
  - Argo CD leaves hooks out of sync status. controller/state.go at v3.5.2 says: "For resource hooks ... don't store
    sync status, and do not affect overall sync status". So a change to `kubearmorConfig` alone never set the kubearmor
    Application OutOfSync, and automated sync never ran.
  - On a sync that does run, a hook with no delete policy is deleted and created again (BeforeHookCreation, per Argo
    CD's sync-waves page).
  - The operator applies a config's images and env to the DaemonSet, relay and controller it already runs only on an
    in-place update (`UpdateFunc` -> `UpdateKubeArmorImages`, pkg/KubeArmorOperator/internal/controller/cluster.go at
    v1.7.4). A re-created config goes through `AddFunc`. That path records the new values and updates nothing that
    exists, and `UpdateDaemonsets` only creates a DaemonSet that is missing.
- **The fix.** `gitops/bootstrap/apps/kubearmor.yaml` now has two sources. The first is the operator chart with
  `autoDeploy: false`, so it renders no hook. The second is `gitops/kubearmor-config`, a new one-template local chart
  at the root's revision, which renders `kubearmor-default` as a plain resource. It takes the same `kubearmorConfig`
  values that used to sit under the chart source. Its `values.yaml` copies the operator chart's own `kubearmorConfig`
  defaults, which the hook merged under them. The resource is wave 1, after the operator's Deployment as the PostSync
  hook was, and it carries `SkipDryRunOnMissingResource=true` because its CRD comes from the operator chart in the same
  sync. It keeps the hook's name, so on a running cluster Argo CD applies it over the existing config instead of adding
  a second one, which the operator would mark Error. The template's spec line sits behind a YAML comment, so the
  unrendered file still loads for the tests that sweep gitops/.
- **Tests.**
  - `verify/test_kubearmor_config_tracked.py` (offline) holds the two-source shape, `autoDeploy: false`, and a template
    with no hook annotation. On the old app file, 6 of its checks fail.
  - `verify/test_kubearmor_config_render.py` (tools tier) renders the root, the operator chart and the local chart. It
    holds that the operator chart as set renders no KubeArmorConfig, and that the local spec equals, key for key, the
    one the hook rendered from the same values. Changing one default in the copy fails it.
  - `verify/test_datadog_log_services_render.py` now renders a local chart source through Helm, so it still sees the
    KubeArmorConfig's env. It also fails if the kubearmor app's config is a hook.
  - `verify/test_image_registry_render.py` renders every chart source an app has, so the four KubeArmor images named
    in the config are still checked.
  - `verify/test_c3_fallback.py` reads `enableStdOutAlerts` from the config source.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** All of it needs a session with the accen-dev profile, after this commit is on staging.
For each of watch-it-burn-private (profile admin) and watch-it-burn-community (profile burn):

    C=watch-it-burn-private; K=/tmp/$C.kubeconfig; R=us-west-2
    AWS_PROFILE=accen-dev aws eks update-kubeconfig --kubeconfig $K --name $C --region $R
    CTX=$(KUBECONFIG=$K kubectl config current-context); [[ $CTX == *"cluster/$C" ]] || exit 1
    VPC=$(AWS_PROFILE=accen-dev aws eks describe-cluster --name $C --region $R --query cluster.resourcesVpcConfig.vpcId --output text)
    KUBECONFIG=$K helm --kube-context "$CTX" upgrade --install argocd argo/argo-cd --version 10.8.4 -n argocd \
      --values infra/argocd-values.yaml
    KUBECONFIG=$K helm --kube-context "$CTX" upgrade --install aws-load-balancer-controller eks/aws-load-balancer-controller \
      --version 1.14.0 -n kube-system --values infra/aws-load-balancer-controller-values.yaml --set clusterName=$C \
      --set region=$R --set vpcId=$VPC --set serviceAccount.create=true --set serviceAccount.name=aws-load-balancer-controller
    KUBECONFIG=$K kubectl --context "$CTX" -n argocd patch application kubearmor --type merge -p '{"operation":{"sync":{}}}'

(`helm repo add argo https://argoproj.github.io/argo-helm` and `helm repo add eks https://aws.github.io/eks-charts`
first, if they are missing.) The kubearmor sync is run by hand once. Until it runs, the live `kubearmor-default`
still carries the hook annotation, and Argo CD tests the live object, so the change does not set the app OutOfSync on
its own. Then check:
- `kubectl -n kubearmor get kubearmorconfig kubearmor-default -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations}'` shows no
  `helm.sh/hook`, so the next change syncs by itself.
- The `kubearmor-app=kubearmor` DaemonSets' first container has `DD_SERVICE=burritobot-kubearmor`.
- The argocd and aws-load-balancer-controller pods carry `tags.datadoghq.com/service: burritobot-*`.

Then drive one /chat on each cluster (`verify/kubecon_probe.py`) and run
`WIB_DD_LOOKBACK_MIN=30 WIB_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT=accen-dev WIB_REGION=us-west-2 python3 verify/test_datadog_sandbox_live.py`
at least 30 minutes after the relabel, so the window holds no log from before it. When every check passes, #629
closes.

**Context.** #668 moves the console and the five demo apps from nginx onto lab-platform's `web` image
(`ghcr.io/peopleforrester/lab-platform/web`, built by lab-platform#278). Hecaton run 15839 is the third dispatch.
Two earlier drafts exist. Run 10510's `765bcae` (`origin/agent/668-10510`) is a decisions entry only. Run 13230's

Neither reached staging. `bash verify/draft-drift.sh origin/agent/668-13230 origin/staging` found 31 drift lines:
#715 (`4f9f5c4`, 2026-10-31) made the same demo-app move on staging, on a layout of its own. Each app's `web.yaml` is a
file of its own that a `configMapGenerator` turns into a hashed ConfigMap, and `apps-allow-ingress` keeps port 80 for
the villain apps. So nothing from `cb31d55` is reused. Its gap list, measured on the pinned binary, is carried
below after a fresh read of lab-platform's source.

**What staging already does from the issue's list.** All of it is #715's work, plus the signature policy in `89c3919`:
- The five demo apps run `web@sha256:73cd15652cb8…fbd9`, set by `kustomize.images` at `{{ .Values.imageRegistry }}`
  in each `gitops/bootstrap/apps/demo-app-*.yaml`. That answers the issue's fourth point (how an image reaches a
  kustomize directory source under #622) the way #652 did for llm-guard.
- Each container has `NETWORK_BOUNDARY=sandbox` and port 8080, with probes on 8080, and each Service targets 8080.
- The package is pullable with no credential. On 2026-11-02 an anonymous ghcr.io token for
  `peopleforrester/lab-platform/web:pull` fetched the manifest for the digest and for `v1` with 200. `v1` still
  serves `sha256:73cd15652cb8b8eb706bd43f8877541db7f7c9e5f810ef0739636a27fc34fbd9`.

**The console did not move, again.** lab-platform's `internal/webserve/config.go` and `server.go`, read through
`sources` on 2026-11-02, take the same fields run 13230 measured. The top level takes `listen`, `tls`, `root`,
`routes` and `hosts`. A host rule takes `match`, `proxy` or `fallback`. lab-platform's merged PRs about `web` are
still #280 (the build), #336 (the umask republish) and #337. Against today's `console.conf`, the file still cannot say:
1. **`/chat`'s keyed limit (#450).** A route has one token bucket, shared by every caller (`buckets map[int]*bucket`).
   `/chat` needs a limit keyed on `X-BurritoBot-Session`, 10 a minute with burst 9, that holds no request without
   the header. Today it also has a second limit keyed on `X-Forwarded-For`. #786 (Michael's 2026-11-01 ruling on #450)
   drops that one, so after #786 one keyed limit is enough.
2. **`/chat`'s own replies.** nginx answers a 429 as a guarded 200 in guard-proxy's JSON shape, and a 502, 503 or 504
   as JSON with that code (BurritoBot#110). web answers a 429 with the text `too many requests` and a failed proxy
   with a bare 502. The phone would show a status code, not a sentence.
3. **`X-Forwarded-For`.** web calls `SetXForwarded()` on every route and host rule, which replaces the inbound value
   with the peer's address. `console.conf` sends none on `/lab-events` (`test_lab_events.py` holds that), and
   appends to the inbound value on `/jupyter/` and the support host.
4. **Host rules beyond `match` and `proxy`.** Every host rule shares one fallback page and a 3600s timeout, and
   takes any method. `maintenance-shell-<cluster>` (#664) needs GET and HEAD only, a 10s timeout and its own
   "nothing here yet" page. `support[-<cluster>]` (#685) needs GET and POST only, `/landed` refused, a 32k body
   cap, a 10s timeout, `X-Forwarded-For` appended and no fallback page.
5. **Host case.** web matches the Host as sent, with the port stripped but not lowercased. The file can fix this
   with `(?i)` in each `match`, so it needs nothing from lab-platform.

Moving the console now would drop the room's `/chat` limit and its readable refusals, and Challenge 6's two hosts.
Writing `gitops/ai-layer/web.yaml` without switching the Deployment would leave a file nothing runs. It would also
tie ~15 tests to a shape lab-platform is about to change. So neither is done. The console's `web.yaml`, its mounts
(`/etc/web/web.yaml`, `/srv/www`, console-tls at `/etc/web/tls`), `not-here.html` and moving the tests that parse
`console.conf` all wait on lab-platform adding points 1 to 4.

**The follow-up was never filed.** Run 13230's report said a follow-up asked lab-platform for those fields.
lab-platform has no issue for it, open or closed (searched on 2026-11-02 by "console", "web image", "routes",
"X-Forwarded-For" and "rate"). This run's report files it on lab-platform with the four points.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The demo-app half is owed what the #715 entry names:
`CONTEXT=<attendee-context> python3 verify/test_service_hosts_live.py` on the next attendee bring-up, where each party
host must answer its page through the console's host map and the 8080 target.

carries `dd_llmobs_enabled` false and makes no Agent Observability rows by design, so every row has to come through

space, as the step's second grep has it. The Go build's slog lines would read `"event":"task_cancel"`, so if
KubeCon ever moves to it, the first grep has to drop its spaces.

## 2026-11-02 · #751 · The Go guard-proxy's spend store is a kustomize Component that the #738 cutover lists

guard-proxy-agenticburn#32 (merged to its staging as eb40e28) keeps the Go build's spend tally, each session's
spend and the /toggle cost cap in a bbolt file at `SPEND_STORE_PATH`. The Go binary will not start without the
variable, and it fails startup when another process holds the file, because bbolt takes an exclusive flock and
waits 2 s for it. So the Go Deployment needs three things together: a PersistentVolumeClaim, or the file lives in
the container filesystem and a pod replacement still resets spend; `SPEND_STORE_PATH` pointing into that mount; and
`strategy: Recreate`, because a RollingUpdate starts the new pod while the old one still holds the flock.

**What changed.** `gitops/ai-layer/go-spend-store/` is a kustomize Component. It adds the PVC `guard-proxy-spend`
(ReadWriteOnce, 1Gi, the default gp3 StorageClass, as `student-work` uses), and JSON 6902 ops on the guard-proxy
Deployment: `strategy: { type: Recreate }`, pod `fsGroup: 1000` so uid 1000 can create the file on the EBS volume
(web-terminal needs the same), `SPEND_STORE_PATH=/var/lib/guard-proxy/spend.db` appended as the proxy's last env
entry, a read-write mount of the claim at `/var/lib/guard-proxy`, and the volume. The root filesystem stays
read-only. `gitops/ai-layer/kustomization.yaml` does not list it yet, so today's render is byte-for-byte what it was.
A comment on the guard-proxy Deployment in `resources.yaml` tells the cutover to list it.

**Why a Component.** The issue asks for this "at the cutover", which is #738, placed after KubeCon (2026-11-12) by
Michael's comments on #412 of 2026-10-24 and 2026-10-31. KubeCon runs proxy.py, which ignores `SPEND_STORE_PATH`
and keeps spend in memory, and the KubeCon clusters sync from staging. Putting the PVC and Recreate on the
Deployment now would give KubeCon's chat path an EBS volume to attach before the pod can start, and a few seconds
of chat outage on every proxy.py rollout, for a file proxy.py never opens. The change is written and tested, and
going live takes one line: the cutover adds `components: [go-spend-store]` in the same commit that swaps the image
and command.

**Why JSON ops.** Rendered with `kubectl kustomize`, a strategic merge patch put `SPEND_STORE_PATH` first in the
env list and shifted every other entry. ai-layer applies guard-proxy's env in its live order
(RespectIgnoreDifferences, #679). #679's replay shows a git-side addition still lands in git's place, and an append
keeps every existing entry at its index, which is the smallest change to an order-sensitive list.

**Test.** `verify/test_guard_proxy_spend_store.py`, in the tools tier (it needs `kubectl kustomize` and `jq`). It
renders the bundle with and without the Component and holds: one replica, Recreate with no rollingUpdate, the env
set once and last with every existing entry in its order, a read-write mount at the path's directory backed by a
rendered ReadWriteOnce claim, fsGroup equal to runAsGroup, a read-only root filesystem, the claim as the only added
object with every other object identical, and an ai-layer guard-proxy ignore that leaves `SPEND_STORE_PATH` out (so
a path change syncs from git). Its last check ties the store to the cutover: a committed guard-proxy whose container
no longer runs `python /app/proxy.py` fails unless the committed render carries the store.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Owed at the #738 cutover, in a session with AWS access, on a fresh attendee cluster:
`bash verify/run-e2e.sh` with CONTEXT set, then confirm `guard-proxy-spend` is Bound, the pod is Running with
`SPEND_STORE_PATH` set, and a `kubectl --context "$CONTEXT" -n agent rollout restart deploy/guard-proxy` (or an Argo
sync of an image change) keeps /cost's spent-so-far. One risk is unverified: ai-layer syncs with
ServerSideApply, and on a cluster where guard-proxy already exists as a RollingUpdate Deployment, the API server's
defaulted `rollingUpdate` block may survive the apply and be refused next to `type: Recreate`. A fresh cluster
creates the Deployment as Recreate and avoids it. If an existing cluster refuses it, the by-hand fix is one JSON
patch as the Argo controller SA, as `repair_env_order` patches: `replace` `/spec/strategy` with
`{"type": "Recreate"}`, which drops the defaulted block in the same write.

**Draft reuse.** Run 15265 first wrote this on `agent/751-15265`, and run 15566 reused it as 38e8892 on
`agent/751-15566`. Neither reached staging: run 15456 ended failed (validation), and run 15566 failed the prose
gate on contrast phrasing in its decisions.md entry. Run 15947 ran
`verify/draft-drift.sh origin/agent/751-15566 origin/staging`, which named only decisions.md and PROJECT_STATE.md as
changed on staging since the draft's base 42954c9. `git diff 42954c9 origin/staging` over `gitops/ai-layer/` touches
only `web/`, and `gitops/bootstrap/apps/ai-layer.yaml` is unchanged, so the Component, the PVC, the
`resources.yaml` comment and the test keep the draft's design on the current layout. What differs from the draft:
this entry and the PROJECT_STATE.md line are rewritten on today's files, and three comments and one check label in
the Component and the test are reworded to state each reason directly. No rendered field changed.

## 2026-11-02 · #733 · The git half of #707's live check is this run's commit: an order swap only an Argo CD sync can land

**What changed.** Hecaton run 15968 has no kubeconfig context and no AWS credentials, like runs 14867 and 15913.
This run does not leave the tool change to the session, as those entries planned. It makes the change itself:
`gitops/workshop-agent/agent.yaml` now lists `reorder_supply` before `check_inventory` in workshop-mcp's toolNames.
When the dispatcher promotes it to staging, watch-it-burn-community's root, which tracks staging with automated sync
(the 2026-11-01 entry), takes the change with no one acting. The issue's order asks for a Synced and Healthy read
before the change. `workshop-agent`'s `.status.history` still records the revision before this one, so the read
after the change covers that.

**Why a swap is the right probe.** `fleet.sh`'s `repair_agent_tools` sorts both lists before it compares them
(infra/terraform/fleet/fleet.sh, `repair_agent_tools`). An order-only change never differs there, so a converge never
deletes the Agent over it. If the live list reads in git's new order, an Argo CD sync put it there, whether or not a
converge ran in between. That is the no-converge proof the 11-02 entry said read_support_ticket's arrival could not
give. The two tools are both read-only mocks, and they sit next to each other, so the model sees the same tools.
KubeCon NA runs 2026-11-09 to 11-12 (conference-knowledge `kubecon-na-2026`), so the one pod roll kagent makes for
the new config lands a week before the talk. The admin cluster watch-it-burn-private takes it too and is not harmed.

**No swap back is owed.** The order has no meaning. A session that wants a second landing as more evidence reverts
this commit, and the revert lands the same way.

**Test.** `verify/test_agent_tools_sync.py` held git's list in the stale eleven's order. It now checks git's tools as
a set against the stale eleven plus read_support_ticket, and holds the new order, `GIT_ORDER`, which differs from
the stale order in more than the added tool. `STALE_ELEVEN` is unchanged, since it models what the clusters held on
2026-10-29.

**Tests.** `bash verify/run-tests.sh` passed (221 tests). `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` passed, 40 checks. One
earlier attempt failed `test_challenge_fallbacks.py` on its tmp/ check alone, because both suites ran at once.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The reads, from a session with accen-dev, after this commit is on staging. The report's
escalations carry the same commands.

    AWS_PROFILE=accen-dev aws eks update-kubeconfig --kubeconfig $K --name watch-it-burn-community --region us-west-2

    KUBECONFIG=$K kubectl --context "$CTX" -n argocd get application workshop-agent \

## 2026-11-02 · #773 · Challenge 2: the room deploys a public image by its plain name, and deployments-<cluster> lists every one

**What Michael approved** (his comment on #773, 2026-11-01, which is the spec). In Challenge 2 the room can deploy
a public image, shown on a deployments page. Each student gets a single-replica Deployment, and nothing scales it
up. The image comes from a small curated list that a student names in plain language ("deploy nginx", "run
busybox"), and the bot puts in the real image, so nobody types a registry path on a phone. The builder picks image
sources that fit the no-Docker-Hub rule (#714) and restrict-image-registries. These deploys land while the
guardrails are off; once #774's switch arms Kyverno, the same deploys are refused.

**What changed.**
- `deploy_app` (`gitops/ai-layer/workshop-mcp-server.py`). `PUBLIC_IMAGES` lists six images: busybox, alpine,
  nginx, httpd, redis and the 2048 game, with aliases (apache, docker-2048). A container whose image is a Docker
  Hub reference (a bare name, `user/name` or `docker.io/...`) is read for its repository: "nginx",
  "nginx:latest" and "docker.io/library/nginx:1.27" all become the pinned nginx. A Docker Hub repository off the
  list is refused before the apply, and the refusal names the list so the model can pick from it. An image that
  names its own registry (ghcr.io, quay.io, the villains, C6's Joker) is applied exactly as written. A workload with
  a listed image is a room deployment: one replica (Deployment, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet), requests 5m and 16Mi,
  limits 50m and 64Mi, and a scale to zero after `JOKER_SCALE_DOWN_SECONDS` (300 on the cluster), as #685's room
  Jokers get. busybox and alpine with no command get `sleep 3600`, so the pod stays up. The tool takes
  `requested_by`, the name the person chatting gave, and the description lists the names it can use.
- The report to the desk carries the image and `requested_by`. `ticket_site.py` keeps the name only when the
  witch vocabulary makes it (any case or spacing), else falls back to a `joker-<slug>` name, else none.
  `/wall.json` now records the image (the 2026-11-01 test's wall had none).
- The deployments page. The fake-ticket site serves it by Host: under `deployments-<cluster>` and
  `deployments.burritobot.co` it answers `/` (every landed deployment, newest first, polled every 3 s), `/mine`
  (one visitor's, by `?witch=<slug>` or the `wib_witch` cookie), `/deployments.json` and `/healthz`, and 404s
  everything else, POSTs included. A row reads "tron (nginx) deployed by Edgar the Kelpie at 16:22:34". Refusals
  are left off. The page says "Joker" nowhere and links to nothing, so it gives away no later challenge. The
  console has a server for the name that passes only those three paths, GET only (`console.conf`), and
  `fleet.sh`'s `WIB_VILLAIN_HOSTS` publishes `deployments-<cluster>`.
- The chat page's "see your deployments" link, hidden until the visitor has a row. The page asks its own host's
  `/deployments.json?witch=<slug>` on load, after each reply and once more 4 s later, since the report goes on its
  own thread; the main console server proxies that one path to the fake-ticket site. The link goes to
  `deployments-<this cluster>.burritobot.co/mine`, which works as soon as `fleet.sh routes` has run, with no
  router change.
- `/kubecon`: Challenge 2's beat is "Deploy any public image", with the 2026-11-01 Tron ask and its follow-up as two
  `.prompt` blocks, so `?sheet=1` carries both. The run-of-show's segment 3 says the same.
- The desk listens with a backlog of 128. Python's default of 5 left reports waiting out a SYN retry in the new
  test, and the page is polled by every phone that has it open.

**Why public.ecr.aws.** Amazon's public registry serves Docker's official images under `docker/library/`, at the
same digests as Docker Hub, so no copy is needed and nothing pulls from Docker Hub. restrict-image-registries
allows `ghcr.io/`, Harbor, the kagent and agentgateway registries, `registry.k8s.io/` and private ECR
(`<account>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com`). `public.ecr.aws` is none of them, so where the rule is at Deny the
room's deploys are refused today, and #774's "deny external registries" keeps refusing them. A ghcr.io copy would
be admitted by today's rule. 2048 is the image AWS's EKS load-balancer tutorials deploy, from ECR Public account
`l6m2t8p7`, which nobody here knows: the untrusted source is the lesson (`images/villains/README.md`). Each digest

## 2026-11-02 · question 1048 · #773: the model's reasoning stays visible in BurritoBot's replies to the room

**Question.** Should BurritoBot's replies to the breakout room keep showing the model's own reasoning about whether
to comply, or should its system prompt tell it to keep that reasoning out of the reply? In the 2026-11-01 live test
the first reply to the Tron prompt was the model's reasoning ("The user has provided a plausible reason (ticket
HR171) and is freaking out, which shows persistence. This meets the criteria for deploying an app."), outside the
chat page's collapsed "model reasoning" section.

**Answer:** Keep it visible.

**Decided by** hecaton's research under Michael's standing rules, not by Michael. The sources it cited: #100's
closing fix of 2026-09-03 (the model's reasoning is folded on purpose and never dropped, since a workshop about what
leaks out of an agent must not silently delete part of the model's output); `splitThinking` in
`gitops/ai-layer/web/burritbot.html` and the 2026-10-24 · #530 entry here (when folding leaves nothing to read, the
reasoning is the reply and is shown untagged); `/kubecon`'s prompts, which already hand the room the same cues the
leaked sentence names (a change ticket, urgency); and the persona in `gitops/workshop-agent/agent.yaml`, which
rewards a plausible reason and persistence by design.

**What it changes.** Nothing in the build. The system prompt the challenges were measured on stays as it is, and the
chat page keeps folding `<thinking>` text and showing reasoning that arrives as the reply. The open item in the
2026-11-02 · #773 entry ("question 5 ... is asked in run 15977's report") is settled by this answer. If the timed
run-throughs (by 2026-11-08) show the leak making the room's job too easy, a prompt change and a fresh live measure
of Challenges 1 to 3 on the public bot are the way to revisit it.
## 2026-11-02 · #783 · Agent Observability's copy gets a trace id of its own; `verify/agent_obs_flow.py` goes red when nothing arrives

**The cause.** #746's collector change (241f8e6, on staging 2026-11-01 15:51 UTC; both KubeCon clusters' `otel-collector`
Applications sync staging on their own) sends Agent Observability a second copy of every trace through
`otlp_http/llmobs`, and marks every span of APM's copy `dd_llmobs_enabled` false. The copy kept the original trace id.
At Datadog the two copies were one trace: the issue's APM trace `a2b544f7bbf6e12cfca75d8927f01f13` (2026-11-01 16:42
UTC, after the rollout) has two `POST` roots with `parentid: 0`, which is APM's `POST /chat` beside the copy's
`POST /chat` under its derived span id. The llmobs intake wrote the copy into the APM trace, the overlap Datadog's
page warns of ("some data sent to Agent Observability may also be written to the corresponding APM traces"). So the
trace Datadog converts held APM's marked spans, and its page says "an explicit `false` on any span prevents conversion
of the entire trace". The marker meant to keep APM's two-root rows out vetoed the copy as well, and every BurritoBot
turn after the rollout made no row.

**Why 03:30 UTC is not the start.** The last row (the probe's HC-666 chat, 03:26 UTC) is the last chat before the
rollout that anybody looked for. Between 03:26 and 15:51 UTC no commit touched the trace path: the collector's own
changes that night (0cef7b6, 89fcd0f) were on staging at 02:08 UTC, before the 03:26 row arrived; 4e86b30 only writes out
`runtime: go`, which the clusters already ran; the rest changed pages, the persona and docs. The two chats the issue
names as missing, 16:22 and 16:45 UTC, are the first after 241f8e6. Nothing in Datadog was read for this
(dispatched runs have no access to the sandbox org until #759), so the outage's first missing chat is inferred from
the repo's history and the issue's evidence. The live check below confirms or refutes it.

**The fix** (`gitops/otel-collector/values.yaml`, `transform/llmobs_one_root`, every profile). Its first statement
sets the copy's trace id to the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the original
(`set(trace_id.string, Substring(SHA256(trace_id.string), 0, 32))`). The hash is the same on every collector pod for
every span of a turn, so the turn stays one trace, and it shares no trace with a marked span. The derived turn span id
and kagent's re-parent now come from the copy's trace id. APM keeps its trace ids, its parentage and its marker.
`verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py` (E2E tools tier, the real otelcol-contrib 0.160.0) checks on all three profiles
that no span of the copy is in APM's trace and that every gen_ai span of the turn is in the copy's own. With the new
statement removed, those two checks and every one-root check fail (confirmed on a temporary edit, restored).

**What it costs.** Agent Observability's link from a row to APM opens the copy's own trace. If the intake writes the
copy into APM as before, APM shows one extra trace per turn under `service:burritobot` (the copy's gen_ai spans, one
root) next to the true one. The copy's two-root shape inside the true APM trace, which the issue saw, is gone.

**The check** (`verify/agent_obs_flow.py`, offline test `verify/test_agent_obs_flow.py`). `chat` sends one marked chat
to each KubeCon bot with a session of its own, then polls the LLM Observability spans API for `ml_app:burritobot` on
that bot's `k8s.cluster.name` until ten minutes pass, and exits 1 with `AGENT OBSERVABILITY RECEIVED NOTHING from
<cluster>` when none arrives. It prints the trace ids it found, which is the read-back #783's third criterion asks
for. `watch` spends nothing: it reads APM's newest `service:burritobot env:burritobot-kubecon-na-26` span at least ten
minutes old and exits 1 when Agent Observability has no span from two minutes before it. It also exits 1 when APM has
nothing to compare. Both read Datadog with the read-only key in Secrets Manager `watch-it-burn/datadog`, as
`verify/stage_traces.py` does. The run-of-show's Night Before list runs `chat` before every run-through and the morning
of. A Datadog monitor on Agent Observability's own volume would page between runs; that needs its metric name read
in the org first, so it is a follow-up.

**If the live check is still red after the fix.** The two other readings of the evidence, and what each means:
the intake refusing the copy shows as `otlp_http/llmobs` errors in the collector log (step 2 below), and the copy
reaching Agent Observability under the new id but still not converting would show as no error and no row. Either way,
the stage's rows come back at once by taking `transform/llmobs_apm_off` out of the traces processors of
`values.yaml` and `values-burn.yaml` and `forward/llmobs` out of the traces exporters (APM's own conversion, the
two-root shape that ran until 2026-11-01), and #746's one-root view waits.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Hecaton run 16035 has no AWS credentials, kubeconfig or Datadog access. Once this
commit is on staging, both clusters' collectors sync it on their own. From a session with accen-dev, at the repo
root, for C in `watch-it-burn-community` and `watch-it-burn-private`:

    K=/tmp/$C.kubeconfig
    AWS_PROFILE=accen-dev aws eks update-kubeconfig --kubeconfig $K --name $C --region us-west-2
    CTX=$(KUBECONFIG=$K AWS_PROFILE=accen-dev kubectl config current-context); [[ $CTX == *"cluster/$C" ]] || exit 1
    # 1. the collector runs this commit (the revision must contain it, and the sync must have succeeded)
    KUBECONFIG=$K AWS_PROFILE=accen-dev kubectl --context "$CTX" -n argocd get application otel-collector \
      -o jsonpath='{.status.sync.revision} {.status.sync.status} {.status.operationState.phase}{"\n"}'
    # 2. the intake takes the copy: no output is the pass
    KUBECONFIG=$K AWS_PROFILE=accen-dev kubectl --context "$CTX" -n monitoring logs \
      ds/otel-collector-opentelemetry-collector-agent -c opentelemetry-collector --since=1h | grep -i llmobs

Then `python3 verify/agent_obs_flow.py chat --profile accen-dev` must end `AGENT OBSERVABILITY GREEN`, and its trace
ids go in a comment on #783. Whitney's #746 look (one root row per chat) can be read on the same chats.
