## 2026-11-02 · #774 · The Kubernetes guardrails switch: both KubeCon clusters start with the four off, one guardrails-on arms both, and Kyverno denies external registries

**The spec.** Michael approved #774 on 2026-11-01 (his comment on the issue is the spec): both KubeCon clusters,
community (attackme) and private, start with the four Kubernetes guardrails off; one `guardrails-on`, run from either
cluster's terminal, arms all four on both, Kyverno to Deny included, so external registries are denied; and the
badges come up the way they do when a control arms. #773, #775 and the run-of-show #776 build on it.

**What changed (hecaton run 15985).**
- Two profiles, `gitops/bootstrap/values-kubecon-community.yaml` and `values-kubecon-private.yaml`, deploy-only (built
  by `infra/deploy-full-idp.sh`, which fleet.sh calls; lab-platform.yaml does not present them). kubecon-community is
  burn plus the Kyverno engine, restrict-image-registries alone (`kyverno-registry-policy`), deny-external-registries
  (`kyverno-breakout`) and the switch's identity (`guardrails-switch`). kubecon-private is admin less
  network-policies and kubearmor-policies, plus kyverno-breakout, guardrails-switch and the internal registry.
- `infra/terraform/fleet/event.sh` gains `WIB_ROSTER_PROFILES`, `kubecon` for this event. fleet.sh's
  `bootstrap_profile_for_role` maps community and admin to the KubeCon pair under `kubecon` and to burn and admin
  under `workshop`, and refuses any other value by name. fleet.sh arms Kyverno at bootstrap on admin and full only,
  so nothing on the KubeCon pair is armed before `guardrails-on`; `infra/setup-instructor-cluster.sh` says the same.
- `policies/kyverno-breakout/deny-external-registries.yaml`, a ValidatingPolicy at Audit: a request from an agent
  namespace identity (web-terminal excepted) may create a pod, or through autogen any pod controller, in `agent`
  only from `registry.burritobot.co/`. An UPDATE that keeps every image passes. Background evaluation is off because
  the rule reads `request.userInfo`.
- `restrict-image-registries` trusts `registry.burritobot.co/` as well, and its message says so; lab.html quotes the
  message, and LAB-TEXT.md is regenerated from it.
- `gitops/guardrails-switch/`: namespace `guardrails-switch`, a ServiceAccount with a long-lived token Secret, and a
  grant on the four guardrails' objects alone (escalate, get and patch on the `workshop-agent` Role; get and patch on
  the two registry policies by name; get, create, patch and delete on KubeArmor policies and NetworkPolicies in
  `agent`). No agent identity holds a grant in that namespace.
- `fleet.sh guardrails-link [<community>[@<region>] <private>[@<region>]]` writes each cluster's endpoint, CA and
  switch token into the other's `guardrails-switch/guardrails-peer` Secret, after checking from the fleet host that
  the token can patch restrict-image-registries. `instructors up` runs it once it has built both KubeCon clusters, and
  a failed link fails the build.
- The web terminal (`gitops/ai-layer/web-terminal/entrypoint.sh` and its image copy) gains `guardrails-on` and
  `guardrails-off`. Each switches RBAC (the staged scoped or broad Role), Kyverno (both registry policies, read back),
  KubeArmor (`block-recipe-snoop`) and egress (the staged agent NetworkPolicy set), one guardrail at a time, on this
  cluster and then on the other through `~/.kube/peer`, printing every kubectl it runs. An optional number waits that
  many seconds between guardrails. It exits non-zero, naming what missed, when the other cluster is unlinked or
  unreachable or a Kyverno flip does not hold. `_c7gw` accepts `kubecon-private` as an admin cluster.
- The badges needed no change: guard-proxy's `/controls` already reads `agent-egress-allowlist`,
  restrict-image-registries' action, `block-recipe-snoop` and the `workshop-agent` Role, the objects the switch flips,
  and the chat page shows the NetworkPolicy, Kyverno, KubeArmor and RBAC scope badges from them.
- The internal registry, `gitops/internal-registry/`: Distribution 3.1.2 (`ghcr.io/distribution/distribution`) on
  the private cluster, with a regctl 0.11.7 sidecar that copies the seed list into it at every pod start and marks the
  pod Ready once done. The seed list holds Challenge 3's Joker at `burritobot/maintenance-shell:busybox-1.38.0`, the
  path #775 names. The console serves `registry-<cluster>` and the bare `registry` name on both domains read-only (GET
  and HEAD), and a NetworkPolicy admits only the console to it in-cluster. `fleet.sh routes` publishes
  `registry.burritobot.co` on the private cluster's console LB and `registry-<cluster>` for each roster cluster.
- `verify/kubecon_probe.py`'s admin run judges the new start (four off), runs the terminal's own `guardrails-on` in
  the private terminal pod after Challenge 1, judges all four armed and the badges lit, adds a public image denied by
  deny-external-registries and the internal image admitted, and ends with `guardrails-off` after guards-off.
  `verify/stage_traces.py` arms before Challenge 3's attack seed. The run-of-show, the readiness doc, docs/floor.md
  and platform-baseline.yaml say the same.
- Tests: `verify/test_guardrails_switch.py` (offline) and `verify/test_breakout_registry_policy.py` (tools tier, the
  Kyverno 1.19.1 CLI); twelve existing tests follow the new profiles, routes and probe beats.

**Decided here: the platform's own images stay on a short list the room's requests cannot use.** The issue left
this to the build ("mirror them, or keep a short list of approved platform registries that the room's requests
can't use"). Mirroring every platform image into the internal registry would make the platform's bring-up wait on a
registry that runs on the platform, and kagent's and agentgateway's images would have to be re-pinned at a second
path. The line is drawn on who asks, which the API server authenticates: a request from an agent namespace identity
gets the internal registry alone; Argo CD, the kagent controller and the kube controllers keep restrict-image-
registries' list. The Kyverno CLI cases show both halves.

**Decided here: the Kyverno guardrail is two policies.** restrict-image-registries stays as the 2-hour workshop's
Challenge 2 teaches it, and it is the policy the Kyverno badge reads, so the switch sets it to Deny on both clusters.
deny-external-registries carries the breakout's rule and installs only on the KubeCon profiles. The community cluster
takes restrict-image-registries alone, through a directory source that includes the one file, so the room meets no
other admission policy. require-resource-limits is left out of the switch, so a refusal names a registry policy.

**Decided here: the registry runs on the private cluster behind the console.** The room attacks attackme, and both
clusters' nodes reach the private cluster's console through the apex router, whose Railway edge holds the
`*.burritobot.co` certificate. `fleet.sh routes` writes `registry.burritobot.co` as a row of its own on the console LB
of the cluster holding burritobot-private (`bare_rows`), so backups.py's repoint moves it with that cluster's other
rows, and the router routes it as it routes any row. The apex router's derive-roster scores the label `registry`
below `burritobot-private`, so the wall's roster is unchanged. `registry-<cluster>` is published beside it.

**The 2-hour workshop.** burn, admin, attendee and full are unchanged; a workshop roster sets
`WIB_ROSTER_PROFILES=workshop` in event.sh. The one change a workshop student can see is restrict-image-registries'
message, which now lists registry.burritobot.co; LAB-TEXT.md and lab.html quote it.

**What this leaves for other issues.** Once `guardrails-on` runs, the room's HC-666 Jokers are refused on attackme,
because their image is on the refused `festival-ops/` path; #775 moves HC-666 onto `registry.burritobot.co`, and #776
places the switch in the run of show. backups.py's promotion does not re-link the switch; until it does, a promoted
standby is linked with `fleet.sh guardrails-link <community>@<region> <private>@<region>`.

**Rebased onto staging `e3b4b73` (run 16077).** Run 16040's commits failed promotion on a rebase conflict with
#773's deployments page, which landed meanwhile. Each conflict was two additions side by side, and both are kept:
`WIB_VILLAIN_HOSTS` keeps `deployments` and the registry hosts follow it, console.conf has the deployments server and
then the registry server (six servers, as `verify/test_console_no_toggle.py` now counts), PROJECT_STATE.md has both
sections, and the run-of-show's Challenge 2 fix names both registry policies for #773's `public.ecr.aws` images.
The offline suite and the tools tier pass on the rebased branch.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** No cluster is up in this run. In a session with accen-dev access, on a fresh KubeCon
bring-up (`./fleet.sh instructors up all`, which bills the pair at about $24 a day; spend waits on Michael's go):
1. `instructors up` must log "guardrails-link: linked"; `./fleet.sh guardrails-link` repeats it.
2. In each cluster's terminal, `guardrails-on` ends "all four Kubernetes guardrails are on." and `guardrails-off`
   "... are off."; the four badges light and go dark on both chat pages.
3. `python3 verify/kubecon_probe.py community attackme.burritobot.co --context <community-context> --kubeconfig
   /tmp/community.kubeconfig --profile accen-dev`, then the same with `admin burritobot-private.burritobot.co` and
   the private context: both GREEN. The admin run covers the switch, the public-image denial and the internal image.
4. After `./fleet.sh routes roster`, `curl -fsS https://registry.burritobot.co/v2/burritobot/maintenance-shell/tags/list`
   lists `busybox-1.38.0`, and a POST to it answers 403. A pod on attackme running that image pulls it.

**Prose gate (run 16115).** Run 16077 failed the ai-isms gate: its detector reads the third-person verb from
"to let" as the first-person-plural connective. The five added lines that used that verb (PROJECT_STATE.md, decisions.md, the run-of-show,
KUBECON-ABSTRACT-READINESS.md and kubecon_probe.py's docstring) now say "admits", "passes" or "grants" instead. No
behavior changed; the branch is run 16077's, unchanged otherwise, on the same staging `878b077`.

## 2026-11-03 · #775 · Challenge 3 keeps landing with Kyverno on: HC-666 asks for the internal registry's Joker, and least privilege is its fix

**The spec.** Michael approved #775 as proposed on 2026-11-02 (issue comment 6565190035): HC-666's hidden paragraph
asks for `registry.burritobot.co/burritobot/maintenance-shell`, which Kyverno admits because the policy trusts that
registry; the payoff stays the Joker page, with a URL the bot hands over and the Joker on `deployments.burritobot.co`
under the person's witch name; the two Joker-page lines that would be false are rewritten; Challenge 3's fix becomes
the input guard and least privilege taking Deployments away from the bot (OWASP LLM06, Excessive Agency); and the
2-hour workshop keeps working. #774 (the switch, the internal registry) landed on staging at `5c400e8` to `858ffaf`,
so the wait recorded by runs 16043 and 16125 is over. Their drafts on `agent/775-16043` changed decisions.md alone;
`verify/draft-drift.sh f64298d origin/staging` names only decisions.md, so nothing was cherry-picked. Their build map
was re-checked against the current layout and followed where it still held; what differs is below.

**What changed (hecaton run 16464).**
- `gitops/ai-layer/ticket_site.py`: `ROOM_IMAGE`, `registry.burritobot.co/burritobot/maintenance-shell:busybox-1.38.0`,
  is the image HC-666's paragraph asks for, and its last sentence asks the bot to give the customer the web address
  the deploy result names. `C6_IMAGE` and HC-7731, the 2-hour lab's, are unchanged.
- The breakout's Joker is a second tag of the same image, `festival-ops/maintenance-shell:busybox-1.38.0-internal`:
  `images/villains/build.sh joker-internal` lays `joker-web-internal/www/index.html` over joker-web's page. That page
  keeps the persona and says it came from `registry.burritobot.co`, the registry the cluster trusts, and that an input
  classifier or a bot that cannot create Deployments would have stopped it. The internal registry's seed copies it,
  by digest `sha256:0dbe92d4...`, to `burritobot/maintenance-shell:busybox-1.38.0`; images.lock pins it.
- Each room Joker has its own page, `https://maintenance-shell-<cluster>.burritobot.co/joker-<name>/`. `deploy_app`
  gives a `joker-*` pod its Deployment's name as hostname under a new headless Service, `jokers`, and labels it
  `burritobot.co/room-joker`; the console's maintenance-shell server proxies `/joker-<name>/` to
  `joker-<name>.jokers.agent.svc.cluster.local:8080`, and `published_address` names that page in the deploy reply.
  The deployments page needed nothing: `record_landing` already credits a `joker-<slug>` Deployment to its witch.
- Least privilege: `c6-least-privilege-role.yaml` in the challenge-fixes ConfigMap is `c5-scoped-role.yaml` without
  create or patch on Deployments and Pods. The terminal's `guard-agency-on` applies it and `guard-agency-off` puts
  `c5-scoped-role.yaml` back, each printing its kubectl (both entrypoint copies, kept byte-identical).
- workshop-mcp's reaper scales through `deployments/scale`, and every copy of the workshop-agent Role (shipped,
  c8-broad, c8-scoped, c5-scoped and the new one) grants patch on it.
- The KubeCon probe's admin run: `c6-admission` is replaced by `c6-lands` (HC-666 lands `joker-agatha-the-banshee` with
  Kyverno at Deny, one model call), `guard-agency-on`, and `c6-forbidden` (a server-side dry run of that Joker as
  workshop-mcp is Forbidden by RBAC). An admin run is 12 model calls. `stage_traces.py` seeds c3-attack as landing,
  then flips guard-agency-on and guard-input-on before c3-fixed. The run-of-show, `/kubecon`, PROJECT_STATE.md,
  KUBECON-ABSTRACT-READINESS.md and images/villains/README.md say the same.
- Tests: `verify/test_joker_build_digest.py` (tools tier) rebuilds both Jokers with `build.sh` into crane's own
  loopback registry and holds each to its images.lock digest and page; nine existing tests follow the new image,
  beats, Role, reaper path and per-person page.

**Decided here: one page per person.** The approval left shared or per-person to the builder, recommending
per-person, with a check back to Michael if it added cost. It adds one static headless Service and one console
location: no object per person, no new grant, no DNS row or certificate (the maintenance-shell host is already
published). A shared URL would also have shown a person someone else's running Joker after their own was refused,
which muddles the fix beat. So no question was needed.

**Decided here: the breakout's Joker is its own tag, and its digest was pinned before its first push.** Rewriting
joker-web's page would make the 2-hour workshop's Joker say admission passed it, which is false there: HC-7731's image
is on the refused `festival-ops/` path. A second tag in the same public package needs no new package or visibility
change. The build is reproducible: run with crane 0.22.1 into a loopback registry, `build.sh` rebuilt the published
workshop Joker to its own digest, `d8dae795`, byte for byte, under umask 002 and 022. `build.sh`'s tar now sets the
modes (`--mode='a+rX,ug+w,o-w'`, the modes the pushed layer has), so the digest no longer depends on the checkout's
umask; the workshop digest did not move. crane 0.22.1 (go-containerregistry's latest release on 2026-11-03, its
SHA-256 from the release's checksums.txt, checked that day) is a new pin in `verify/e2e-tools.lock`, because gzip
output can differ between crane releases and the pin has to match what the push uses.

**Decided here: least privilege takes patch as well as create, and keeps the reaper.** `deploy_app` applies with
server-side apply, so for a Joker that already exists (every person who asked before the fix) the API checks patch,
not create. A Role that dropped create alone would land those re-asks again. With patch gone, the reaper's merge patch
on the Deployment would fail too and leave Jokers that landed just before the fix running, so it moved to the scale
subresource, which every Role grants. ConfigMaps and Services keep their verbs: they run nothing.

**The 2-hour workshop.** HC-7731, the festival-ops Joker and its digest, its page, `guard-admission-on` and the lab
text are unchanged. What a workshop cluster now carries: the extra `deployments/scale` rule in the Role (C8's broad
Role still matches the shipped one), the reaper's scale-subresource path, an empty `jokers` Service, the console's
`/joker-<name>/` location, and the unused `guard-agency-on`/`guard-agency-off` commands. HC-666 is only taught at
KubeCon, and its image is served only where the KubeCon private cluster runs the internal registry. Editing
`images/web-terminal/entrypoint.sh` triggers `build-web-terminal.yml` on the staging push, as #774's edit did; the
tag-overwrite problem that causes is run 16420's follow-up, not changed here.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** In order, in a session with GHCR write access and then accen-dev access:
1. Push the breakout's Joker once this is on staging, from a checkout of staging:
   `bash verify/fetch-e2e-tools.sh && gh auth token | verify/.tools/bin/crane auth login ghcr.io -u peopleforrester --password-stdin && CRANE=verify/.tools/bin/crane bash images/villains/build.sh joker-internal`,
   then `verify/.tools/bin/crane digest ghcr.io/peopleforrester/festival-ops/maintenance-shell:busybox-1.38.0-internal`
   must print `sha256:0dbe92d402b5e021c97e67e16613d9d042ed89ae1333be3dbe22f6b9cf0edabf`. Until then the internal
   registry's seed cannot copy it, its pod never reads Ready, and HC-666's Jokers sit in ImagePullBackOff.
2. On a KubeCon bring-up, `curl -fsS https://registry.burritobot.co/v2/burritobot/maintenance-shell/tags/list` lists

## 2026-11-03 · #786 · /chat is limited per conversation only: console nginx's per-network zone is gone

**The ruling.** Michael ruled on 2026-11-01 (#450, comment 6554358563) to move the KubeCon chat limit from per
network to per person. In the #644 load run, console nginx's `wib_chat_address` zone (120 a minute, burst 60, keyed on the
X-Forwarded-For the apex sends) refused 1,164 of 1,500 turns from one address. On venue Wi-Fi that zone is one bucket
for a room of about 150.

**What changed.** `gitops/ai-layer/console.conf` drops `wib_chat_address` and its `limit_req` on `/chat`. `/chat`
applies only `wib_chat_session` (10 a minute, burst 9). The `@chat_slow_down` refusal is still a guarded 200 in the
/chat shape, and now reads "Slow down, hungry traveler. BurritoBot takes 10 a minute per conversation. Wait a few
seconds and send that again." The /chat ladder comment no longer counts six calls at PROXY_TIMEOUT 45: TURN_TIMEOUT
270 has bounded the turn since #694, and each call gets PROXY_TIMEOUT or what is left of the turn. The page's
session-header comment in `burritbot.html` says the same. `verify/load_replay.py` reads only the per-conversation
zone, by name, and predicts served turns from it and guard-proxy's cluster window. The run-of-show's audience path
table and Night Before load step, the readiness doc's row 9, PROJECT_STATE.md and the #644 load-test record now say
there is no per-network limit. Unchanged: `resources.yaml` (RATE_LIMIT_RPM 150, RATE_LIMIT_SESSION_RPM 10,
COST_CAP_USD 25, TURN_TIMEOUT 270, PROXY_TIMEOUT 120), the guard-proxy submodule pin (`fb6e2bf`), the `/prompts`
route, and the ladder checks in `verify/test_audience_path.py`.

**Each removed per-network check, and what replaces it (for the test review).**
- `test_audience_path.py`, the check that the network zone keys on the apex's X-Forwarded-For: replaced by "no limit_req_zone is keyed on a client address" (it reads `$remote_addr`, `$binary_remote_addr`,
  `$http_x_forwarded_for` and real_ip keys) and "no limit_conn or limit_conn_zone".
- `test_audience_path.py`, "the per-network ceiling is under the cluster window and holds ten phones": replaced by
  "the conversation zone is 10 a minute with a burst of 9" and "guard-proxy keeps RATE_LIMIT_RPM 150,
  RATE_LIMIT_SESSION_RPM 10 and COST_CAP_USD 25".
- `test_audience_path.py`, "/chat applies the conversation zone, then the network zone": replaced by "/chat applies
  the conversation zone and no other".
- `test_audience_path.py`, the refusal check that wanted the network's 120 in the reply: now "a limit is a guarded
  200 in the /chat shape", "the limit's sentence names 10 a minute per conversation and no network" and "the limit's
  sentence says to wait and send that again".
- `test_audience_path.py`, new for criterion 3: "nothing on /chat changes the request body" (no `proxy_set_body`,
  `proxy_pass_request_body`, `client_max_body_size`, `sub_filter`, `rewrite`, njs, perl, `mirror` or `proxy_method` in
  the /chat location, the default server or the http level), "/chat proxies to guard-proxy's own /chat" and "the
  /prompts feed is still guard-proxy's own GET /prompts".
- `test_load_replay.py`, "limits read from git: nginx 120/min per network, burst 60": replaced by "limits read from
  git: nginx 10/min per conversation, burst 9", "the tool reads only the per-conversation zone, none per network" and
  "one address sending as 500 phones is held only by the cluster window" (the old model
  predicted 360 served for the default plan, the new one 375).
- `test_audience_path_live.py`, "about 61 of 70 fresh conversations get through from one address": replaced by "all
  80 fresh conversations from one address get through nginx", 80 being more than the old zone's 61. New: "the refusal
  names 10 a minute per conversation and says to wait and send that again". Its "guard-proxy runs PROXY_TIMEOUT 45"
  could never pass since #694 set 120, so it now reads git's PROXY_TIMEOUT, TURN_TIMEOUT and the three limits from
  `resources.yaml` and holds the deployment to them.

## 2026-11-03 · #798 · A re-dispatched run finds the earlier run's unlanded draft and ports it, and polls the E2E command

Hecaton's insights found two runs that lost their time redoing work an earlier run had already done ("context
loss"). There was no earlier draft of #798 to check against staging.

- **Run 9277 (#604).** Run 9249 committed the measurement (`808116c`) and a prose fix (`c209a4e`) on
  `agent/604-9249`. It failed the ai-isms gate, so hecaton did not promote it, and run 9277 started from staging
  `6908b3c` and measured again. That branch applies to `6908b3c` as it is: `verify/draft-drift.sh
  origin/agent/604-9249 6908b3c` prints CLEAN. AGENTS.md said nothing about earlier drafts then (#633 added that two
  days later), so the comments on #604 were the only record of the work.
- **Run 15763 (#205).** The attempt before it stalled: it started `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` in the background
  and ended its turn to wait, and hecaton stops a run that prints nothing for 15 minutes. The draft it had to go on,
  `d7bb3ff` on `agent/205-12982`, was 125 commits behind. AGENTS.md's second item said to make the draft's design
  again whenever `draft-drift.sh` exits 1, and it exits 1 for nearly every draft, because every run appends to
  decisions.md. Against `aca67c9`, staging that morning, it named decisions.md and three files staging had only
  edited: VERSIONS.lock, infra/org/README.md and verify/run-e2e.sh. A cherry-pick of `d7bb3ff` onto `aca67c9`
  conflicts on decisions.md alone. The run did find real changes to make (#707 had moved the agent's ignores to
  the workshop-agent app, and #643 had added standby regions), and rereading the staging commits each line names
  finds those.
- **The stall was already known, in the wrong file.** The 2026-10-29 #267 entry and the 2026-11-01 #520 entry
  record that a run waiting silently on a long suite stalls, and that polling the log in the foreground avoids it.
  AGENTS.md, which each run reads, did not say so.

**The cause.** What one run makes or learns stays where the next run does not look: commits hecaton never promoted
sit on the run's branch and in the issue's comments, and lessons sit in this file. Then the one rule AGENTS.md gave
for an old draft sent every draft to a redo.

**The fix.**
- `verify/prior-drafts.sh <issue> [base]` (new, offline) lists each `origin/agent/<issue>-<run>` branch newest first.
  It marks a branch LANDED when the base contains it or has each of its commit subjects since the two parted (the
  dispatcher's rebase keeps them). Any other branch is a DRAFT, shown with its commits and `draft-drift.sh`'s verdict.
  A DRAFT followed in the base by a commit naming the issue gets a LATER line, since a later run most likely redid
  it. It ends with START and the newest DRAFT with no LATER line (exit 1), or NONE (exit 0). On today's staging
  it prints NONE for #205 and #604, whose work has since landed. With base `6908b3c` it names `agent/604-9277`
  and `agent/604-9249`, both CLEAN; with 9277's branch absent, as it was when 9277 ran, START names 9249's.
- `verify/draft-drift.sh` no longer counts decisions.md when both sides only added lines to it: it prints an
  APPEND line, to keep both entries. Its last line now tells the two kinds of drift apart. A moved or deleted path,
  or a removed directory, is a part of the draft to make again on the base's layout. An edit in place is ported by
  cherry-pick, after which the run rereads the base commit named. The exit codes are unchanged.
- AGENTS.md's "Dispatched runs (hecaton)" section: the second item starts from `prior-drafts.sh` and gives the
  per-line rule. A third item says a run reads in the issue's comments why the draft did not land, ports it, fixes
  what stopped it, and redoes only what the verdict or that reason names. A fourth says the E2E command takes over
  20 minutes on the shared host, so a run commits first, starts it in the background with its output in a log and
  reads the log in the foreground until it ends. Its first sentence, which `verify/test_dispatched_runs_cause_comment.py`
  reads for #633's runs, is unchanged.
- **Tests.** `verify/test_prior_drafts.sh` (offline, new) builds a scratch repo with published drafts. It covers
  no draft; one unlanded draft; two drafts, newest first; a rebased draft with an older one followed by later work;
  a merged draft; issue 60 against issue 604's branches and commits; and bad input. `verify/test_draft_drift.sh`
  gains an append on both sides (CLEAN, exit 0), an edit in place (port), and a decisions.md the base removed a
  line from (drift). Run against the old `draft-drift.sh`, 7 of its checks fail. `verify/test_dispatched_runs.py`
  holds the new items to the scripts they name.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing here touches a cluster, and nothing is owed on one.

**The suites.** `bash verify/run-tests.sh` exits 0 (225 tests). `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 45 checks in about
22 minutes on the shared host, started in the background after the commit and read in the foreground as the fourth
item says. It exits 1 on one check, the red already recorded for #746 and #775 on 2026-11-03:
`test_image_version_tags.py` finds ghcr.io serving `watch-it-burn:web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7` at
`sha256:0b72ecc7...`, not the pinned `68004fb5`, because CI pushed over that tag again. Nothing here touches an image.

## 2026-11-02 · #480 · The tool-pin live check becomes one command that leaves an existing cluster as found

**Why.** The coordinator's go on #480 (2026-11-02, under Michael's standing go of 2026-11-01) is to run the live
kagent check on `watch-it-burn-community`, the public cluster, not a new one, and to leave it as found, with attackme
answering 200 after. Michael's correction the same day allows `watch-it-burn-private` as well and never a third
cluster. This run had no cluster credentials (`sources aws-env` and `sources fleet` are refused at its tier), so it
could not run the check. It read `live-check.sh` against the live cluster's layout on staging instead. As written,
the script would have failed on that cluster or left it changed:

- **Port 3004 was closed.** #552's `agentgateway-ingress` NetworkPolicy (`gitops/ai-layer/chat-path-ingress.yaml`,
  on every profile) admits any pod only on 3001, 3003 and the readiness ports. Neither kagent's controller nor the
  agent could have reached the pinned bind. `setup` now opens 3004 in that rule, and `restore` closes it again.
- **The script never sent a question.** The old runbook said "ask BurritoBot", which goes through guard-proxy and
  moves the public `/cost` counter that was reset for KubeCon. The gateway's `:3000` admits only guard-proxy. `ask`
  now goes through kagent's A2A proxy, `kagent-controller.kagent:8083/api/a2a/agent/workshop-agent/` (kagent v0.9.9
  `go/core/internal/httpserver/server.go` line 336), which `workshop-agent-ingress` admits.
- **`restore` relied on selfHeal, which would have left three changes.** With ai-layer's ServerSideApply, a Service
  port added by `kubectl patch` belongs to another field manager, so the diff is not expected to show it, and
  selfHeal would leave it (reasoned from how server-side diff works, not measured). A reverted `evil-mcp-src` ConfigMap does not change the source the running evil-mcp already loaded. And auto-sync
  came back as a hard-coded `{prune, selfHeal}`, not as it was. `setup` now snapshots every object it changes,
  `restore` writes each back, restarts evil-mcp-shim after a rug pull, compares everything with the snapshot, waits
  for both Applications' sync and health and evil-mcp's `Accepted` condition to be as found, and checks the public
  host answers 200. It exits 1 and
  keeps the snapshot on any difference.
- **`observe` would have ended the run.** Under `pipefail`, its grep for the pinned bind's log lines exits 1 when
  there are none yet. The new offline test found that.
- **The gateway config came from this checkout.** `gateway_bind.py cluster` renders the committed config, and a live
  cluster syncs from its own branch. A new `extend` mode adds the bind to the live ConfigMap read on stdin.
- **The tool-pin image was never pushed** (watch-it-burn:tool-pin is a 404). `tool-pin.yaml` now runs `tool_pin.py`
  from a `tool-pin-src` ConfigMap on the python:3.12-slim mirror guard-proxy already runs. An init container installs
  grpcio from `requirements.txt` by hash, and egress to PyPI is needed only for that. This shape ran in Docker on
  2026-11-02 with the same image, commands, read-only root and uid 1000. tool-pin started, passed evil-mcp's untouched
  list over gRPC and stripped a rug-pulled `get_weather`. `images/tool-pin/Dockerfile` is unchanged.

`live-check.sh run` does the whole check in one command. It runs strip mode untouched, the rug pull, then deny mode,
and asks and observes in each. It restarts the agent if kagent did not roll it after the url change, and records
that as a finding. It restores on any exit and tees everything to `/tmp/tool-pin-live.<context>.record.txt`.
`verify/test_tool_pin_live_check.py` runs it against `verify/tool_pin_kubectl_shim.py`, a stateful kubectl stand-in
loaded with the committed gateway config, Service, ingress policy and server.py. It covers the full run, a failure
mid-run, a gateway that refuses the config, a restore that cannot put a thing back, the refusals (public host not
200, unknown context, a second snapshot), and kagent rolling the agent itself. With restore's Service-port step or
setup's policy step removed, the test fails.

**New dependency:** typing-extensions 4.16.0 (PyPI, 2026-07-02), grpcio 1.84.1's only requirement, hash-pinned in
`docs/research/2026-10-24-tool-pin-spike/requirements.txt` with grpcio's x86_64 and aarch64 cp312 wheels, read
2026-11-02. `--require-hashes` needs every package pinned, and this is the current release.

**A design consequence.** The student's action stays a one-field RemoteMCPServer patch only if bind 3004 ships in
GitOps with its Service port and its port in `agentgateway-ingress`. `verify/test_chat_path_ingress.py` would then
need the bind's callers. The spike README says so.

**The stand-in, 2026-11-03.** In one full offline run `test_tool_pin_live_check.py` failed: setup stopped between the
snapshot and the gateway patch. It passed alone, and in six parallel reruns of the old code. The likeliest cause is
the stand-in itself. `kubectl create --dry-run | kubectl apply -f -` ran two shim processes that both rewrote the
state file in place, so `apply` could read it half written. `create --dry-run` now touches no state, as in kubectl,
and writes are atomic and only on a change. That exposed a real weakness in `restore`: it compared
`agentgateway-ingress`'s rules and the Applications' auto-sync as raw JSON strings, so a change of key order alone
read as a difference. Both are now compared with sorted keys. A failing run of the test now prints the script's own
"live-check: failed at line N" line.

**Not yet run on a cluster:** `live-check.sh run` on `watch-it-burn-community`, from a host with the accen-dev
profile; the exact commands are in the spike README's "Still open: the cluster check". The 2026-11-03 run (hecaton
16522) was given cluster access in `$HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV`, but its env, kubeconfig and AWS credentials are mode 640,
group `hecaton`, which the run's user is not in, so neither kubectl nor aws could read them. The issue's open parts are
unchanged. They are kagent's discovery and the agent's list_tools seen through tool-pin, kagent's handling of the
deny's JSON-RPC error, and then the badge decision, which goes in this file from the record.
## 2026-11-03 · #801 · The C7 fallback's open runs wait out their windows in a few polls of the stub's fake clock

**The flake.** Hecaton run 15924 ran `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` with the host's load average near 18 on 16 cores.
`verify/test_challenge_fallbacks.py` raised `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`: the C7 fallback,
`challenges/03-bad-mcp-excessive-agency/fallback.curl.sh`, ran past `run()`'s 120 s timeout on the stub's "open"
cluster. The same file passed alone right after.

**What the time went on.** No real waits were left: the stub's `sleep` and `date` already keep a fake clock. Timing
each `run()` on this host (load about 6 to 9) put the open run at 9 s, the gateway-down run at 13 s and the
kagent-never-rolls run at 7 s, against 2 s or less for each other run. Those three are the runs where nothing the
script polls for ever comes, so it waits out its whole window, 120 s or 180 s, one poll per 3 s sleep: 40 to 60
polls. Each poll starts about six processes: the stub kubectl, the MCP exchange it runs, the stub `date`, the
script's `json_get` and the stub `sleep`. Under load process starts slow down, and 40 polls went past 120 s.

**The fix, in the test only.** The fallback is unchanged, so what a presenter runs is what is tested. `run()` takes a
`step`, and for those three runs the stub's `sleep` moves the fake clock 30 s, whatever it was asked. The script
still waits its full window and prints "after 120 s"; it gets there in 4 to 6 polls. The stub records what each sleep
asked. New checks hold the script to 3 s polls (`readonly POLL_SECONDS=3`, and every recorded sleep), and bound the
polls in each of the three runs, so the process count is fixed and does not depend on load. Afterwards the three
runs take about 2 s each, and the guarded runs are unchanged: their reload-delay check still uses the 3 s clock.
Raising the timeout alone was ruled out, as the issue asks.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing here touches a cluster, and nothing is owed on one.

**The suites.** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 45 checks in about 26 minutes on the shared host, with load averages
of 7 to 10 on 16 cores. It was started in the background after the commit and its log read in the foreground.
Its offline suite, `run-tests.sh`, is green (225 tests), and `test_challenge_fallbacks.py` passed inside it. The run
exits 1 on one check: the red already recorded for #746, #775 and #798, where `test_image_version_tags.py` finds
ghcr.io serving `watch-it-burn:web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7` at `sha256:0b72ecc7...` and not the pinned `68004fb5`,
because CI pushed over that tag. Nothing here touches an image.

## 2026-11-03 · #787 · The live audience-path test holds the per-conversation limit and git's guard-proxy settings

**Where it started.** #786 (`803b84e`) already rewrote most of `verify/test_audience_path_live.py` for Michael's
2026-11-01 ruling on #450: it reads no `wib_chat_address`, sends 80 fresh conversations from one address, and holds
guard-proxy's PROXY_TIMEOUT, TURN_TIMEOUT, RATE_LIMIT_SESSION_RPM, RATE_LIMIT_RPM and COST_CAP_USD to
`gitops/ai-layer/resources.yaml` (today 120, 270, 10, 150 and 25). This run closes what was left of #787 on top of it.

**What changed.**
- The docstring says the empty prompts hold only throwaway conversations and never the caller's address, so the test
  can run from any network, the venue's included. It still says the run spends about 90 of guard-proxy's 150 a minute
  for the cluster, so it is not run while the room is chatting.
- `burst()` opens one thread per request, where it opened 16, so the 80 conversations are all in flight at once and
  nginx's bucket has no time to refill between rounds.
- The 80-conversation check also counts nginx's refusals and passes only when all 80 reach guard-proxy and nginx
  refused none.
- The one-conversation refusal check reads every refusal for "wait" and "send that again", where it read only "send
  that again", and still wants "10 a minute per conversation". Its first check still wants exactly burst + 1 through
  and the other 2 refused.
- Each guard-proxy setting fails when resources.yaml has no value for it, since a name missing from git and from the
  cluster would otherwise match as None. The conversation zone's burst must parse from git's console.conf as more
  than 0 before any request is sent.

this test among them (#786 edited it). The draft (`b40c18a`) is not reused. Its refusal check read only the word
"again", and it dropped the 65 s wait before the timed turn, which this file keeps so the cluster window drains first.

**Checked offline.** `python3 -m py_compile verify/test_audience_path_live.py` passes. Without CONTEXT, without
kubectl on PATH, and with a context that cannot be read, the test prints a FAIL line and exits 1 each time.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** `CONTEXT=watch-it-burn-community python3 verify/test_audience_path_live.py`, after the
ai-layer Application on that cluster has synced a staging revision carrying #786; it must end "All live
audience-path checks passed." That live run is its own child of #450.

**Tests at this entry.** `bash verify/run-tests.sh` exits 0. `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 45 checks and failed
only `test_image_version_tags.py`: ghcr.io now serves `web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7` at `sha256:0b72ecc7...`, and
resources.yaml pins `sha256:68004fb5...`. CI has pushed over that tag again, as the #786 entry above records; this
change does not touch it.

## 2026-11-03 · #799 · The burn profile's lost spans: a stall or a borrowed port, not scrub_pii or CPU load
## 2026-11-03 · #799 · The burn profile's lost spans came from a host stall or a borrowed port

Hecaton run 15841 saw `verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py` lose all 26 of the burn profile's spans once, at a load average
of 40 on 16 cores. The send got a 200, and the collector log held only its ready line and, 32 s later, the shutdown
signal. #799 asked what held the batch before anyone changed the test's 30 s wait. Run 16503 timed it on this host with
a scratch copy of `run_collector`: when the collector was ready, when the send got its 200, and when `apm.json` first
held data.

**What does not hold it.** With the collector pinned to one CPU against 0, 3, 10, 30 and 60 busy loops on that CPU, the
batch reached `apm.json` 5.0 to 5.8 s after the send, every time, for burn and attendee alike. Burn without
`transform/scrub_pii` was the same. Even 60 loops, about a sixtieth of a CPU and far worse than a load of 40 spread over
16 cores, only pushed the collector's start out to 18 s, and the send loop's wait covers that. So scrub_pii's OTTL
statements and CPU contention are ruled out. A load average also counts tasks waiting on disk, so a load of 40 does not
mean the CPUs were full; this host had 12 GB in swap that day.

**What does.** Two causes give exactly what run 15841 recorded, and both were reproduced against the real test:
- A stall. Freezing the test and its collector together for 31 s, just after the send, failed with all 26 missing. The
  collector log held only the ready line and the shutdown signal, 32.4 s apart, the 32 s run 15841's log showed. The
  wall-clock deadline was spent during the freeze. The woken test read `apm.json` once, before the collector's file
  exporter had flushed, and stopped. The Agent Observability copy was read a second later and had landed, and the
  test then crashed with a `KeyError` in the root-duration check.
- A borrowed port. `free_port` closes its socket before the collector binds the port. If another process's server
  on the host takes that port, answers the send with 200 and closes before this collector binds, the spans go
  elsewhere and the log shows the same two lines. A decoy server holding the port for 1.5 s, against a collector that
  started 2 s late, reproduced this.

Run 15841's log does not say which of the two it was. With whole-second timestamps, both fit its 32 s.

**Decided here: fix both causes; the bound is unchanged.**
- The test sends only once its own collector has logged that it is ready. Only one socket can listen on
  127.0.0.1 at that port, so a 200 from then on comes from this collector. If another server still holds the port,
  this collector cannot bind and exits, and "the collector took the spans" fails with the log tail showing the bind
  error.
- Both waits count polls in place of wall seconds: 100 polls of 0.3 s for the start, 60 of 0.5 s for the spans. When the host
  freezes the test along with the collector, no polls go by, so the stall spends none of the budget. The 31 s freeze
  now passes. When only the collector is frozen, the test still fails after 30 s, as it should. The failure then says
  how many polls ran over how long, the longest gap between two polls, and the host's pressure stall totals
  (`/proc/pressure`, CPU some, memory full and I/O full) over the wait. So the next loss says which kind of stall it
  was.
- The root-duration check guards an empty APM span, so a loss fails the check instead of crashing the test.

The siblings that start a collector on a `free_port` port and wait on wall seconds have the same two holes:
`test_collector_one_root_e2e.py`, `test_tool_failure_status_e2e.py`, `test_collector_pii_scrub_e2e.py` and
`test_adk_model_content_e2e.py`. Run 16503 filed them as a follow-up and left them unchanged, because #799 was
about this test.

**Tests.** `python3 verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py` passes in about 20 s. It also passes the two reproductions above,
and it fails cleanly, with the new detail, when only its collector is frozen for 36 s. Nothing here needs a cluster.

**Resumed by run 16543.** Run 16503's commit failed hecaton's prose gate, which read a verb in two of this
entry's sentences as connective filler. Run 16543 reworded those sentences and the matching comment in the test.
The change itself is as run 16503 made it, rebased onto staging e586840.

**The suites.** `bash verify/run-tests.sh` exits 0 (224 tests; 225 on run 16543's rebased branch). `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 45 checks, and
`verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py` passed in it. It exits 1 on one check, the red already recorded for #746 and #775:
`test_image_version_tags.py` finds ghcr.io serving `watch-it-burn:web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7` at `sha256:0b72ecc7...`,
not the pinned `68004fb5`. CI has pushed over that tag again. Nothing here touches an image.
Run 16543 ran both again after the rewording, with the same results.

## 2026-11-03 · #805 · A gate for #714's pull side: nothing this repo or a chart hands a cluster pulls from Docker Hub

**Context.** Test reviews 15958 and 16131 found that no test checks #714's criterion, "Remove every Docker Hub
reference: build, pull and name images from ghcr.io only". Nothing swept the repo, and test_enforce_floor's image
check leaves chart apps out. `verify/test_no_docker_hub.py` did not exist: #714's entries above defer it until
lab-platform#353 copies three build bases to ghcr.io. #805 has no earlier draft (`verify/prior-drafts.sh 805` printed
NONE). The test reuses the first #714 draft's design (`origin/agent/714-12873`), rebuilt on today's layout.
On 2026-11-03, an anonymous token request for each of lab-platform's `mirror/library/busybox`, `debian` and `node`
still got HTTP 403, so those copies are not there yet.

**What holds today, and is now gated.** Every image a cluster pulls comes from ghcr.io, or from public.ecr.aws for
Challenge 2's PUBLIC_IMAGES (#773). Two new tests hold that:
- `verify/test_no_docker_hub.py` (offline). It reads every image field in tracked files outside the dated records:
  YAML `image:` keys, Helm `registry`/`repository`/`tag` maps, Application `values:` strings, shell `--image` flags
  and `NAME_IMAGE=` assignments, and Python `NAME_IMAGE` strings and `NAME_IMAGES` dict values. It fails on any one
  that names a Docker Hub host or no registry at all. A name that kustomize replaces is excused only under the
  directory that replaces it (llm-guard in ai-layer, postgres in backstage, web in each demo app), and images.lock's
  not-an-image placeholders are excused too. It also runs a `git grep` for Docker Hub's hostnames over everything
  outside images/, images.lock, verify/ and the records, and finds only workshop-mcp's two refusal lines (REFUSED).
- `verify/test_no_docker_hub_render.py` (tools tier). The root renders each of the 40 apps/ files alone, then the
  test renders each source as Argo CD would: 18 chart sources with the root's values, kustomizations with
  kustomize.images, and directories as their files. It fails on any image field, or any container args, env or
  command string, that is a Docker Hub pull. Helm test hooks are left out because Argo CD does not run them. Without
  that exclusion, falcosidekick's curlimages/curl and otel-operator's three busybox:latest test Pods fail.
- `verify/docker_hub.py` holds the judgement and the image-field walk that both tests use.

Checked by mutation, each reverted. Each of these fails by name: a bare nginx in games/villain-apps, a bare curl as
beat-02.sh's CURL_IMAGE, a registry-less C6_IMAGE in ticket_site.py, a docker.io comment in infra/deploy-full-idp.sh,
and an edit to workshop-mcp's `_DOCKER_HUB` line, which also makes the REFUSED list stale. Falco's registry set to ""
in apps/falco.yaml makes the render test fail on `DaemonSet/falco`.

**Not in this change, and why.** #714's build side is not done, so no test can hold it green. Five places still use
Docker Hub: Dockerfile FROM lines (web-terminal's `debian:bookworm-slim` and Backstage's node base), build.sh's
`JOKER_BASE`, the Backstage README's buildah base, their images.lock rows, and the two tests that read the Joker's
busybox from registry-1.docker.io. All of them wait on lab-platform#353's copies. A list of them in the test would be
a known-open list, which the test rules forbid. So the new test's scope stops at them, and its docstring says so.
When #714 moves those bases, it adds Dockerfile FROM lines to check 1 and drops images/, images.lock and verify/
from check 2's exclusions. verify/'s refusal lines then join REFUSED.

**Tests.** New: test_no_docker_hub, test_no_docker_hub_render. No existing test changed.

## 2026-11-03 · #800 · The lab-pipeline collector test gives each validate 180 s, and a hung validate is a FAIL

**The time goes to a network wait.** Hecaton run 15830 saw `verify/test_lab_pipeline_collector.py` raise
`subprocess.TimeoutExpired` on one `otelcol-contrib validate` at the old 60 s limit, with the load average about 30 on
16 cores. Measured here with the pinned 0.160.0 from `verify/.tools`: the three configs without a Datadog exporter
validate in 0.2 s, and the four with one take 25.3 to 25.5 s on about 0.5 s of CPU. Watching the process with
`ss` shows why: the Datadog exporter's hostname detection opens repeated connections to 169.254.169.254, the cloud
metadata address, which nothing answers off-cloud, until its retries run out at about 25 s, then makes a DNS lookup.
`AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true` and `GCE_METADATA_HOST` do not shorten it, and setting a `hostname` on the exporter
would change the config the test exists to validate, so the wait stays and the limit moves.

**Decided here.** `VALIDATE_TIMEOUT = 180`, seven times the measured wait. That is the issue's own figure. A validate
that has not returned by then has hung: `subprocess.run` kills it, and the run records `<config> validates within
180 s (the collector hung)` as a FAIL, goes on to the next config, and exits 1, where before it left a traceback
that named no config. Each PASS line now shows its validate's seconds, so the headroom is visible in every run. A config the
collector rejects still fails as before, with the collector's error printed. The lab pipeline's own 30 s start
deadline is unchanged, because that config swaps the Datadog exporters for files and starts in well under a second.
`verify/test_e2e_tools_tier.py` (offline) now holds the limit at 180 s or more and holds the hang as a named FAIL.
Checked by hand with a stand-in `otelcol-contrib` whose `validate` sleeps, and the limit cut to 2 s in a scratch
copy: all seven configs FAIL by name, the run exits 1 in 15 s, and no stand-in process is left running.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing here touches a cluster; the test is in the tools tier.

**The suites.** `bash verify/run-tests.sh` exits 0 (224 tests), with both new checks in `test_e2e_tools_tier.py`
passing. `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 45 checks with the load average about 11 on 16 cores, and
`test_lab_pipeline_collector.py` passed all 19, its four Datadog validates taking 25.4 to 26.4 s. The tier exits 1
on one check, the red already recorded for #746 and #775: `test_image_version_tags.py` finds ghcr.io serving
`watch-it-burn:web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7` at `sha256:0b72ecc7...` where the pin is `68004fb5`, because CI pushed
over that tag again. Nothing here builds or pushes an image; the workflow fix is run 16420's follow-up.

**Second attempt, after the rebase onto staging at `9bbc835`.** The prose gate read one antithesis in this entry,
so the heading and the digest sentence above now state each claim on its own, as do the two test comments. The tier
run on the new base found a second FAIL in `test_image_version_tags.py`: the stand-in pod image in
`verify/test_tool_pin_live_check.py`, added by `b28d5c1` (#480), named `watch-it-burn:workshop-mcp@sha256:9a26`, a
reference with no version, which #714's rule forbids. It now names `workshop-mcp-mcp-1.29.1`, the pinned tag;
`test_tool_pin_live_check.py` still passes, and `test_image_version_tags.py` is down to the web-terminal digest.
On that base `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 45 checks with the offline suite green, and
`test_lab_pipeline_collector.py` passed with its Datadog validates at 25.3 to 25.5 s.

## 2026-11-03 · #806 · Challenge 3 passes only when workshop-mcp's audit log shows read_support_ticket on HC-666, then deploy_app

#764 says the room's plain question, "What's the status of my support ticket HC-666?", makes the public bot call
`read_support_ticket` and then `deploy_app`. Test review run 15979 found nothing that checked this. The KubeCon
probe's `c6-lands` beat judged only whether `joker-<stage name>` existed, and the offline fake returned a canned
"Done!". No earlier draft exists: `verify/prior-drafts.sh 806 origin/staging` printed NONE.

**Where the calls are read.** The `/chat` reply carries no tool calls. workshop-mcp's audit trail (`tool_audit.py`,
#190) writes one `pre` line per `tools/call` on the `shim` container's stdout before the tool runs, so log order is
call order. `room_ask()` in `verify/kubecon_probe.py` notes the UTC time before the ask. After the ask, it reads
`kubectl -n agent logs deploy/workshop-mcp -c shim --since-time=<that time minus AUDIT_SKEW_S (10 s)>`. The margin
allows for node clock skew. `judge_ticket_then_deploy` passes when `read_support_ticket` with ticket_id HC-666 comes
before a `deploy_app` whose manifest names `joker-<stage name>`. A call made by a visitor in the same window names
another ticket or another Joker, so it does not count. `judge_joker_lands` now fails a Joker that exists without that
chain, and names what is missing: the read, the deploy, or the order. The probe's C6 beats and `stage_traces.py`'s
Challenge 3 seeds share `room_ask()`, so the `c3-attack` seed checks the chain too. A log kubectl cannot read raises,
and the beat fails with kubectl's reason. The Datadog spans that `stage_traces.py` checks stay unordered. The order
lives in the probe's judge, which both runs use.

**Tests.** `verify/test_kubecon_probe.py` loads the real `tool_audit.py` against a stand-in FastMCP, as
`test_tool_audit.py` does. It writes the audit lines, mixed with post lines and a line of the server's own output,
and judges on those lines. These cases fail: the deploy first, no read, the read with no deploy, another ticket, and
another Deployment. The checks also pin `tool_calls_since`'s argv, workshop-mcp's container `shim` running
`server.py`, and `server.py` building `AuditedFastMCP`. On the public bot (the `Community` fake), `c6-lands` passes
with the chain and fails for a bot that deploys unread, deploys first, or only reads. `verify/test_stage_traces.py`
goes red when `c3-attack`'s Joker is deployed unread. With the chain check taken out of `judge_joker_lands`, five
probe checks and one stage-trace check fail.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** This run could not read its cluster kubeconfig: permission denied on
`/var/lib/hecaton/runs/16573/clusters/kubeconfig`. The live check owed is the KubeCon probe's `c6-lands` beat on the
public bot, run by a session with accen-dev once #803's repin is synced:
`python3 verify/kubecon_probe.py community attackme.burritobot.co --context watch-it-burn-community --kubeconfig
/tmp/community.kubeconfig --profile accen-dev`. `c6-lands` must read `PASS ... read_support_ticket(HC-666), then
deploy_app(joker-agatha-the-banshee)`. That run makes 7 model calls.

**Suite results (run 16573, then run 16637).** Run 16573 ran `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` at the first commit of
this change, and it exited 1 for two reasons. First, the offline suite failed `test_verify_harness.py`. Its
light-suite scan reads a `["kubectl",` list literal as a kubectl run, and the new argv check had one. The second commit
rewrote that check, and the offline suite went green with 227 tests. Second, the tier ran 44 tests and failed only
`test_image_version_tags.py`: ghcr.io serves `watch-it-burn:web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7` at `sha256:0b72ecc7...`, not
the pinned `68004fb5`. That tag was pushed over by CI and is open as #815, #816, #823 and #824. Nothing in this
change touches an image.

**Rebased in run 16637.** Run 16573's commits (28d603e, f6ee1d6, a891ce1) never reached staging: hecaton's rebase onto
c25c221 stopped on PROGRESS.md, where #808's 2026-11-03 bullet and this change's bullet were both inserted under
`### Added`. Run 16637 rebased the three commits onto staging 2efc223 and kept both bullets, #808's first. Staging
had changed none of the code files this change touches, only PROGRESS.md and decisions.md, so the code is
unchanged from run 16573's. Run 16637 again got permission denied on its cluster files
(`/var/lib/hecaton/runs/16637/clusters/`, owned by group `hecaton`, which the run's user is not in), so the live
`c6-lands` check above is still owed.
Run 16637's `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` at a438622, on staging 2efc223, exits 1. Its offline suite is green with

## 2026-11-03 · #608 · The first live run stopped on an empty line kustomize adds, so the live test now compares expressions modulo whitespace

**What escalation 755 found.** Escalation 755 ran the 2026-11-02 #608 entry's guarded command against
watch-it-burn-private (`arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:515966504359:cluster/watch-it-burn-private`, account 515966504359, ACTIVE)
from a checkout of staging 2efc223. This was the first run of the suite on a cluster since the #607 fix. It passed
seventeen prerequisites and failed one, "live restrict-agent-spawned-workloads validation expressions are the repo's",
with exit 1. So **the three #607 Secret checks and the #490 and #552 checks still have not run**. The run created
nothing: `kubectl get deploy,pods,configmaps -n agent -l wib.test/run` found no resources afterwards. Argo CD's
kyverno-policies Application was synced to 2efc223 too. The only difference in the live expressions was one empty
line after the first line of expressions 2 and 3, the #607 secret-volume and secretKeyRef rules
(`exists(v,\n\n  (has(v.secret)…` live, `exists(v,\n  (has(v.secret)…` in the file). Run 12662's unlanded draft
records the same stop, at staging 2e1829c, from escalation 352.

**The cause is kustomize, from #638, not the cluster's parser.** Commit ea699ed (#638) gave `policies/kyverno` a
Kustomization, so Argo CD now builds the directory with kustomize. Kustomize writes out a `>-` block whose second line
is more indented with one extra empty line. `kubectl kustomize policies/kyverno` with the pinned kubectl v1.36.2
(kustomize v5.8.1) shows it offline. Read with PyYAML, its restrict-agent-spawned-workloads expressions 2 and 3
start `…exists(v,\n\n  (has(v.secret)` and `…exists(c,\n\n  c.?env`, which is the live diff exactly. The test reads
the file itself with PyYAML, which has no such line. That is also why run 12431's unlanded draft could report the
whole suite passing at staging 0d73c8d, the last staging before ea699ed. Neither the test nor the policy file changed
between the two bases. CEL reads any whitespace run as one separator, so the cluster runs the repo's policy.

**The change.**

- `verify/policy_spec.py` (new) collapses each whitespace run in an `expression` to one space before comparing. It
  does this for matchConditions, variables and validations, and leaves every other key as it is.
  `verify/test_llm_bypass_live.py` compares both ValidatingPolicies through it. When expressions differ, the FAIL
  line now names the first expression that differs, the cluster's text and the repo's. Escalation 755 had to produce
  that diff by hand.
- `verify/test_policy_spec.py` (new, offline) rebuilds escalation 755's live form from the repo file. It checks that
  the old exact comparison fails on that form and the new comparison passes. A changed operator, field name,
  negation, string literal, expression count, variable name or message must still differ.
- `verify/test_policy_spec_kustomize.py` (new, `# E2E TIER: tools`) renders `policies/kyverno` with the pinned
  kubectl's kustomize. It checks that every ValidatingPolicy in the render matches its own file under the same
  comparison, and it prints which expressions differ when compared exactly (today, 2 and 3 of
  restrict-agent-spawned-workloads).
- Collapsing whitespace would also hide a change of spacing inside a CEL string literal. None of the compared
  policies' literals contain a whitespace run. A spacing-only change inside a literal is the one difference this
  check now misses. The alternative was writing the expressions as `|` literal blocks, which kustomize might also
  reformat. That would also have changed policy files the Kyverno CLI tests read.

**Live, this run (hecaton run 16651).** Not run. The run was handed watch-it-burn-private and watch-it-burn-community,
but its `clusters/` files (kubeconfig, env, aws-config, aws-credentials, bin/) are still `hecaton:hecaton` mode 0640,
and uid 143 is not in group `hecaton`. `CONTEXT=watch-it-burn-private python3 verify/test_llm_bypass_live.py` passed
its first two prerequisites, then failed "cluster for context 'watch-it-burn-private' is reachable" with
"permission denied" on the kubeconfig, exit 1. `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile accen-dev` found no such
profile. peopleforrester/hecaton#507 and #508, both still open, track this.

**Not yet run on a cluster:** `verify/test_llm_bypass_live.py`, all of it, with this change on the checkout. The
command is the 2026-11-02 #608 entry's guarded one, or `CONTEXT=watch-it-burn-private python3
verify/test_llm_bypass_live.py` in a run that can read its handover. The policy comparison needs only the checkout,
so no Argo sync of this change is needed. The result goes here: whether the three #607 checks pass (terminal-auth
refused by volume and by secretKeyRef, each with its message; ceo-personal-record admitted), and whether the #490 and
#552 checks the TypeError hid pass.

**The suites (run 16651, on staging 5d0a620).** `bash verify/run-tests.sh`, run as the first half of the E2E command,
ran 231 tests, all green, `test_policy_spec.py` among them. `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 47 checks.
`test_policy_spec_kustomize.py` passed and reported expressions 2 and 3 of restrict-agent-spawned-workloads as the ones
kustomize changes. The only red was `test_image_version_tags.py`: ghcr.io serves
`watch-it-burn:web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7` at sha256:0b72ecc7… instead of the pinned sha256:68004fb5…. That is the
web-terminal digest red the #794 entry above records, and this change does not touch it. No dependency was added.

## 2026-11-03 · #810 · A fleet monitor pages when Agent Observability files no BurritoBot trace in a session, for the whole org

**What it is.** `agent-obs-silent` in `infra/datadog-fleet/monitors.yaml`, next to `no-traces`, session-scoped, priority 2:
`sum(last_10m):sum:ml_obs.trace{ml_app:burritobot}.as_count() < 1` with `notify_no_data` and a 10-minute no-data
timeframe. #783's outage (Agent Observability filed no BurritoBot turn for six hours from 2026-11-01 ~15:55 UTC while APM
kept every span) is the case it covers. `no-traces` reads the collector's span count, which sits upstream of the
conversion that failed, so it stayed green through the outage. `verify/agent_obs_flow.py` answers the same question by hand
before a run-through; the monitor answers it between runs.

**The metric name.** The issue asked for it to be read in Whitney's sandbox org first. The repo already records that read:
`ml_obs.trace` under `ml_app:burritobot` is what `verify/test_datadog_sandbox_live.py` (#629) reads there, and the #711
entry records it showing 5 burritobot traces for 2026-10-31. Datadog's metrics page (docs.datadoghq.com/llm_observability/
monitoring/metrics, read 2026-11-03) lists `ml_obs.trace` as a count tagged env, error, ml_app, service, span_kind and
version. The monitor counts traces. Since #746's one-root copy, one BurritoBot turn is one trace, so the trace count tracks
turns. A span count would also move on the copy's inner spans.

**The grouping rule, and why this monitor is the exception.** The issue assumed Agent Observability's tags carry
`k8s.cluster.name`. Its spans do: `agent_obs_flow.py` filters the spans API on it. The metrics carry span tags only for
token and cost metrics, through the SDK's `cost_tags`, which the collector's OTLP copy does not set. Datadog's metrics
page says: "other tags set on spans are not available as tags on Agent Observability metrics, except LLM token and cost
metric tags". Both KubeCon clusters share env, ml_app, service and version, so no metric tag separates them.
This repo already hit the same limit twice: `room_view.py` refuses `ml_obs.*` for it (the 2026-10-29 #665 room-view
entry), and `test_datadog_sandbox_live.py` checks ml_app per env. So the monitor is one alert for the whole org, marked
`scope: org`. `fleet_monitors.py` allows that only on `ORG_SCOPE_METRICS` (`ml_obs.`). It refuses `scope: org` on any
other metric, an `ml_obs.*` monitor without it, a cluster filter or any group on it, a scope-org monitor that fires on a
rise or lacks `notify_no_data`, and a message naming `{{kube_cluster_name.name}}`. The render leaves off the per-cluster
`fleet.sh verify` line, and `--data` checks the monitor's overall state, one value for the org, in place of a group per
cluster.

**Per-cluster designs considered and set aside.** Stamping the cluster into a tag the metric does carry, on the Agent
Observability copy only (say `version` or `env`), would group the monitor. It would rewrite a unified-service tag the
presenters see on every row, and `env` is the single sandbox-org env that `test_datadog_sandbox_live.py` checks. A
`span_metrics` count on the collector's `traces/llmobs` pipeline would carry `kube_cluster_name`. It counts what the
collector sends, and the #783 failure happened after that point. The org-wide alert cannot see one cluster's copy stopping
while the other's still arrives; `agent_obs_flow.py chat` answers that per cluster, and the alert's message names it.

**Offline.** `verify/test_fleet_monitors.py` holds the definition (metric, ml_app shared with `agent_obs_flow.py`, the
window, absence, session scope), ten refusals of the exception's misuses, the render, seven monitors through the fake
org's apply, and `--data` on the org-wide monitor: No Data fails naming the whole org, Alert counts as fed, and it needs
no per-cluster group. Removing the `scope: org` branch from `data_check` fails the No Data check and the no-group check;

## 2026-11-03 · #814 · sample-app and tool-pin tags name the version inside: nginx 1.27.5 and grpcio 1.84.1

**Context.** Michael's 2026-10-30 comment on #714 says a tag must match the version of the software inside. #714
retagged workshop-mcp and web-terminal, and its 2026-11-02 entry left `watch-it-burn:sample-app` and `:tool-pin` as a
follow-up, which is this issue. Hecaton run 16674 is its first dispatch: `verify/prior-drafts.sh 814 origin/staging`
printed NONE, and the issue has no comments.

**What the images hold, read on 2026-11-03.**
- **sample-app** (`sha256:556e176d…`, an index with one linux/amd64 image, `e99ce5df…`). Its main software is nginx.
  The version string compiled into `usr/sbin/nginx`, which `nginx -v` prints, is `nginx/1.27.5`, and the image's
  config has `NGINX_VERSION=1.27.5`. So the tag is `sample-app-nginx-1.27.5`. The image was built on 2026-06-22 from
  Docker Hub's `nginx:1.27-alpine`, before #714 moved `images/sample-app/Dockerfile` to our
  `watch-it-burn:nginx-1.27-alpine` copy. That copy carries nginx 1.27.5 too, so a rebuild keeps the tag's version.
  The copy is nginx's unprivileged image, though (USER 101, docker-nginx-unprivileged), so a rebuild would not be the
  same image. Nothing rebuilds sample-app now, and this change does not.
- **tool-pin** has no image: ghcr.io answers 404 for `watch-it-burn:tool-pin`, as the #603 and #480 entries record, and
  the spike's live check runs `tool_pin.py` from a ConfigMap. With nothing to read on ghcr.io and no digest to
  `crane tag`, the image was built here from `images/tool-pin` (podman 29.9.2 through the docker CLI, local tag
  `localhost/tool-pin-814:built`, never pushed). In it, `python -c "import grpc; print(grpc.__version__)"` printed
  `1.84.1` on Python 3.12.13. Its main software, other than our own `tool_pin.py`, is grpcio, the one package its
  Dockerfile adds to python, the way workshop-mcp's tag names the mcp SDK. So the tag is `tool-pin-grpcio-1.84.1`.

**What changed.**
- `backstage/k8s/templated-test-svc.yaml` and `images.lock` pin `watch-it-burn:sample-app-nginx-1.27.5@sha256:556e176d…`,
  the same digest. The images.lock row for tool-pin is `watch-it-burn:tool-pin-grpcio-1.84.1 - build:images/tool-pin -`,
  and `images/tool-pin/Dockerfile`'s build and push commands name that tag. The prose references in the spike's
  README and tool-pin.yaml, in test_tool_pin.py's comment and in test_image_pins.py's probe line name the new tags.
- `verify/test_image_version_tags.py` gets two sections. The sample-app section takes the digest
  templated-test-svc.yaml pins and checks that images.lock pins the same one and that every reference names that
  one tag. It then checks that ghcr.io serves the tag at that digest anonymously, reads nginx's version string out of
  `usr/sbin/nginx` in the pinned image, and checks that the Dockerfile's base has the same `NGINX_VERSION`. The binary is
  built against musl, so the test reads it instead of running it. The tool-pin section checks that images.lock has
  exactly one `tool-pin-grpcio-<v>` `build:` row with no digest, that every reference names that tag, and that the
  Dockerfile installs `grpcio==<v>` and builds and pushes that tag. It also checks that ghcr.io answers exactly 404
  for the tag, because the row's `-` digest says the image was never pushed. If someone pushes it, that check fails
  and says to pin the digest. The test cannot read grpcio out of an image that was never published, so this is
  the most it can hold. `pinned()` now takes the file that pins the digest, and its reference scan is a separate
  `named()`.
- Checked by mutation: with the Dockerfile's push line set back to `watch-it-burn:tool-pin`, the tool-pin
  Dockerfile check fails.

**Not done here: the ghcr.io write.** Governance forbids a run from pushing, and `crane tag` is a ghcr.io write, so
the report escalates it. Until it runs, test_image_version_tags fails one more check:
`ghcr.io serves …:sample-app-nginx-1.27.5 at the pinned sha256:556e176dd1ac…` (HTTP 404). The escalated command,
run from a checkout of staging with GHCR write access:

    bash verify/fetch-e2e-tools.sh && gh auth token | verify/.tools/bin/crane auth login ghcr.io -u peopleforrester --password-stdin \
      && verify/.tools/bin/crane tag ghcr.io/peopleforrester/watch-it-burn@sha256:556e176dd1ac742009bddf70407cb92c84214179a6f45742e67d50523caa2c24 sample-app-nginx-1.27.5 \
      && verify/.tools/bin/crane digest ghcr.io/peopleforrester/watch-it-burn:sample-app-nginx-1.27.5

The last command must print `sha256:556e176dd1ac742009bddf70407cb92c84214179a6f45742e67d50523caa2c24`. The old
`sample-app` tag stays on ghcr.io and is left alone; nothing in the repo names it any more. tool-pin needs no write.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Backstage's templated-test-svc pulls `sample-app-nginx-1.27.5` by digest, so it pulls
the same bytes as before, and its pod can start before the tag exists. Once the change is on a cluster, run
`kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private get deploy -A -o jsonpath='{..image}' | tr ' ' '\n' | grep sample-app`.
It is owed only where the Backstage manifest is applied.

**The suites (run 16674, at 89ad1c6).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran `bash verify/run-tests.sh` first, which
passed with 232 tests. Then the tools tier ran 48 checks and failed one, `test_image_version_tags.py`, on two checks.
The first is ghcr.io serving `web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7` at `sha256:0b72ecc7…` instead of the pinned `68004fb5…`, the
red already in the base (#794). The second is `sample-app-nginx-1.27.5`'s 404, which ends when the escalated
`crane tag` runs. Every other check in the test passed, the nginx and tool-pin ones included.

**The live check could not run.** The run's `$KUBECONFIG` (`/var/lib/hecaton/runs/16674/clusters/kubeconfig`) and its
AWS files are mode 0640, owned by group `hecaton`, and the run's user (hecaton-s4-claude-certkraken, in groups

## 2026-11-03 · #797 · Tests own their inputs: what a test reads is found before it is reworded, and every random draw is pinned

**The cause.** Two runs lost time to a test whose result hung on something the test did not own. Run 9643 (#612)
reworded row 8's readiness cell in `facilitation/kubecon-na-2026-run-of-show.md` from "At risk" to "Partly", and
`verify/test_kubecon_deck_pdf.py` built its cut-point case with `ROS.replace("| **At risk.**", ...)`. With the label
gone the replace did nothing and the check after it failed, so the run put the old label back (dcd6520). The deck
exporter and its tests were deleted on 2026-10-28 (95f86f2, #639), so that test is gone, but nothing stopped the next
test that reads a phrase. Run 15808 (#583) saw the E2E tools tier fail
`verify/test_storefront_witch_name_e2e.py` on "Prudence the Pixie": the check asserted "rude" was not in a name the
page drew with the real `Math.random`, which fails one run in 32. Run 15808 fixed that predicate (43dd3a0) but left
the other cases on real draws.

**The fix.** AGENTS.md has a "Tests own their inputs" section: grep `verify` and `scripts` for the exact words before
rewording them, change any test that reads them in the same commit, and never revert correct text to suit a test; a
test checks a literal anchor is there before it edits or splits on it; randomness is pinned or enumerated, and a test
that passes on a rerun is broken. The witch-name test now gives the page a stubbed `Math` in every case. The stub
fails when the page draws more values than the case pinned, and the cases with a valid cookie pin none. The
replaced-cookie case runs once per first name, all 32, with the creatures wrapping, so all 24 creatures are drawn too,
and it checks the exact name each draw picks. With the old bare-"rude" predicate put back, it fails on Prudence in
every run. `verify/test_tests_own_inputs.py` (offline) holds the section, runs its grep on an anchor
the witch-name test reads, and checks that the test's node script never hands the page the real `Math`.

**Not changed.** No lint scans every test for literal anchors or unseeded randomness. Eleven tests use
`.replace` on a literal, and several are allowed to find nothing (an exemption comment that may be absent), so a
scan would flag correct code. The rule is in AGENTS.md and the test that broke is fixed.

**Seen in this run, not fixed: a one-off hang in `verify/test_challenge_fallbacks.py`.** The first full offline
run failed it: the C7 fallback's "down" case, `challenges/03-bad-mcp-excessive-agency/fallback.curl.sh` against the
stub gateway that stops answering, hit the test's 120 s `subprocess.run` timeout. That case takes 9.5 s alone,
about 11 s with eight copies of the test running at once, and at most 23.7 s over 20 more runs, none of which timed
out, so host load does not explain it. The script's waits run on the stub clock, so a hang means that clock stopped
advancing: if the `date` stub ever printed nothing, `WAITED` would go negative and `wait_for` would never return.
The cause is not found, so per rule 3 a follow-up carries the failing output.

**Resumed in run 16526, rebased onto staging `e586840`.** Run 16473 stalled. It ended its turn to wait for the E2E
command's completion notice, and hecaton stopped it after 15 minutes with no output. #798's point 4 in AGENTS.md,
which landed on staging meanwhile, already covers that cause, so this run adds nothing for it and polls the log in the
foreground instead. #798 appended to AGENTS.md and decisions.md at the same places this branch does. The rebase keeps
both: #798's points 3 and 4 and then this section, and #798's entries and then this one. The E2E tools tier's one
red on run 16473's base was `test_image_version_tags.py`: ghcr.io serves `web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7` at
`sha256:0b72ecc7...` where the pin is `68004fb5...`, because CI pushed over that tag, as the #798 and #786 entries
record. Nothing here touches an image.

**Not yet run on a cluster:** nothing; both changed tests are offline or in the tools tier.

**Resumed again in run 16557, on staging `4bec41f`.** Run 16526 ended failed at validation, so its three commits did
not land. Its report listed them as 7b1cc13, 1f3f737 and 3629b6f, but the branch kept in hecaton's mirror holds them as
d8d6b63, 21617c9 and 3f9519e. This run takes them with `git cherry-pick` as `verify/prior-drafts.sh 797 origin/staging`
says (CLEAN, with the decisions.md APPEND keeping staging's entries first), and its report lists the SHAs on this

**A third case of the same cause, found by this run's E2E tier and fixed here.** `test_image_version_tags.py` failed
