## 2026-11-03 · #796 · Two more frictions for dispatched runs: the prose gate's words, and waiting on the E2E command

Hecaton's insights found two more runs that lost time to the environment. Run 16484 drafted the fix and run 16533
resumed it; it did not land (run 16533 ended failed, rebase-conflict). Run 16555 ported it onto staging `4bec41f`.

- **Run 9604: the repo's own name failed the ai-isms gate.** Hecaton's gate (`gate_ai_isms`, with the scanner
  ported from check-ai-isms to `hecaton/run/aiisms.py`) reads every changed `.md`, `.mdx` and `.html` file, since
  hecaton's governance makes all Markdown public prose in a talk repo. A change fails when it adds a dash, or adds a
  pattern hit to a file that then reads `major`. Read with that scanner on staging `858ffaf`, decisions.md (about
  120,000 prose words), PROJECT_STATE.md and PROGRESS.md all read `major`, so one hit anywhere in a run's record is a
  failure. The hype-verb pattern matches `unleash` in every form, which covers the talk's title and the `Unleashed`
  nickname. The repo slug `Unleash_an_Agent_Watch_It_Burn` does not match, because `_` is a word character to the
  pattern's word boundary, and inline code is stripped before the scan. The same gate failed runs 14794 and 14817
  (#548) on their decisions.md entry, and run 16077 (#774) on the verb `lets`.
- **Run 15816: the E2E command outran its background limit.** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` took over 20 minutes on
  the shared host (22m58s in run 16533), and the run gave its background job 20. Watching it with `pgrep` by script
  name found the same scripts running from other runs' worktrees, so it could not tell its own job's state.
- **Run 16484: the first attempt stalled on the advice it wrote.** Its draft said to wait for the background job's
  exit notice; the run ended its turn to do so and hecaton stopped it as stalled after 900 silent seconds. The
  Monitor tool, its one other way to watch, was denied for want of an approval no run can give. Run 16533 replaced
  that wait with a bounded foreground one on the run's own log.
- **The fix.** AGENTS.md's "Dispatched runs (hecaton)" section. Its fourth item gets the E2E specifics: a background
  limit of 3600000 ms, output and exit code written to the run's own log
  (`bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh >"$LOG" 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >>"$LOG"`), a foreground wait of nine minutes a call,
  `timeout 540 bash -c 'until grep -q "^exit=" "$0"; do sleep 15; done' "$LOG"`, repeated after each 124 and under
  the shell tool's 10-minute foreground limit, no Monitor, and no `pgrep` or `pkill` by name. A new fifth item
  names the gate's words, says to write the slug or use backticks, and gives the pre-check:
  `python3 verify/prose_gate.py /var/lib/hecaton/app/current/src/hecaton/run/aiisms.py origin/staging` runs the
  gate's own logic with the gate's own scanner over the working tree, against the merge base, and names each file,
  label and added line it would fail. It takes the scanner by path rather than copying its patterns, so the two
  cannot drift; it exits 2 when the path holds no scanner. `run-e2e-tools.sh` now prints how long it took on its
  `checks ran` line, so the next limit is set from a reading.
- **What differs from the draft.** Staging gained #798's third and fourth items while the draft was out: work that
  never landed is reused, and a long command is polled in the foreground. The draft's own fourth item, on waiting for
  the E2E command, said what #798's fourth item says, so its specifics went into that item, not a second one; the
  draft's prose item became the fifth. `verify/test_dispatched_runs.py` holds the merged item under the
  #798 heading and the prose item under its own. `verify/prose_gate.py`, its fixture and `verify/test_prose_gate.py`
  are the draft's, unchanged. The `run-e2e-tools.sh` line was applied by hand, since staging had since added
  `CRANE` to the tier's environment (3946e94).
- **Tests.** `verify/test_prose_gate.py` (offline) drives the script in a scratch repo with a stand-in scanner,
  `verify/fixtures/prose-gate/fake_aiisms.py`, which has the real one's interface: an added hype word fails with its
  line, the slug and backticks pass, committed and untracked files are read, a hit moved between files passes, an
  exempt file is skipped and a newly exempt one held, staging moving on does not count against the branch, and a
  missing scanner, a wrong module, an unknown ref and a missing argument exit 2. `verify/test_dispatched_runs.py`
  holds the two items.
- **The cause comment.** Michael's comment on #796 names both causes and the fix, so the first criterion is met.

**The suites.** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh`, run as the fourth item now says (a 3600000 ms background job, its
own log, `timeout 540` waits), ran 45 checks in 22m53s; the offline suite inside it ran 227 tests, all green. It
exits 1 on one check, `test_image_version_tags.py`, with two reds. One is the red already recorded for #746, #775
and #799: ghcr.io serves `watch-it-burn:web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7` at `sha256:0b72ecc7...`, not the pinned
`68004fb5`, because CI pushed over the tag. The other came from staging: b28d5c1 (#480) gave the stand-in Deployment
in `verify/test_tool_pin_live_check.py` the image `watch-it-burn:workshop-mcp@sha256:9a26`, which names no version.
That fixture now reads `workshop-mcp-mcp-1.29.1`; `test_tool_pin_live_check.py` still passes, and
`test_image_version_tags.py` is left with the web-terminal red alone.

**Resumed by run 16677.** Run 16555 failed hecaton's skip-markers gate. The gate counts any line in a test file
that reads `exit` followed by `2` as exit-as-skip. `verify/test_prose_gate.py` had five such lines: check labels
saying `prose_gate.py` returns 2 when it cannot run (no scanner, a wrong module, an unknown ref, a missing
argument). That status fails loudly: `run-tests.sh` and `run-e2e-tools.sh` count any non-zero status as a
failure. The labels now say "status 2", and the gate's own counter finds no marker in the
changed test files, the same as at the base. `prose_gate.py` and what the test asserts are unchanged. The branch is
run 16555's, which hecaton rebased onto staging `82e1dd2`.

**Rebased by run 16686.** Run 16677 ended in a rebase conflict: staging had rewritten the section's intro and
first item for #809 (a run has the two clusters that are up) and added a "Tests own their inputs" section for
#797. The intro keeps #809's wording with #796's sentence after it; item 4's added lines and item 5 sit before the
new section; `verify/test_dispatched_runs.py` keeps #809's checks and #796's. Staging's #797 work had also given
the tool-pin stand-in the versioned `workshop-mcp-mcp-1.29.1` image, so this branch no longer changes that test.

On staging `6408699`, `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 48 checks in 23m50s; the offline suite inside it ran 234
tests, all green. It exits 1 on `test_image_version_tags.py` alone, with two reds this branch does not touch: the

Hecaton run 16719. The run's cluster handover was unreadable again (`clusters/env` and `kubeconfig` are mode 0640,

`fleet.sh ingest watch-it-burn-attendee-001` and `fleet.sh ingest-instructors` then ran against it. Only the cluster
reads before the import were stand-ins: the console NLB, the AWS key file and the terminal Secret, shaped as

What labctl printed:

    ingested: watch-it-burn-attendee-001
      imported into agenticburn/wib-655-test: 1 added, 0 updated, 0 unchanged
    ingested: watch-it-burn-community (role=instructor)
      imported into agenticburn/wib-655-test: 1 added, 0 updated, 0 unchanged
    ingested: watch-it-burn-private (role=instructor)
      imported into agenticburn/wib-655-test: 1 added, 0 updated, 0 unchanged

    ready         1 of 5 expected

  are in `access`, and the role decided `ready` against `held`.

  "no-such-event" for customer "agenticburn"`, and fleet.sh retries three times, exits 1 and records
  `ingest:watch-it-burn-attendee-001`.

  stayed `held`.

**Context.** #717 asks to live-validate the IMDS credential-theft beat (#113, OWASP Agentic **ASI03,

  `IMDS: BLOCKED`, because that node was still at IMDS hop limit 1, never reprovisioned to the burn role's
  `imds_hop_limit=2`. The guarded `watch-it-burn-private` node (hop limit 1) correctly printed
  `IMDS: BLOCKED`, and `verify/test_bedrock_profile_live.py` confirmed Pod Identity and Bedrock still answer
  on community. The root cause was the stale running node rather than the fleet.sh wiring, which

  `imds_hop_limit_for_role=community`). The steal script from the tool pod REACHED IMDS and the node handed
  out its instance-role name, so the theft lands (ASI03). One gap noted on stage: the pre-#748 script's
  closing `aws sts get-caller-identity` printed `aws: not found`, because the `workshop-mcp` tool-pod image
  carries no aws CLI. That gap was filed as #748 and fixed the same day (commit `7805261`): the script now
  reads the node instance-identity document with the stolen token and prints the node role name plus its

## 2026-11-03 · #782 · weaver/registry declares the attributes the Go guard-proxy wrote by hand, and go-otel stages its OTEL_* env

guard-proxy-agenticburn#36 (PRD #412 M5) generates the Go build's attribute keys from `weaver/registry`, and wrote
three keys by hand in `internal/telemetry/semconv/extra.go` because the registry did not declare them. Two changes
land here.

- **The registry.** `gen_ai.request.model` is on the `sanitize` span, required, since proxy.py always sets it. The
  /chat root is the POST SERVER span, so `span.witb.guard_proxy.http` gains `gen_ai.operation.name` and
  `gen_ai.request.model` (conditionally required: on the /chat root) and the two opt-in message attributes.
  `error.type` is on `span.witb.guard_proxy.egress`, conditionally required when the forward fails. The new
  `span.witb.guard_proxy.chat` INTERNAL group is the /chat `chat` span. The new `metric.witb.guard_proxy.cost` group is
  the `gen_ai.client.cost` gauge (unit `USD`, as proxy.py registers it), with `gen_ai.provider.name` and
  `gen_ai.request.model` required. semconv v1.37.0's `gen_ai.provider.name` enum has `aws.bedrock`, the value
  proxy.py observes. All are refs to upstream; nothing is redefined locally.
- **Held offline.** `verify/test_weaver_guard_proxy_spans.py` reads the pinned proxy.py. It maps each span variable
  to its group, checks each span's name and kind, and fails when proxy.py sets an attribute its group does not
  declare or does not set one its group requires. It also holds the gauge's name, unit and observed attributes.
- **weaver joins the tools tier.** Until now `weaver registry check` ran only in
  `.github/workflows/weaver-registry-check.yml`, which the hecaton gate does not see. It now has a row in
  `verify/e2e-tools.lock`: weaver v0.24.2 with the workflow's SHA-256, and `test_e2e_tools_tier.py` holds the row to the
  workflow's pin. `fetch-e2e-tools.sh` gains a `.tar.xz` case, so both runners now list `xz` as a prerequisite.
  `verify/test_weaver_registry_check.py` (`# E2E TIER: tools`) runs the check. It also confirms that a typo'd ref
  fails, and it resolves the registry to check the groups above and the `aws.bedrock` member. A new tool pin, recorded
  here as the governance asks: it is the version CI already used, so nothing new is trusted.
- **The Go build's OTEL_* env is a Component, `gitops/ai-layer/go-otel/`.** It replaces the guard-proxy pod's
  `inject-python` annotation with `instrumentation.opentelemetry.io/inject-sdk: watch-it-burn-python`. Read from the
  Operator's `internal/instrumentation/sdk.go` (main, 2026-11-02): `injectSdk` adds the CR's `spec.env`
  (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf`) and common SDK config (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` from
  `spec.exporter.endpoint`, port 4318; service name, resource attributes, propagators, sampler) and no language agent.
  It never overrides a variable the container sets, so the pod's `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=burritobot` and
  `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT` still win. The Component swaps the old annotation out for the new one, because the
  Operator's pod mutator refuses two injections on a pod that names no containers. The issue suggested the value
  `"true"`. It names the CR instead: `"true"` fails with more than one Instrumentation in the namespace, and the
  ordering gate and the chart test already read this name.
- **Why a Component.** KubeCon (2026-11-12) runs proxy.py, which needs `inject-python`, and its clusters sync from
  staging. #751 staged the spend store the same way, and the #738 cutover lists both under `components:` in the commit
  that swaps the image and command. go-otel does not depend on go-spend-store, and the two patch different fields of
  the Deployment. `verify/test_guard_proxy_go_otel.py` (`# E2E TIER: tools`) renders
  the bundle with and without the Component and checks the CR's 4318 endpoint and http/protobuf. It checks that the
  pod sets no `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` of its own and that nothing else in the render changes. It fails a committed
  guard-proxy that no longer runs proxy.py without go-otel, which a simulated cutover confirmed.

**What guard-proxy-agenticburn still has to do (follow-ups filed).** Its codegen filter in
`weaver/templates/registry/go/weaver.yaml` selects `span.witb.` and `registry.witb.` groups only. So
`gen_ai.provider.name`, declared on the metric group alone, is generated only once `metric.witb.` is added. With that
filter, a local run of its template on this registry generated `GenAiProviderNameKey` and
`GenAiProviderNameAwsBedrock`, which renames extra.go's `GenAiProviderNameAWSBedrock`. Separately, proxy.py's /chat
`agent.forward` span sets no `url.full`, which `span.witb.guard_proxy.egress` requires, so a live-check of a /chat
turn would flag it. This change leaves that requirement alone, as it predates #782.

## 2026-11-03 · #782 · The inject-sdk dry run on watch-it-burn-private: Kyverno's resource-limits rule refused the probe

**Where this belongs.** The 2026-11-03 #782 entry ("weaver/registry declares the attributes the Go guard-proxy wrote by
hand, and go-otel stages its OTEL_* env") is on run 16462's branch `agent/782-15696` (`d7fb73c`, `b2d036c`), which
has not reached staging. Its "Not yet run on a cluster" part names this server-side dry run. This entry is that run's
result. When the draft is ported, keep both entries.

**What ran.** Escalation 737, hecaton's higher-privilege tier, ran the one act it was given. Credentials came from the
operator's `accen-dev` profile into an isolated kubeconfig, and the target was confirmed first. The context
`watch-it-burn-private` resolves to `arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:515966504359:cluster/watch-it-burn-private` (ACTIVE, 1.36).
Namespace `agent` exists, and it has the `watch-it-burn-python` Instrumentation with endpoint
`http://otel-collector-opentelemetry-collector.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:4318`. Then:

    kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private -n agent run otel-sdk-probe \
      --image=ghcr.io/peopleforrester/watch-it-burn:python-3.12-slim@sha256:6c4dd321d176d61ea848dc8c73a4f7dbae8f70e0ee48bb411ea2f045b599fa8e \
      --restart=Never --dry-run=server -o yaml \
      --annotations=instrumentation.opentelemetry.io/inject-sdk=watch-it-burn-python

It exited 1 with no pod spec:

    Error from server: admission webhook "vpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail-d07fe444" denied the request:
    Policy require-resource-limits failed: CPU and memory resource limits are required on every container.

`require-resource-limits` is a Kyverno ValidatingPolicy whose `validationActions` is `["Deny"]`. Validating webhooks
only run after the mutating ones, but a denied request returns no object, so this run could not see what the
Operator injects. Nothing was created, and no policy or cluster object was changed.

**Still owed.** The same dry run with a probe that passes the cluster's validating policies. `kubectl run` has no
resource-limits flag, so the probe needs `--overrides` that give the container CPU and memory limits. It may also
need what `require-probes` and `require-labels` check. The other way is to set `require-resource-limits` to Audit
for the one call and set it back to Deny straight after. Either is a different act from the one escalated, so it
needs its own escalation. Expected as before: `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` on 4318,
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf`, and no init container.

## 2026-11-03 · #813 · A live test reads a fresh chat on each KubeCon cluster back from Agent Observability, by its own session

**What #813 asks.** Test review run 16093 found that #783's criterion "a fresh chat on each cluster shows up in Agent
Observability, read back through the Datadog API" was held only by `verify/test_agent_obs_flow.py`, which runs
`verify/agent_obs_flow.py` against a fake Datadog. No test read a real chat back. No earlier draft of #813 exists
(`verify/prior-drafts.sh 813 origin/staging` prints NONE, and the issue has no comments).

**The live test** (`verify/test_agent_obs_flow_live.py`, `# SUITE: e2e`, so `run-e2e.sh` runs it and `run-tests.sh`
lists it with the live suite). It runs `agent_obs_flow.py chat --own-session` on both KubeCon bots
(attackme.burritobot.co on burritobot-public, burritobot-private.burritobot.co on burritobot-private), reading the read
pair in `watch-it-burn/datadog` as `WIB_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` (default accen-dev) in `WIB_REGION`, as
`test_dd_traces_live.py` does. It passes only when both chats' own spans are read back, and prints their trace ids.
No aws CLI, an unreadable secret, a Datadog refusal, a bot that does not answer, a cluster that sends nothing and a
cluster whose spans lack the chat's session each fail it with the reason. It spends two model calls, about a cent.

**Why `--own-session`, new in `agent_obs_flow.py`.** `chat` without it is GREEN on any `ml_app:burritobot` span from
the cluster since the chat, which answers #783's question (is anything arriving?) but not this criterion's (did this
chat show up?): during a run-through another visitor's chat would pass it. With `--own-session`, `check_chat` asks the
spans API for `k8s.cluster.name:<cluster> session_id:<the chat's session>` and checks the `session_id:` tag on each
span again, so a widened query cannot pass another session's spans off. When spans from the cluster arrive but none
carry the session, the RED says `THE CHAT'S OWN SPANS NEVER ARRIVED` and names the other trace ids, which separates a
missing session tag from #783's `RECEIVED NOTHING`. The flag is keyword-only, so `chat` without it, `watch`, and the
run-of-show's Night Before command behave as before. The session tag is the one `verify/stage_traces.py` already
reads (`session_id:<session>` on each span's tags), from the `session` the /chat body carries; it has not been read
live yet either. If the live test's first run reports spans without it, that is a finding to fix in the bot's
tracing, and the test stays as written.

**Offline** (`verify/test_agent_obs_flow.py`, its fake now parsing both query terms). New cases: each chat's own
session is asked for on its own cluster and read back by its own trace ids and not another visitor's; another
session's spans on the cluster are RED with the session named; a Datadog that ignores the session term is still RED;
nothing at all is #783's RED; without the flag any span is still GREEN; and through `main`, exit 1 with one chat
missing and exit 0 with both. Forcing `check_chat` to ignore `own_session` fails six of the new checks, and dropping
the second tag check fails the widened-query case (both confirmed on a temporary edit, restored).

**The live run did not happen: the session files could not be read.** Run 16661's `clusters/env`, `aws-config`,
`aws-credentials` and `kubeconfig` are mode 640, group `hecaton`, and the run's user (`hecaton-s6-claude-certkraken`,
groups `hecaton-runs` and `hecaton-tools`) is not in it, so `. "$HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV"` is "Permission denied", as for
runs 16420, 16574, 16647 and 16653 (hecaton#508). At 2026-11-03T13:59Z `python3 verify/test_agent_obs_flow_live.py`
printed `FAIL: Datadog could not be read: cannot read watch-it-burn/datadog as profile accen-dev in us-west-2: aws:
[ERROR]: The config profile (accen-dev) could not be found` and exited 1, which is the loud failure it is written to give.

## 2026-11-03 · #816 · The web-terminal build no longer pushes over a version tag, and puts a moved pinned tag back on its digest

**The fault.** `.github/workflows/build-web-terminal.yml` ran `docker push` on every run, and its build is not
reproducible, so each push run that touched `images/web-terminal/**` or the workflow wrote a new digest over
`watch-it-burn:web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7`. The tag has been seen at `d6acd503`, `0b72ecc7`, `7e5f8986` and, read on
2026-11-03 by this run, `cb00c5b7` (build-web-terminal run 41696390852, 18:42 UTC). `gitops/ai-layer/resources.yaml`
and images.lock pin `sha256:68004fb5...`, an OCI index that still exists and still carries its cosign signature
(`sha256-68004fb5....sig` answers 200), so clusters pulling by digest were not affected. The tag stopped naming the
pin, and `verify/test_image_version_tags.py` went red.

**Which of the issue's two fixes.** Pinning the new digest is not one: the 2026-11-03 #746 entry records that the
rebuild carries no cosign signature and `verify-image-signatures` requires one, a dispatched run has no signing key,
and the next push run would move the tag again anyway. So the workflow stops pushing over a tag that already
exists. On its own that would leave the tag on `cb00c5b7`, and moving it back needs a ghcr.io write this run may not
make. The workflow holds `GHCR_TOKEN`, so the same step puts the tag back: the first push run after this change
reaches staging, which this change starts because it edits the workflow, does that write in CI.

**What changed.**
- `scripts/ghcr_version_tag.py` is the push step. It reads the digest that `resources.yaml` and images.lock pin for
  the tag the build read (it refuses when they pin more than one). When the tag serves that digest it does nothing;
  when the tag serves another, it fetches the pinned manifest, checks its bytes hash to the pinned digest, PUTs
  those bytes with their own media type to the tag, and checks that the tag now serves the pin. In neither case is the
  build pushed. When nothing pins the tag, it pushes the build only if ghcr.io lacks that tag, which is how a new ttyd
  version is pushed once; a later run, the main promotion's for example, leaves that first push in place and names its
  digest to pin and sign. It exits 1 when the pinned digest is not in the registry.
- The workflow's Push step runs the script with `GHCR_USER`, `GHCR_TOKEN` and the version step's tag in its
  environment, and the workflow also runs on a change to the script.
- `verify/test_ghcr_version_tag.py` (offline) runs every case against a fake registry on loopback that keeps
  manifests by digest and tags by name, with the docker push stubbed. It checks that the put carries the pinned
  manifest's exact bytes and media type, holds the workflow to calling the script and to having no `docker push` of
  its own, and holds both pin files to the one digest.

**What this does not do.** A change to the image under the same ttyd version (an entrypoint copy, kubectl) is no
longer shipped by the push run, since its tag already exists. The pods take the entrypoint from the
`web-terminal-entrypoint` ConfigMap, not the image. Shipping a rebuild under the same ttyd version needs a tag of its
own, which is a question about #714's tag scheme and is left to it.

**Live checks run.** The script's registry reads, run anonymously against ghcr.io on 2026-11-03: the tag serves
`sha256:cb00c5b7e716...`, the pinned `68004fb5` manifest is 856 bytes of `application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json`
that hash to the pin, and a missing tag answers 404. The cluster reads did not run: this run's `clusters/kubeconfig`
and `clusters/env` are mode 640, group `hecaton`, and `kubectl --context watch-it-burn-community` (and `-private`)
fails with "permission denied" on the kubeconfig, which is hecaton#508's to fix. Nothing on either cluster was read
or changed.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The build-web-terminal run that the promotion of this change to staging starts must
log `... is back on the pinned sha256:68004fb5...`. After it, `python3 verify/test_image_version_tags.py` (inside
`bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh`) must pass the check
`ghcr.io serves ghcr.io/peopleforrester/watch-it-burn:web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7 at the pinned sha256:68004fb5ed2d...`.
The run on main's promotion must log `serves the pinned`, with no put and no push.

No dependency was added: the script uses only Python's standard library, which the runner's python3 has.

**The suites (run 16758, at b13c01c).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 49 checks (the offline suite and 48 tier
tests) in 24m05s. The offline suite inside it ran 235 tests, all green, `verify/test_ghcr_version_tag.py` among them.
It exits 1 on `test_image_version_tags.py` alone, with two reds, both in what the registry serves: ghcr.io serves
`web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7` at `sha256:cb00c5b7...`, which this change's first CI run puts back on `68004fb5`, and
`sample-app-nginx-1.27.5` answers 404, which is #814's escalated `crane tag`.
## 2026-11-03 · #648 · The input guard refuses PII, `stage_traces.py pii` measures it, and `seed` adds the PII trace

**Context.** The coordinator's live check on 2026-10-31 found that `stage_traces.py pii` did not exist (`invalid choice:
'pii'`) and that the input guard had no PII scanner. Both had been in 768f368 (origin/agent/648-12515), and 7d830b3
rebuilt only `seed` and `check`. Runs 14409 (origin/agent/648-14409) and 15817 (origin/agent/648-15817) rebuilt them,
and both ended failed at validation, so none of it reached staging. Run 16717 found the cause with
`verify/prose_gate.py`: the draft's decisions.md entry said a guard `that lets PII through`, and the ai-isms gate reads
`lets` as `let's`, a connective, in a file that already reads `major`. That sentence now says "a guard that would pass
PII"; nothing else in the draft failed the gate. Measured again from the repo and guard-proxy's pinned source (88b9b52):
the input guard still catches no PII. Its block-list holds destructive verbs and recipe phrases, and LLM Guard's only
input scanner was PromptInjection.

**Checked against staging, cherry-picked.** `verify/prior-drafts.sh 648 origin/staging` started from 042936f
(origin/agent/648-15817), 139 staging commits behind, with four edits in place and a decisions.md append. Each named
staging commit, reread against the draft:

- 526f709 (#775) reshaped Challenge 3: `guardrails-on` before the attack, the Joker now lands with Kyverno on, and the
  fix is `guard-agency-on` (least privilege) and then `guard-input-on`. The draft still had the Joker refused at
  admission and only `guard-input-on` before `c3-fixed`. Staging's shape is kept everywhere: `c3-pii` now runs after
  `guard-agency-on`, `guard-input-on` and `c3-fixed`, so the beat order is staging's with `c3-pii` added, and the
  run-of-show's Challenge 3 tab keeps "point 5 (least privilege)" and drops the draft's "and the admission denial".
- 42a9e8b (#806) judges Challenge 3 on workshop-mcp's audit log. The fake cluster in `verify/test_stage_traces.py`
  keeps staging's audit, `kubectl_rc` and witch name and adds the draft's `guard_verdicts`; the call count is seven.
- 3e291e3 (#485) and the #783 Agent Observability step edited the run-of-show's Night Before list: the draft's seed
  paragraph is kept with "seven prompts", and staging's #783 item follows it unchanged.
- 6d8505a repinned guard-proxy to 88b9b52, which forwards the `/chat` witch name. `verify/test_input_pii_guard.py` runs
  the pinned proxy.py and passes on it: `blocklisted`, `_post_guard` and `input_verdict` are unchanged by name and
  behaviour, and `/chat` still refuses the stage prompt by `Regex` with zero tokens.

**The change.**
- `llm-guard-scanners` gains a Regex input scanner: one pattern, the burn collector's four scrub patterns (e-mail,
  card, SSN, phone; `gitops/otel-collector/values-burn.yaml`, #647) joined as an alternation, `is_blocked`, no redact,
  `match_type: search`. It sits under the existing `guard-input-on` and needs no guard-proxy change. The public bot's
  input guard is never on, so attackme is unchanged.
- llm-guard's pod template carries `checksum/scanners-yml`, sha256(scanners.yml)[:12]. The API reads scanners.yml once
  at start and the ConfigMap's name is stable, so without it the scanner would sync green on the running private
  cluster and never load (guard-proxy's `checksum/proxy-py` is the same fix).
- `verify/test_input_pii_guard.py` (offline) holds the pattern equal to the scrub's and the checksum to the file. It
  checks that every scrub case, the five samples and the stage prompt are refused and the untouched text is not, and
  that no support-desk ticket, probe prompt, topic case, `/kubecon` page, prompt catalog or LAB-TEXT line trips it. It
  runs `pii`'s in-pod script on the pinned proxy.py against a fake LLM Guard that applies the configured scanners (5 of
  5 refused, the order passes), and serves the pinned proxy's `/chat` with the input classifier on, which refuses the
  stage prompt by `Regex` with zero tokens. `verify/test_input_pii_guard_llm_guard.py` (E2E tools tier) builds the
  scanner with llm-guard 0.3.16 itself, through `get_scanner_by_name("Regex", params)` as the API does, under the same
  uv environment `test_injection_classifier.py` already uses, so it adds no dependency.
- `stage_traces.py pii <host> --context ...` runs guard-proxy's own `blocklisted` and the `/analyze/prompt` call
  `input_verdict` makes, in its pod, on a card, an SSN, an e-mail, a phone number and the stage prompt, then a plain
  order. No model call, no toggle; it ends `PII GREEN: THE INPUT GUARD REFUSES 5 OF 5`. It refuses the room's host and
  a missing context, and asks nothing when the identity check fails.
- `seed` gains `c3-pii` after `c3-fixed`, while the input guard is on: the neighbor's test card, 555 number and
  example.com address. It is sent only once guard-proxy's input stages say they refuse it, so a guard that would pass
  PII never sends it to the model. It is judged on the reply: guarded, `blocked by the input guardrail`, `Regex`
  named, zero input tokens.
- A refused prompt never gets a gen_ai span, so `c3-pii`'s view is APM's Trace Explorer on
  `service:burritobot @session.id:<session>`, read through `/api/v2/spans/events/search`. Its trace must be stamped
  `input_classifier`, carry no `burritobot-agent` span and hold none of the three PII values. 768f368's `retention`
  subcommand is not rebuilt, because it needs a Datadog write key the repo does not have. Instead the Night Before step
  has Whitney create the APM retention filter (`@session.id:wib-stage-*`, 100%) in the UI before seeding, and the
  morning `check` goes red on `c3-pii` if the filter did not keep it.

**A side effect, accepted.** guard-proxy's topic stage calls `/analyze/prompt` suppressing only PromptInjection, so
with `guard-topic-on` a PII prompt that matches no on-topic phrase is now also refused as off-topic by the classifier
step. The room would want that refusal anyway, and changing it would need a guard-proxy release this does not.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Run 16717 could not run a live check: its session files
(`/var/lib/hecaton/runs/16717/clusters/env`, `kubeconfig` and the AWS credentials) are group `hecaton`, mode 0640,
and the run's user is not in that group, so `. "$HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV"` printed `Permission denied` and kubectl could
not load the kubeconfig (hecaton#508). Owed, in this order. On watch-it-burn-private, today, with the current deploy:
`python3 verify/stage_traces.py pii burritobot-private.burritobot.co --context watch-it-burn-private --profile
accen-dev` is the baseline and must end `REFUSES 0 OF 5`. Once hecaton promotes this and Argo CD syncs it (llm-guard
restarts on the checksum), the same command must end `REFUSES 5 OF 5`. Then, on the Night Before (2026-11-11), the
retention filter and `seed`, whose `c3-pii` read-back is the first live test of whether the read-only key may search
APM spans and whether `@session.id` is the facet Trace Explorer finds the root span by; then Whitney saves the printed
links as views, and `check` runs the morning of.

**Suite results, run 16717.** On 7847a10, `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 49 checks (the offline suite and 48 tier
tests) in 22m39s. The offline suite ran 235 tests, all green, `test_stage_traces.py` and `test_input_pii_guard.py`
among them, and the tier's `test_input_pii_guard_llm_guard.py` printed "The deployed Regex input scanner refuses the
five PII prompts and passes the workshop's own text". It exits 1 on `test_image_version_tags.py` alone, with the two
reds staging 382d570 already records in #796's entry and that this change does not touch: the web-terminal tag
ghcr.io now serves at another digest, and the 404 for `sample-app-nginx-1.27.5` (#814).

**Resumed by run 16764.** Run 16717 failed hecaton's skip-markers gate, not the prose gate. The gate counts any

## 2026-11-03 · #784 · GenAI telemetry: Act 2 redacts the messages, the collector maps tool definitions, weaver pins semconv v1.41.1, and guard-proxy's token counts go to guard-proxy-agenticburn

**What Datadog documents.** Datadog's OpenTelemetry page for Agent Observability (docs.datadoghq.com/llm_observability/instrumentation/otel_instrumentation,
read 2026-11-03) says it supports "OpenTelemetry 1.37+" GenAI conventions and gives no upper bound. Its mapping table
names `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` and `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, the cost attributes (`gen_ai.usage.cost.amount` with
`gen_ai.usage.cost.currency` USD, `gen_ai.usage.cost`, `gen_ai.cost.*`), and `gen_ai.tool.definitions`, which it maps
to `meta.tool_definitions`. It reads input and output from `gen_ai.input.messages` and `gen_ai.output.messages` first,
and from the `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details` event after that. It names none of `gen_ai.agent.version`,
the cache and reasoning token attributes, any `mcp.*` attribute or MCP span, or a span-kind split for `invoke_agent`.
It also warns that exporting the same model calls twice counts their tokens twice.

**1. Token counts on guard-proxy's model-call span.**
- *The row the issue saw is already gone from Agent Observability.* The `skipped_tokens_missing` row (trace
  `c943363f5467508c8bfc14c6a40c4b59`, 2026-11-01) came from guard-proxy's `chat` span being sent as an llm row with no
  tokens. Agent Observability received no BurritoBot row after about 03:26 UTC that day (#783), and #746's copy was
  committed at 15:51 UTC, so that row came from before the copy. Since #746, `filter/llmobs_one_root` drops that span
  from Agent Observability's copy, and guard-proxy's turn span becomes the `invoke_agent` root. The llm rows under it
  are kagent's `generate_content` spans, which carry `gen_ai.usage.*` themselves. `verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py`
  checks that every llm row in the copy has both counts. Datadog prices those rows from the tokens, so it can estimate
  a cost for the trace. The live look below still has to confirm this.
- *Setting the counts on the span itself is guard-proxy-agenticburn's change.* proxy.py is in the
  `gitops/ai-layer/guard-proxy` submodule, and a run cannot move that gitlink (question 766: Michael pins, and a run
  does the rest). The change is filed as a follow-up in guard-proxy-agenticburn: set `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`
  and `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, summed from `kagent_usage_metadata` as `chat_usage_tokens` already reads them, on
  the `/chat` `chat` span. It may add `gen_ai.usage.cost.amount` with `gen_ai.usage.cost.currency` USD as well. The
  Go build (#738) needs the same change. The counts belong only on that span, never on the `POST /chat` root or on
  `sanitize`. Both of those become the `invoke_agent` root in the copy, and counts there would be the turn's second
  count next to kagent's. On that span the counts show in APM. Agent Observability never adds them, because the copy
  drops the span. The `gen_ai.client.cost` metric stays as it is. `weaver/registry` now declares the span
  (`span.witb.guard_proxy.chat`) with both counts as recommended, so the repin conforms. The
  `url.scheme` precedent is that an attribute declared Recommended and not emitted does not fail `live-check`.

**2. The redaction.** `gitops/otel-collector/otel-collector-act2-overlay.yaml` redacted the `content` attribute of the
`gen_ai.content.prompt` and `gen_ai.content.completion` events. Semconv v1.37 dropped those names, and nothing in the
stack emits them: proxy.py writes the two message attributes in every capture mode and emits no event. So Act 2
redacted nothing. `transform/redact_sentinel` now replaces, on every span and on every span event (the details event
is Datadog's fallback), the same keys that burn's `transform/scrub_pii` keeps for its scrub. Those are the messages,
`gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` and `.result`, and the `gcp.vertex.agent.*` keys they are copied from. The scope covers every
span, guard-proxy's and the rest: `transform/adk_model_content` copies the prompt onto every kagent model call. The
messages become one message in the semconv shape whose text is `[DEMO-REDACTED]`, so Datadog's panel still parses
them. The other keys become the bare string. The overlay's steps now name where the config lives (`values.yaml`,
`values-burn.yaml` on burn), and it goes last in the traces processors, after the ADK copies and before every
exporter, `forward/llmobs` included, so both copies carry the redaction. The Challenge 3 runbook and
MASTER-RECREATION-SPEC say the same.
*Which config redacts the KubeCon clusters' content:* neither cluster loads the overlay (no file under `gitops/`
names it, and the new offline test holds that). watch-it-burn-community runs `otel-collector-burn`, whose
`transform/scrub_pii` (values-burn.yaml, #647) replaces e-mail addresses, card numbers, SSNs and phone numbers in
those same keys before any exporter runs. watch-it-burn-private runs `otel-collector` on the admin profile and
redacts nothing. That is by design: the presenters' cluster carries no attendee's text.

**3. Semconv v1.41.1, only where Datadog maps it.**
- `weaver/registry/manifest.yaml` pins `semantic-conventions` v1.41.1 (2026-05-11), the last release that carries
  the GenAI conventions. Weaver 0.24.2 (the CI's sha-pinned binary, run here) passes `weaver registry check` on it.
  Diffing the resolved registries at v1.37.0 and v1.41.1 for every attribute the groups ref shows only new enum
  members (`retrieval` and `invoke_workflow` for the operation, `QUERY` for the method) and `peer.service`, which is
  deprecated from v1.38 and renamed to `service.peer.name`. The proxy keeps emitting `peer.service`: Datadog's
  service map reads it, and Datadog documents nothing for `service.peer.name`. The registry note says so.
- *Adopted:* the `gen_ai.usage.*` token counts on guard-proxy's chat span (above), and `gen_ai.tool.definitions`
  (new in v1.38). `transform/adk_model_content` now writes `gen_ai.tool.definitions` on kagent's model calls from the
  ADK request. adk-go v2.1.0 packs every declaration into the first `genai.Tool` that has `functionDeclarations`
  (tool/toolutils PackTool and agent transfer both do this; read at tag v2.1.0), so that one list is the whole set.
  Each entry is `{"type":"function","name","description"}`. The semconv makes the description optional, and it is
  kept here because a poisoned tool description is what Challenge 3 is about. The parameters schema is left out, as
  the semconv recommends for size by default.
- *Not adopted, because Datadog does not document them:* the `invoke_agent` client/internal split (v1.41). Datadog
  maps `invoke_agent` to the agent kind whatever the span kind, so the collector keeps stamping it as before. Also
  not adopted: MCP's conventions and spans (v1.39), `gen_ai.agent.version` (v1.40), and the cache and reasoning token
  attributes (v1.40, v1.41), which Datadog maps only in its OpenInference and Langfuse sections. `execute_tool` spans
  already carry the tool name (ADK names them `execute_tool {gen_ai.tool.name}`), so v1.41's naming changes nothing.
  `verify/test_genai_semconv_pin.py` fails if a registry group or a collector config adopts any of these. Revisit
  each one when Datadog's page documents it.
- *The move to semantic-conventions-genai.* From semantic-conventions v1.42.0 (2026-06-12) every `gen_ai.*`
  convention is deprecated in the main repository and maintained in open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai. On
  2026-11-03 that repository had no tag and no release (GitHub API). The pin stays on v1.41.1 until then. **Revisit
  when semantic-conventions-genai tags its first release:** add it as the registry's GenAI dependency (weaver 0.24.2
  accepts a second dependency), check it against Datadog's page again, and move the guard-proxy groups' `gen_ai.*`

## 2026-10-31 · question 947 · #471: Istio stays, and the console and guard-proxy are enrolled in the ambient mesh

**Question 947:** Should the workshop drop the Istio ambient mesh, enroll the agent and apps namespaces in it,
or keep it installed and unenrolled?

**Answer:** "So why are you recommending that we drop Istio when this is part of the stack? I know we don't have
any agents and apps in there but we could enroll at least one application in there. Why wouldn't we do that? Why
is this being brought up as a thing to talk about? I don't understand. What's the problem with just leaving it
there? What is the issue exactly?"

**Decided by:** Michael (verdict: overridden; the recommendation was to drop Istio).

**Read as:** keep Istio, and enroll at least one application in it. To answer the question in the reply: leaving
Istio installed was never the problem. The problem was that the pages said it encrypted traffic while it
encrypted nothing, because no pod or namespace carried `istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient`. Drop was recommended
because enrolling looked like more work than the one sentence it made true. Enrolling the right pods turned out
to be smaller than that.

**What it changes.**
- **Enrolled: the console and guard-proxy, per pod.** Both pod templates in `gitops/ai-layer/resources.yaml`
  carry `istio.io/dataplane-mode: ambient`, and no Namespace does. That hop carries every chat message, and it
  is now mutual TLS between `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/agent/sa/default` (the console) and
  `.../sa/guard-proxy-reader`. On the burn profile, which has no Istio, the label does nothing.
- **Not enrolled: agentgateway, workshop-agent and the rest of `agent`, and all of `apps`.** Mesh traffic
  arrives on HBONE port 15008. `gitops/ai-layer/chat-path-ingress.yaml` (#552) admits only app ports into
  agentgateway and workshop-agent, so enrolling them would cut the chat path. `apps` ingress has the same
  problem on the admin profile. Either can be enrolled later with a 15008 rule.
- **agent's mTLS mode is PERMISSIVE.** `security/istio/peer-authentication.yaml` sets PERMISSIVE because the
  console's ip-target NLB, the beat scripts and the agent's tool pod reach the enrolled pods from outside the
  mesh, and STRICT would refuse them. Between the two enrolled pods, traffic is still mutual TLS. The apps
  STRICT policy applied to nothing and was removed.
- **The pages say what it carries.** The lab tour bullet (and `challenges/LAB-TEXT.md`) names the hop and gives
  two commands: `kubectl get pods -n agent -L istio.io/dataplane-mode`, and a ztunnel `connection complete`
  line. The same correction went into the `docs/STACK-WALKTHROUGH.md` row and SPIFFE note, the
  `facilitation/governance-map.md` row 1d, the August run-of-show layer table, the `links.html` entry and
  `docs/MASTER-RECREATION-SPEC.md`. The #238 evaluation carries an outcome note.
- **Tests.** `verify/test_mesh_enrollment.py` now holds that exactly those two pod templates carry the label,
  no namespace does, no Ingress NetworkPolicy in `agent` selects an enrolled pod without admitting 15008, agent
  is PERMISSIVE, and the tour names the hop. `verify/test_mesh.py` checks the mode. The new E2E check
  `verify/test_mesh_live.py` checks four things on a cluster: istio-cni redirected those two pods and no others
  on the chat path, they are Ready, the console reaches guard-proxy, and ztunnel logged that connection with
  both identities.
- **Not yet run on a cluster.** This run could not deploy. The live check is
  `CONTEXT=<ctx> python3 verify/test_mesh_live.py`, plus the existing chat beats (`verify/run-all.sh`) and
  `verify/test_console_no_toggle_live.py`, which go through the console and guard-proxy. Install time and app
  count do not change: the five Istio apps stay.
- **Ported in run 16694 (2026-11-03).** Run 7101's two commits never reached staging. `verify/prior-drafts.sh 471`
  found six paths that staging had edited in place since the draft's base, `bc00203`, plus the decisions.md append.

the build only under a tag ghcr.io lacks and puts a pinned tag that has moved back on its pinned digest. That covers
the issue's second step, and its first runs in CI with the workflow's `GHCR_TOKEN`, so this run makes no code change
and no ghcr.io write. What this run did was check that the restore happened and that the digest is the signed one.

  logged `...web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7 served sha256:cb00c5b7e716...; it is back on the pinned

## 2026-11-03 · #812 · A live test for #783's "on staging and applied to both clusters"

**What it checks.** `verify/test_otel_trace_id_fix_live.py` (`# SUITE: e2e`) is the test #783's criterion "the fix is on
staging and applied to watch-it-burn-community and watch-it-burn-private" lacked. It fetches GitHub's `staging`, the
branch both clusters' Argo CD reads, into FETCH_HEAD and checks that `67c956a` is in its history. It then checks that the
collector values at that commit run `set(trace_id.string, Substring(SHA256(trace_id.string), 0, 32))` as the first
statement of `transform/llmobs_one_root`, which is first in `traces/llmobs`, fed by the traces pipeline's
`forward/llmobs`. It renders that per cluster: the community cluster's burn Application (values.yaml plus
values-burn.yaml) and the private cluster's instructor one (values.yaml), each alone and with every file of its Datadog
overlay. The statement has to be first because the span id and kagent's re-parent are derived from the copy's trace id.
Then, on each cluster, with `--context` from COMMUNITY_CONTEXT and PRIVATE_CONTEXT, it checks that the context is that
cluster (its name or its EKS ARN). It also checks that the `otel-collector` Application reads its values source at
`staging`, is Synced, Healthy and Succeeded, and is synced at a revision that is on staging and contains `67c956a`. The
collector DaemonSet must have rolled its current template out, available, to every node. Last, the relay ConfigMap the
DaemonSet mounts must run the statement, alone and with each overlay file. It only reads.

**Why not a commit pin alone.** A cluster synced at a staging commit after 67c956a could still run a config without the
statement if a later commit reverted it. So the live ConfigMap is read as well, and staging's tree is checked as well
as its history.

**Offline half.** `verify/test_otel_trace_id_fix_live_checks.py` runs the same `run` against a fake git and fake clusters
built from this checkout's own collector values (`collector_render`). The healthy pair passes. Each of these fails it:
the statement reverted or moved second on staging, burn's traces/llmobs without the processor, staging without the
commit, a fetch that fails, an Application reading main, OutOfSync, Degraded or Failed, a sync at a pre-fix or
off-staging revision, a missing Application or DaemonSet, a half-rolled or unavailable DaemonSet, a live relay without
the statement, without the processor or without the forward, a missing overlay ConfigMap or relay key, swapped
contexts, and a standby context (`watch-it-burn-community-b01`).

**run-e2e.sh now requires PRIVATE_CONTEXT** beside COMMUNITY_CONTEXT, with the same reachability check, and AGENTS.md
names it. No dependency was added.

**What ran live.** The staging half ran against GitHub: staging `41c0b9c0aeb0` contains `67c956adc5a2`, and both
profiles' collector values run the statement first (three PASS). The cluster half did not run. This run's
`$KUBECONFIG` (`/var/lib/hecaton/runs/16657/clusters/kubeconfig`) and `$HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV` are owned
`hecaton:hecaton` mode 0640, and the run's user (`hecaton-s4-claude-certkraken`, groups `hecaton-s4-claude-certkraken`,
`hecaton-runs`, `hecaton-tools`) is not in group `hecaton`. So the full run ended with "the cluster can be read" FAIL on
both clusters: `open /var/lib/hecaton/runs/16657/clusters/kubeconfig: permission denied`. That is the same block the
#733, #746 and #783 re-dispatch entries above record (hecaton#508).

**Not yet run on a cluster.** `COMMUNITY_CONTEXT=watch-it-burn-community PRIVATE_CONTEXT=watch-it-burn-private python3
verify/test_otel_trace_id_fix_live.py`, from a session whose kubeconfig names both contexts. Its PASS lines replace
step 1 of the 2026-11-02 · #783 entry's commands. #783's `agent_obs_flow.py chat` read-back is still owed after it.

**The suites.** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran the offline suite first: 231 tests, "ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS
GREEN", `test_otel_trace_id_fix_live_checks.py` among them, so the Test command passes. The tools tier then ran 45

volume was wiped, its presenter page says "Datadog accounts not yet configured on the distributor" because
`ADMIN_DATADOG_EMAIL` and `ADMIN_DATADOG_PASSWORD` are unset, and its fleet console reads "runner is not up: no health
report has arrived". The report asks this repo two decisions. The answers below cite
`facilitation/kubecon-na-2026-run-of-show.md` as it stands on staging at `53b2c9c`.

**Decision 1: KubeCon uses neither `/eks-claim` nor the presenter bundle.** The session is a demo. Nobody in the room
provisions a cluster, and nobody is pointed at the attendee lab or the provisioning page (lines 11 to 16). The
presenters drive from `/kubecon`, which carries no provisioning or student-lab content (lines 24 to 29). The session
runs on the roster in `infra/terraform/fleet/roster.tsv`, and the attendee pool is outside it (lines 271 to 273). The
router table carries the roster only, and nobody is pointed at the provisioning distributor (lines 302 to 306). The
Night Before brings up the roster with `./fleet.sh instructors up all` and says the attendee pool is not provisioned
for this session (lines 891 to 893). The presenters log in to the private cluster's terminal with the presenter login [value redacted, #911]
and read that login off the cluster's `terminal-auth` Secret (lines 446 to 449). The provisioning app stays up as the
C1 beacon collector only (lines 912 to 916, and open question 9 at lines 1285 to 1292, #502 and question 714). So the
empty pool is correct for KubeCon, and no ingest against the Railway host is owed for it. The unset
`ADMIN_DATADOG_EMAIL` and `ADMIN_DATADOG_PASSWORD` do not affect the session: they only fill the presenter page, which
nobody opens at KubeCon, and both KubeCon clusters ship to Whitney's sandbox Datadog org (open question 3 at lines
1250 to 1252, and the people table at line 52, #629).

**Decision 2: `fleet.sh serve-actions` does not run during the talk.** The admin console has no step in the KubeCon
run of show. `git grep` finds no `/eks-claim`, presenter page, admin console or `serve-actions` in
`facilitation/kubecon-na-2026-run-of-show.md` or `gitops/ai-layer/web/kubecon.html`. A presenter runs each Night
Before and on-stage action in that file directly, from a checkout or a cluster's terminal. So the console's "runner is not up: no
health report has arrived" line is expected for KubeCon and needs no action. The 2-hour workshop keeps the runner:
`docs/admin-console.md` says to start `fleet.sh serve-actions` before the doors open and leave it up for the length of
the workshop (question 629).

**Who decided.** Run 16785 decided both answers from the repo's records, under the decision ladder (the spec, then
decisions.md, then the rules). The run-of-show and `docs/admin-console.md` settle both, so no question went to
Michael.

**What differs from the earlier drafts.** `origin/agent/720-13664` and `origin/agent/720-14845` carried the same two
answers alongside a fix to the C1 fallback's beacon view URL. Staging has since taken that fix (d2264c1d moved the
fallback to `https://beacon.burritobot.co/beacon/view`), so this entry carries the answers alone, with line citations
on the current run-of-show. Nothing changes in code, and no cluster check applies: the answers rest on the records.

**Suite results, run 16785.** On 636a6c3, `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 52 checks (the offline suite and 51 tier
tests) in 24m12s. The offline suite ran 237 tests and ended `ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`. The tier exits 1 on
`test_image_version_tags.py` alone, on one check: ghcr.io answers 404 for `sample-app-nginx-1.27.5` at its pinned
digest (#814). This change edits decisions.md alone and does not touch that tag.

## 2026-11-03 · #793 · model_pin_check and the cost tests price by whichever guard-proxy build is pinned; the repin to 2cff90d is Michael's commit

**Context.** guard-proxy-agenticburn#37 (c8ac56e, release note of 2026-11-02) has guard-proxy price each request at
the tier of the `workshop-agent` Agent's `spec.declarative.modelConfig` (`bedrock-nova`, `-haiku`, `-sonnet`, `-opus`),
read at most every 5 seconds with the `guard-proxy-reader` token, which already has `get` on that Agent.
`MODEL_TIER` becomes the start-up default and the price of a ModelConfig with no tier, and `/cost`'s `tier` is the
tier in effect. This is build piece 1 of `docs/research/2026-11-02-workload-management-exercises.md`.

then 2cff90d) and both failed hecaton's forbidden gate, "adds submodule gitops/ai-layer/guard-proxy". The gate's
`gate_forbidden` (hecaton `run/validate.py`) fails every changed path whose tree mode is 160000, so it refuses a bump
of an existing submodule as well as a new one. That is the rule question 766 settled, "Michael pins, a run does the
rest" (the #559 and #762 entries above), and run 16752 missed it. Run 16791 (this entry) keeps the gitlink at staging's
88b9b52 and `checksum/proxy-py` at `5ef84f383407`, and puts Michael's repin in its escalate: move the gitlink to
2cff90d, guard-proxy-agenticburn main's head, which carries #37, #38 (1cfa6d6, spans and `gen_ai.client.cost` name the
priced model) and #43 (82b7daf, both rate-limit replies end "Wait a few seconds and send that again."), and set
`checksum/proxy-py` to `19fbbe48283e`, the sha256 of 2cff90d's proxy.py. `verify/load_replay.py` tells the two limits
apart by `/min per conversation.)` and `/min cap on this cluster.)`, which #43's replies keep.

**So the rest holds at either pin.** Everything here is written to be right before and after that commit, and its
tests pass with the submodule at 88b9b52 and at 2cff90d (both run; see the suites below):
- `verify/model_pin_check.py` reads which build is pinned: `prices_bound_model` is true when the pinned proxy.py
  defines both `_tier_of` and `bound_tier`, which #37 added. On such a build it prices the pin at the bound
  `bedrock-<tier>` ModelConfig's tier, else `MODEL_TIER`, so a live patch of the Agent to `bedrock-haiku` with
  `MODEL_TIER` left at `nova` passes, and a ModelConfig with no `bedrock-<tier>` name prints a non-failing `WARN` and
  is judged at `MODEL_TIER`. On an earlier build it prices at `MODEL_TIER` alone, as that build does, so the same
  patch fails as mispriced. It prints which pricing it read, and the GREEN line names the priced tier.
- `verify/test_model_pin_check.py` judges both builds on every run. With bound pricing: live patches to haiku, sonnet
  and opus pass with `MODEL_TIER` at nova, `MODEL_TIER=sonnet` on a `bedrock-nova` pin passes (the issue's case
  "MODEL_TIER pricing another model fails the pin" is false there), a `bedrock-<tier>` ModelConfig whose model is
  another tier's fails, and untiered names warn. With `MODEL_TIER` pricing, the issue's case still fails the pin, and
  the three patches fail unless `MODEL_TIER` moves with them. It also checks `prices_bound_model` on three stand-in
  sources and against the imported pinned proxy.py, and then holds the check to the pinned build: on a #37 build
  `bound_tier` agrees with its `_tier_of` on every ModelConfig the manifests define and five odd names; on an earlier
  one the build's fixed price is the `MODEL_TIER` row.
- `verify/test_cost_counter.py` and `verify/test_finale_cap.py` priced through `COST_PER_1K_IN`, which #37 removes.
  They now take the `MODEL_TIER` row of `TIER_PRICES_PER_1K`, which is the off-cluster price on both builds. The

  `_AGENT_PATH` is. At 2cff90d that read resolves to `agents/workshop-agent`, which `guard-proxy-reader` is granted

- `docs/MASTER-RECREATION-SPEC.md`'s tier-swap bullet: the swap is the Agent patch alone from #37 (guard-proxy 2cff90d)

## 2026-11-03 · #828 · keep-sample-app-tag.yml creates sample-app-nginx-1.27.5 on ghcr.io when staging takes it

**The red.** The heavy gate on staging (`858ffafb9af2`) failed `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` on
`test_image_version_tags.py` alone, on one check: ghcr.io answers 404 for `watch-it-burn:sample-app-nginx-1.27.5`.
#814 renamed sample-app's pin to the nginx inside it, at the digest the old `sample-app` tag served
(`sha256:556e176d…`), and escalated the `crane tag` that creates the new tag, since a run may not write to ghcr.io. That
command has not run, so the gate has been red on this one check since #814 merged, and main has not moved.
`bash verify/prior-drafts.sh 828 origin/staging` printed NONE: no earlier draft.

**The fix: CI makes the tag, as #816 and #824 did for web-terminal.** #824's entry above records the precedent:
web-terminal's tag went back on its pinned digest through `scripts/ghcr_version_tag.py`, run by
`build-web-terminal.yml` with the repo's `GHCR_TOKEN` on the push to staging, and no run wrote to ghcr.io. That
script's pinned rows already do what sample-app needs: when a pin file pins `<tag>@D` and the tag does not serve D,
it puts D's manifest, byte for byte, to the tag (the same registry call `crane tag` makes). Two changes:
- `scripts/ghcr_version_tag.py` takes `-` as its local image, meaning no build. Pinned tags act as before, and a
  missing tag now prints `was not on the registry; it now serves the pinned D` instead of `served None`. An unpinned
  tag with no build is refused, so the step can never push anything the repo has not pinned.
- `.github/workflows/keep-sample-app-tag.yml` (new) reads the one `sample-app-nginx-<v>` tag that
  `backstage/k8s/templated-test-svc.yaml` pins and runs the script with `-` on that file and `images.lock`. It runs on
  a push to staging or main that changes either pin file, the script or the workflow, and on dispatch. It builds
  nothing. The push that brings this change to staging adds the workflow, so it runs then, minutes before the tier
  reaches `test_image_version_tags.py`. Editing the script also starts `build-web-terminal.yml` on that push. #816
  made that run safe: it finds `web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7` on its pinned digest and pushes nothing.

**Tests.** `verify/test_ghcr_version_tag.py` (offline) gains these cases against its loopback registry: a pinned tag
ghcr.io lacks, with and without a build (one put, at the pinned digest, with the pinned manifest's bytes and media
type, and nothing pushed); a moved pinned tag with no build; an unpinned tag with no build, present or not (refused,
nothing put); and `-` on the command line reaching `keep()` as no build. It holds the workflow to calling the script
with `-` on both pin files, to its four trigger paths and to building and pushing nothing of its own. It runs the
workflow's pin step in bash against the repo's templated-test-svc.yaml and checks that the step reads
`tag=ghcr.io/peopleforrester/watch-it-burn:sample-app-nginx-1.27.5`, and that a file pinning two such tags fails the
step. Last, it checks that both pin files pin that tag at one digest. Checked by mutation: with the no-build refusal
removed from `keep()`, three checks fail.

**Live checks run (run 16802).** `python3 verify/test_image_version_tags.py` on the base fails only
`ghcr.io serves …:sample-app-nginx-1.27.5 at the pinned sha256:556e176dd1ac…, anonymously (manifest: HTTP 404)`. It
also passes `the image at sha256:556e176dd1ac… carries usr/sbin/nginx`, so the digest the workflow will put is in the
`watch-it-burn` repository. The cluster read #814 owes did not run: this run's `clusters/kubeconfig` and
`clusters/env` are mode 0640, owner and group `hecaton`, so `kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private` and
`--context watch-it-burn-community` both fail with "permission denied" (hecaton#508). Clusters pull sample-app by
digest, so creating the tag changes nothing on them.

**Not yet run on a cluster or in CI.** The keep-sample-app-tag run started by the push that promotes this change to
staging must log `ghcr.io/peopleforrester/watch-it-burn:sample-app-nginx-1.27.5 was not on the registry; it now serves
the pinned sha256:556e176dd1ac742009bddf70407cb92c84214179a6f45742e67d50523caa2c24`. After it,
`python3 verify/test_image_version_tags.py` passes the sample-app check, and the heavy gate's
`bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` goes green. If that run fails at login or on the put, `GHCR_TOKEN` cannot write to the
package, and #814's escalated `crane tag` is the way to make the tag.

**The suites (run 16802).** On 9709756b, `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 53 checks (the offline suite and 52 tier
tests) in 24m39s. The offline suite ran 240 tests and ended `ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`. The tier exited 1
on `test_image_version_tags.py` alone, on two checks. One is the 404 above, which only the workflow's run on staging
ends. The other was this change's own: the second-tag case in `test_ghcr_version_tag.py` wrote out a
`watch-it-burn:sample-app-nginx-9.9.9` reference, which `test_image_version_tags.py` holds to the pinned tag. The
case now builds that reference from the pinned one, and `test_image_version_tags.py` run alone is down to the 404.

## 2026-11-03 · #826 · C1 fallback reads the beacon count from the view the Night Before checks

**What #826 asked.** Split from #720. The C1 fallback `challenges/c1-exfil-s3/fallback.kubectl.sh` once set
`BEACON_VIEW="https://provisioning.agenticburn.com/beacon/view"`. That host was retired on 2026-10-29 (#651,
`apex-agenticburn#44`) and now answers the apex router's unknown-host 404, so `curl -fsS` read no count, the
"beacon view readable" check failed, and the script exited before its POST. The fix: the fallback's `BEACON_VIEW`

**Why.** Step 2 of question 961's plan (the 2026-10-31 #655 entry) runs `fleet.sh up watch-it-burn-attendee-001`.
For an attendee name, `fleet.sh`'s bootstrap takes the Nth non-admin row of `watch-it-burn/datadog-pool` and `-pool-2`
(`datadog_keys_for`) and refuses the cluster when there is none ("BOOTSTRAP FAILED ... refusing to fall back to the
shared org"). Datadog no longer issues per-student orgs, so no KubeCon pool was loaded (#629), and the 2026-11-02 #608
and #544 entries found the plan stops there. #655, #532 and #608 all wait on that cluster.

**The way chosen is the one question 926 already took.** Question 926 (the 2026-10-30 #587 entry) chose a one-row
pool copied from `watch-it-burn/datadog` for #461's attendee run, so the cluster's own org is Whitney's sandbox org.
#587 made the platform ship that way: on one org the identity script writes no `datadog-admin-secret`, the attendee
collector uses its one-org config, `converge` leaves the cluster alone and `verify/datadog-orgs.sh` passes it as "one
org by design". What was missing was the row itself: nothing in the repo loaded it or took it out again, so each plan
said "load one row" in prose. No fleet.sh change: an opt-out of the refusal would give attendee clusters two paths to
their keys, and `converge`, which resolves keys through the same function, would need the same switch on every call.

**What changed.**
- New `infra/terraform/fleet/datadog-pool-row.sh` with three verbs. `show` prints each pool secret's row count and
  roles, never a key, and what `watch-it-burn-attendee-001` resolves to: nothing (`up` refuses it), `watch-it-burn/datadog`'s
  key, or a pool row's own key. `load` copies `watch-it-burn/datadog`'s api-key, app-key and site into one row with
  role `attendee`, `loaded-by: datadog-pool-row.sh` and empty org, email and password (no attendee gets a Datadog login,
  #647), puts it in front of `watch-it-burn/datadog-pool`, drops any earlier row of its own from either pool, and reads
  the pools back with `datadog_keys_for`'s selection to confirm attendee-001 resolves to that key. `remove` takes out
  only its own rows and leaves every other row as it was; a pool secret that `load` had to create is deleted again once
  it holds nothing else.
- It reads and writes with fleet.sh's account and region (`WIB_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT`, `WIB_SECRETS_REGION`, same
  defaults). A pool it cannot read for any reason but "not found" stops it before it writes, so an access error is
  never taken for an empty pool. Keys never reach a command line: the secrets go through a mode-700 temporary
  directory, jq reads files, and `aws` writes with `--secret-string file://`.
- Putting the row in front, not at the end, matters if the pools still hold DevOpsDays Portland's rows (staged for
  2026-09, expired 2026-09-18 per docs/GO-LIVE-CHECKLIST.md): there attendee-001 would bootstrap on Portland's first
  expired org instead of being refused. `load` prints how many other non-admin rows it found, since each now sits one
  slot later. No attendee fleet is up, so nothing reads those slots.
- `infra/terraform/README.md`'s fleet usage names the step.

**Question 961's run, in order** (the #655 entry's steps, with the first and last added). Each command runs from
`infra/terraform/fleet` in the session with the fleet's AWS profiles.

0. `./datadog-pool-row.sh show`, then `./datadog-pool-row.sh load`. It must print `loaded:`, and a second `show` must
   say attendee-001 resolves to `watch-it-burn/datadog`'s key.
1. `labctl create-event agenticburn burn@2.1.0 <event> <attendance> <hours>`, then `export WIB_EVENT=<event>` in that
   session's shell only.
2. `./fleet.sh up watch-it-burn-attendee-001`; it must log `ingested: watch-it-burn-attendee-001` and no `ingest:`
   failure. With the row loaded, its bootstrap log says "no dual shipping ... datadog-admin-secret absent", which is
   one org as #587 designed it, not a fault.
3. to 5. as the #655 entry has them (the ingests and `labctl status`, the claim and re-ingest, #532's
   `reconcile-pool`, `fleet-hygiene.sh` and `ingest pool`).
6. `./fleet.sh down watch-it-burn-attendee-001`, not `down all`.
7. `./datadog-pool-row.sh remove`, then `./datadog-pool-row.sh show`: the pools are back to what step 0's first `show`

The same step 0 and step 7 go around #544's `WIB_NO_INGEST=1 fleet.sh up 1` and its `down` (the #544 entry's "First,
`watch-it-burn/datadog-pool` needs one non-admin row"), and around #461's run.

## 2026-11-03 · #836 · A test holds #603's save: every row images.lock owes a tarball is dated and in the archive

**Context.** #603 asks to record the digests of the images this workshop depends on and to save them, starting with
laiyer/llm-guard-api:0.3.16. The digests are held by `verify/test_images_lock.py` and `verify/test_images_lock_render.py`,
but no test checked the save: the first accepts `-` in the saved column, and all 70 rows that owe a tarball still
carry it. Test review run 16745 filed this gap as #836.

**The test, split by need.**
- `verify/images_saved.py` is the judge. A row owes a save unless mirror-images.sh `save` skips it (a not-an-image:
  row, or a build: row with digest `-`). A row is saved when its saved column is a date and the archive's
  `manifest.tsv` has a line for its ref at its current digest (the part after the @ for a name@sha256 row), and that
  line's file is in the archive and hashes to the file_sha256 it recorded. Matching on the current digest matters:
  save keeps the old date in the saved column when a digest moves, so a date alone would vouch for a copy of an
  image that was never saved.
- `verify/test_images_saved.py` is `# SUITE: e2e`, not in the tools tier. It reads images.lock and the archive at
  mirror-images.sh's `MIRROR_IMAGES_DEST`, default `~/repos/private/image-archive` on netcup, under michael's home,
  which the gate host cannot read. It names laiyer/llm-guard-api:0.3.16 first, then every owed row, and fails with
  the archive's path when the archive or its manifest is missing.
- `verify/test_images_saved_judge.py` runs offline. It holds the judge to fixture archives: a real save, a name@sha256
  row and one good line among stale ones pass. `-`, a bumped digest, a missing, empty or swapped file, an undated
  line, a path outside the archive and a malformed manifest each fail. It also runs `test_images_saved.py` whole,
  once on an absent archive (exit 1, path named, the llm-guard-api row failed by name) and once in a fixture repo
  whose lock is fully saved (exit 0, until one tarball changes).

The docstrings of the two images.lock tests now point at this test for the save.

**Live check (run 16818).** `python3 verify/test_images_saved.py` on this tree exits 1. Its four failing checks are
the archive directory, its manifest.tsv, laiyer/llm-guard-api:0.3.16 and "no row left unsaved (70 of 70)". That is
the criterion as it stands: #603's save has not run. Through sources, `repo-ls private/image-archive` still answers
"not a directory". This run cannot write under michael's home and has no Docker, so it cannot save.

**Not yet run where it can pass.** As michael on netcup, in this repo on staging:
`~/repos/workflow/llm-coding-workflow/scripts/mirror-images.sh save .`, then commit the dates it writes into
images.lock and run `python3 verify/test_images_saved.py` there. That is #603's remaining step (llm-coding-workflow#372
