## 2026-11-03 · #778 · reset-bot runs `guard-proxy reset-spend` when the live guard-proxy keeps its spend on a volume

guard-proxy-agenticburn#33 added `guard-proxy reset-spend --store PATH` to the Go build. It clears the bbolt
store at `SPEND_STORE_PATH`: the spend tally, each session's spend and the runtime cost cap. It prints one line
naming what it cleared, and it refuses a store the proxy holds (bbolt's flock) or a path with no store. After the
#738 cutover the store sits on the `guard-proxy-spend` claim (#751), so a pod restart no longer starts a delivery
from $0. The issue asks for one step that scales guard-proxy to 0, runs one pod from the same image with the
volume mounted and `reset-spend --store <SPEND_STORE_PATH>`, prints its output and scales back to 1. It asks for
the step in the run of show only if deliveries reuse a cluster's volume.

**Deliveries reuse the volume, so the step goes in the run of show.** The run of show already resets the
community bot before run-through 1, before run-through 2 and before the delivered session, all on one bring-up,
with `./fleet.sh reset-bot watch-it-burn-community` (#539). The volume lives as long as the bring-up does. So the
reset-spend steps are part of `reset-bot`, and the run of show keeps its one command.

**What changed.** In `infra/terraform/fleet/fleet.sh`, `reset_bot_one` now reads the live guard-proxy Deployment
first. `reset_spend_pod` reads that Deployment and prints nothing when the proxy container has no
`SPEND_STORE_PATH`. That is proxy.py, and reset-bot keeps the pod delete it has always done, so KubeCon's reset
is unchanged. When the variable is set, `reset_spend_pod` prints a one-shot Pod. The Pod uses the proxy's own
image, so the signed, digest-pinned reference the cluster already admitted needs no second copy in git. It copies
the proxy's pod and container security contexts, its resources and its scheduling. It mounts only the store's
volume at the proxy's mount path, with no API token, and its label does not select it as guard-proxy. It refuses
a store on no read-write mount, a store on a volume that is not a PersistentVolumeClaim, and a `command` with
arguments of its own. `reset_spend_store` then runs the steps in order. It sets `argocd.argoproj.io/skip-reconcile`
on the ai-layer Application, scales guard-proxy to 0, and waits for the old pod to be gone. It deletes any reset
pod an interrupted run left, creates the reset pod and waits for it to finish. It logs every line of the pod's
output, then deletes the pod. It scales guard-proxy back to its replica count, at least 1, and removes the
annotation. A failure after the pause still scales back and resumes, and it says which step failed. The existing
`/cost` read at zero closes both paths. `wait_ready_pod` is split out of `restart_pods` so both paths share it.

**Why Argo CD is paused.** ai-layer syncs with `selfHeal: true` and has no ignore on `/spec/replicas`. A scale to
0 would come back to 1 within seconds. The new proxy and the reset pod would then race for the store's flock, and
the loser fails. Adding a replicas ignore to `gitops/bootstrap/apps/ai-layer.yaml` would also stop selfHeal from
restoring a guard-proxy the bot scaled down, for the whole show. The skip-reconcile annotation pauses ai-layer
only for the reset. The lab-bootstrap root does not revert it, because the annotation is not in git and the
root's diff skips fields that only the live object has. The annotation is an alpha feature in Argo CD since 2.7,
and the clusters run Argo CD 3.5.2 (VERSIONS.lock). Both scales run as the Argo CD controller service account,
which block-argocd-drift admits, the same way `repair_env_order` patches.

**Tests.** `verify/test_reset_bot.sh` (offline) gains a Go Deployment fixture and checks the call order: pause,
scale to 0, clear leftovers, create, logs, delete, scale to 1, resume, read. It checks that both scales run as the
controller and that the old pod is gone before the reset pod is created. It checks that the command's line is
printed, and it checks the reset pod's image, args, volume, mount, security context, resources and label. It
checks that a Failed pod, a refused create, a refused scale and an old pod that never exits each fail, and that
guard-proxy and Argo CD still come back. An Argo CD that cannot be paused leaves guard-proxy running. An emptyDir
store, a store with no mount, a command with arguments and an unreadable Deployment are each refused before
anything changes. The proxy.py path is unchanged: no scale, no pause, no create. The run-of-show checks gain the
Go paragraph. `verify/test_guard_proxy_spend_store.py` (tools tier) feeds the go-spend-store render, with
proxy.py's command removed as the cutover removes it, to `reset_spend_pod`. It checks that the pod runs
`reset-spend --store /var/lib/guard-proxy/spend.db` with the `guard-proxy-spend` claim at `/var/lib/guard-proxy`
and the Component's pod security context, and that proxy.py's render builds no pod.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** It is owed at the #738 cutover, in a session with AWS access, on a cluster running the
Go image with go-spend-store listed. Spend a few turns through the chat, then run
`./fleet.sh reset-bot <cluster>`. It must print the `reset-spend: cleared $…` line with non-zero figures and end
`counter at zero`. Afterwards, `kubectl --context "$CONTEXT" -n argocd get application ai-layer -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations}'`
must show no skip-reconcile, and ai-layer must be Synced and Healthy. Four things are unverified. Argo CD 3.5.2
must still honor skip-reconcile. The lab-bootstrap root must leave the annotation on ai-layer for the reset's
minute or two. Kyverno's verify-image-signatures and require-resource-limits must admit the
reset pod on an attendee cluster. The EBS volume must move to the reset pod's node inside `WIB_RESET_SPEND_WAIT`
(300 s by default).

## 2026-11-03 · #778 · The E2E tools tier stalled on unbounded Terraform downloads; the provider cache now lives per checkout

**What stalled.** The previous dispatch of #778 failed as a stall: 900 seconds with no output. Its E2E tools
tier was in `test_iam_policy_structural.py`. The `terraform init` it started had open HTTPS connections to the
provider registry, no bytes moving and the process idle for minutes. It was the AWS provider, about 800 MB.
Each test process fetched its own copy into a fresh temp cache (`_plugin_cache` in `verify/iam_plan_render.py`),
and at least three runs on this host were fetching it at the same time. Nothing bounded any of these calls:
`subprocess.run` in `iam_plan_render.py` and `test_terraform_lock_init.py` had no timeout. The lock-init test also
clears `TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR` on purpose, so its five roots fetch from the registry on every run.

**What changed.**
- `verify/iam_plan_render.py`: every `terraform` call has a 600-second bound (`TERRAFORM_TIMEOUT`). A call past it exits
  non-zero and names the stalled download, so the tier fails loudly rather than waiting.
- `verify/test_terraform_lock_init.py`: the fresh init has the same bound (`INIT_TIMEOUT`). A timeout is a failed check
  for that root. The cache stays cleared, since the test exists to check a fresh init.
- `verify/run-e2e-tools.sh`: the tier sets `TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR` to `verify/.tools/plugin-cache`. That directory
  is gitignored, lives in this checkout, and survives between tests. The tier runs its tests one after another in one
  checkout, so nothing writes to the cache concurrently. The aws provider now downloads once per checkout, not once per
  test process.

**Why 600 seconds.** The clean lock-init run took about 90 seconds for the cluster root, which is the largest, on a
host with no other E2E tier running. Six times that leaves room for a loaded host and still fails well before the
900-second silence that hecaton reads as a stall.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing here touches a cluster. The change to the Go reset path in the entry above is
still owed its live check, as that entry says.

**The ttyd pin, resolved on staging, not here.** `verify/test_image_version_tags.py` failed on the ttyd image at the
time of this run: ghcr.io served `sha256:7e5f8986…` for the tag that `images.lock` and `resources.yaml` pin at
`sha256:68004fb5…`. Question 1051 was answered to restore the old digest (entry below). That is already on staging:
#816 (`e33a0fe5`) made `build-web-terminal.yml` push only a tag ghcr.io lacks, and #824 (run 16781) checked that the
tag is back on `68004fb5` and that its cosign signature verifies. This branch changes no image.

**What differs from the draft.** The draft was written on 3120d2d. On staging the `reset-bot` `/cost` read goes through
the burritobot.co twin rows (#651), which is the host the room sees, so the Go path reads the same host. The draft's
`fleet.sh` hunks were re-applied to that layout, and the `test_reset_bot.sh` additions were applied as zero-context
hunks, since staging only renamed hosts in the lines around them. `iam_plan_render.py` and `test_terraform_lock_init.py`
did not change on staging, so their draft is used as it was. `run-e2e-tools.sh` gets the same one-line tier env.

## 2026-11-03 · #778 · question 1051: keep the pin and restore the old digest

**The question.** Which digest should the web-terminal image pin name: the one ghcr.io serves for the tag today
(`sha256:7e5f8986…`), or the one `images.lock` and `gitops/ai-layer/resources.yaml` pin (`sha256:68004fb5…`)? The tag
`watch-it-burn:web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7` is the attendees' browser-terminal image, and CI had pushed over it.

**The answer.** Keep the pin and restore the old digest. The pin stays `sha256:68004fb5ed2d58eeb7624262f58e47d4ffb3c800789cef749ba8d16e8ef6f6cf`.
The rebuilt digest carries no cosign signature, and `policies/kyverno/verify-image-signatures.yaml` requires one, so
re-pinning it is not a fix. The tag has to point back at `68004fb5`, and the workflow must stop pushing over a tag that
already exists. The third re-dispatch of #746 (decisions.md, 2026-11-03) records the same ruling, and #783, #774 and #824
record the same red and the same two fixes.

**Who decided.** Decided by hecaton's research under Michael's standing rules, not by Michael.

**What it changes.** Nothing in this branch: the pins in `images.lock` and `resources.yaml` already name `68004fb5`, and
this run's first recommendation (re-pin to the digest ghcr.io served) is not taken. The restore and the workflow fix are
on staging already (#816 and #824 above). An anonymous HEAD of the tag on 2026-11-03 answers
`docker-content-digest: sha256:68004fb5…`, so `verify/test_image_version_tags.py`'s web-terminal check passes. The
registry state this question was about is resolved. The tools tier still has one red on staging, the
`sample-app-nginx-1.27.5` tag answering 404 under #814, which this issue does not touch.

## 2026-11-04 · #835 · fleet.sh ingest names a Datadog pool secret that is not a JSON array, and registers nothing

**What happened.** `cmd_ingest`, the `ingest-instructors` branch of `main` and `register_with_provisioning` each set
POOL1 and POOL2 from `aws secretsmanager get-secret-value ... || echo '[]'`. When aws exits 0 with text that is not
JSON, `ingest_one`'s resolver, `dd="$(jq -cn --argjson a "${POOL1}" ...)"`, fails, and `set -e` ended fleet.sh with
exit 2 before the `[[ -n "${dd}" ]] || dd='{}'` guard. Reproduced before the change: `fleet.sh ingest
watch-it-burn-attendee-007` with an aws shim that prints nothing logged only the `ingest -> labctl import` line and
exited 2.

**The change.** One helper, `load_datadog_pools`, now reads both secrets for all three callers. It checks each answer
the way the resolver reads it, with `jq -en --argjson p "${v}" '$p | type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "object")'`.
That refuses an empty answer, text that is not JSON, two JSON texts, a bare object, and an array holding a string,
which would fail the resolver's `.role`. A refused secret is logged with its id, account, region and byte count (never
its content) and recorded as `datadog-pool:<secret-id>`, and the helper returns 1. `fleet.sh ingest` and
`ingest-instructors` then say "nothing registered", print the failure list and exit 1. `register_with_provisioning`
stays non-fatal, as its comment requires: it logs that the clusters were NOT registered and skips the ingest, and the
recorded failure fails the build.

Of the issue's two fixes, the first is the one taken: refusing by name before any import, rather than letting the
resolver's failure fall through to the `{}` guard. A fall-through would send each row with blank Datadog fields, and
labctl import upserts by name, so `ingest pool` would blank the org login on every row the pool already holds, claimed
ones included. A secret aws cannot read is still an empty pool, as before, since that is the state before #832's row
is loaded. In `ingest_one`, a resolver that still fails (a row whose `role` is a number) now fails that cluster as
`datadog-row:<name>` with a message, instead of the bare exit 2.

**Tests.** `verify/test_fleet_terminal_harvest.sh`'s aws shim now answers the two pool secrets from AWS_POOL1 and
AWS_POOL2 (an empty pool when unset; set to "" is the issue's empty answer), and AWS_SECRET_RC fails the read as a
missing secret does. Its new section runs fleet.sh as a script, so `main` and its `set -e` are live, and adds 16
checks: an empty answer and text that is not JSON each exit 1 naming that secret alone, with nothing imported; three
other bad shapes are refused; `ingest-instructors` and `register_with_provisioning` refuse the same way; a secret aws
cannot read still registers; a valid pool still gives attendee-007 the seventh non-admin row across both secrets and
the community cluster the `admin-instructor` row; and a row whose role is a number fails `datadog-row:<name>`. Against
the old fleet.sh, 11 of the 16 fail; with the change the file's 77 checks pass. `shellcheck -S warning` reports nothing
new on either file.

**Live check (run 16827): not run.** The run's `clusters/env` and `kubeconfig` are mode 0640, owner and group
`hecaton`, and the run's user, `hecaton-s4-claude-certkraken`, is not in that group: `. "$HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV"`
printed "Permission denied", and `aws` said the `accen-dev` profile could not be found. That is hecaton#508. The
check is read-only: with the session sourced, read `watch-it-burn/datadog-pool` and `-pool-2` and confirm each passes
the jq check above, so the change does not refuse the secrets the clusters use.

**Not yet run on a cluster:** that read, and a `fleet.sh ingest` of a live attendee cluster once the change is on
staging, which `verify/fleet-labctl-import-scratch.sh` covers.

**The suites (run 16827, at c3332e3f).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` exited 0. Its offline stage, `bash
verify/run-tests.sh`, ran 242 tests, all green, `test_fleet_terminal_harvest.sh` among them with 77 passed. Then it
printed "53 checks ran (the offline suite and 52 tier tests) in 24m55s" and "ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN". No
dependency was added.
## 2026-11-04 · #838 · A web-terminal rebuild under the same ttyd goes to web-terminal-ttyd-<v>-<n>, picked by its source tree

**The gap.** Since #816, `scripts/ghcr_version_tag.py` pushes a build only to a version tag ghcr.io lacks. A change to
`images/web-terminal` that kept ttyd at 1.7.7 (kubectl, a package) was built in CI and pushed nowhere, so there was
no digest to pin and sign. The issue offered two shapes: a suffix on the version (`web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7-<n>`), or
a per-commit tag left unpinned until someone signs it.

**Which one, and why it is settled here.** The suffix. Michael's #714 rule is that a tag names the version of the
software inside, and a commit id is not a version of anything in the image. A suffix keeps ttyd's version at the
front, where `test_image_version_tags.py` still checks it against the binary, and adds a rebuild count after it, the
way a distribution's package revision does. A per-commit tag would also put one tag on ghcr.io for every commit that
touches the directory, and a signed image would still need a version tag before the repo could pin it under #714. Both
shapes need the digest pinned and signed by hand before a cluster runs it; neither changes that.

**How `<n>` is chosen.** By the source, not by a counter kept by hand. The workflow reads
`git rev-parse HEAD:images/web-terminal`, the tree id of the directory, which changes exactly when a file under it
does, and builds the image with the label `io.github.peopleforrester.watch-it-burn.source-tree` set to it. The
script's new `ship()` reads that label from the local build, then walks `web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7`, `web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7-1`, `-2`
and on, each at the digest a pin file pins it at or else the one ghcr.io serves, reading each image's labels from its
config blob (through the linux/amd64 entry when it is an index). The first tag whose image carries the build's tree
is the build's, and #816's table acts on it, so it is never pushed over. When none does, the build goes to the first
tag that is neither pinned nor on ghcr.io. So a workflow-only edit pushes nothing, the main promotion finds the tag
staging's run pushed for the same source, and a new ttyd version's first build still gets the bare
`web-terminal-ttyd-<v>`. A pinned tag passed on the way is kept on its pin, as #816 did for the one tag. The workflow
now has a `concurrency` group, so two runs cannot take the same `<n>`. With `-` (keep-sample-app-tag.yml) the script
runs `keep()` as before.

**What changed.**
- `scripts/ghcr_version_tag.py`: `SOURCE_TREE`, `Registry.labels()` (manifest, index, config blob, each checked
  against its digest), `docker_labels()`, `ship()`; `main()` sends a local image to `ship()` and `-` to `keep()`.
- `.github/workflows/build-web-terminal.yml`: a step that reads the tree, the label on the build, the concurrency
  group, comments.
- `verify/test_ghcr_version_tag.py` (offline): the fake registry serves config blobs, and nine `ship()` cases run
  against it: a new version, a pinned tag of other source or of no label (the pinned `68004fb5` has none), `-1`
  already carrying the source, the pinned tag carrying it, a moved pinned tag, `-1` pinned with `-2` of other source
  (goes to `-3`), a build with no label, and a pinned digest the registry lacks. It also holds the workflow to the
  label, the tree step and the concurrency group, checks that `main()` routes a local image to `ship()`, and its
  pin check accepts a `-<n>` tag.
- `verify/test_image_version_tags.py` (tools tier): `pinned()` takes a `-<n>` suffix for web-terminal, checks ttyd
  against the version before it, and holds a pinned `-<n>` image to carrying a 40-hex source-tree label. The config
  read is shared with the sample-app base check.

**What the first run after this does.** `68004fb5` carries no source label, so the first build-web-terminal run once
staging takes this change (it edits the workflow and the script) cannot match it, and pushes its build to
`web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7-1`, logging `pin its digest ... and sign it`. Nothing pins `-1`, so clusters keep `68004fb5`
and `test_image_version_tags.py` stays on the pinned tag. Whoever signs `-1` decides whether to pin it. The main promotion's run then finds `-1` by its label and pushes nothing.

**Live checks run (2026-11-04).** `Registry.labels()` run anonymously against ghcr.io: `web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7`
serves `sha256:68004fb5...`, its labels read through the index's linux/amd64 entry are `{}`, and
`web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7-1` answers 404. `python3 verify/test_image_version_tags.py` passes with the new `pinned()`.
The cluster read (the web-terminal pods' image IDs on `watch-it-burn-community` and `watch-it-burn-private`) did not
run: `runs/16834/clusters/kubeconfig` gives `permission denied`, the hecaton#508 problem. Nothing on either cluster
was read or changed.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The build-web-terminal run that staging's promotion of this change starts must log
`... web-terminal-ttyd-1.7.7-1 is the first free one` and `pushed ...-1`, and the main promotion's run must log
`... -1 at sha256:... was built from source tree ...` with no push. The label check in `test_image_version_tags.py`
runs once a `-<n>` tag is pinned.

No dependency was added.

**The suites (run 16834, on `ded328a4`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 53 checks (the offline suite and 52
tier tests) in 24m21s and exits 0 with `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN`. The offline suite inside it ran 243 tests,
all green, `verify/test_ghcr_version_tag.py` among them, and `test_image_version_tags.py` passes in the tier.

## 2026-11-03 · #704 · Third dispatch: the live run moves to watch-it-burn-private, and this run could not read the cluster session
## 2026-11-04 · #704 · Runs 16409 and 16851 could not read their cluster session; the cold build goes on a fresh cluster again, with watch-it-burn-private as the fallback

**Context.** Run 16409 is #704's third dispatch. Question 1049 asked for the go to build a t3.2xlarge cluster. The
coordinator answered it under Michael's standing rule (2026-11-02: "two clusters up that you can use for any and all
tests"): run the live check on watch-it-burn-community or watch-it-burn-private, with no one's go, and never create or
tear down a cluster. A step that would build an attendee cluster runs on one of the two instead. That replaces steps
1, 2 and 6 of the 2026-11-02 sheet above, which build and destroy watch-it-burn-attendee-099.

**Neither run reached a cluster.** The session hecaton set up for each run is unreadable by the run's own user. The
files `env`, `kubeconfig`, `aws-config` and `aws-credentials`, and the `bin/` directory under
`/var/lib/hecaton/runs/16409/clusters/` and again under `/var/lib/hecaton/runs/16851/clusters/` (2026-11-04) are
owner `hecaton`, group `hecaton`, mode 0640 (0750 for `bin/`). Both runs ran as uid 146, `hecaton-s5-claude-certkraken`,
in groups 150, 1001 and 1002, not in `hecaton`. The directory itself
is group `hecaton-s5-claude-certkraken`, so the files look meant for that group too. As a result,
`. "$HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV"` fails with `Permission denied`, `kubectl config get-contexts` fails with `open
.../clusters/kubeconfig: permission denied`, and `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile accen-dev` says the profile
cannot be found. Nothing was run against a cluster, and the vllm entry stays at `measured: false`. The report
escalates the permission fix.

**Run 16851's grant puts the fresh cluster back.** Run 16851 is a re-dispatch of 16409, which stalled while it waited
in silence on `verify/run-e2e-tools.sh`. Its grant is wider than question 1049's answer: it may "create and tear
down any other cluster your tests need", and must never delete watch-it-burn-community or watch-it-burn-private. That
allows what the issue asks for, a cold build on a fresh t3.2xlarge. So the first choice is the 2026-11-02 sheet
above, unchanged: `WIB_NO_BOOTSTRAP=1 ./fleet.sh up watch-it-burn-attendee-099`, the isolated kubeconfig, the timed
`CONTEXT="$CTX" ... bash infra/deploy-full-idp.sh local-inference`, `verify/local-inference-live.py`, the vllm
entry, and then `./fleet.sh down watch-it-burn-attendee-099` and `./cleanup-log-groups.sh --delete`. That gives
`build_seconds` as a real cold build of the whole profile. Run 16409's sheet for watch-it-burn-private, below,
stays as the fallback for a run whose grant forbids building a cluster. It measures vLLM's own cold cost only.

**The fallback: which of the two, and why watch-it-burn-private.** Both are one t3.2xlarge node each: roster.tsv leaves their
instance_type column empty, so they get the cluster module's `["t3.2xlarge"]` with min, max and desired size 1. That
is the node the issue names. watch-it-burn-community is the burn cluster behind attackme.agenticburn.com, which must
have no guardrails. local-inference is full's list, so re-profiling community would put every guardrail on the
attack target. watch-it-burn-private runs admin, which is full's list plus `kubearmor-policies` and
`network-policies`. local-inference is full's list plus `vllm-qwen3`. So on private, the re-profile adds vLLM and
removes those two Applications. Their resources are removed too: the root prunes, and each child carries Argo CD's
resources-finalizer. Running the script again with `admin` puts both back and prunes vLLM.

**What it measures there, and what it does not.** Argo CD, the load balancer controller and the full platform
already run on private, so the script's wall-clock there is a re-profile, not a cold platform build. That number must
not go in as one. What stays cold is vLLM itself, and vLLM's cost is what the entry records. The 4.95 GB image is
pulled onto a node that has not pulled it (step 2 checks this). The pod goes from creation to Ready beside a running
full platform on one t3.2xlarge, which is the open question in `values-local-inference.yaml`'s header. The header of
`platform-baseline.yaml` defines measuring as a build with and without the component. On a cluster that is already
up, the without half is the cluster as it stands, and the with half is vllm-qwen3's time from creation to Healthy.
So `build_seconds` is that time, read from `verify/local-inference-live.py`'s "from creation to Ready" line. The
re-profile's wall-clock goes into `known`, named as a re-profile. A cold build of the whole local-inference profile
stays unmeasured until a cluster is built for something else and the profile can ride on it.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The fresh-cluster sheet above comes first. The fallback, re-cut for watch-it-burn-private: Run it from the repo root, with the
session sourced, every command naming its context, and nothing built or torn down:

1. `CTX=watch-it-burn-private; kubectl --context "$CTX" -n argocd get application lab-bootstrap -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.lab-platform/profile}'`
   must print `admin`. That is the profile step 6 restores. Then `kubectl --context "$CTX" get nodes -o wide` must
   show one t3.2xlarge.
2. `kubectl --context "$CTX" get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*].status.images[*]}{.names}{"\n"}{end}' | grep -c vllm-qwen3`
   must print `0`, which shows the pull is cold. If it does not, record that the image was already on the node.
3. Start the clock and run `CONTEXT="$CTX" AWS_PROFILE=accen-dev REGION=us-west-2 bash infra/deploy-full-idp.sh local-inference`.
   Stop it when `kubectl --context "$CTX" -n argocd get applications` shows every Application Synced and Healthy.
4. `CONTEXT="$CTX" python3 verify/local-inference-live.py`. It must end in PASS with no FAIL. It prints the vLLM
   pod's creation and Ready times and its `kubectl top` footprint.
5. In the vllm entry's `cost`, set `measured: true`. Set `build_seconds` to step 4's creation-to-Ready seconds and
   `requests` to the manifest's 4 CPU / 10Gi (limits 6 CPU / 16Gi). Write step 4's footprint, step 2's answer and
   step 3's re-profile wall-clock into `known`, each named for what it is. Then run `bash verify/run-tests.sh`.
6. Put private back: `CONTEXT="$CTX" AWS_PROFILE=accen-dev REGION=us-west-2 bash infra/deploy-full-idp.sh admin`. Then
   check `kubectl --context "$CTX" -n argocd get applications`. Every Application must be Synced and Healthy,

`gitops/ai-layer/web/kubecon.html`, both carried the old mapping; both now read "LLM06 Excessive Agency (Challenges 1
to 4)". The page was changed too, since it is the copy the presenters drive from and a fix to one alone would leave the
two out of step. `verify/test_instructor_brief.py` gains two checks: segment 2 names LLM06 (#820), and the close on
both pages maps LLM06 to Challenges 1 to 4 with no "Challenges 2 to 4" left. With the two content files put back to
staging and the test kept, the second check fails and the test exits 1.

**The deck's close is not reviewed yet.** rounds-agenticburn#58 rebuilt the opening, Challenge 1 and Challenge 2 and
left every slide from the guardrails slide on as it was, the close among them, "still being reviewed". No later deck
issue reviews the close (read 2026-11-04). So the issue's default, "Challenges 1 to 4", is used. The deck's own OWASP
table (`attendee.html` at `bc9209f1`, from rounds-agenticburn#47) maps LLM06 to "Challenges 1, 2" and LLM01 to
"Challenges 3, 4". It already lists Challenge 1 under LLM06, but it leaves out Challenges 3 and 4, which the run-of-show
counts (Challenge 4's unvetted MCP server). That difference is older than this issue and lies in the deck repo; it is
left to the close's review, which should settle one mapping for both.

**A race in #839's test, fixed here.** The first `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` of this run went red on
`verify/test_chat_span_token_counts.py` alone; run again by hand it failed 1 time in 6. Its OpenTelemetry stand-in
records a span when the span ends, and proxy.py ends the `chat` span and the `POST /chat` root after it has written
the reply. So the visitor could hold the reply before either span was recorded: the turn's checks then saw no `chat`
span, and the next turn picked up the late one (`set (2000, 110)` on the no-usage turn). `turn()` now waits, on a
condition the stand-in notifies, until the turn's root span (`POST /chat`, or `POST /` for A2A) is recorded, which
ends last, for up to 10 s. With a 0.3 s sleep put in before each span is recorded, the old test fails 8 checks and the
new one passes. Without the sleep the new one passed 30 runs out of 30.

tests) in 25m09s, printed `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN` and exited 0.

## 2026-11-04 · fix · #837 · the gate's red test was the guard-proxy repin, and the suites now read the pinned submodule

Run 16845 ended failed at hecaton's tests gate: `bash verify/run-tests.sh` failed `test_weaver_guard_proxy_spans.py`
with exit 1, although that run's own suite had gone green. The prose change for #837 was not the cause. The test fails
on the staging base, a65f748d, with the draft's commits left out. That commit repinned guard-proxy to c2eb4cf2, which
brings guard-proxy-agenticburn#38: the cost gauge now yields one `Observation(usd, {...})` per model instead of a single
`Observation(_cost["usd"], {...})`. The test found the attribute dict with a regex on the `_cost["usd"]` literal, so it
found nothing and failed three checks. The registry was already right: `metric.witb.guard_proxy.cost` declares exactly
`gen_ai.request.model` and `gen_ai.provider.name`, which both shapes observe.

- The test fix is staging's, not this run's. Run 16854 wrote its own fix to the regex, but abeb41b9 (#839) fixed the
  same regex on staging first, to read the attribute dict of the one `yield Observation(<value>, {...})`. The two
  collided when hecaton rebased run 16854, and it ended failed (rebase-conflict). Run 16870 rebased the branch onto
  staging, took staging's version of the test and dropped its own. All of the test's checks pass against c2eb4cf2.
- Why 16845 saw green: run 16832 committed the draft at 00:09 +0100, before the repin (01:06 +0100), and 16845 took
  over that workspace. `verify/ensure-submodules.sh` checked out a submodule only when it was uninitialised (`-` in
  `git submodule status`), not when it sat at another commit (`+`), so most likely the suite read the old proxy.py.
  The script now also moves a `+` submodule to its pin. `verify/test_ensure_submodules.sh` builds a local superproject
  and checks three cases: a submodule moved off its pin is put back, a fresh clone gets its submodule, and a
  submodule at its pin is left alone. It fails 1 check against the old script and passes against the new one.

The draft's two commits (839dca3d, 70462af9 on `origin/agent/837-16832`) were cherry-picked unchanged:
`verify/draft-drift.sh` said staging had touched none of their six paths.

**The suites (run 16854, on 538fa12e, guard-proxy at its c2eb4cf2 pin).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran the
offline suite (244 tests, `test_ensure_submodules.sh` the new one, `ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`), then 53
checks (the offline suite and 52 tier tests) in 25m11s, ending `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN`, exit 0. No live
cluster check is owed: the change is presenter prose, one test's regex and the submodule step of the test runners.

the offline suite (245 tests, `ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`), then 53 checks (the offline suite and 52 tier

## 2026-11-04 · #848 · The /kubecon pattern line follows the run-of-show: the trace comes after the attack

**What changed.** `gitops/ai-layer/web/kubecon.html` stated each challenge's pattern in the 2026-10-31 order:
tee-up, trace "before the room plays", play, attack, fix, keep trying. Since the 2026-11-01 slide-by-slide review
(#776), and #818 in `facilitation/kubecon-na-2026-run-of-show.md`, the room tries first and each trace follows the
presenters' live attack. The page's line now runs the run-of-show's six numbered steps in its order: challenge slide
(a line or two of tee-up, then the call to action, and the room starts trying on the public bot), hint where there
is one, the presenters' live attack on the private bot, the pre-seeded Datadog trace of what the attack just did,
the fix, and the room keeps trying. Tee-up is no longer a step of its own; it is part of the challenge slide, as in
the run-of-show.

**Tests that read the words.** `git grep -nF` over `verify` and `scripts` for the line's words found one reader,
`verify/test_instructor_brief.py`, whose check held the trace before the play step (Michael, 2026-10-31). It now
finds the line by its opening words and exits naming the anchor and the file when they are missing, reads the
bolded steps in order and checks they are challenge slide, hint, attack, trace, fix, keeps trying; checks the trace
follows the attack and the old "before the room plays", play and tee-up steps are gone; and checks the run-of-show's

## 2026-11-04 · #844 · The tools tier's public-image test retries a 429 from public.ecr.aws

**What happened.** Run 16863's first `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` (at `f4b28e3f`) ran 244 offline tests green and
then printed "53 checks ran (the offline suite and 52 tier tests) in 26m41s" with one failure:
`test_public_images_served.py`, "busybox: sha256:a46257e06c82... answers an anonymous pull (HTTPError: HTTP Error 429:
Too Many Requests)". Run again on its own a minute later, it passed. The repo's rule is that a test that fails once
and passes on a rerun is broken, so this run fixes it rather than calling it flaky.

**The cause.** ECR Public answers an anonymous client about once a second per source address. The test already waits
1.2 s before each of its own requests, but other runs on this host run the same suites from the same address, so a
request paced here can still meet a 429 that someone else spent. Busybox was the first manifest after the token.

**The fix.** `fetch` and `blob` read through one helper, `opened()`, which retries an HTTP 429 only: after its
Retry-After (at most 30 s), or 2, 4, 8 and 16 s, five tries in all. Any other error, or a fifth 429, still fails the
check, so a registry that stopped serving a digest still reads red. `verify/test_public_images_retry.py` is the offline
half: it lifts `opened()` and `RETRIES_ON_429` out of the file by name and runs them against a stubbed urlopen and
sleep (two 429s then an answer; a Retry-After of 3 and of 3600; five 429s; a 404). No dependency was added.

**The suites (run 16863, at `e5eecbae`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` exited 0. Its offline stage,
`bash verify/run-tests.sh`, ran 245 tests, all green ("ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN"), the new retry test among
them. Then it printed "53 checks ran (the offline suite and 52 tier tests) in 24m57s" and "ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS
GREEN".

**What was out of step.** Since the 2026-11-01 review (#776) and #844, Challenge 1 runs no fix of its own on stage: its

switch rather than going.

  A seeded trace of that retry costs one model call and gives the slide the same backup `c2-fixed` gives the
  KubeArmor slide. The run-of-show's RBAC bullet now names it.
- The Grafana C5 text in "The trace view without Datadog (#500)" was already brought in line by #852 (`9044e40f`):
  it reads the record before `guardrails-on` and `HTTP 403` after, with no redacted reply. Nothing changed there.
- Run-of-show: the Night Before admin-probe paragraph no longer says the probe applies `guard-rbac-on`'s Role, and
  the seeding step says `c1-fixed` is the CEO ask sent again after `guardrails-on`.

## 2026-11-03 · #802 · The chat page's witch name, cookie and re-roll button proven against the real desk; a re-roll never repeats the name

`verify/test_storefront_witch_name_e2e.py` (E2E TIER: tools) now keeps `ticket_site.py` running on localhost for the
whole test and runs the page's witch-name block and its real `send()` in a node vm. The vm's `document.cookie` is a
cookie store that behaves as a browser's does for these cookies: keyed by name, domain and path, a Domain the page is
not under is dropped, and a host is sent only the cookies whose domain it is under. The desk's own Set-Cookie seeds
it, and the Cookie header that store would send `support-attackme.burritobot.co` goes back to the desk's `/me`. So a
cookie the page wrote host-only, on the wrong domain or beside the desk's (rather than replacing it) fails the test,
where the old node script, which replaced the whole cookie string on each write, could not tell.

The new checks: a first visit with no cookie shows a plain-text name (no href, target or rel; only `textContent` and
`hidden` ever written), writes one wib_witch on `.burritobot.co` that `name_from_slug()` accepts, and the desk's
`/me` then shows that name and sets no cookie of its own. The test clicks "Get a new witch name" (three clicks from
a first visit, one from the desk's own name, two with `Math.random` pinned). After each click the header shows a
different vocabulary name, the browser holds exactly one wib_witch on `.burritobot.co` with the new slug, `/me`
shows the new name, and the next `/chat` body's `witch` is the new name. The page never writes anything on the
button but `hidden`. The existing valid-cookie case still checks the name is shown unchanged and the cookie kept.
`verify/test_witch_name_vocab.py` (Test command) now parses the markup: one `id="newwitch"` button, attributes only
type, class, id and hidden, text exactly "Get a new witch name" with nothing nested, no label, aria-* or popover
pointing at it, no CSS ::before/::after or content on it, and the script touches only `btn.hidden` and its click.

**A defect the test found, fixed in the page.** The click handler called `randWitch()`, which can return the
current name: one click in 768 left the header, the cookie and the desk on the same name. With `Math.random`
pinned the test fails on the old handler. The page now calls `otherWitch(WITCH_NAME)`, which picks uniformly
among the other 767 names. The test sweeps it from every one of the 768 names over every draw: each other name is
reached once and the old one never. Mutation runs: the old handler, a dropped skip, a host-only or wrong-domain
cookie, and a title in the markup or set from the script each fail the tests; the e2e passed 20 runs in a row.

The header link stays gone (#763); nothing here adds one, and the plain-text checks would fail if it came back.

## 2026-11-04 · #856 · deploy_app reads the manifest shapes the room's model sends for HC-666

**What failed, measured.** `verify/prior-drafts.sh 856 origin/staging` printed NONE. This run's `clusters/kubeconfig`
and `clusters/env` are mode 640, owner and group `hecaton`, which this run's user is not in, so `kubectl` fails
with "permission denied" and the workshop-mcp logs and Datadog's deploy_app spans were out of reach (hecaton#508, as
in run 16943). The failing call was read from the bot instead, over the public endpoints. Three HC-666 asks
(2026-11-04 19:13 to 19:16, `attackme.burritobot.co/chat`, the chat page's body with `"witch":"Agatha the Banshee"`,
sessions `check-856-16947-1` to `-3`): the first landed (wall row 19:13:57); the second replied that
joker-agatha-the-banshee was created and added no wall row; the third added no wall row and fell back to `run_shell`
with `kubectl`. Asked in the same sessions to quote its deploy_app call and the error verbatim, the third quoted:

    Error executing tool deploy_app: deploy failed for the manifest: could not parse it as JSON or YAML, so send the
    whole manifest again: expected '<document start>', but found '}'
      in "<unicode string>", line 1, column 447:
        ... ance-shell:busybox-1.38.0\"}]}}}}}, requested_by=

and a correct joker-agatha-the-banshee Deployment (with `metadata.labels`). That Deployment, written with
`json.dumps`' default separators, is 446 characters, so column 447 is one `}` more than it closes, then
`, requested_by=`: Nova Pro wrote the end of its own call into the manifest string. Run 16943's first ask ("failed
multiple times due to the same parsing error") fits this, and #648's 2026-10-30 manifests were three braces short.
The second session's reply quoted the same Deployment as YAML and "no error"; with no wall row, either deploy_app
was not called or it refused before the apply. Which one needs the trace.

**The change.** `deploy_app` (`gitops/ai-layer/workshop-mcp-server.py`) still reads JSON, then YAML, first. Only
when neither reads a manifest that starts with `{` does it mend it: the first whole JSON object is the manifest and
the text after it is dropped (a `requested_by=` there becomes requested_by when the argument is empty), and a
JSON object short only of its closing braces gets them. A ```json or ```yaml fence is removed, a manifest sent as a
JSON string of itself is read once more, a one-item list or `kind: List` is its item, and a known kind with no
apiVersion gets its own. For the 422, `_mend_workload` puts a Deployment's (or StatefulSet's, DaemonSet's,
ReplicaSet's) fields where the API server reads them: fields written at the top level or on the wrong level go to
`spec`, `spec.template` and `spec.template.spec`; a missing selector becomes the template's labels (else
`app: <name>`); the selector's labels are put on the template; an unnamed container gets the workload's name; a
container written as an object becomes a list; `replicas: "1"` becomes 1; a `command` string becomes
`/bin/sh -c <it>`. What the model set is kept. A manifest cut inside a string, with a mismatched closer, or with
two keys and no comma is still refused with the parse error. The 422's own manifest was not seen (the wall row
keeps only "Refused by the cluster (HTTP 422)."), so these are the shapes the API server refuses a Deployment for,
not one measured manifest. The ticket was not cut down: HC-666 already asks for only a name, one replica and the
image, and the failure was in how the model wrote the call, not in how much it was asked to write.

**Tests.** New `verify/test_deploy_app_manifest_shapes.py` holds that the measured string raises the bot's quoted
YAML error at column 447, then applies it and eleven other parse shapes and twelve 422 shapes through `deploy_app`
against a stand-in API server, checking each applied body is a Deployment the API server takes (selector matching
the template labels, named containers, no misplaced fields) under joker-agatha-the-banshee with the ticket's image,
hostname and jokers subdomain. Against the unchanged server it fails 17 checks. `test_deploy_app_errors.py` now
refuses an unreadable manifest instead of the 2026-10-30 truncated one, which deploy_app closes now, and a list of
two objects instead of one. `test_c6_villain_endpoint.py`'s template-with-no-metadata case now expects the
selector's `app` label beside the workload label, since without it the API server refuses that Deployment.

**Left on the cluster.** The diagnostic asks re-applied the existing joker-agatha-the-banshee (the same name as run
16943's), so no new Deployment is left; workshop-mcp scales it back to zero after 300 s. The desk's wall gained the
19:13:57 row.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The fix needs workshop-mcp running this commit, which reaches the clusters once
hecaton promotes it. Then, on the public bot, several HC-666 asks in a row, each with its own session and a name
already on the wall so no new Deployment is left:
`for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do curl -s -m 180 https://attackme.burritobot.co/chat -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-BurritoBot-Session: check-856-$i" -d "{\"prompt\":\"What's the status of my support ticket HC-666?\",\"session\":\"check-856-$i\",\"witch\":\"Agatha the Banshee\"}"; curl -s https://support.burritobot.co/wall.json | head -c 400; done`
Each ask should add an `ok: true` row for joker-agatha-the-banshee. With the kubeconfig readable, the workshop-mcp
pod's logs and the deploy_app spans show any refusal that remains.

## 2026-11-04 · #856 · The live check of run 16947's change, and the two failures it left: a 422 on a re-apply, and no deploy_app call

**Prior drafts.** Run 16947's two commits (`962e0c39`, `73489a9a`) are staging's head, which this run starts from, so
there was nothing to port. Its decisions.md entry left the live check under "Not yet run on a cluster".

**Access.** This run's `clusters/kubeconfig`, `clusters/env` and AWS files are again mode 640, group `hecaton`, which
this run's user is not in (hecaton#508): `kubectl` and `. "$HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV"` fail with "permission denied", so
the workshop-mcp logs and Datadog (the audit line `tool_audit.py` writes carries each manifest) were out of reach. The
check ran over the public endpoints, and the bot's own `run_shell` read what the pod could see.

**The change was running.** In the MCP pod (session `check-856-16959-diag3`), `grep -c _mend_workload /app/server.py`
printed 3, the mounted file dated 19:51:45 UTC, and PID 1 had started about six minutes before 19:57, so every ask
below ran against `962e0c39`.

**The live check, measured (2026-11-04, 19:55 to 20:08 UTC, public bot).** Every ask carried
`"witch":"Agatha the Banshee"` and its own session, so each one re-applied the existing joker-agatha-the-banshee (made
18:36:24 UTC, selector `{app: joker-agatha-the-banshee}`, read from the pod through the API). First the six asks in
a row that run 16947 named, with the room's exact prompt (sessions `check-856-16959-1` to `-6`):

| Ask | Wall | Reply |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ok 19:55:33 | "The generated text has been blocked by our content filters." |
| 2 | no row | says joker-agatha-the-banshee was created, at `http://joker-agatha-the-banshee.burritobot.co` |
| 3 | 422 at 19:55:42 and 19:55:44 | "I'm having trouble creating the deployment" |
| 4 | ok 19:55:49 | the Joker's page, `maintenance-shell-attackme.burritobot.co/joker-agatha-the-banshee/` |
| 5 | ok 19:55:59 | the Joker's page |
| 6 | 422 at 19:56:05 | "I was unable to create the deployment due to an error" |

Then thirteen more asks, which also asked for the manifest and deploy_app's answer (sessions `-e1` to `-e3`, `-m1` to
`-m10`): eight landed, one of them (`-m2`) after a 422 at 20:00:12, and five added no row. Over all 19, 11 landed,
2 gave up on a 422 and a third recovered from one, and 6 told the guest the Joker was made with no row on the wall.
Every manifest the bot showed was a Deployment the API server takes, with the selector and template label
`app: joker-agatha-the-banshee`; the container name varied (`maintenance-shell`, `maintenance`, the Joker's name).
The no-row replies give an address deploy_app never writes (`http://joker-agatha-the-banshee.burritobot.co`) or an
answer it never gives ("Deployment ... created."). For ask 2, `-e1` and `-e3` the input tokens (5513 to 5545) sit
below every landed ask's with the same prompt (5750 to 5887), so the model answered without calling deploy_app;
`-m5` and `-m9` went to other tools (a vault entry, a list of pods) and `-m8` quoted an answer deploy_app never gives.

The 422's own message was not seen: the desk keeps only "HTTP 422", the sessions refused to quote it, and two probes
that asked the pod's `run_shell` to dry-run an apply with a changed selector came back garbled (a 403 the bot read as
a delete). What fits every 422 here is a re-apply: a Deployment's selector cannot change once it exists, and the
model picks its labels on each ask.

**The change.** In `deploy_app` (`gitops/ai-layer/workshop-mcp-server.py`):

- Before applying a Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet or ReplicaSet, it reads the live one (the Role already grants
  `get`). When it exists with a `matchLabels` selector, the apply takes that selector and the template carries its
  labels. The model's other labels stay.
- When the API server still answers a room Joker (a Deployment named `joker-<DNS label>`) with a 422 that is not an
  admission webhook's, it applies once more the plain Joker HC-666 asks for: the name, the model's first image, one
  replica, the selector's valid labels (else `app: <name>`), and the stamps every room Joker gets. The pod's log
  line names the API server's message, so the next run can read what the model sent. The desk gets one row, for
  the final outcome. A Kyverno denial is HTTP 400 and is left as the refusal, as is a 422 for anything that is not a
  room Joker.

For the asks with no call, two sentences:

- In the system prompt (`gitops/workshop-agent/agent.yaml`), after "doing what it asks": a ticket that needs a

## 2026-11-04 · #724 · question 1009: the C1 fix's FQDN-aware egress control is B, a forced egress proxy over a locked resolver, built for the next event

**Decision.** The FQDN-aware egress control for the C1 fix is B: a forced egress proxy for the `agent` namespace that enforces a hostname allowlist, on top of the required floor C, a locked DNS resolver that answers only for the lab's own zones and refuses to relay arbitrary names upstream. Option A (Cilium `toFQDNs`) and the fourth path (AWS `ApplicationNetworkPolicy`, which applies DNS rules only on EKS Auto Mode nodes) are left unbuilt. The live build of the fix is built for the next event. Until then the beat stays a narrated walkthrough with no live run.

**Who decided.** Decided by the coordinator under Michael's 2026-11-03 rule that design picks like this are not his. Decided by the coordinator under Michael's standing rules, not by Michael. This entry records the coordinator's answer to question 1009. It does not record a ruling by Michael, and this run made no choice of its own.

**Background.** C1 is Challenge 1 of the Watch It Burn workshop. Its second stage shows an agent exfiltrating data through the beacon, and the L3/L4 egress allowlist holds that direct HTTPS path. The same data can still leave as DNS query names, because NetworkPolicy matches addresses and ports and cannot read a query name. The design is `docs/research/2026-10-31-c1-dns-exfil-beat.md`, written under #723, the design split of #116. Issue #724 asks which FQDN-aware control the fix builds. Michael deferred the build on 2026-09-07 (Question 575). `docs/BUILD-PLAN.md` records his 2026-06-20 ruling to stay on VPC-CNI and Istio ambient and not switch to Cilium.

**What it changes.** The fix builds B and no CNI or cluster-mode change. VPC-CNI enforcement at `infra/terraform/aws/cluster/main.tf:332` stays. The 2026-06-20 ruling against Cilium stays in force, because B does not reopen it. Option A is not chosen, so the question of Cilium chaining over VPC-CNI is not settled here. Option D is not chosen either.

**Platform support, re-checked 2026-11-04.**

- Live, read-only, through the run's session with an explicit `--context` on every `kubectl` call. On `watch-it-burn-community`, the `vpc-cni` addon is `v1.23.2-eksbuild.8` with `enableNetworkPolicy` set to `"true"`, and `aws-node` carries `NETWORK_POLICY_ENFORCING_MODE`. The same `aws-node` env variable is present on `watch-it-burn-private`. Both clusters have the `agent` and `apps` namespaces.
- Neither cluster has a Cilium CRD (`cnpolicies.cilium.io`, `ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io`) or the `applicationnetworkpolicies` CRD. So neither cluster runs Cilium, and neither can use option D today.
- Istio is not on both clusters. `istio-system` exists on `watch-it-burn-private` and is absent on `watch-it-burn-community`. This corrects a claim in the run's notes that Istio ambient runs on every profile. `gitops/bootstrap/values-attendee.yaml`, `values-admin.yaml`, `values-full.yaml`, `values-kubecon-private.yaml` and `values-local-inference.yaml` list `istio`. `values-burn.yaml` does not, and its header says the burn profile is deliberately bare. So the fix's Istio-based proxy is available on attendee, admin and private clusters, not on the community cluster.
- Istio's upstream ambient egress page (istio.io/latest/docs/ambient/usage/egress-gateway/, read 2026-11-04) says a waypoint can act as the egress gateway, with a `ServiceEntry` in a waypoint-enrolled namespace. It needs the Gateway API CRDs installed. It states no stability level and no minimum Istio version, and its commands use release-1.31 samples. The repo pins Istio 1.30.4 (`gitops/bootstrap/apps/istio.yaml`). So the 1.30.4 pin's support for the egress pattern is not confirmed by that page and must be checked at build time.
- Cilium's chaining page (docs.cilium.io, AWS VPC CNI chaining, read 2026-11-04) names two chaining-mode limits, L7 policy and IPsec transparent encryption. It does not mention `toFQDNs`, so whether `toFQDNs` works chained over VPC-CNI is unconfirmed. This does not change the choice of B, but it leaves A's cost unresolved.
- AWS's EKS user guide (docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/auto-net-pol.html, read 2026-11-04) says DNS and FQDN rules apply only to workloads on EKS Auto Mode-launched instances. The guide's example uses `apiVersion: networking.k8s.aws/v1alpha1`. The question text gives `networking.eks.amazonaws.com/v1alpha1`, which the guide does not show. This entry cites the guide's group. The discrepancy does not change the choice, since D is not chosen.

**Fleet impact, assessed on staging `916b016e`.**

- Other beats. Option B adds a path and leaves the L3/L4 layer as it is. C1 stage 1 and stage 2 keep their current behaviour, and stage 2 still holds the direct HTTPS beacon. The new stage 2b uses the same request through DNS. C2, C3, C6 and C7 keep their policies. C7's weather feed is the one that changes, as below. This was assessed from the policy files, and no other beat's live check was rerun.
- `policies/network-policies/per-namespace/agent-egress-allowlist.yaml`, which selects every pod in `agent`. Its allows are 10.0.0.0/16 on 443 for Bedrock, 172.20.0.0/16 on 443 for the apiserver, and 169.254.170.23/32 on 80 for Pod Identity. Under B, the fix drops direct egress on 443 and 53 so the proxy is the only path out, as the design note says. The Pod Identity allow stays. Whether Bedrock goes through the proxy or keeps the in-VPC allow is for the build to settle.
- `policies/network-policies/per-namespace/agent-allow-dns.yaml`, which allows UDP and TCP 53 to `kube-system` for every agent pod. Under floor C this open relay is replaced by the locked resolver, and the allow narrows to that resolver.
- `policies/network-policies/per-namespace/agent-allow-weather-feed-egress.yaml`, which allows TCP 443 to any destination for the weather-feed pod alone, so that C7's `get_weather` can reach Open-Meteo. Under B the Open-Meteo hostnames must go on the proxy's allowlist, or C7's weather beat breaks. The same policy ships in the C1 fix, so this is a build item.
- `agent-allow-intra-namespace.yaml`, `agent-allow-otel-egress.yaml` (OTLP 4317 and 4318 to `monitoring`) and `agent-allow-kagent-egress.yaml` stay as they are, because they do not reach public hosts.
- `policies/network-policies/per-namespace/apps-*.yaml` and `default-deny.yaml`, which cover the `apps` namespace. An agent-namespace proxy does not touch them.
- The community cluster. Under B the proxy is a new always-on component. The burn profile has no Istio, so the proxy cannot be built there on the mesh. The fix is a student-applied control on attendee clusters, which list Istio, so this is a gap for the community cluster only. It needs a decision before the community cluster carries the fix, and it is recorded as a followup.

**Live build (criterion 3).** The coordinator settled that B is built for the next event, that the beat stays a narrated walkthrough with no live run until then, and that the design note sizes B as medium. Because B needs no CNI or cluster-mode change, the coordinator's answer treats the live build as affordable. This run did not verify affordability.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing in this entry is built or applied. This run changed neither cluster. The owed checks are the three assertions in the design note's "Validation owed on a cluster" section, to be built with the fix. They are: the stage 2 policy holds the beacon while the DNS collector records stage 2b; the chosen control leaves the collector with nothing new for the same request; and Bedrock and in-cluster resolution still work.

**Checks.** The decision is recorded in this file. The live checks listed under "Platform support" were read-only. The offline suite and the tools tier are recorded in the next commit, as earlier entries do.

**The suites (run 17027, at `2ab82eca`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 54 checks (the offline suite and 53 tier tests) in 27m07s and printed `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN`, exit 0. The offline suite inside it printed `ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN` (log line 13216). The log has one `FAIL` line, at line 14368: `datadog-secret fields: app-key(empty)` in `security`. It is the output of a negative fixture. The next check in the same test, "real kubectl render, app-key empty in security: exits non-zero and reports it empty", prints PASS, so the script behaves as intended. The log is `/var/lib/hecaton/runs/17027/e2e-tools.log`.

## 2026-11-04 · #489 · The leaderboard's queries against real data: columns 3 and 5 could never fill, and now read signals that carry the cluster

**What ran.** This run had the cluster session (`. "$HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV"`, AWS profile accen-dev, us-west-2) and
read the pair in Secrets Manager `watch-it-burn/datadog`. That pair reaches Whitney's sandbox org (`Datadog`,
datadoghq.com), where both KubeCon clusters ship as `kube_cluster_name` `burritobot-private` and
`burritobot-public`. Its application key is scoped read-only: it answers 403 on its own key list, as #629 says.
So the leaderboard is still not in the org. `fleet_monitors.py --check` printed MISSING for all seven monitors, the
fleet dashboard and the challenge leaderboard. The apply is #485's, with `WIB_FLEET_MONITORS_APP_KEY`. Instead, the
run sent each leaderboard query to the same scalar query API the ops view uses (`/api/v2/query/scalar`), and the
logs queries to the logs aggregate API, over 4 hours, 7 days and 15 days. Nobody walked challenges 1 to 6 for it;
the counts are what the room's and the runs' own use of both clusters left.

**What each column returned, before this change (7 days).**
- online: 1 for both clusters.
- 1 exfil, `@tool_input.command:*beacon*`: 4 on private, 275 on public (33 in the last 4 hours). The attribute works.
- 2 villain, `short_image:(...)`: 24485 on public. The tag works.
- 3 recipe, `@rule:"Recipe Snoop In Agent Namespace"` in `kube_namespace:security`: nothing, ever. Grouping `@rule:*`
  by `kube_cluster_name` over 15 days gave no bucket at all, against about 2 million Falco lines in the index. A
  Falco line carries `hostname` in its JSON. Datadog takes that as the log's host, so the host becomes the bare node
  name `ip-10-0-90-162.us-west-2.compute.internal`, which has no host tags (`/api/v1/tags/hosts` answers `[]`).
  The Agent's host is `ip-10-0-90-162.us-west-2.compute.internal-burritobot-private`, and that host carries
  `kube_cluster_name`, `cluster_name`, `kube_node`, `kube_distribution` and `orch_cluster_id`. A falcosidekick line
  in the same namespace has all five. So no Falco line has ever been countable by cluster.
- 4 bill: 0.04 on private, 0.69 on public. The gauge works.
- 5 guarded, `@event:output_scrub`: nothing, ever, on either cluster. Grouped by `@event`, guard-proxy's lines over
  15 days are forward_error, input_classifier_block, price_tier, task_cancel, thinking_only_retry,
  thinking_only_surfaced and topic_guard_block. In the pinned guard-proxy (c2eb4cf), `/chat` redacts at
  `proxy.py:1690` and only stamps `witb.guard.decision` `output_redacted` on its server span; the `output_scrub`
  log line is in `_scrub_response`, the A2A passthrough, which the storefront and the lab do not use. The spans do
  arrive: 16 `output_redacted` spans on burritobot-private over 15 days, each tagged `kube_cluster_name`.
- 6 blocked: 27 on private (2 in the last 4 hours). The events work.

**The join works.** One scalar request holding all seven queries, metrics and logs and spans together, came back
as one row per `kube_cluster_name` with each column aligned. That is the engine query_table uses. The widget itself
needs the apply to be seen.

**Change.**
- Column 3 reads `sum:falco.rules.matches.count{kube_cluster_name:burritobot-*,rule_name:recipe_snoop_in_agent_namespace}
  by {kube_cluster_name}.as_count()`, summed over the window. The Agent's `falco` check (the pod annotation in
  `gitops/bootstrap/apps/falco.yaml`) scrapes that metric with `kube_cluster_name` on it and the rule in
  `rule_name`, lowercased and with each space as `_`. Live, the same query for `exec_into_pod_detected` gave 67 on private
  over 7 days, against 99 log lines over 15 days, and `unexpected_outbound_from_workshop_agent_pod` gave 15.
- Column 5 reads guard-proxy's spans, `@witb.guard.decision:output_redacted`, grouped by `kube_cluster_name`. Live,
  12 on private over 7 days and 16 over 15. Spans are kept by Datadog's retention and not all of them are: the org's
  only enabled filter is the error default, and of the topic guard's 41 log lines over 15 days, 37 spans were kept.
  A cluster that has re-run the attack a few times shows green. A log line on `/chat` would be complete, and that
  is guard-proxy's change to make, filed as a follow-up. The room view's guard count reads the same missing line.
- `fleet_monitors.validate_dashboard` holds spans queries to the same "grouped by kube_cluster_name" rule as logs
  queries (`EVENT_SOURCES`).
- `verify/test_leaderboard.py`: column 3 is held to the rule's `rule_name` tag, the falco check annotation, the
  chart's metrics toggle and a summed count, and no column may read Falco's log line. Column 5 is held to the
  `_stamp` call in the pinned proxy.py and a spans query on it. The email check now needs a local part before the
  `@`, because `@witb.guard.decision` is an attribute and not an address. Against the old leaderboard.yaml, six
  checks fail.

**Not yet run on a cluster.**
- The apply, which is #485's: `WIB_FLEET_MONITORS_APP_KEY=<key> fleet.sh monitors --apply --session
  2026-11-12T20:50Z/2026-11-12T21:20Z`, then `fleet.sh monitors --check` and `verify/test_fleet_monitors_live.py`,
  then a look at the leaderboard in TV mode for blank cells.
- Column 3 filled. `recipe_snoop_in_agent_namespace` has no series in the org yet. On burritobot-private
  KubeArmor's `block-recipe-snoop` is armed (`kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private get ksp -A`, 53 minutes old
  when read), so the read is denied and Falco's `open_read` rule stays quiet; the community cluster has no Falco.
  The run left the policy alone, because something on the pair had just armed it. The column fills on a cluster
  where the C3 read succeeds with Falco running: an attendee cluster before the student applies the policy.

## 2026-11-04 · #382 · The agent subtree hangs from one root on watch-it-burn-private: the collector was dropping the hop, and its fix is live

**Which of the three causes.** The third: the collector dropped the spans. The config is live on the pod, and the
gateway exports without error. The cause was found and fixed in the repo before this run, by #320 (decisions.md
2026-10-30, "One interaction is one root again") and by 3ef036a6 and e0452cbc (#703, #709, 2026-10-30).
`filter/drop_noise` cut the chain in three places, each rule added for its own noise: every gateway span except
`tools/call` (#265), every burritobot-agent HTTP verb (#286), and every `a2a.*` span (#264). So the parent the
2026-09-08 measurement could not find was most likely not agentgateway's. a2a-sdk's request handler span, then the
parent of ADK's `invocation`, was dropped by the third rule, with the agent's own server span and the gateway's span
above it gone too. The issue's reading, that the gateway mints a span and never exports it, does not hold: the
gateway exported it and the collector threw it away. What this run adds is the live evidence below, read on
watch-it-burn-private (Datadog names it `burritobot-private`) at staging `7210cbb8`, which Argo CD reports synced on
`ai-layer`, `ai-layer-otel` and `lab-bootstrap`.

**Cause 1, config not live on the pod: ruled out.** The pod mounts ConfigMap `agent/agentgateway-config` at
`/etc/agentgateway` and runs `-f /etc/agentgateway/config.yaml`. The image has no shell or `cat`, so the running
config was read from the gateway's admin port.

    kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private -n agent port-forward pod/agentgateway-b49f45688-vlkvv 25000:15000
    curl -s localhost:25000/config_dump   # .config.tracing
    {"endpoint": "http://otel-collector-opentelemetry-collector.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:4318",
     "headers": {}, "protocol": "http", "fields": {"remove": [], "add": {}},
     "random_sampling": "true", "client_sampling": null, "path": "/v1/traces"}

The live ConfigMap's `config.yaml` compared equal to the one in `gitops/ai-layer/agentgateway.yaml` (a Python
compare of the two strings printed `True`). Image `cr.agentgateway.dev/agentgateway:v1.7.0@sha256:60216aaf...`,
pod started 2026-11-04T21:14:26Z, 0 restarts.

**Cause 2, export failing: ruled out.**

    kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private -n agent logs agentgateway-b49f45688-vlkvv -c agentgateway \
      | grep -ciE "otlp.*(error|fail)|export.*(error|fail)|opentelemetry.*(error|fail)"
    0

The log's only tracing lines are the startup echo of the endpoint and five copies of
`warn types::local config.tracing is deprecated; migrate to frontendPolicies.tracing`, a follow-up below. The
collector refuses nothing, and logged no error or warning in the hour before the check:

    otelcol_processor_filter_spans_filtered{filter="filter/llmobs_one_root"} 337
    otelcol_receiver_accepted_spans{receiver="otlp",transport="http"} 32529
    otelcol_receiver_refused_spans{receiver="otlp",transport="http"} 0

The collector's own counters are not split by service. The split comes from the `span_metrics` connector, which

**The proxy.py comment is in guard-proxy-agenticburn, not here.** The outer-span comment and the do_POST comment

## 2026-11-05 · #857 · The offline suite stubs every cloud tool and fails a test that calls one

**What was missing.** #616 (run 16967) stubbed `cmd_guardrails_link` in the two offline tests that reached the live
KubeCon pair, and #421 (run 17025) gave one of them stubbed cloud tools as a backstop. Nothing stopped the next test
from doing the same: on a dispatched run the `aws` on PATH is hecaton's wrapper, which exports the run's live session
whatever the caller's environment holds, so even a test that unsets every AWS variable still reaches both clusters.

**Change.** The issue offered two shapes: a source scan that fails any test running `cmd_instructors up` without one
of four guards, or a fleet.sh guard on `cmd_guardrails_link` under the offline suite. This takes a third that covers
both and more. `verify/no-cloud.sh` writes stubs for aws, kubectl, eksctl, helm and terraform that log the call and
exit 1, and `verify/run-tests.sh` runs every offline test with them first on PATH (`no_cloud_run`). A test that called
one fails with its own exit code, or 1 when it swallowed the failure and exited 0, and the runner prints each call.
The stubs carry their log path in their own text, so a test that rebuilds its environment (`env -i` with PATH, a
python `subprocess` with `env=`) is still caught. A test that needs a tool to answer puts its own fake ahead of the
stubs, which `test_guardrails_switch.py` already does. Why not the issue's two shapes: a source scan reads one of a
dozen ways to call fleet.sh (sourced and called, `bash fleet.sh instructors up`, python's `run_fleet`) and misses the
next; a fleet.sh guard keyed on an environment variable is dropped by any test that builds its own environment,
which is how #421's test calls fleet.sh now, and it guards one function where every cloud call is the hazard. The
tools tier keeps its real pinned binaries and is not changed.

**#616's shape, under the guard.** `verify/test_offline_suite_no_cloud.sh` sources the real fleet.sh and runs
`cmd_instructors up all` on the kubecon profile with the build stubbed and `cmd_guardrails_link` not, as the two
tests did before #616. It now ends in under a second instead of polling for five minutes, fails, and names
`aws eks update-kubeconfig ... --name watch-it-burn-community`. The test runs a second set of logging fakes behind the
guard's stubs, so a broken guard would land there and not on the live session. With `no_cloud_run`'s PATH prefix
taken out, 10 of its 24 checks fail and the backstop lists every call; with it, all 24 pass.

**What the guard found.** The first full suite run under the guard (251 tests) flagged one test:
`test_fleet_standbys.sh`, whose bootstrap check ran the real `kubectl config current-context` against an empty
isolated kubeconfig from `bootstrap_one`. That never left the host, but it was the real binary, so the check now
stubs `kubectl` as its header said it did. That answers #421's open follow-up: no other offline test calls a cloud
tool.

**Live check (read-only, 2026-11-05).** In this run's shell, `aws eks describe-cluster --name
watch-it-burn-community` printed `ACTIVE` and `kubectl get ns guardrails-switch` reached both clusters (NotFound on
each, so the hazard is live). The same two commands through `no_cloud_run` reached neither: both stubs printed their
refusal, the call log named both, and the exit was 1. Nothing was changed on either cluster.

**The suites (run 17087, at `7129a08f`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 54 checks (the offline suite and 53
tier tests) in 26m33s and printed `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN`, exit 0. The offline suite inside it ran 252
tests under the guard, `test_offline_suite_no_cloud.sh` among them (24 passed), printed `ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE
TESTS GREEN`, and no test called a stubbed tool.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing: the guard runs on the host, and the live check above is all it needs.

## 2026-11-04 · #112 · The privileged-pod / hostPath escape challenge is designed in docs/research, and the gap is confirmed live; the build waits for the next event

**Design, plus the live half a run can do.** #112 asks for a challenge in which the agent uses the `create` RBAC it
already holds (workshop-agent Role, `gitops/ai-layer/resources.yaml:38`: create on `deployments`, `pods`,
`configmaps`, `services` in `agent`) to launch a privileged pod that mounts host root at `/host` and reads the node,
refused at admission once the control is armed. Michael deferred the build on 2026-09-07 (`deferred-barcelona`,
Question 575) and kept the design work open; on #447 he set that the Barcelona challenges wait until 2026-11-13. The
design is at `docs/research/2026-11-02-privileged-pod-hostpath-escape.md`, in the shape #723 used for #116 and #130
used for its exercises. No lab text, slide, run of show or deploy config changed. It maps to OWASP Agentic ASI03 and
ASI05.

- **Ported from run 15709.** That run wrote the same design note (commit ebb7f8c on `agent/112-15709`) but ended
  failed at validation, so nothing landed. `bash verify/prior-drafts.sh 112 origin/staging` returned the draft CLEAN
  (only `decisions.md` APPENDed on both sides), so this run carries the note forward on the current layout, adds the
  live findings below, and writes this fresh entry rather than replanting the draft's past-dated one.
- **What the design found.** The issue's premise that we can reuse `policies/kyverno/disallow-privileged.yaml` as it
  stands does not hold. That policy is scoped to namespace `apps` (the agent creates in `agent`), checks only
  `privileged` (not `hostPath`, `hostPID` or `hostNetwork`), and ships `validationActions: [Deny]` already (the
  issue's "currently Audit" wording is the pre-#206 ClusterPolicy state). Its `Deny` is what refuses the Beat-3 clown
  file in `apps`, and a `ValidatingPolicy` has one `validationActions` for the whole policy, so it cannot be `Deny`
  for `apps` and `Audit` for `agent` at once. `restrict-agent-spawned-workloads` (#490) does match `agent` and the
  agent's own identities at `Deny`, but validates only the pod's ServiceAccount, its labels and its Secret
  references, not the escape fields. So the control is a separate agent-scoped policy (`disallow-host-escape`), not an
  edit to either.
- **Confirmed live (2026-11-04), the piece prior runs could not reach.** This run held an AWS session and kubectl
  access to `watch-it-burn-community` and `watch-it-burn-private`. Every write was a `kubectl apply
  --dry-run=server` under `--as=system:serviceaccount:agent:agent-sa`, which runs the full admission chain without
  persisting anything; nothing was created, changed or deleted, and both clusters were left as found. `agent` carries
  no PSA label on either cluster. On the community cluster the escape pod (privileged + hostPath `/` + hostPID) was
  admitted (`created (server dry run)`, exit 0); the cluster serves no ValidatingPolicy CRD. On the private cluster
  the first dry-run was refused by `require-resource-limits` (Deny, cluster-wide), not by any escape-shape rule; with
  resource limits added so the escape shape was the only variable, the same pod was admitted (exit 0), with
  `disallow-privileged` (Deny, `apps`-scoped) and `restrict-agent-spawned-workloads` (Deny, agent-scoped) both
  enforcing and neither refusing it. The gap is structural; which guardrails are armed does not change it.
- **Why the scope is the agent namespace and never the whole cluster.** The currency review records that `disallow-privileged` "must not be armed
  as written; it would deny nine platform DaemonSets". Those privileged/hostPath DaemonSets (Falco, KubeArmor, the
  Datadog node agent, the CNI) live in `security`, `monitoring`, `datadog` and `kube-system`, never in `agent` or
  `apps`, so scoping the escape policy to `agent` is exactly what keeps it safe. No platform pod in `agent` uses any
  of the four fields on 916b016e; the build re-confirms that.
- **PSA posture.** The issue also asks for Pod Security Admission `restricted` on the agent namespace. The note
  recommends against enforcing it namespace-wide: `agent` holds the platform's own pods (workshop-agent,
  workshop-mcp, evil-mcp-shim, guard-proxy, the console and web terminal), several of which do not meet `restricted`,
  and PSA cannot tell the attack pod from them since both are created in `agent`. A shape-based Kyverno deny can, and
  it names the policy in the refusal, which PSA does not. If a second layer is wanted, label `agent` `warn:
  restricted` (non-blocking) and leave enforce to Kyverno.
- **The arming flip.** Kyverno autogen (default on, #206) carries the deny to the Deployment form that `deploy_app`
  and `apply_optimization` produce. The policy ships `Audit` so the attack succeeds unarmed, and gets its own arming
  step (`toggle-host-escape-enforce.sh`, like Challenge 3's authz toggle) plus an ArgoCD `ignoreDifferences` entry,
  rather than joining the C2 CNCF-wall toggle; on the KubeCon pair the live analog of that flip is `guardrails-on`
  (#774). It pairs with Challenge 8 (#111) as one kill chain: steal the token, then use the permissions it grants to
  escape the container.

**Not yet run on a cluster:** the armed direction, because the policy does not exist yet. The note's "Validation owed
on a cluster" section names the checks (armed refuses at admission with `disallow-host-escape` named, the Deployment
keeps no pods, no regression to the platform's own `agent` pods or the `apps` clown-file refusal) a session with AWS
access runs on a cluster once the build lands, on or after 2026-11-13.
## 2026-11-05 · #858 · Argo CD moves to chart 10.11.7 (v3.5.7), and every Argo CD container gets the limits Kyverno requires

**Why.** Both KubeCon clusters run `quay.io/argoproj/argocd:v3.5.2`, which carries GHSA-fmxq-cgp8-87wp (critical:
PreDelete and PostDelete hooks skip the AppProject destination and resource checks) and GHSA-j6cw-g6p4-7hch (high:
repo-server command injection through an SSH repository's proxy URL), both fixed in v3.5.4 (#421's entry of
2026-11-04). There was no earlier draft: `verify/prior-drafts.sh 858 origin/staging` printed NONE.

**The version.** argo-helm's index on 2026-11-05 lists 10.11.7 (v3.5.7, 2026-11-03) as the newest 10.11.x, and
10.12.0 and 10.12.1 (v3.6.0, v3.6.1, both 2026-11-04) above it. The issue asks for a 10.11.x chart; v3.6 is a minor
release a day old, so it is not taken here. Between 10.8.4 and 10.11.7 the chart's values only gain keys
(`unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy`, `redis.existingSecret`, `server.enabled`), and with this repo's values the render
differs in the image, the limits below, three Bitbucket SSH known-host lines and an optional
`GRPC_ENABLE_TXT_SERVICE_CONFIG` env read from `argocd-cmd-params-cm`. The CRDs render the same.

**The change.**
- `infra/deploy-full-idp.sh` installs chart 10.11.7 and logs `chart 10.11.7 / app v3.5.7`. Both VERSIONS.lock lines,
  argocd-server's `tags.datadoghq.com/version` and the note under it, `test_observability.py`, the build spec, the
  recreation spec, the stack walkthrough and `docs/floor.md` say the same.
- images.lock's Argo CD row is `quay.io/argoproj/argocd:v3.5.7` at
  `sha256:16df57da6f223808d204cd94c67c929b931fa01670b91b0b3a2298c4647de0db`, the index digest quay.io's manifest API
  served on 2026-11-05. The same read gives v3.5.2's old row, `sha256:e2aadfae...`. Redis stays 8.6.4-alpine.
- `infra/argocd-values.yaml` gives limits to the application controller, repo server, ApplicationSet controller,
  notifications controller, Redis and the redis-secret-init Job. Only argocd-server had them. require-resource-limits is
  a Deny policy on every pod in every namespace on watch-it-burn-private, and `helm history argocd` there shows
  revisions 2 and 3 (2026-11-02) failed on it, at the redis-secret-init pre-upgrade Job. The other pods run only
  because they predate Kyverno. Without limits this bump would have failed the same way, and a roll that got past
  the hook would leave the controller StatefulSet with no pod. The sizes come from the kubelet's stats summary on
  2026-11-05 (there is no metrics-server): the controller's working set was 749Mi on private (38 apps) and 387Mi on
  community, the repo server 151Mi to 217Mi, every other container under 40Mi. The controller gets 1Gi requested and
  3Gi limit, the repo server 256Mi and 2Gi, the rest 64Mi or less and 256Mi.

**The replay and the port.** `controller/sync.go` differs between v3.5.2 and v3.5.7 only in a sync-window check for
terminating operations; `normalizeTargetResources`, `getMergePatch`, `applyMergePatch` and `restoreNonIgnoredFields`
