## 2026-11-05 · #860 · question 1077: the community cluster never carries the C1 DNS-exfil fix, so the burn profile gains no Istio

**Decision.** The community cluster never carries the fix for Challenge 1's stage 2b, the DNS-exfiltration beat.
The burn profile (`gitops/bootstrap/values-burn.yaml`) gains no Istio, and the fix's forced egress proxy is not
rebuilt without the mesh. Option B from question 1009 (#724) is built once, on the Istio ambient layer of attendee
and admin clusters.

**Who decided.** Decided by hecaton's research under Michael's standing rules, not by Michael. This entry records
that answer to question 1077, which run 17167 asked. The run made no choice of its own.

**Background.** Question 1009 (#724, 2026-11-04) chose option B, an egress proxy that all `agent` namespace
traffic is forced through, over a locked resolver. Run 17027 found that the planned proxy uses Istio ambient as an
egress waypoint, and that the community cluster runs no Istio. Issue #860 asked whether the burn profile gains
Istio or the proxy is built without the mesh. Question 1077 added a third option, that the community cluster
never carries the fix, and that is the answer.

**Why.** The burn profile's header says it is deliberately bare, with nothing defending the agent, and that this
stays as it is. The design note (`docs/research/2026-10-31-c1-dns-exfil-beat.md`) already sets the community
cluster at stage 1, egress open, and puts the policy and the fix on admin and attendee clusters, which run Istio.
So nothing is added to the cluster built to burn, and no Istio upgrade is forced. The upgrade question is still
open for attendee and admin clusters: the repo pins 1.30.4, and Istio's ambient egress page shows 1.31 samples.

**What it changes.**
- `docs/research/2026-10-31-c1-dns-exfil-beat.md` gains a "Where the fix runs" paragraph under the fix's options.
- `gitops/bootstrap/values-burn.yaml` gains a header comment saying the profile carries no Istio and why. Its app
  list is unchanged, so the rendered profile and `verify/test_bootstrap_chart.py`'s counts are unchanged.
- `values-kubecon-community.yaml` (#774) is unchanged. Its guardrails-on egress step still applies
  `challenges/c1-network-policy.yaml`, the L3/L4 stage 2 policy, which leaves the DNS path open. A later breakout
  profile that wants the full fix on its community cluster makes that choice in its own issue.

**Live check (run 17167, 2026-11-05, read-only, explicit `--context` on every call).** On `watch-it-burn-community`
the `lab-bootstrap` Application renders `values-burn.yaml`, and there is no `istio-system` namespace and no Istio
Application. On `watch-it-burn-private`, `lab-bootstrap` renders `values-admin.yaml`, and `istio-base`,
`istio-cni`, `istio-mesh-config`, `istiod` and `ztunnel` are present. Run 17178 changed neither cluster.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing is built. The fix's three owed checks stay as the design note lists them, for
attendee and admin clusters only.

## 2026-11-05 · #862 · A test that fails until the leaderboard is applied and every column fills

**Why.** Test review run 17104 found that nothing checks #489's criterion, "apply the challenge leaderboard to the
next event's instructor org and confirm every column fills". `test_fleet_monitors_live.py` runs `--check`, which
only finds the board by title, and `--data`, which skips every dashboard but the fleet one (`DATA_DASHBOARDS`),
because the leaderboard is blank until the room plays. The per-column counts in #489's entry came from one-off
queries.

**Change.**
- `fleet_monitors.py --board --cluster NAME ...`, read-only. It finds the leaderboard in the org and reads its
  definition back by id. It fails as DRIFT when the org's table differs from `leaderboard.yaml` in its window, any
  query's source, filter (whitespace aside), aggregator or grouping, or any column's formula, title or green rule.
  Then it sends the table's whole request, all seven queries and all seven formulas, in one
  `/api/v2/query/scalar` call over the widget's 4 hours. That is how query_table joins metrics, logs and spans on
  `kube_cluster_name`. A cell is filled when it is green under its column's conditional format (online, 1, 2, 3, 5
  and 6 at 1 or more), or above 0 for the bill, which has no green rule. Each named cluster must fill every column;
  each blank is printed as `BLANK    challenge leaderboard / <column>: <cluster> (<value>)`. `--data` is unchanged.
- `verify/test_leaderboard_live.py` (`# SUITE: e2e`, so `run-e2e.sh` runs it) runs `--board` for
  `WIB_LEADERBOARD_CLUSTERS`, default `burritobot-private`: the KubeCon cluster with Falco, since column 3 never fills
  on the Community cluster. The cluster has to have been walked through challenges 1 to 6 in the 4 hours before.
- `verify/test_fleet_monitors.py` drives `--board` through the fake org, which now stores each dashboard body it is
  given and answers a joined scalar request. Covered: a full board passes with one joined request and no writes. Each
  blank column fails and names the column and cluster: no value, a count of 0, a bill of 0, online at 0. With two
  clusters only the blank one is named. A missing board fails before any query, and a changed query, aggregator,
  green rule or window is DRIFT. A joined answer with no `kube_cluster_name` column fails. `--board` needs a
  `--cluster`.
- `fleet.sh` usage and `infra/datadog-fleet/README.md` describe `--board`.

**Live check (run 17194, 2026-11-05 00:27Z, the sandbox org `Datadog` through `watch-it-burn/datadog` as accen-dev in
us-west-2).** `python3 verify/test_leaderboard_live.py` printed `MISSING  challenge leaderboard 'Watch It Burn:
challenge leaderboard': not in the org` and exited 1, with `WIB_LEADERBOARD_CLUSTERS` set to `burritobot-private`
and again to both clusters. That is the correct verdict: #489's criterion does not hold yet. The secret's
application key is read-only, so the board cannot be applied from a run. To check the half after the lookup, the
run called `table_scalar` and `filled` directly on the repo's table. The joined answer came back as one
`kube_cluster_name` column and one number column per formula, named by the formula, which is the shape the code
reads. Over 4 hours: burritobot-private filled online, 4 bill (0.073) and 6 blocked (2), with 1, 2, 3 and 5 blank.
burritobot-public filled online, 1 exfil (33) and 4 bill (0.42), with 2, 3, 5 and 6 blank. Over 7 days: private
had online, 1 (4), 4, 5 (12) and 6 (27), public had online, 1 (275), 2 (24485) and 4. Those are #489's counts, so
the joined request reads the same data the single queries did. Column 3 is blank on both clusters over both
windows, as #489 recorded: `recipe_snoop_in_agent_namespace` has no series in the org yet. Nothing was written to
the org or to either cluster.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** `verify/test_leaderboard_live.py` passing, which is #489's work and needs three things.
First, the apply with Whitney's write key: `WIB_FLEET_MONITORS_APP_KEY=<key> fleet.sh monitors --apply --session
START/END`. Second, a cluster with Falco and without KubeArmor's `block-recipe-snoop` walked through challenges 1 to
6. Third, the test run within 4 hours of that walk. The DRIFT comparison has not yet read a board that Datadog
stored. If Datadog rewrites a query string on save, the first run after the apply prints `DRIFT ... query <name>
differs: the org has (...)`, and the comparison is then fixed to normalize that rewrite.

## 2026-11-05 · #863 · The cause-comment tests read an issue's comments with gh's token, not GitHub's anonymous quota

**What happened.** In run 17065 (#814) the tools tier failed on one check alone: GitHub answered
`verify/test_dispatched_runs_cause_comment.py`'s anonymous read of #633's comments with 403, "0 anonymous requests
left this hour". Every dispatched run on the host shares one IP and so one quota of 60 anonymous requests an hour,
and the test printed it as "GitHub answers an anonymous read ... with at least one" failing, which reads as a missing
comment. Its result hung on a quota other runs spend, which "Tests own their inputs" forbids.

**The change.** `verify/gh_comments.py` (new) reads an issue's comments with `gh issue view <n> -R <owner/repo>
--json comments`, which sends gh's token (`gh auth login`, or GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN) and refuses to read without
one. There is no anonymous read left to fall back to. Its `check_read` prints the read's checks in order, each only
when the one before it held: gh on PATH with a token (no gh, or gh's exit 4, names the missing token and how to give
one), the rate limit not spent (gh's "rate limit" or HTTP 429 is its own named failure), gh answering, and at least
one comment. So a spent quota now reads as a spent quota. All three cause-comment tests had the same anonymous
`urllib` read, so all three move to the helper: `test_dispatched_runs_cause_comment.py` (#633),
`test_agent_obs_cause_comment.py` (#783) and `test_prose_gate_e2e_wait_cause_comment.py` (#796).

**Why `gh issue view` and not `gh api`.** The issue offered either. On this host gh is a wrapper that runs gh as
michael. Dispatched runs get the wider form, which allows `gh api` GETs, but the promotion gate's user gets the
read-only `/var/lib/hecaton/cli/sources`, which refuses `gh api` ("gh api is not a read-only command this allows")
and allows `gh issue view`. The gate runs the tools tier, so `gh api` would have turned it red on every promotion.
`gh issue view --json comments` reads every comment through GraphQL, which names a GitHub App's bot by its slug,
`hecatongithub`, without the REST API's `[bot]`; the three tests' AUTHORS sets now read `hecatongithub`.

**The token's quota is shared too, but not with anonymous readers.** gh runs as michael, so its 5,000 requests an
hour are shared with every tool on his token. Each test spends one GraphQL query per run, and a spent token quota
fails as its own named check rather than as a missing comment.

**Tests.** `verify/test_gh_comments.py` (offline, new) puts a stub gh alone on PATH and checks: every comment comes
back as login, body and url, with a null author read as "?"; gh is called as `issue view 7 -R owner/repo --json
comments`; an empty issue fails "has at least one comment" alone; no gh, and gh's exit 4, fail the token check and
print nothing after it; a primary, a secondary and a 429 rate limit each fail the rate-limit check after a passing
token check; a 404, output that is not JSON, JSON with no comments list and a list holding what is not a comment are
errors; and the three cause-comment tests call the helper and hold no `urllib` read of their own.

**Live check (run 17195).** Through the host's gh, all three cause-comment tests passed: #633's cause at
issuecomment-6483003262, #783's at issuecomment-6578827445, #796's at issuecomment-6595960290. With PATH
`/usr/bin:/bin`, whose gh has no token, `test_dispatched_runs_cause_comment.py` exited 1 on the one check "gh is on
PATH with a token, so the read does not spend the host's shared anonymous quota (#863)", quoting gh's
"please run: gh auth login". No cluster is touched by this change.

**The suites (run 17195, at `ca2d6976`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 54 checks (the offline suite and 53
tier tests) in 25m42s and printed `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN`, exit 0. The offline suite inside it ran 253
tests, `test_gh_comments.py` among them, and printed `ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`. All three cause-comment
tests passed in the tier through gh.
## 2026-11-05 · #864 · agentgateway's tracing moves from the deprecated config.tracing to frontendPolicies.tracing

**What changed.** Both gateway ConfigMaps in `gitops/ai-layer/agentgateway.yaml`, agentgateway-config and
agentgateway-c7-config, drop `config.tracing` and say the same thing as a top-level frontend policy:

    frontendPolicies:
      tracing:
        host: otel-collector-opentelemetry-collector.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:4318
        protocol: http
        randomSampling: true

This is the same configuration the binary already ran. v1.7.0 reads `config.tracing`, logs `config.tracing is
deprecated; migrate to frontendPolicies.tracing` five times, and turns the block into exactly this
(`crates/agentgateway/src/types/local.rs`, `merge_deprecated_frontend_policies`, read at tag v1.7.0 on 2026-11-05):
the endpoint URL's host and port as an inline backend, `otlpProtocol` as `protocol`, `randomSampling` as it is,
`clientSampling` unset in both (an incoming sampled traceparent is followed, `eval(client_sampling, true)` in
`telemetry/log.rs`). The 2026-06-26 DECISION-LOG rows say `frontendPolicies.tracing` crashed v1.3.0 with "no variant of
enum SimpleLocalBackend". That attempt wrote the old block's `otlpEndpoint` key. The policy names its target as
`host`, `service` or `backend`, so it had no target. The file's header said gRPC :4317, and it now states what the
config sends. The comment by the Deployment's env and the current docs (`docs/MASTER-RECREATION-SPEC.md`,
`docs/READINESS-CHECKLIST.md`) say `frontendPolicies.tracing` too. PRD 20, PROGRESS.md and DECISION-LOG are records and
keep their wording.

**The tests.** `verify/test_agentgateway_config.py` holds, for both ConfigMaps, no `config.tracing` and the tracing
policy above, and holds the header to `frontendPolicies.tracing`, http and :4318 and to no gRPC or :4317. Against the
old file it fails six checks. The v1.7.0 schema still takes `config.tracing`, so the schema check alone would not
catch the old key coming back. `verify/test_agentgateway_tracing_e2e.py` is new, in the tools tier. For each
ConfigMap it runs the real binary on the committed tracing, with the collector swapped for a loopback OTLP receiver
and the binds for one loopback route. It holds no deprecation line in the log, OTLP/HTTP protobuf POSTs to
`/v1/traces`, the incoming traceparent's trace id in what was exported, and a request with no traceparent traced as
well. A control puts the same tracing back under `config.tracing` and must see the warning (5 lines), so a log the
test cannot read does not pass as clean. With `randomSampling: false` the untraced-request check fails on both
ConfigMaps, so it is not vacuous.

**A new pinned tool.** The binary is agentgateway v1.7.0's release asset `agentgateway-linux-amd64`, SHA-256
`1b2fc01a2de29ca113bbb6258b5cae7b1eb3c724071c09d687a449132f2f42f8`, the release's own `.sha256` file, read
2026-11-05. It is now a row in `verify/e2e-tools.lock`, and `fetch-e2e-tools.sh` downloads it. `run-e2e-tools.sh`
and `run-e2e.sh` set `AGENTGATEWAY` to it. `test_e2e_tools_tier.py` holds its version to the Deployment's image tag and
its URL to that tag's release, so a gateway bump has to move this pin as well. Then the tier runs the bumped config on
the bumped binary, and a version that dropped the old key would have failed here first. The image's `/app/agentgateway`
is a separate build of the tag: other bytes (`c7ef326b...`), the same `--version` 1.7.0, so what the pin holds equal
to the image is the version. The release binary is used because the tier host has no container runtime it can count
on.

**Run on the image's own binary (run 17196).** `/app/agentgateway` was copied out of the pinned image
(`podman create`, `podman cp`) and run on loopback on each ConfigMap, old form and new. The old form logged 5
deprecation lines each and exported to `/v1/traces`. The new form logged none and exported the same way.
`--validate-only` accepts both forms and prints no warnings, so it cannot tell them apart.

## 2026-11-05 · #859 · Every offline test that runs fleet.sh guards itself, so a test run by hand stays offline too

**What was left after #857.** #857 (run 17099, `ac98b960`) runs every test `verify/run-tests.sh` runs behind
`verify/no-cloud.sh`'s stubs for aws, kubectl, eksctl, helm and terraform, and fails one that calls them. That covers
the suite. It does not cover a test run on its own, `bash verify/test_x.sh` or `python3 verify/test_x.py`, which a
run does while it iterates: that goes past the runner with the run's live KUBECONFIG and AWS session for
watch-it-burn-community and watch-it-burn-private. That is the path #421's test took to the community cluster.

**Change.**
- `verify/no-cloud.sh` gains two per-test entry points. `no_cloud_guard <dir>` runs `no_cloud_setup`, puts the stubs
  first on PATH for the test and everything it starts, and clears the cloud environment the way #421's backstop did:
  the AWS profile, region, key and role variables and HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV unset, KUBECONFIG, AWS_CONFIG_FILE and
  AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE pointed at files that do not exist, and AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED set. A real kubectl
  reached by an absolute path, or boto3 in a helper, then finds no context or credentials. `no_cloud_clean` passes
  when nothing was called and otherwise prints each call and fails.
- `verify/no_cloud.py` is the same for the Python tests. It runs `no_cloud_setup` and reads `NO_CLOUD_UNSET` from
  no-cloud.sh, so the tool list, the stub text and the variables cleared have one source.
- Each of the 30 offline tests that sources fleet.sh or hands it to bash (24 shell, 6 Python) calls the guard once
  its temp dir exists and ends with the check "no check above called aws, kubectl, eksctl, terraform or helm".
  Under the runner its stubs stand ahead of the runner's, so a leak fails the test's own last check and names the
  call there. `test_presenter_student_retired.sh` drops its inline copy of #421's stubs and its `env -u` wrapper for
  the shared guard, which clears the same variables and more.
- `verify/test_no_cloud_by_hand.sh` holds the guard to blocking and logging each tool, clearing the environment and
  giving way to a test's own fakes. It holds no_cloud.py to writing the same stubs byte for byte and clearing every
  listed variable. It finds the tests that drive fleet.sh by what their code does and fails, naming each, on one
  without the setup and the closing check. Like #857's test it has a second set of fakes behind the stubs, so a
  broken guard never reaches the live session. With the closing check deleted from `test_reset_bot.sh`, the
  coverage check fails and names it. With the `kubectl` stub taken out of `test_fleet_standbys.sh`, that test's own
  last check fails and names `kubectl config current-context`.

**What differs from the draft.** Run 17118's draft (`f8817815`, `f5067aad`) was cut from staging `64c115f6`, before
#857 landed, and did not land: hecaton's rebase hit #857's edits to `run-tests.sh` and `test_fleet_standbys.sh`. That
draft had its own runner guard and helpers (`verify/nocloud.sh`, `verify/nocloud.py`, `verify/test_nocloud.sh`), and
its audit found the same one leak #857 found, the standbys test's `kubectl config current-context`. This run keeps
#857's runner guard and its standbys stub as they are and drops the draft's runner guard and helpers. It takes the
draft's per-test edits to the other 29 tests, which staging had not touched since `64c115f6`, and points them at
no-cloud.sh. It adds the same guard to staging's `test_fleet_standbys.sh`. The draft's runner checks are not carried
over, because `test_offline_suite_no_cloud.sh` covers the runner.

**Live check.** None beyond the suites: the change is to tests only and touches no cluster. The suites ran in this
run's environment, which carries the live KUBECONFIG and AWS session for both clusters, and no test was named for
calling a cloud tool.

## 2026-11-05 · #203 · The live proof ran on watch-it-burn-private, and Access Analyzer's first run dropped two actions IAM does not have

Run 17262 ran #203's live half for the first time, on the two clusters a dispatched run now has (CLAUDE.md, Dispatched
runs, point 1). The code is run 10971's, on staging since `024c19ae` and `7c96ce83`, with #743's pod-spec read;
`verify/prior-drafts.sh 203 origin/staging` printed NONE, so nothing was ported.

**Which cluster.** watch-it-burn-private renders `values-admin.yaml`, which lists `cluster-network-policies` as the
attendee profile does, so it carries `agent-deny-imds`. watch-it-burn-community renders `values-burn.yaml`, which
leaves the deny off on purpose (that file says why), so the IMDS step of the live test cannot pass there and was not
run there.

**The live check.** `CONTEXT=watch-it-burn-private python3 verify/test_agent_cloud_credential_live.py` passed every
check and printed `All live agent cloud-credential checks passed.` agent-sa has no `eks.amazonaws.com/` annotation and
`automountServiceAccountToken: false`; BurritoBot's pod runs as agent-sa with
`AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI=http://169.254.170.23/v1/credentials`, no static key and no default token mount;
workshop-mcp runs as its own account and mounts its token; `agent-deny-imds` is on the cluster with the committed spec.
The probe Job, applied from `challenge-fixes` as the lab applies it, printed:

```
  who am I (sts get-caller-identity)   UNREACHABLE (network policy)
  Bedrock: Nova Pro (on the list)      ALLOWED   Ok.
  Bedrock: a model NOT on the list     DENIED by IAM
      User: arn:aws:sts::515966504359:assumed-role/watch-it-burn-private-bedrock-f6b983a70663c80a8ff9a04e96/... is not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel
  S3: list buckets                     UNREACHABLE (network policy)
  EC2: describe instances              UNREACHABLE (network policy)
  IAM: look up any role or policy      UNREACHABLE (network policy)
  curl -m 2 http://169.254.169.254/    BLOCKED (curl exit 28)
  IMDSv2 token request                 BLOCKED (curl exit 28)
```

So from a pod holding agent-sa's credential, `sts get-caller-identity` and IMDS both fail, Nova Pro answers, and the
one thing the credential reaches past the egress allowlist is refused by IAM for any model off the list. The test
deletes its Job, and none was left in `agent` afterwards.

**What Access Analyzer found.** `verify/test_iam_policy_aws.py` had never run (#207's entry above says so). Its first
run, as `accen-dev`, failed check 1 on the cluster root: `ERROR INVALID_ACTION: The action bedrock:Converse does not
exist` and the same for `bedrock:ConverseStream`, in both statements of `aws_iam_policy.bedrock_invoke` and of
`aws_iam_policy.tutor_bedrock_invoke`. IAM has no such actions: the Converse API is authorized by
`bedrock:InvokeModel` and ConverseStream by `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream`, which both policies already
grant. They are removed from the four statements in `infra/terraform/aws/cluster/main.tf` and from the staged copy
the lab shows (`agent-bedrock-policy.json` in `challenge-fixes`), and `verify/test_agent_cloud_credential.py` now
holds the agent policy to the two actions. The effect is unchanged, since IAM never matched the two names; the live
probe above ran under the old document and Nova Pro answered. After the change check 1 passes on every document:
boundary 1, cluster 11, audit 3, no ERROR or SECURITY_WARNING, and no Resource in the agent policy is a bare `*`.

**A broken case in check 2.** The widening case added `s3:GetObject` to the agent statement, whose resources are
Bedrock ARNs alone. That grants nothing, and check-no-new-access answered PASS, so the test failed on a true answer.
The case now appends `arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/*`, the widening #138 closed, and fails check 2 naming
`aws_iam_policy.bedrock_invoke.policy` as it should. The narrowing case drops `InvokeModelWithResponseStream`,
as `ConverseStream` is gone. All three check 2 cases pass.

**Not yet run.** Check 4 of `verify/test_iam_policy_aws.py`, the simulator over `infra/org/effect-tests.yaml`.
The run's `accen-dev` session is a session token, and IAM refuses every call made with it
(`InvalidClientTokenId` on `iam simulate-custom-policy`, `iam simulate-principal-policy` and
`iam list-account-aliases` alike), while Access Analyzer accepts it. It needs a credential IAM accepts:
`IAM_PIPELINE_PROFILE=<profile> IAM_PIPELINE_REGION=us-west-2 python3 verify/test_iam_policy_aws.py`. The live
probe covers the same boundary for the credential the cluster hands out. The two-action policy reaches AWS at the next
`terraform apply` of a cluster root; until then both clusters hold the four-action document, which grants the same.

**The suites (run 17262, at `2169d4ff`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 55 checks (the offline suite and 54

  allocation tags". So the measured figure is by date.
- **`teardown/delivery-cost.py` is new.** For each `--profile` it prints the tag-filtered total as it comes back (so
  the day the tags are active the figure is in the report), then the account's billed usage on the window's UTC days
  (record type Usage, unblended), by service and by day, and the EKS cluster hours from usage type
  `AmazonEKS-Hours:perCluster`, so the cost per cluster hour is measured too. Tax, credits and refunds are listed and
  left out: tax is posted on the bill's own days (1st, 15th and 17th in June on accen-dev), not on the usage days. The
  day before and the day after the window are read too, and either one above 1.00 USD and 5% of the window's busiest
  day prints `WINDOW CUTS SPEND`. It refuses a window whose day after is not over, and a profile given twice or two
  profiles on one account. A failed call ends the run with exit 3 and prints no total. Only `sts get-caller-identity`
  and `ce get-cost-and-usage` are called, with the profile per call and `--region us-east-1`.

  CloudTrail, which keeps 90 days, so the World's Fair was already out of reach. The bill by date reaches back 13

## 2026-11-05 · #205 · Run 17269: both drift acceptance cases run live; the drill and the report's creator lookup fixed

**Context.** Run 17269 is the first #205 run with a readable session for the two clusters that are up and for accen-dev
(account 515966504359, us-west-2), after hecaton#508. `bash verify/prior-drafts.sh 205 origin/staging` printed NONE:
the #205 work is on staging (`939cd82`, `5743323`), and the only unmerged draft, `fa10d01` on `agent/205-6695`, is
older than it. So nothing was ported. This run did the live checks #795 lists that a run can do, and fixed what they
found.

**Kubernetes plane, the NetworkPolicy drill.** `CONTEXT=<ctx> python3 verify/test_drift_selfheal_live.py`, first run:

- watch-it-burn-community: `ai-layer` quiet for 5255 s, `selfHealAttemptsCount 0`; `agent/platform-console-egress`
  back after 20.1 s as a new uid with the tracking annotation and git's spec; the sync automated and Succeeded.
  `Self-heal drill passed.`
- watch-it-burn-private: back after 25.2 s, every check green but the last, `the sync that did it was automated and
  succeeded (phase Running)`. The Application then read startedAt 02:55:15, the policy's creationTimestamp 02:55:39,
  finishedAt 02:55:45, `Succeeded`, automated. The policy is back when the sync applies it, which is before the sync
  ends, so the check raced the sync.

The fix: the drill now records the operation's `startedAt` before the delete, and after the policy is back waits up to
`SYNC_WAIT_S` (120 s) for an operation that started later to leave `Running`. It compares with the server's earlier
timestamp, so this host's clock skew cannot pass it. It then checks that operation ended `Succeeded` and
automated. Rerun after the fix, both clusters: `ai-layer` quiet 301 s, back after 1.3 s, the new sync (started
03:00:39 on community, 03:00:48 on private) `Succeeded`, `Self-heal drill passed.`, exit 0. Both clusters were left as
found: `ai-layer` Synced and Healthy, the policy present with git's spec. The documented 30 s window held on all four
deletes.

**AWS plane, the drift report.** `python3 infra/terraform/drift/drift-report.py --accounts accen-dev --region
us-west-2` ran live, plan-only, and exited 2 (findings). This host holds no fleet, network, boundary or audit state, so
it planned nothing and listed `watch-it-burn-community` and `watch-it-burn-private` (tags ManagedBy=terraform,
event=kubecon-na-2026) as unmanaged. That is expected from a host without the states, and docs/floor.md now says to
run the report where they are. It also reported `NO recorder in us-west-2`: `describe-configuration-recorders` and
`describe-trails` both return empty in accen-dev, so the audit root has not been applied there.

Its "created by" column said `no CreateCluster event in us-west-2's 90-day event history` for two clusters made on
2026-10-28. That was a bug. `creator()` looked CloudTrail up by `ResourceName` and read 50 events, and the newest 50
for `watch-it-burn-community` were 46 `AssumeRoleForPodIdentity`, 3 `ListAssociatedAccessPolicies` and 1
`ListAccessEntries`. A lookup by `EventName=CreateCluster` returned 111 events in 2.5 s, among them both clusters'
creates by `user/nwuser`. `creator()` now asks by event name, reads every page, caches one lookup per account, region
and event, matches the resource by `Resources[].ResourceName` or `requestParameters` (`bucketName`, `name`), and
skips an event with an `errorCode`, since a refused create made nothing. Rerun: both clusters `created by
arn:aws:iam::515966504359:user/nwuser at 2026-10-28T12:39:25+01:00` (and `12:39:33` for private).
`verify/test_drift_report.py`'s fake CloudTrail now answers a lookup by resource name the way the live account did,
with 50 pod identity events, and puts a refused attempt on the same name and another resource's create in the
event-name answer. Four new checks hold the lookup to that. Against the old `creator()` the test fails 4 checks; with
the fix it passes.

**AWS plane, the hand-made bucket.** The operator profile made `wib-drift-oob-515966504359-20261105030111` in
us-west-2 at 03:01:13Z, tagged project=watch-it-burn and Purpose=drift-acceptance-205. CloudTrail event history had
its `CreateBucket` by 03:03:09Z. The next drift report listed it under Unmanaged: `accen-dev | s3-bucket |
wib-drift-oob-515966504359-20261105030111 | 2026-11-05T03:01:16+00:00 | arn:aws:iam::515966504359:user/nwuser at
2026-11-05T04:01:13+01:00 | NOT recorded`. The bucket was then deleted, and `head-bucket` returns 404. So the drift
report half of the acceptance case holds live. The Config half does not, because there is no recorder.

**What this run could not do, and why.** The session hecaton hands a run is a `GetSessionToken` session without MFA,
and IAM refuses every call from one: `iam get-policy`, `list-users` and `list-attached-user-policies` all returned
`InvalidClientTokenId`. The audit root creates an IAM role and looks up the permissions boundary, so this session
cannot apply it, and it cannot mint a key with the attendee grant for the refusal half. The attendee key CSVs
(`infra/terraform/fleet/aws-pool/`) and the fleet states are kept on the operator machine only. So these stay owed,
from a principal that can call IAM:

event=kubecon-na-2026`. Then `WIB_ATTENDEE_ACCOUNTS=accen-dev DRIFT_PROFILE=accen-dev

see the recipe rule fill: KubeArmor's `block-recipe-snoop` blocks the read on workshop-mcp, so Falco's `open_read`
never matches there. The policy's selector is `app: workshop-mcp` only, while the Falco rule matches any container
in namespace `agent` that reads a file whose name ends in `secret-sauce-recipe.conf`. So this run read a decoy
there instead of lifting the policy: in the private cluster's web-terminal pod, `echo probe-489 >
/tmp/wib489-secret-sauce-recipe.conf`, two `cat`s of it, then `rm`. Falco's log (pod `security/falco-n27ws`)
printed `"rule":"Recipe Snoop In Agent Namespace"` twice at 03:48:51Z. Talon left the pod alone, because the rule is
WARNING and Sidekick forwards only critical. Datadog had the metric within a minute:
`sum:falco.rules.matches.count{kube_cluster_name:burritobot-*} by {kube_cluster_name,rule_name}.as_count()` over 30
minutes returned `burritobot-private | recipe_snoop_in_agent_namespace => 2.0`, next to the other rules in the same
shape (`exec_into_pod_detected`, `sensitive_file_read_in_container`). The tag value is the rule name lowercased
with each space replaced by `_`, which is the name leaderboard.yaml and verify/test_leaderboard.py use, so the query stays as it is.

## 2026-11-05 · #480 · The tool-pin check ran live on the community cluster: strip mode works, deny fails the whole chat, and the badge reads the pin's wiring

**What ran.** Hecaton run 17293 ran `live-check.sh run` on `watch-it-burn-community` (attackme), as the coordinator's go
of 2026-11-02 names, from 03:48 to 03:56 UTC at `50416777`. Its output is
`docs/research/2026-10-24-tool-pin-spike/live-2026-11-05-community.txt`, and the spike README's new section "The
cluster check, 2026-11-05" reads it row by row. The cluster runs agentgateway v1.7.0 and kagent 0.10.1, whose agent
runtime is now Go (`golang-adk:0.10.1`, on adk-go v2.1.0), not the Python runtime the v0.9.9 reading covered.

**A fix first, before the run.** The community gateway's last hot reload, at 01:28, had failed: "cannot use deprecated
config.tracing together with frontendPolicies.tracing". #864's ConfigMap had synced, the pod had not restarted, and
v1.7.0 refuses that reload because the process started with `config.tracing`. So the gateway served its 2026-11-04
config and would refuse the pinned bind too. `setup` now records the gateway's last config load, and when that was a
failure it restarts the gateway on the pinned config, and `restore` restarts it again on the ConfigMap it writes back
(`50416777`). The pinned config was first run through the v1.7.0 release binary's `--validate-only` ("Configuration is
valid!"). The cluster's gateway therefore now runs its committed config: its main container logs no `config.tracing
is deprecated` line. That is #864's intended state, and not the stale one found, which nothing could put back. The
c7 container still logs 5, because `agentgateway-c7-config` is under ignoreDifferences on existing clusters by design.

**What was seen.**
- Discovery and the agent's `list_tools` both pass through tool-pin: bind 3004's `tools/list` lines come from the
  kagent controller every 60 s and from the agent's pod once per question, each with a verdict.
- kagent rolled the agent by itself after evil-mcp's url changed, both ways, so the student's one-field patch needs no
  restart.
- Strip mode after the rug pull: `get_weather` left `discoveredTools`, `Accepted` stayed True, and the agent called no
  evil-mcp tool. A `tools/call` for it by name came back as an `isError` result with tool-pin's reason.
- Deny mode: JSON-RPC `-32001` to both callers, and `Accepted=False` with tool-pin's reason, with `discoveredTools`
  left as last listed. **The chat answer failed outright**: the A2A reply was the toolset error text. adk-go v2.1.0's
  `internal/llminternal/tools_processor.go` line 43 returns on the first toolset whose `Tools()` errors, where the
  Python runtime dropped only that toolset.
- Restore: every object as snapshotted, both Applications Synced and Healthy with auto-sync as found, evil-mcp
  `Accepted=True` on :3003 with its three tools, attackme 200.

**Decided.**
- **The pin runs in strip mode.** Deny on kagent 0.10.1 turns a rug pull into an outage of the whole agent and shows
  the user the error. failClosed has the same consequence for a tool-pin outage (reasoned from the same code path,
  not staged); failClosed or failOpen is left to the #117 build, with this written down.
- **The badge reads the pin's wiring, not its verdicts**, as the spike recommended on 2026-10-24: "Tool pin: on" when
  evil-mcp's RemoteMCPServer url is the pinned bind and `tool-pin-baseline` pins every name in the Agent's evil-mcp
  `toolNames`. It needs `get` on those two objects in the `guard-proxy-reader` Role. It reads neither
  `discoveredTools`, which showed a list and not the pin in both modes, nor the `Accepted` condition, which only deny
  sets. The recommendation's second state, "pin tripped" from `Accepted=False`, is dropped with deny.

**Also changed.** `observe` printed "live-check: failed at line 249" for a `tools/list` from the probe pod, which is
gone by then (the run went on), and its agent-log grep missed the Go runtime's wording. Both are fixed, and
`verify/test_tool_pin_live_check.py` holds the stale-gateway restarts and the gone caller; each new check fails
against the code before it.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing for #480: the issue's cluster half is this run. Building the pin into GitOps,
the badge and the bind's Service port and ingress rule, is #117's.

tests) in 27m07s and printed `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN`, exit 0. The offline suite inside it ran 255 tests and
printed `ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`.

lab-platform#344.

**The certificate is requested.** `infra/front-door-cert.sh accen-dev us-west-2` found no certificate in the account
and requested one: `arn:aws:acm:us-west-2:515966504359:certificate/8bae04a8-4896-4123-8de4-88aa6e4f75d8`, for
`*.agenticburn.com` and `*.burritobot.co`, PENDING_VALIDATION. It is issued once these two CNAMEs resolve:

- agenticburn.com: `_4d348e16229f1796413ec16e36e29d56` to `_a29fcc4eb94adc0bce08cab3decf1f70.wzccmgtwzk.acm-validations.aws`
- burritobot.co: `_90187e86eafa67a1d14cbd74ee24810d` to `_e7304390c80b79c4d4e72c7ed42df78a.wzccmgtwzk.acm-validations.aws`

Both zones are on Namecheap (`dig NS` answers registrar-servers.com), whose API answers only netcup's allowlisted
address with the key in Michael's `~/secrets/dns/namecheap.env`, which a run cannot read. So the two writes go to the
custodian as `infra/dns/set-demo-dns.py --apply` commands run as Michael from his checkout, whose copy of the script
is the same as staging's. ACM gives up on a pending certificate after 72 hours. If that happens first, the helper
requests a new one, and ACM's validation names are the same for the same account and domain, so the records still
serve it.

**The patch is checked live, on its own NLB.** `verify/front_door_tls_live.py` (new) renders the chart for the burn
profile with an ARN, applies the ai-layer patch with kustomize as Argo CD does, and creates the patched console
Service as `agent/front-door-check`, so the console Service Argo CD manages, the community cluster's real front door,
is never touched. It waits for that Service's NLB, connects to 443 with the roster name as SNI, verifies chain and
name against the system roots (or `--cafile`), sends `GET /`, and deletes the Service on every exit. Since the real
certificate is still pending, the run imported a self-signed certificate for attackme and burritobot-private into
ACM and ran the check with that certificate as the CA, on watch-it-burn-community:

```
created agent/front-door-check on watch-it-burn-community with arn:aws:acm:us-west-2:515966504359:certificate/97e88746-9db6-4279-bf8f-304353e7f69d
its NLB: k8s-agent-frontdoo-806507b0e5-d17b722eb434d81e.elb.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
PASS: 443 verifies for attackme.agenticburn.com against /tmp/fdc-17359/cert.pem: subject attackme.agenticburn.com, SANs ['attackme.agenticburn.com', 'burritobot-private.agenticburn.com'], issuer attackme.agenticburn.com
PASS: through the NLB's re-encrypt to nginx, GET / for attackme.agenticburn.com answers HTTP/1.1 200 OK
deleted agent/front-door-check
```

So the four annotations give an NLB that terminates TLS with the ACM certificate and re-encrypts to nginx, and
nginx answers through it. The first attempt read an empty answer to `GET /` right after the handshake: the NLB
completes the handshake itself before its targets are healthy. The check now keeps asking until its deadline. As the
control, the live console NLB on the same cluster (TCP pass-through) was refused against the system roots for
attackme.agenticburn.com: `self-signed certificate`, which is the refusal the issue describes.

**Left as found.** `front-door-check` and its NLB are gone (`aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers` lists only the two
console NLBs). The imported certificate was deleted once ACM dropped the deleted NLB from its in-use list, a few
minutes later; `aws acm list-certificates` then listed only the pending one. The pending
certificate stays: it is the one the event uses.

`verify/test_front_door_tls_live_logic.py` (new, tools tier) checks without a cluster that the Service the live
check creates is the kustomize build's console Service with the four annotations, under its own name and label, and
that its handshake verifies a local server's certificate for the roster name, refuses it for another name, and
refuses a self-signed one against the system roots.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Once the two CNAMEs are written and `infra/front-door-cert.sh accen-dev us-west-2`
exits 0, the same check against the system roots:
`python3 verify/front_door_tls_live.py --context watch-it-burn-community --arn arn:aws:acm:us-west-2:515966504359:certificate/8bae04a8-4896-4123-8de4-88aa6e4f75d8 --name attackme.agenticburn.com`.
Then the definition of done's own leg, lab-platform#344: `labctl event up ... --front-door-cert=<that ARN>` logging
`front doors: 2 roster clusters recorded`, and `labctl tls-check attackme.agenticburn.com` through lab-platform's
gateway, which is lab-platform's to run once lab-platform#122 moves the wildcard.

**Suites (run 17359, at a41023e4).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran the offline suite (256 tests, ALL OFFLINE
RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN) and then the tools tier, `test_front_door_tls_live_logic.py` among it with all 8 checks
passing: 56 checks in 26m54s, ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN, exit 0.

## 2026-11-05 · #647 · Run 17362 ran the scrub's live checks on the community cluster: the scrub holds in Datadog, and only the post-talk purge is left

Every earlier #647 draft is on staging (`verify/prior-drafts.sh 647 origin/staging` prints NONE). Three checks were
owed on a cluster: the 2026-10-29 entry's prompt read back as `[EMAIL]`/`[PHONE]` in the `burritobot-public` tab, and
its look at one agentgateway `tools/call` span for MCP arguments under a key the scrub does not cover; and the
2026-11-02 entry's phone check of the hidden Datadog button. This run had both KubeCon clusters and the read pair in
`watch-it-burn/datadog`, so it ran all three and made them repeatable.

- **Why a sent span, not a chat.** Since #648 the public bot's input guard refuses a prompt carrying any of the four
  kinds before guard-proxy's root span is given it, so a chat with an e-mail in it puts none of it in a trace and
  tests nothing about the scrub. The check sends one OTLP span into attackme's collector over a kubectl port-forward
  to `svc/otel-collector-opentelemetry-collector` :4318, the port every BurritoBot pod sends to, from a service of its
  own (`wib-pii-scrub-check`) so it lands in no BurritoBot view. It carries `pii_scrub_cases.ATTENDEE` on
  `gen_ai.input.messages` and on a span event, a tool call's arguments and result with an e-mail, a phone number and a
  card, and a `session.id` holding an e-mail. Its span name carries the run's stamp, because APM kept it by diversity
  sampling (one span per service and resource each 15 minutes), not by the retention filter BurritoBot's spans match.
- **What came back.** APM, by trace id: every conversation key and the span event hold the scrubbed text, `session.id`
  is whole, and no raw value is anywhere else in the span. Agent Observability files the copy under ml_app
  `wib-pii-scrub-check` with trace id `sha256(apm trace id)[:32]` (traces/llmobs's `transform/llmobs_one_root`), found
  by its `otel.trace_id:` tag; its input is scrubbed and so are the tags it makes from the tool arguments.
- **What is stored.** Every APM span for `kube_cluster_name:burritobot-public` over 168 hours (38,331) and every
  `ml_app:burritobot` Agent Observability span on that cluster (14,250) was read with the scrub's own patterns over the
  conversation: the eight keys `keep_keys` names and each span event's attributes on APM, input and output on Agent
  Observability. No match. Datadog's span count for the same query, read 10 minutes later, was 38,900. Real traffic
  shows the scrub at work: in the newest 20,996 spans, read by hand first, 320 `[EMAIL]` in `gcp.vertex.agent.tool_call_args`
  and as many in `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments`, 66 in tool results, 76 in guard-proxy's replies. Pattern matches outside
  the conversation are ids the scrub leaves whole on purpose (numeric `session.id` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`
  values, kagent's default `kagent.user_id` `admin@kagent.dev`) and span-event `time_unix_nano` values, which is why
  the scan reads only the conversation.
- **agentgateway records no MCP arguments.** The `burritobot-gateway` spans' keys over the week are request metadata
  (`mcp.method.name`, `mcp.target`, `mcp.session.id`, `gen_ai.tool.name`, `url.path`, `url.query`, `http.*`, `k8s.*`
  and the like); none carries a tool call's arguments or result, and no pattern matched in any of them. The scrub's
  key list needs nothing for the gateway.
- **The button.** In headless Chromium at 390x844, `attackme.burritobot.co` and `attackme.agenticburn.com` (event.js's
  `publicHosts`, read from the file) hide `#ddbtn` and show no link to datadoghq.com, and
  `burritobot-private.burritobot.co` shows the button. A phone viewport, not a phone: it proves what the served page
  and event.js do on each host.

**Live output (run 17362, 2026-11-05).** `COMMUNITY_CONTEXT=watch-it-burn-community python3
verify/test_collector_pii_scrub_live.py`: 22 PASS, sent trace `78742ddddc93f5ae832fca398438f225`, "APM: the scan read
every span of the last 168h (38331 read)", "Agent Observability (ml_app:burritobot): the scan read every span of the
last 168h (14250 read)". `python3 verify/test_public_datadog_button_live.py`: 11 PASS. Before the test existed the
same span was sent by hand as trace `744913650f2c2b1b9455ad463a8936ce`, with the same result.

**What it leaves.** Those two spans, in Whitney's org under `burritobot-public`, and a `wib-pii-scrub-check` entry in
APM's service list and Agent Observability's ml_app list. The run-of-show's purge step now names that service, since
its spans fall on build days outside the session window. Nothing on the cluster changed.

**Tests.** `verify/test_pii_scrub_live_logic.py` (offline) runs `pii_scrub_live.run` against a fake kubectl and a fake
org: green on a healthy pair, and red on each of 17 breaks (no scrub, a scrub that never merges back, the scrub not
last, another cluster's name, a refused send, a span that never arrives in either product, raw text read back on each
key, the span event or an Agent Observability tag, a rewritten `session.id`, raw text stored in a reply, a span event
or an Agent Observability input, and a scan that cannot finish). The leak check's raw strings are long enough that no

**Not yet run.** The purge of `burritobot-public` from Whitney's org, per the run-of-show's Teardown step, on or after

## 2026-11-05 · #608 · First live run: the #607, #490 and #552 checks pass; the PolicyReport checks waited on a starved reports controller

Hecaton run 17353 ran `CONTEXT=watch-it-burn-private python3 verify/test_llm_bypass_live.py` from its own
checkout of staging 9974cf1 against watch-it-burn-private
(`arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:515966504359:cluster/watch-it-burn-private`, ACTIVE, account 515966504359, through the
run's handed-over kubeconfig and accen-dev session). Argo CD's kyverno-policies, ai-layer and lab-bootstrap
Applications were Synced and Healthy at 9974cf1. `verify/prior-drafts.sh 608 origin/staging` printed NONE:
the unlanded drafts of runs 12431 and 12662 are followed in staging by later #608 work, and neither holds anything
this entry lacks. Run 12431's draft reported the whole suite passing at 0d73c8d; that run is not repeated here,
and this entry records the first run whose output is on record.

**The first run (run id e2e538): 52 PASS, 5 FAIL, exit 1.** Every prerequisite passed, the restrict-agent-spawned-workloads
expression comparison included, so the whitespace fix from the 2026-11-03 #608 entry holds live.

- **The three #607 Secret checks pass.** A Pod mounting terminal-auth as a secret volume and a Pod reading it
  through an env secretKeyRef, each made as agent-sa on the default ServiceAccount, are refused by
  restrict-agent-spawned-workloads, and a Pod mounting ceo-personal-record and reading it by secretKeyRef is
  admitted.
- **The #490 checks pass.** agent-sa may create the default-endpoint, envFrom and valueFrom pods; each exists and
  no NetworkPolicy allows it a public API; the console label does open egress.
- **The #552 checks pass.** The plain pod is Ready, as are agentgateway, workshop-agent and guard-proxy. The plain
  pod's connections to agentgateway :3000 and :3002 and to workshop-agent :8080 are dropped while the hop before
  each is admitted (kagent to workshop-agent :8080 too), guard-proxy still reaches agentgateway :3000, and the six
  impersonating shapes are refused by restrict-agent-spawned-workloads.
- **The guarded path passes:** guard-proxy's and agentgateway's own pods are reported PASS.
- **The five PolicyReport checks failed** with "no result for this policy" after the 150 s wait: the four bypass
  shapes (bare Pod, Deployment, the guard-proxy-named Deployment, the init container) that should read FAIL, and
  the guard-proxy-routed Pod that should read PASS.
- Cleanup held: `cleanup (wib.test/run=e2e538): done`, and `kubectl get pods,deploy,rs,cm -A -l wib.test/run`
  found nothing afterwards. Nothing called a model.

**Why the reports were late.** The policy was right and the report did come: one probe Pod shaped like the bare
bypass case got `deny-llm-endpoint-bypass: fail` after 528 s. The reports controller was the cause. Prometheus on
the cluster showed it at its 200m CPU limit and throttled in 99.9% of CFS periods, over the last hour and six hours
earlier (the oldest data the cluster's Prometheus holds). Its own metrics over one minute: 358 background-scan
reconciles and 330 PolicyReport updates, about 58 CPU-seconds. The 30 s `backgroundScanInterval` that #323 set
rescans each of ~350 resources (74 Pods, 189 ReplicaSets, Services and the rest) twice a minute, which needs about a
whole CPU, so a new Pod's report queued behind the rescans for minutes.

**The measurement.** To test this, the run paused automated sync on lab-bootstrap and the kyverno Application,
edited the kyverno-reports-controller Deployment, and timed the same probe Pod (created, its report read every
3 to 18 s, then deleted):

| Interval | CPU limit | State | Report after | Controller CPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30s | 200m | as deployed | 528 s | 0.20, throttled |
| 30s | 1 | settled | 115 s | 0.98 |
| 1h | 1 | settled | 46 s | 0.03 |
| 1h | 200m | 2 minutes after a restart | 275 s | 0.20, startup scan |
| 1h | 200m | settled | 45 s | 0.01 |

A new Pod is scanned when it is created, whatever the interval; the interval only sets how often every unchanged
resource is scanned again. The startup scan took about two minutes at 1 CPU and about ten at 200m. The fourth row
is what #323 saw on 2026-09-08 at the 1h default (no report after two minutes for the Pod just deployed, while
every older Pod had one): a controller still in its startup scan after a config change, not the interval.

With 1h and 1 CPU, the whole suite ran again (run id 1e36b3): **57 PASS, no FAIL, exit 0**, "All live
deny-llm-endpoint-bypass and restrict-agent-spawned-workloads checks passed.", the five PolicyReport checks
included. Cleanup held again.

**Left as found.** The run restored both Applications' syncPolicy from the copies it saved (automated, prune,
selfHeal and their syncOptions). Argo CD put the Deployment back to `200m` and `--backgroundScanInterval=30s`
within ten seconds, and both Applications read Synced and Healthy.

**The change.** `gitops/bootstrap/apps/kyverno.yaml` sets `features.backgroundScan.backgroundScanInterval` to 1h
(the chart's default, kept explicit) and the reports controller's CPU limit to 1 (request unchanged at 50m), and its
comment carries the table above in place of #323's reasoning. `verify/test_collector_config.py`'s #323 block now
holds 1h under the same feature-block key and a limit of a whole CPU, with the measurements. The comments on
`REPORT_TIMEOUT_S` in `verify/test_llm_bypass_live.py` and `verify/test_kyverno_cel_live.py`, which named the 30 s
rescan, now name the 45 s measured; the 150 s wait itself is unchanged. The watch-it-burn-community cluster runs no
Kyverno, so the change reaches watch-it-burn-private and attendee clusters. On an attendee cluster with about forty
Pods, a 30 s rescan at 200m also cannot finish inside its interval, so Challenge 2's report was late there too.

**Not yet run on a cluster:** the change itself, once Argo CD syncs it to watch-it-burn-private:
`CONTEXT=watch-it-burn-private python3 verify/test_llm_bypass_live.py` with the Deployment reading `cpu: "1"` and
`--backgroundScanInterval=1h`. The next run on #608, or any run on the cluster, records it here. The measured run
above was on the same values set by hand.

**Suites (run 17353, at 3ba5016).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran the offline suite (256 tests, ALL OFFLINE
RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN, `test_collector_config.py` among them) and then the tools tier: 55 checks in 25m37s,

**Live, on watch-it-burn-private (accen-dev, us-west-2), at staging `a2c7309`, which Argo CD had synced.** This is

burritobot-private.burritobot.co --context watch-it-burn-private --kubeconfig "$KUBECONFIG" --profile accen-dev`
printed CAUGHT for the card, the SSN, the e-mail, the phone number and the stage prompt, each by `Regex` at 1.0, then
"OK order a plain order passes both input stages", and ended `PII GREEN: THE INPUT GUARD REFUSES 5 OF 5`. No model
call, nothing toggled. The skipped `REFUSES 0 OF 5` baseline is moot: the scanner has been on staging since `53b2c9c`.

**Read from Whitney's org with the repo's key (`watch-it-burn/datadog`).** The key reads APM retention filters, APM
span search and LLM Observability spans. It may not write: creating the `@session.id:wib-stage-*` retention filter
answered 403, so that filter stays the Night Before click in the UI. The org has no such filter today, only Datadog's
four defaults. `@session.id` is the facet APM finds guard-proxy's root span by: `service:burritobot
@session.id:wib-stage-*` found the 13 sessions of the 2026-10-31 seeds on `burritobot-private`. LLM Observability
still held every one of those seeds five days on (c1-attack 7 spans with `get_vault_entry`, c3-attack 13 with
`read_support_ticket` and `deploy_app`, c4-attack 9 with `get_weather` and `read_internal_config`). The browser route
could not save views: Michael's Chrome on tanjiro-wsl2 opened app.datadoghq.com on its sign-in page.

**What the live reads found, and the three changes.**
- `check` read a fixed 48 hours, so on the 2026-10-31 seeds it printed "no spans" nine times and `STAGE TRACES RED`
  while Datadog held them. `seed` now writes `seeded_at`, and `check` reads back to it plus two hours, never under 48
  (`lookback_hours`). A views file without `seeded_at` is status 2, naming the field.
- Datadog's saved-views page (docs.datadoghq.com/logs/explorer/saved_views, read 2026-11-05): "Saved View is meant to
  track live time ranges", and a fixed range is converted to a live one when saved. A seed view saved on its own
  window would read the last half hour on stage and find nothing. Each seed's link now carries `start`, `end` and
  `paused=true` (and `historicalData=true` on the Trace Explorer one), from five minutes before the seed starts to ten
  minutes after it ends, so the link finds its trace whenever it is opened. The run-of-show has Whitney set Past 7 Days before saving a seed
  view, and Past 15 Minutes for the two live tabs, which stay unpinned. These are the parameters run 10444's draft
  used; whether LLM Observability honors them is not measured, since no browser here is signed in. A page that
  ignores them opens on its live default, as every link did before.
- The private cluster was not at the stage's start state: `lab-bootstrap` renders `values-admin.yaml` there (and
  `values-burn.yaml` on the community cluster), so Argo CD applies KubeArmor's `block-recipe-snoop` and
  `agent-egress-allowlist`, and `deny-external-registries` is not installed. The probe records a failed start-state
  and goes on, so a seed there would have spent eight model calls on wrong seeds and then had its closing
  `guardrails-off` strip two Argo-managed guardrails. `seed` now reads the identity and the start state first and,
  when either fails, prints `SEEDED RED`, sends nothing, flips nothing and writes no views file. Live, on
  watch-it-burn-private: it printed the start-state FAIL above and `SEEDED RED: not at the stage's start state, so
  nothing was sent and nothing was flipped`, exit 1, no views file; `block-recipe-snoop` and `agent-egress-allowlist`
  were still applied after it. Nothing on the cluster changed.

`verify/test_stage_traces.py` gains the checks: a five-day-old seed found by `check` over a window reaching back to it
(a fake Datadog that answers empty to a shorter window), the 48-hour floor, the missing `seeded_at`, every seed link
paused on a window around the seed and the live tabs unpinned, and a cluster left armed refused before any `/chat`
with an empty action log. Against the previous `stage_traces.py` the new checks fail.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The seed itself needs the stage's start state, which neither cluster has today: the
KubeCon bring-up on the `kubecon-private` profile, or the Night Before (2026-11-11). There, in order: the retention
filter in the UI, `seed` ending `SEEDED GREEN`, Whitney saving the views on Past 7 Days, and `check` the morning of.

  the crane pin, the script or itself. It fetches crane 0.22.1 from `verify/e2e-tools.lock`'s row and checks its

## 2026-11-05 · #771 · A live judge of #746's five checks, read from the LLM Observability spans API

**What was asked.** Whitney's done-when list on #746 was read by eye in her sandbox org: one root row per chat; the
prompt and the final reply on it; `read_support_ticket` and `deploy_app` under it; a duration covering the whole chat;
tokens and an estimated cost, with no `cost_estimate_status:skipped_tokens_missing`. #771 asks for that look as a
SUITE: e2e live test on the read-only key path, written against a real response once #759 gave runs read access, with
an offline test that judges a recorded payload. `verify/prior-drafts.sh 771 origin/staging` printed NONE. #759 is
done (run 17391, `b499c839`), and run 17405 read with its session.

**The response, as read.** Datadog's API reference has no response schema for `/api/v2/llm-obs/v1/spans/events`, so
the fields were read off a real response first (trace `098fcb005cbe5ed190ad9022a96b03c0`). Each `data[].attributes`
holds trace_id, span_id, parent_id (the string `undefined` on a root), name, span_kind, start_ns, duration in ns,
status, `input` and `output` as `{"value": ..., "messages": [...]}`, `metrics` and `tags` as `key:value` strings.
guard-proxy's root carries `url.path:/chat`, `span.kind:server` and `session_id`. The llm rows' metrics carry
input_tokens, output_tokens and total_tokens. No row carried a cost metric; Datadog's cost docs name it
`estimated_total_cost`, in nanodollars, and the llm rows carry the tag
`cost_estimate_status:skipped_unsupported_model_pricing`. `filter[from]` and `filter[to]` take ISO 8601 times, and
`filter[tags]` and `filter[session_id]` are ignored (both returned the whole window).

**The judge.** `verify/llmobs_chat_judge.py` lists the window (`--minutes`, default 1440), takes the traces holding a
`url.path:/chat` span, and judges the newest that called both tools; with none, the newest chat, which then fails
check 3 by name; with no `/chat` at all, it fails and says to send the HC-666 prompt. It reads that trace whole by
its id, and lists every span in the root's own interval, one second each side. The checks:
1. exactly one root, guard-proxy's `/chat` server span, with a session_id, and no span of another trace in the
   interval carrying that session (a second row for the chat); a listing that fills a page fails, since a second row
   could be past it;
2. the root's input is not empty, and its output is not empty and not the prompt again (the old "No content" root);
3. a tool row of each name whose parent chain reaches the root;
4. the root starts no later than the first span and ends no earlier than the last, with 100 ms of slack for the
   three pods' clocks (kagent's own 14 ms server span, the root #746 replaced, fails it by seconds);
5. at least one llm row, every one with input and output tokens and `estimated_total_cost` above zero, and no row
   with `cost_estimate_status:skipped_tokens_missing`. A failed cost check names the status and the issue that owns
   it (#784 for missing tokens, #876 for an unpriced model).

The root's reply is not required to equal the last model reply, though on both chats below it does: Act 2's output
guard can rewrite the reply on guard-proxy's span, and that would read as a failure that is not one.

**Tests.** `verify/test_llmobs_chat_judge_live.py` (SUITE: e2e) runs the judge as `WIB_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` in
`WIB_REGION`, as `test_datadog_sandbox_live.py` does, over `WIB_LLMOBS_JUDGE_MINUTES` (default 1440). The offline
`verify/test_llmobs_chat_judge.py` serves `verify/fixtures/llmobs-chat-judge/chat-098fcb00.json`, two real responses
recorded by this run (the trace by id, and its interval), through a fake transport. Only the `messages` lists and
`tool_definitions` are cut to a count. As recorded it fails the cost check alone, as the org did; with a cost put on
the llm rows it passes all five; and each of 15 breaks (a second root, a second trace with the session, a full page,
a root that is not `/chat`, no session, an empty output, an echoed prompt, an empty prompt, no `deploy_app`, a 14 ms
root, a late root, no output tokens, no cost, `skipped_tokens_missing`, no llm row) fails exactly its check. It also
covers the choice of chat, the empty window, GETs only, and a key that reaches another org.

**Live, 2026-11-05.** `. "$HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV"` then `python3 verify/test_llmobs_chat_judge_live.py` at 09:26:44Z
picked trace `098fcb005cbe5ed190ad9022a96b03c0` (the newest of 37 `/chat` traces that called both tools; run 17389's
HC-666 chat on `burritobot-public`, 08:29:02Z) and exited 1:

    PASS  the chat's trace has exactly one root row
    PASS  the root is guard-proxy's /chat server span (url.path:/chat, span.kind:server)
    PASS  the root carries the chat's session_id
    PASS  the listing of the chat's interval is complete (under 500 spans)
    PASS  no other trace in the chat's interval carries its session_id (no second row for the chat)
    PASS  the root's input is the prompt (not empty)
    PASS  the root's output is the reply (not empty, not the prompt)
    PASS  a tool row read_support_ticket sits under the root
    PASS  a tool row deploy_app sits under the root
    PASS  the root starts with the chat and ends after its last span (100 ms slack)
          root 4886 ms; the chat's spans span 4886 ms
    PASS  the chat has model-call (llm) rows
    PASS  every llm row carries input and output tokens
    FAIL  every llm row has an estimated cost (metrics.estimated_total_cost)
          3 of 3 llm rows have none; cost_estimate_status: skipped_unsupported_model_pricing
          16666 tokens over 3 model calls, estimated cost 0.000000 USD
    PASS  no row reads cost_estimate_status:skipped_tokens_missing

`--trace e9fb58989b865e2c9ce24f338cd16c71` (the same chat on `burritobot-private`, 08:27:48Z, root 5878 ms, 17282
tokens) read the same: four checks green, the cost check red on `skipped_unsupported_model_pricing`. `--trace
39fba3d0574259a99e1a646ed1e89818`, the community send guard-proxy answered with a 502, failed the reply, both tool
checks and the llm-row check, so the dropped chat that reads as a green row in the UI reads red here.

**What this says about #746.** Four of the five checks hold on live traces from both clusters, as run 17389's look
found. The fifth holds for tokens and for `skipped_tokens_missing`, and fails for the estimated cost: Datadog has no
price for the cluster's Bedrock application inference-profile ARN, which is the model name. That is #876, already
open. The live test stays red until #876's change reaches the clusters; it is the check #876's run can close on.

## 2026-11-05 · #733 · #707's live check passes on watch-it-burn-community, and the audit log shows how the first move went on both clusters

**No code changed.** Hecaton run 17386 is the first #733 run that could read its cluster session (hecaton#508 is
fixed). It ran every read the 2026-11-02 entries name, on watch-it-burn-community (the public burn cluster), and the
first-move reads on watch-it-burn-private (the admin cluster) as well. EKS control-plane audit logging is on for both
clusters, and their CloudWatch log groups (`/aws/eks/<cluster>/cluster`) keep events with no expiry, so the first
move of 2026-10-31 was read from the API server's own record, not inferred from timestamps.

**Synced and Healthy at a revision carrying 4cd52ed.** On community, `workshop-agent` read `Synced Healthy` at
`ad18f774`, and `lab-bootstrap` read `Synced Healthy` at `f709b00e`, this run's base. `813404e` (4cd52ed as it reached
staging) and `a29bb91` (the swap) are both ancestors of `ad18f774`. The Agent's tracking-id is
`workshop-agent:kagent.dev/Agent:agent/workshop-agent`.

**The git change reached the cluster with no converge.** Run 15968's swap, `a29bb91`, put `reorder_supply` before
`check_inventory`. `workshop-agent`'s history records it as an automated sync at 2026-11-02T10:40:10Z, and the audit
log has the matching server-side apply patches by `argocd-application-controller` at 10:40:10.7. The issue's read
printed git's list, in git's order:

    $ kubectl --context watch-it-burn-community -n agent get agent workshop-agent \
        -o jsonpath='{.spec.declarative.tools[0].mcpServer.toolNames}'
    ["lookup_customer_records","reorder_supply","check_inventory","get_order_history","get_marketing_intel",
     "search_web","read_support_ticket","post_marketing","get_vault_entry","list_services","deploy_app","run_shell"]

A converge could not have done it: `repair_agent_tools` compares sorted lists and deletes the Agent when they differ,
and the audit log has no create or delete of the Agent from 2026-10-31 08:52Z to this run. Every write to it in that
time is by `argocd-application-controller` (seven syncs, each matching a history entry), by kagent's and the garbage
collector's service accounts, or by the web terminal's `kubectl patch` (the C7 toggle, on 11-02 at 10:45 and 10:47
and in this run). No user identity wrote it.

**guard-mcp-on survives a reconcile.** Before: evil-mcp's toolNames read
`["get_weather","read_internal_config","apply_optimization"]`. At 08:27:48Z this run ran
`kubectl --context watch-it-burn-community -n agent exec deploy/web-terminal -c ttyd -- bash -c '"$HOME/guard-mcp-on"'`.
It took the `toolnames` branch, patched `/spec/declarative/tools/1/mcpServer/toolNames` to `["get_weather"]`, and
exited 0. Argo CD's reconciliation period here is 120s with 60s of jitter. `workshop-agent` next reconciled at
08:30:40Z and stayed `Synced Healthy`, with no new operation (its last is still the 2026-11-04T20:45:56Z sync). At
08:32:05Z, 85 seconds past that reconcile, evil-mcp still read `["get_weather"]` and workshop-mcp's list was unchanged.
Then `guard-mcp-off` in the same terminal put the list back to all three, the Application read `Synced Healthy`, and
the agent Deployment read 1/1 ready: the cluster is as this run found it.

**How the first move went: the two clusters raced, and each went a different way.**
- *watch-it-burn-community: ai-layer pruned the Agent, and workshop-agent made it again.* ai-layer's sync to
  `813404e` began at 08:50:10Z on 2026-10-31. At 08:50:27.5 `argocd-application-controller` deleted the Agent; the
  `workshop-agent` Application did not exist yet (the root created it at 08:51:03.9), so the delete was ai-layer's
  prune. Argo CD prunes with foreground propagation, so the Agent stayed, marked for deletion, until the garbage
  collector had removed its dependents. kagent's controller kept making the agent Deployment again, and the
  collector kept deleting it: 30 Deployment creates and 30 pods scheduled between 08:50:30.5 and 08:51:34.6, about
  one every two seconds. workshop-agent's first sync at 08:51:04.7 applied to the Agent while it was still being
  deleted, which did not stop the delete. The collector released the Agent at 08:51:34.1, and workshop-agent's next
  sync created it at 08:51:34.6 (HTTP 201). The current Agent and Deployment both date from 08:51:34Z. So the agent
  was down for about 67 seconds and its pod cycled about thirty times, where the #707 entry expected one cycle. Any C7
  state live then was reset.
- *watch-it-burn-private: workshop-agent took the Agent over first.* The root created `workshop-agent` at 08:49:04Z,
  and its sync patched the Agent at 08:49:05.6, changing its tracking-id before ai-layer's sync (which began at
  08:49:02.9) reached its prune. The audit log has no delete of the Agent and no create of the agent Deployment
  there, and the Agent still carries its 2026-10-28T11:59:00Z creation time. On private `workshop-agent` reads
  `Synced Healthy` at `9c9c414a`, with the same twelve tools in git's order.

Both clusters have moved, and a cluster built from now on gets the Agent from `workshop-agent` alone, so neither
outcome can recur from #707. The finding is general: when a kagent Agent changes Application on a running cluster
and the old one's prune wins, the agent is down for about a minute while kagent and the collector loop on its
Deployment.

**Reads, for a later run.** The first-move queries are CloudWatch Logs Insights on
`/aws/eks/watch-it-burn-community/cluster`, over 2026-10-31 08:40Z to 09:05Z:

    fields @timestamp, verb, objectRef.resource, responseStatus.code, user.username
    | filter objectRef.namespace="agent" and objectRef.name="workshop-agent"
      and objectRef.resource in ["agents","deployments"] and verb in ["create","delete","patch"]
    | sort @timestamp asc

The audit policy is at Metadata level, so request bodies (the delete's propagation policy among them) are not
recorded. The collector's two patches of the Agent just before it vanished are what foreground deletion does when
it removes its own finalizer.

**Tests.** No code changed; this run's suite results follow in the next entry.

llm-guard-cpu-offline reported its state on #719 (2026-10-31): main at `31962f2`, and `llm-guard-0.3.16-cpu.5`
(`sha256:4c66fd0f…8579791`), which bakes BanTopics' zero-shot model `deberta-v3-base-zeroshot-v2.0` at `8e7e5af5` and is past
GHSA-xcq7-p3pf-p88h, the OpenTelemetry advisory about unbounded tracestate parsing. The deployed guard, lab-platform's
`llm-guard:v1` (`sha256:6cdbf3a2…`, #652 and #730), has neither. The issue asks two things: whether to move this repo's
submodule pin, and which image BanTopics will run in for #455, the on-topic guard.

**Decision 1: images/llm-guard should move from f2fcb8f to 31962f2.** lab-platform's `build-llm-guard.sh` reads the API's source
at the llm-guard-cpu-offline commit this submodule pins, and lab-platform `27f4a49` (lab-platform#341) moved its
`SOURCE_COMMIT` to 31962f2 for the zero-shot model's licence file. cpu.5 was built from 31962f2 too. Nothing deployed changes:
`git diff --quiet f2fcb8f 31962f2 -- src` is clean, so the API files v1 was built from are the same, and nothing in this repo
builds from the submodule. The move brings llm-guard-cpu-offline's tests, `config/`, `overrides.txt` and the `model-zero-shot/`
mirror into `images/llm-guard`. 31962f2 is on that repo's main (fetched 2026-11-02, main now `28cc8b1`, which only records the
signed cpu.5 release in its README and decisions.md). The pin goes to 31962f2 rather than 28cc8b1 so it names the commit
lab-platform's build and cpu.5 both read.
- **Not committed here.** Run 15912 committed the gitlink move, and the dispatcher's `forbidden` gate failed run 15974 on
  it. The gate (hecaton `run/validate.py`, `gate_forbidden`) flags any changed path whose mode is 160000 as "adds
  submodule", so a run cannot move an existing pin either. Every pin move on staging was made in Michael's own sessions
  (`git log -- gitops/ai-layer/guard-proxy images/llm-guard`). Run 16431 put the gitlink back to f2fcb8f and escalated
  the move as exact commands, for a session that can commit a gitlink and push to staging:
  `git -C images/llm-guard fetch origin && git -C images/llm-guard checkout 31962f2074f758a2e9e06a9a91b4d758bcd56f03 &&
  git add images/llm-guard && git commit -m "Pin images/llm-guard at llm-guard-cpu-offline 31962f2 (#719)" &&
  bash verify/submodule-pins-pushed.sh && git push origin staging`. Nothing deployed waits on it: cpu.5 is pulled by

## 2026-11-05 · #793 · The live tier swap on watch-it-burn-community: /cost reads haiku in 3.8 s and new spend is at the Haiku row

**Context.** #793 had four items. Items 2 and 3 landed in 6525992e (run 16791, the 2026-11-03 · #793 entry), and the
repin, item 1, is Michael's a65f748d to c2eb4cf2, since moved again to 0f0c809 by 9f2b575c; both carry
guard-proxy-agenticburn#37 (c8ac56e), and `verify/test_guard_proxy_pin_bound_pricing.py` (#841) holds that. Item 4,
the swap on a cluster, was owed because runs 16460, 16752, 16791, 16852, 16869 and 16876 could not read their cluster
files (hecaton#508). Run 17416 could, and `bash verify/prior-drafts.sh 793 origin/staging` answered NONE: every
earlier draft is in staging or followed there by later #793 work, so nothing was ported.

**What changed.** The swap is now a live check that any cluster build reruns, not a hand procedure:
- `verify/test_tier_swap_live.py` (`# SUITE: e2e`, so `verify/run-e2e.sh` runs it on CONTEXT) checks that guard-proxy
  runs the pinned proxy.py (pod template, resources.yaml and the sha256 of the pinned file agree) with no
  COST_PER_1K_IN or COST_PER_1K_OUT override, that the Agent starts on bedrock-nova with `/cost`'s tier nova, then
  patches the Agent to bedrock-haiku and nothing else. A poller inside the guard-proxy pod reads the Agent with
  guard-proxy's own token and `/cost` on loopback on one clock, so the delay it reports carries no exec or clock-skew
  overhead; it bounds the delay from above by timing from the start of the last read that still showed bedrock-nova.
  The check wants that bound under the 5 s cache plus 1 s for the poll cycle, one `price_tier` log line naming
  bedrock-haiku, MODEL_TIER untouched, and, once kagent has rolled the agent out on the new config-hash, one /chat
  turn whose `cost_usd` is its tokens at the Haiku row and a `/cost` growth equal to the tokens it gained at the Haiku
  row. That last judge holds with a visitor's turn in the same window, since every turn after the swap is priced at
  Haiku, so the public bot's traffic does not make it fail. It then patches back to bedrock-nova and checks the tier
  and the rollout again; the swap back runs whatever failed after the first patch. The rates come from the pinned
  proxy.py's `TIER_PRICES_PER_1K`, not a copy. Patches go `--as` Argo CD's application controller, which Kyverno's
  block-argocd-drift always admits, so an armed cluster needs no policy flip and the policy is left as found.
- `verify/test_tier_swap_live_judges.py` (offline) runs the judges on the readings below and on each way they should
  fail: a 6.5 s flip, a poller timeout, a turn or counter priced at the Nova row, a guarded turn, a counter that did
  not count or was reset, a stale pod template, a price override, a `price_tier_unknown` line. It also compiles the
  two in-pod scripts and checks the poller reads the `_AGENT_PATH` the pinned proxy.py prices from.
- `docs/MASTER-RECREATION-SPEC.md`'s tier bullet no longer says the live patch is not validated live, and
  PROJECT_STATE.md's #793 section no longer lists the swap as owed. `verify/run-e2e.sh`'s header names what the new
  check spends.
