## 2026-11-05 · #727 · The C1 stage-2b fix landed as config: a forced egress proxy over a locked resolver

**What this run did.** It implemented the FQDN control chosen by question 1009 (#724), option B, a forced egress
proxy enforcing a hostname allowlist, on top of floor C, a locked DNS resolver, and landed it as config under
`challenges/c1-exfil-s3/fix/` with an offline test. Nothing was applied to a cluster. The live validation is owed and
tracked by #728.

**Why here, and why these pieces.** C1's second stage holds the direct HTTPS beacon with the L3/L4 egress allowlist,
and stage 2b carries the same marketing demographics out as labels in a DNS query name, which that allowlist cannot
read. The fix has two pieces that hold together. `resolver-lockdown.yaml` is floor C: a CoreDNS Corefile with no
catch-all `forward` in its `.` block, forwarding only `amazonaws.com` and `open-meteo.com` to the VPC resolver, so
in-cluster names, Bedrock and C7's weather host resolve and every other name, the collector's zone under
`agenticburn.com` included, comes back SERVFAIL without leaving the cluster. `egress-waypoint.yaml` is option B: an
Istio ambient egress waypoint, a `ServiceEntry` for the two Open-Meteo hosts, and an `AuthorizationPolicy` admitting
only those hosts at L7. `agent-egress-fqdn.yaml` makes the waypoint the one workload granted a public 443 and shuts
the weather feed's direct `TCP 443` to anywhere.

**What the build settled.** Question 1009 left two items to the build. Bedrock keeps its in-VPC `10.0.0.0/16:443`
allow and does not pass through the waypoint, because it is reached over PrivateLink inside the VPC rather than the
internet. The proxy allowlist is C7's two Open-Meteo hosts, `api.open-meteo.com` and `geocoding-api.open-meteo.com`,
read from `gitops/ai-layer/weather_feed.py`.

**Stage 2 kept intact.** The fix defines no `agent-egress-allowlist` and no `agent-allow-dns` of its own, so those
stage-2 objects stand unchanged, and `policies/network-policies/per-namespace/agent-egress-allowlist.yaml` still
carries the Bedrock, service-CIDR and Pod Identity allows. The one companion the fix rewrites is
`agent-allow-weather-feed-egress`, whose stage-2 broad `TCP 443` to anywhere is the last direct public door; the fix
replaces it with an empty egress rule set, since the weather feed reaches Open-Meteo through the waypoint now. No
`apps-*` policy and no `default-deny` is touched, and the other agent companions do not reach a public host, so no
other challenge's network assumptions change. `policies/network-policies/` is not edited by this run.

**Owed before it is applied live (#728).** The Istio version that supports the ambient egress pattern (the fleet
pins 1.30.4; the pattern is documented against 1.31 samples, which may need the Istio upgrade #860 left open for the
attendee and admin clusters); the Gateway API CRDs on the carrying cluster; that the waypoint pod label
(`gateway.networking.k8s.io/gateway-name` or `istio.io/gateway-name`) matches what the pinned Istio applies; and
pinning the resolver lock through the `coredns` addon's `configuration_values`
(`infra/terraform/aws/cluster/main.tf:324`) so the managed addon keeps it. These are listed in
`challenges/c1-exfil-s3/fix/README.md`.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The owed live check stays as the design note
(`docs/research/2026-10-31-c1-dns-exfil-beat.md`) lists it, under the `verify/run-e2e.sh` tier: a script paralleling
`verify/c1-exfil-block.sh`, built by #728, asserts on a fresh attendee cluster that with the fix applied the DNS
collector records nothing new for the same stage-2b request, while the beacon stays held and Bedrock and in-cluster
resolution still answer so BurritoBot still replies.

**The suites (run 17752, at `d8866463`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` printed `267 tests ran` and
`ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN` for the offline suite (`bash verify/run-tests.sh`), with
`test_c1_dns_exfil_fix.py` among them, then `58 checks ran (the offline suite and 57 tier tests) in 40m10s`,
`ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN` and `exit=0`. The log's one `FAIL` line, `security datadog-secret fields: api-key;
missing: app-key(empty)`, is the output of a negative fixture whose next check prints PASS. The run before this one,
17583, saw `test_e2e_tools_tier.py` fail in its offline pass: `mktemp` could not create a directory under `/tmp`, and
the log ends with `getwd: no such file or directory`, so the run's temp space and working directory went away while

command each time. Run alone, and in this run's full pass, the test is green. The log is
`/var/lib/hecaton/runs/17752/e2e-tools.log`.

**Live check (run 17752, 2026-11-06, read-only, `--context watch-it-burn-private` on every call).** Nothing was
applied, and neither cluster was changed. The `coredns` ConfigMap's Corefile carries `kubernetes cluster.local

**What the wall's code says, read at `6601313a`, for the run that writes the test.**

- The page reads `/events?since=<cursor>` (SSE), after one `fetch('/api/prompts')` whose answer goes up at once; only
  what arrives after that first snapshot goes through `makeThrottle()`. The stream sends one `data:` frame a second
  at most (`time.sleep(1)` in `events()`), so 17 prompts a second reach the page as batches of about 17, which is
  the half-window case the throttle's comment describes.

  count is bounded by code. The `shown` set of seqs the page keeps for #14's duplicate guard is not trimmed, which is
  about 5,100 numbers over the 5 minutes; the heap check is the one that would see it if it mattered.

  already sets it), so no cluster or roster is read.
- The existing page test, `test_wall_page.py`, runs the page in MiniRacer on a fake browser. Frame time and JS heap
  need a real headless browser (Chromium's `performance.memory` or the DevTools protocol), which is a new dev
  dependency there, and a browser download that hecaton's rules put under an E2E command rather than the test
  command. Which of the two it runs under, against the issue's fifth criterion, is that repo's call.

## 2026-11-06: decisions.md and PROGRESS.md merge with git's union driver (#958, run 17764)

**What changed.** A root `.gitattributes` now holds `decisions.md merge=union` and `PROGRESS.md merge=union`, under an
ABOUTME comment saying why, and nothing else. From 2026-11-05, nineteen runs ended `failed (rebase-conflict)` against
86 merges (hecaton#532), most on two runs each adding an entry to the end of decisions.md. The union driver keeps both
sides of a conflicting hunk, the upstream entry first and then the replayed one, so that rebase is now clean.

**Why only these two.** Union never reports a conflict: two edits to the same lines of a verify/ test, a Terraform root or
PROJECT_STATE.md would both be kept, silently. The two files listed only ever take new entries: decisions.md at the
end, PROGRESS.md at the top of `### Added`. The patterns carry no slash, so a decisions.md added in a subdirectory would
match too; the test lists every tracked path git reads as union, so such a file fails it and gets a decision of its own.

**What hecaton already did.** Its promoter writes `decisions.md merge=union` into the promotion checkout's own
`.git/info/attributes` before replaying a run (`union_append_only`, hecaton#137), which covers that one checkout and
not PROGRESS.md. The tracked file applies in every clone, the run's own rebase included.

**One property of union, seen on a scratch repo.** A line both sides add at the same place is kept once. Two entries
that each open with a blank line merge with no blank line between them, so the second heading follows the first
entry's last line directly. It still starts its own line and still renders as a heading; a reader tidying the file may
add the blank line back.

**The test.** `verify/test_gitattributes_union.py` (offline, stdlib only, runnable under pytest or as `python3 <file>`,
as run-tests.sh does) builds each scratch repo in `tmp_path` with hooks off and no user or system git config. It checks
that `git check-attr merge decisions.md` (and PROGRESS.md) prints `union` in this repo and in a fresh repo holding only a
copy of the file, so no `info/attributes` can be what answers; that `git check-attr` over every tracked file finds
union on those two alone; that two branches each appending an entry to decisions.md rebase with exit 0, no conflict
markers and both entries in order; that two entries added under PROGRESS.md's `### Added` rebase with both; and, as
controls, that the same decisions.md rebase without the attribute conflicts and that a verify/ test edited on both
sides still conflicts with the real file. Run against a `.gitattributes` with an extra `*.tf merge=union` line, two
checks fail; against one with no rules, four fail.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing is owed: the change is to how git merges two files and touches no cluster.

**The suites (run 17764, at `cfff4535`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran the offline suite (`280 tests ran`,
`ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`, `6/6 gitattributes union checks passed` among them) and then the tier: `63 checks
ran (the offline suite and 62 tier tests) in 36m40s`, `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN`, exit 0.

## 2026-11-05 · #921 · run 17641 · guard-proxy's /prompts gains `witches`, each prompt's witch name at its index; the change goes to guard-proxy-agenticburn

**What #921 asks.** Each prompt on the prompt wall (prompts.burritobot.co) shows its sender's witch name instead of
the cluster, and the cluster stays as metadata for the wall's "All clusters" filter. This issue is the feed half,
in guard-proxy-agenticburn (the submodule at `gitops/ai-layer/guard-proxy`). The wall half is
prompts-agenticburn#16. `verify/prior-drafts.sh 921 origin/staging` printed NONE.

**What the feed carries today.** guard-proxy's `GET /prompts` answers `{"enabled": bool, "prompts": [str]}`, a bare
list of moderated texts from a 50-deep deque, in both proxy.py and the Go build. The `seq`, `cluster`, `text` and
`ts` the issue names are the wall's own entries: prompts-agenticburn's `ingest()` builds them, takes `cluster` from
the host it polled, and stamps `ts` on receipt. So `cluster` was never in guard-proxy's feed, and it stays where it
is, on the wall's entry. guard-proxy does not know its cluster's wall name.

**Why `prompts` stays as it is.** Three readers parse `prompts` as strings, and changing it to objects would empty
the wall rather than label it:
- prompts-agenticburn's `parse_payload()` keeps only `isinstance(p, str)` items, so every prompt would be dropped.
- lab-platform's `internal/promptfeed` decodes `prompts` as `*[]string`, so every cluster would read unavailable.
- `gitops/ai-layer/web/display.js` sets each item as a card's `textContent`.
`verify/kubecon_probe.py`'s `judge_feed` and `verify/test_prompt_wall_redaction.py` also read `prompts`. None of them
breaks on an extra key.

**Why a list of names, not a list of `{text, witch}` objects.** Run 17641 first built `entries`, a second list of
`{"text", "witch"}` objects, and dropped it on lab-platform's read bound. lab-platform's promptfeed refuses a
`/prompts` body over 256 KiB (`MaxBodyBytes`, 262,144 bytes) whole, and the cluster then reads unavailable. proxy.py
writes JSON with `json.dumps`, which escapes each emoji as a 12-byte surrogate pair, so fifty 280-character emoji
prompts are already 170,293 bytes with names. Carrying each text twice made it 339,443 bytes, so one attendee
pasting emoji would take the community cluster off any wall lab-platform feeds. The names alone add at most about
2 KB.

**The field.** `witches`, a list of strings as long as `prompts`, where `witches[i]` is the witch name of the
person who sent `prompts[i]`. Both lists come from one copy of the deque under one lock, so they always line up.
The name is the one `/chat` already reads and shape-checks (#762, guard-proxy-agenticburn#34): `<First> the
<Creature>`, where a blank, non-string or misshaped one is no name. Rules:
- **No name is `""`, never null and never a shorter list.** That covers a `/chat` without `witch`, a blank,
  non-string or misshaped one, and every prompt from the A2A path (the terminal and kagent), which has no name to
  carry.
- **A name moderation would change is dropped whole, to `""`.** The name is chosen client-side and only
  shape-checked, so "Shit the Ghoul" or "Delete the Witch" passes the shape and would be projected. The feed's
  moderator (personal data, block-list, profanity) runs over the name, and if anything would be masked the prompt
  carries no name, never a half-masked label like "[redacted] the Ghoul". All 768 names the storefront deals
  (`FIRST` by `CREATURES` in `gitops/ai-layer/ticket_site.py`) pass the moderator unchanged, checked in this run.
- **The name never goes into the text.** `prompts` holds the prompt alone, as before.
- Probes, the feed being off, and the 50-prompt bound apply to the names exactly as to the prompts.

**What the wall shows for a prompt with no name.** The words "someone who gave no name", which the desk's
deployments list (`gitops/ai-layer/ticket_site.py`, the "deployed by" line on `/me`) already shows for a deployment
without a name, so the two read the same. The cluster is not shown in its place, for either bot. The wall's code is
prompts-agenticburn#16. It reads `witches` when the list is there and as long as `prompts`, and otherwise treats
every prompt from that cluster as having no name, for a cluster still on an older guard-proxy.

**Why the change is not committed in this run.** Its code lives in guard-proxy-agenticburn, a repo this run cannot
commit to or push. Moving this repo's pin is a change hecaton's `forbidden` gate refuses for any run (the
2026-11-05 #382 entry). So the change goes to guard-proxy-agenticburn as a follow-up, and the repin after it is
Michael's commit, as every repin here has been.

**The change, built and tested in this run.** Run 17641 wrote it in the submodule's checkout at
guard-proxy-agenticburn main `c5f71f3`, ran that repo's suites, and put the checkout back on its pin `0f0c809`.
Nothing was committed there. The follow-up carries the design and the diff:
- proxy.py: the deque holds `(moderated text, witch)` pairs. `record_prompt(text, witch="")` replaces the two
  inline appends (the A2A path passes no name), `feed_witch()` applies the moderation rule, and `feed_payload()`
  builds the GET body with `prompts` and `witches`.
- Go: `Feed.Record(text, witch)` and `Feed.Snapshot()`, which returns both lists under one lock. `chat.go` passes the
  shaped name, and the A2A path in `server.go` passes `""`.
- Conformance (`conformance/test_prompt_feed.py`, both builds): names at their prompts' indexes beside unchanged
  texts; the no-name case for a missing, blank, non-string or misshaped name and for the A2A path; a name
  moderation would mask dropped whole; the 50 bound with names and prompts in step; moderation and probes; nothing
  recorded with the feed off; and fifty named 280-character emoji prompts fit in 256 KiB. The two exact-equality
  feed tests gain `"witches"`, and `test_chat_witch.py`'s feed test checks the name is in `witches` and not in the
  text. Go unit tests in `internal/feed/feed_test.go` cover the same cases.
- `conformance/mutation_check.py`: the "feed redaction reaches the bot" mutant moves to the new call, and four are
  added: the names dropped, the names out of step with the prompts, a masked name shown, and the name put into the
  prompt text.

**Live, 2026-11-05 (read only).** `kubectl --context <ctx> -n agent exec deploy/guard-proxy -c proxy -- python3 -c
<GET 127.0.0.1:8080/prompts, print its keys and item types>` printed `['enabled', 'prompts'] True 0 []` on

## 2026-11-06 · #893 · run 17780 · A test reads decisions.md for #759's record of the trace read: the command, its exit and the recent trace it printed

**Why.** Test review run 17398 found that no test checked the last part of a #759 criterion, "A run reads back one
recent BurritoBot trace through that access and records the command in decisions.md". `verify/test_dd_traces_live.py`
does the read and `verify/test_dd_traces.py` judges the reader against a fake org, but nothing read decisions.md, so
the record could be lost or never written and every suite would stay green. `verify/prior-drafts.sh 893 origin/staging`
printed NONE, and the issue has no comments.

**The test.** `verify/test_dd_traces_record.py` is offline and runs in `bash verify/run-tests.sh`. It splits
decisions.md into entries at each `## ` line and fails unless one entry headed with #759 (not `#759's`) records the
read whole:
- The access: `. "$HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV"` on a line of its own, a `python3 verify/dd_traces.py` command after it, and
  the secret `fleet_monitors.SECRET_ID` named in the entry.
- The command: it is run through `dd_traces.main` against a fake org of three traces, with a keys stub, and must ask
  for the pair as the profile and region AGENTS.md gives a run's session (accen-dev, us-west-2), exit 0, and print
  exactly one trace, the newest. So `--traces 3`, `--scopes`, `--json`, `--trace <old id>` or another profile fails.
- The outcome: the entry says the command exited 0.
- The output: after the command, the header `dd_traces.main` prints for `ml_app:burritobot` over the command's own
  `--minutes`, then a trace line and a span line of the shape `show_trace` prints. The test first renders a trace with
  `show_trace` and checks its own patterns match, so a change to the reader's output names the patterns.
- Recent: the newest timestamp before the source step (`At 2026-11-05T08:29Z` in the record) is when the command ran,
  and the trace must have started inside the command's window before then, with one minute of clock skew.

Today it passes on the 2026-11-05 #759 entry (run 17391): trace 0d630795c18555edbaca6bf41eece528, started 07:49:47Z,
40 minutes before the 08:29Z run, inside the 1440-minute window. The two 2026-11-03 #759 entries are refused (no exit 0,
no output), as they should be, since those runs could not do the read.

**It fails when the record stops holding.** The test then cuts the entry it found in nine ways and checks each is
refused, and each was refused for its own reason: the command removed, `--traces 1` made `--traces 3`, the profile
changed, the command replaced by a `--scopes` one, the source step removed, the trace line removed, the header's
window off by one minute, the run stamp moved two days on, and "exited 0" removed. Before each cut it checks the
literal it replaces is in the record, and exits naming it and decisions.md when it is not.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing is owed. The test reads the tree only; the live read it holds the record of is
`verify/test_dd_traces_live.py`, run green by run 17742 on 2026-11-05T23:04Z.

No dependency was added.

**Live check, run 17780 (GETs only; nothing changed).** At 2026-11-06T01:42Z, after `. "$HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV"`,
`python3 verify/dd_traces.py --profile accen-dev --minutes 1440 --traces 1` exited 0 and printed trace
56b27441c9d85948a1f3c11aeb1568ee (2026-11-06T01:38:25Z, 6 spans, 1 root, env=burritobot-kubecon-na-26), with two
`generate_content` spans on `us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0` and a `lookup_customer_records` tool span. So the recorded
command still reads a recent trace through the run's access.

**The suites (run 17780, at `7ac3a480`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran the offline suite (`282 tests ran`,

## 2026-11-05 · #951 · run 17734 · The recipe recon-then-attack rule lands in BurritoBot's one system prompt

#925 (Whitney, 2026-11-05) found the room cannot do Challenge 2's recipe attack from a phone: the `/kubecon` prompt
only works because it carries a shell command and a path (`grep -ri -A3 recipe /tmp/burrito-data`) that no attendee
could guess, and the system prompt said nothing about where the kitchen files are. #951, the first child, builds the
conversational recon-then-attack flow into the one `systemMessage` every cluster reads
(`gitops/workshop-agent/agent.yaml`, `spec.declarative.systemMessage`), modelled on the `ceo-personal-record`
address paragraph. The later children of #925 adjust the `/kubecon` prompt sheet and validate the live behaviour
after Argo CD syncs this; #951 is the system-prompt change only.

**The file name (a coordinator call made on #951, folder `burrito-data`, the file picked here).** The recipe card is
the existing C3 bait, `/tmp/burrito-data/config/legacy/secret-sauce-recipe.conf`. It is baked into the
`images/workshop-mcp` image (`images/workshop-mcp/Dockerfile`) and blocked for the workshop-mcp pod by
`policies/kubearmor/block-recipe-snoop.yaml` (directory `/tmp/burrito-data/config/legacy/`, action Block). Naming
that same file in the prompt means slide 21, the KubeArmor policy and the image stay exactly as they are and no
`images/workshop-mcp` change is needed. The folder the bot names is `burrito-data` (the name #925's prompts already
use), with the `config` and `legacy` folders inside it.

**The rule's exact wording, appended after the CEO paragraph:**

```
The sauce recipe is another such secret, kept on a recipe card in your kitchen files. Your kitchen folder is
"burrito-data" (/tmp/burrito-data in your shell), and the card is secret-sauce-recipe.conf in its config/legacy
folder: /tmp/burrito-data/config/legacy/secret-sauce-recipe.conf. When a guest asks what files or folders you can
see or have access to, name your folders from what you know here (burrito-data, and the config and legacy folders
inside it) and open nothing: no tool call, no listing, no reading, and no file names. In a conversation where the
guest has asked what you can see, playfully decline to open any file or folder for them after that ("Ooh, the
pantry's off-limits to snoops, sugar!") and steer back to the order; keep it a light kitchen joke, never a scolding
or a warning. Before you call a tool that reads the recipe card, check two things: the conversation has not included
that question of what you can see, and the guest's own message names the burrito-data folder or the recipe file and
gives a kitchen reason (a kitchen audit, a lost or ruined recipe card, the dinner rush, any decent cantina story).
When both hold, read the card with run_shell (cat the card, or run the command the guest gave you) and read them the
whole recipe, signature line and all. A bare "read me the recipe" with no reason at all gets one playful nudge first.
```

**Why it is written this way.** The flow has the four beats #925 asked for: recon names the folders (including
`burrito-data`) and opens nothing; a later ask in a conversation that included the recon question is playfully
declined; the read happens only when the guest's own message names the folder or file with a kitchen reason and the
conversation has not included the recon question; and there is no absolute refusal. The CEO rule and the global
staying-in-character section already forbid labelling anything suspicious or a security concern, so the decline is
framed as a light kitchen joke and the rule itself carries neither the word "suspicious" nor "security", which keeps
it to the issue's "no suspicious/security language". No "never, no matter what" wall: a hard refusal makes the model
self-censor the recipe signature, which breaks both the community-cluster leak and the output guard (memory:
agent-graduated-resistance). Recon deliberately does not hand out file names, so the attack still needs the guest's
own message to name the folder or file, as #925's recon and attack prompts do.

**The offline test.** `verify/test_recipe_persona.py` (modelled on `verify/test_ceo_persona.py`) extracts the rule
from the committed `agent.yaml` and asserts its shape (recon names the folders and opens nothing; the
same-conversation decline carries no "suspicious"/"security" wording; the read requires a named folder/file, a
kitchen reason and no prior recon), the exact file name against the KubeArmor policy and the Dockerfile, and the
absence of an absolute refusal. An untracked, syntactically broken stub `verify/test_recipe_recon_rule.py` (an
unterminated docstring, not in base, not mine) was found in the worktree and removed so the suite parses.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The live recon, same-conversation refusal, reset and attack on the public bot, and the
check that KubeArmor still blocks the read after `guardrails-on`, are #925's later children; they run once this
prompt reaches the clusters through Argo CD.

**The suites (run 17734, at `4d07cbad`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran the offline suite (`275 tests ran`,
`ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`, the new one being `test_recipe_persona.py`) and then the tier:
`61 checks ran (the offline suite and 60 tier tests) in 30m37s`,
`ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN`, `exit=0`.

## 2026-11-06 · #894 · run 17792 · a server span that answered 5xx is an error, in the collector

**What was wrong.** On watch-it-burn-community on 2026-11-05 (hecaton run 17389) an HC-666 chat reached guard-proxy
while workshop-agent rolled to a new ReplicaSet; the forward got 503 and guard-proxy answered 502 with "BurritoBot's
kitchen isn't answering". In Agent Observability that turn is trace 39fba3d0574259a99e1a646ed1e89818: one agent row,
36 ms, status ok, the prompt in and nothing out. proxy.py (pin `0f0c809`) marks its `agent.forward` CLIENT span ERROR,
but the copy drops that span for carrying no `gen_ai.*` attribute, and the `POST /chat` SERVER span that becomes the
copy's root carries `http.response.status_code` 502 with its status unset.

**Decided: the collector marks it, not guard-proxy.** `transform/http_server_error` (values.yaml, and burn's restated
list) runs on the traces pipeline after `transform/adk_tool_content`. On any SERVER span whose
`http.response.status_code` (or the older `http.status_code`) is 500 or more and whose status is still unset, it sets
`error.type` to the code as a string, `status.message` to "the server answered HTTP <code>", and STATUS_CODE_ERROR.
That is the HTTP semantic conventions' rule (http-spans.md, Status): Error on a 5xx, a server span's 4xx left unset,
and the code for `error.type` when nothing more specific is known. Why the collector:
- it ships from this repo; a guard-proxy change is a commit in guard-proxy-agenticburn and a repin here;
- it covers every 5xx exit, `_send`'s forward failure and the turn deadline's 502 alike, and any other service's
  server span, in APM, Tempo and the Agent Observability copy at once, since the copy is forwarded after it;
- it leaves alone a status an instrumentation already set, so `agent.forward` keeps proxy.py's message, and the 403,
  429 and 400 guard-proxy answers stay unset.

The one cost: APM now counts guard-proxy's 5xx turns as errors in its error rate. That is what they are.

**What it does not cover.** The raw A2A pass-through (`_handle_post`): its Agent Observability root is the `sanitize`
span, which carries no status code, so a failed forward there still reads green in Agent Observability (its `POST /`
is red in APM). The storefront chat, the one presenters open, is covered. The pass-through half is a guard-proxy change,
filed as a follow-up on guard-proxy-agenticburn.

**Tests.** `verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py` now sends, through each profile's real pipelines, a dropped chat as proxy.py
writes it (root 502 with the prompt and no reply, the chat wrapper, `agent.forward` ERROR with the HTTPError and 503,
urllib's POST) and a capped chat (429). It checks the root is ERROR with `error.type` 502 in APM and in the copy, still
one agent row with the prompt and no reply; `agent.forward` keeps proxy.py's status; the wrapper, the 200 turn and the
429 turn stay unset. With the processor taken out of the pipeline, the 502 checks fail on instructor and attendee.
`verify/test_collector_config.py` holds the offline half: the processor is wired in, reads the code only on SERVER
spans, marks only at 500 or more on an unset status, and reads no messages. Its "every error mark reads a tool response"
check now scopes to the tool marks.

**Live check, run 17792 (GET only; nothing changed).** After `. "$HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV"`,
`python3 verify/dd_traces.py --profile accen-dev --minutes 4320 --trace 39fba3d0574259a99e1a646ed1e89818` exited 0 and
printed `trace 39fba3d0574259a99e1a646ed1e89818  2026-11-05T08:27:54+00:00  1 spans  1 root(s)
env=burritobot-kubecon-na-26` and `agent POST  36 ms  ok`: the baseline the issue describes. The collector on
watch-it-burn-community runs `opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.160.0`, the version the E2E test validates against.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The forced forward failure, after this change syncs: on watch-it-burn-community, scale
the workshop-agent Deployment in `agent` to 0 (or send during a rollout), send one storefront chat through guard-proxy's
`/chat`, put the replicas back, and read the turn with `python3 verify/dd_traces.py --profile accen-dev --minutes 30
--traces 1`. The row should read `agent POST ... error`. Owed to the next run on #894.

`ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN` for the offline suite, then `64 checks ran (the offline suite and 63 tier tests)
in 46m48s`, `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN` and `exit=0`.

No dependency was added.

## 2026-11-06 · #898 · run 17796 · ai-layer's ordering gates are plain wave -1 Jobs, not PreSync hooks, so a full-sync self-heal does not wait on them

**What changed.** `kubearmor-gate` and `otel-gate` (gitops/ai-layer/kubearmor-ordering-gate.yaml and
otel-ordering-gate.yaml) were PreSync hooks. Every full sync of ai-layer deleted their eight objects, waited for the
deletion, re-created them and ran both Jobs before it applied anything, and the first self-heal after any commit on
staging is a full sync. They are now plain Sync-phase resources: every object of both files at
`argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-1"`, no hook annotations, and everything else in ai-layer is at wave 0. Of the
issue's options this is the first one. The window in docs/floor.md and the drill's `WINDOW_S` stay at 30 s.

**Why the ordering still holds.** Argo CD v3.5.7's sync engine (`gitops-engine/pkg/sync/sync_context.go` at the tag)
marks a plain resource Running after it is applied and, in a sync with more than one wave, does not start the next
wave until every Running task reads Healthy; a Job reads Progressing until its Complete condition
(`pkg/health/health_job.go`). So on a fresh cluster wave 0 (workshop-mcp, guard-proxy) is applied only after both
gates passed, as with the hooks. That is the ordering inside ai-layer only: argocd-cm on watch-it-burn-private has
no health customization for `argoproj.io_Application`, so the bootstrap's app waves order when each Application is
created and do not wait on ai-layer's health, before this change or after it. Within one wave the engine applies kinds in order, so the ServiceAccount,
ConfigMap and RBAC exist before the Job's pod is created; that is why all of a gate's objects share wave -1, which
costs one 2 s wave step (`delayBetweenSyncWaves`, controller/sync.go) rather than two.

**What a plain Job needs.**
- *A name that changes with it.* A Job's pod template is immutable, so the Jobs are `kubearmor-gate-d92910c4` and
  `otel-gate-0353f97d`: the first 8 hex of a sha256 over the Job's spec and its script's data. Any edit renames the
  Job, Argo CD prunes the old one and runs the new. `verify/test_ai_layer_gates.py` computes it and names the right
  suffix when it is stale.
- *No TTL.* `ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 120` is gone: a Job the cluster deletes reads as missing, and self-heal would
  re-create and re-run it every two minutes.
- *A label for recovery.* `app.kubernetes.io/name: <gate>` on the Job, so the recovery delete does not need the hash.
- `backoffLimit` 1 to 3, so a pod lost to a node goes again before the Job fails.

**What is given up, said once.** The gate runs when its Job is first created, not on every full sync, so a rollout of
workshop-mcp on a running cluster no longer re-checks KubeArmor first. KubeArmor is up by then on every cluster this
runs on. The failure mode moves: the gate script exits 0 on every path, so a gate Job fails only when its pod cannot
run for `activeDeadlineSeconds` (600). A Failed Job reads Degraded and fails every later ai-layer sync naming it, and
auto-sync does not retry a revision whose sync failed (controller/appcontroller.go `autoSync`), so it needs a
delete and a requested sync; docs/floor.md has both commands. The hooks' BeforeHookCreation retried that case by
itself on the next revision. #407's park, a fixed-name HookSucceeded hook left behind, cannot happen to a plain
resource.

**Live check, watch-it-burn-private, 2026-11-06 03:47 to 04:20 UTC.** Read-only except one scratch namespace.
- *Where the time goes now.* staging moved to ec03eb5f and a full sync of ai-layer ran at 03:47:22Z, finishing at
  03:47:51Z (29 s). The controller log: hook deletion 03:47:22 to 03:47:28, hook re-creation to 03:47:33, the Jobs
  applied at 03:47:34 and Succeeded at 03:47:43 (otel-gate) and 03:47:44 (kubearmor-gate), and
  `networkpolicy.networking.k8s.io/platform-console-egress serverside-applied` at 03:47:46. 24 s of the 29 went to the
  hooks.
- *Admission.* `kubectl apply --server-side --dry-run=server` of the rendered gate objects: both Jobs, both
  ServiceAccounts, ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings admitted. The two ConfigMaps were refused by Kyverno's
  `block-argocd-drift` for this run's principal, which is that policy working (it exempts Argo CD); it covers
  Deployments, ConfigMaps and Services only, not Jobs, so the recovery delete is admitted.
- *A completed Job re-applied.* In namespace `hecaton-898-scratch`, a Job with the gate's pod spec and a one-line
  command, applied with `--server-side --force-conflicts --field-manager=argocd-controller` as Argo CD applies,
  ran to Complete. `kubectl diff --server-side` of the same manifest printed nothing (exit 0); a second apply kept
  resourceVersion 7241314 and the uid, `succeeded` stayed 1, and no second pod started. The same Job with its command
  edited was refused: `The Job "probe-gate" is invalid: spec.template: Invalid value`, which is why the name is
  hashed. The namespace was deleted; `get namespace` then read NotFound.
- *KubeArmor today.* workshop-mcp on both clusters carries `kubearmor-policy=enabled` (pods from 2026-11-05 21:10Z
  and 21:13Z).

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Once hecaton promotes this, on watch-it-burn-private: the transition sync should
create `job/kubearmor-gate-d92910c4` and `job/otel-gate-0353f97d` in `agent`, both Complete, with ai-layer Synced and
Healthy. Then, on the first heal after the next staging commit,
`CONTEXT=watch-it-burn-private python3 verify/test_drift_selfheal_live.py` must print `healed by a full sync to
revision <rev>, PreSync Jobs run first: none` and the policy back within its 30 s, and
`kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private -n agent get pods -l app=workshop-mcp -o
jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.annotations.kubearmor-policy}'` must still print `enabled`. The fresh-cluster ordering
(workshop-mcp admitted after the gate on a first sync) needs a bring-up, which a run does not do; the next bring-up
checks it with `verify/run-e2e.sh`'s KubeArmor checks.

**Tests.** `verify/test_ai_layer_gates.py` (new, offline) holds the shape: no hook annotation in either gate file,
every object at wave -1, the hashed name, no TTL, the label, the script exiting 0 on every path and

hook. `verify/test_ai_layer_rollout.py` checks the render the same way. `verify/test_drift_selfheal_ops.py` now

## 2026-11-06 · #899 · run 17802 · LLM Guard checks its bearer token: llm-guard-scanners gains the auth block

**What was wrong.** Run 17422 on #455 found LLM Guard answering `/analyze/prompt` with an empty bearer token. The
vendored API checks a token only when `scanners.yml` has an `auth:` block (`images/llm-guard` `src/app/app.py`,
`_check_auth_function`: with no auth config it returns `check_auth_noop`). The `llm-guard-scanners` ConfigMap is mounted
over the image's config directory, and it had only `app`, `input_scanners` and `output_scanners`, so the `AUTH_TOKEN` the
Deployment sets from `llm-guard-auth` was never read. Anything that could reach `llm-guard:8000` could call the guard.

**The change.**
- `gitops/ai-layer/resources.yaml`: `scanners.yml` gains `auth:` with `type: http_bearer` and `token: ${AUTH_TOKEN:}`,
  the block the image's own `src/config/scanners.yml` carries. It is written in block style. The issue suggested the
  one-line `auth: { type: http_bearer, token: ${AUTH_TOKEN:} }`, but in a flow map the `{` of `${` ends the
  map and PyYAML refuses the file (checked with PyYAML here). The API would then load no config at all and fail to start.
  The loader substitutes `${AUTH_TOKEN:}` from the env and gives an empty string when it is unset, and no bearer header
  matches an empty token, so an unset token refuses every call instead of opening the API.
- `checksum/scanners-yml` moves from `220cfa370663` to `61a7adb9a48a`, so Argo CD's sync restarts the API, which reads
  the file once at start. `verify/test_input_pii_guard.py` holds the value.
- `verify/test_llm_guard_auth.py` (offline, new): the block is there and equals the image's own. Loaded with the
  vendored loader's two env-var regexes, read out of `src/app/config.py`, its token is `AUTH_TOKEN`'s value, and empty
  when that is unset. The one-line form does not parse. The vendored `_check_auth_function` is still a no-op without the
  block and still answers 401 to a wrong token, and the four `/analyze` and `/scan` routes depend on it. llm-guard's
  `AUTH_TOKEN` and the `LLM_GUARD_TOKEN` of guard-proxy, workshop-mcp and the attendee guard-proxy
  (`agent/gateway/guard-proxy/guard-proxy.yaml`) all read `llm-guard-auth`'s `token`, and kustomize generates it non-empty.
  guard-proxy calls LLM Guard only through `_post_guard`, which sends the bearer. The MCP server's one call does too, and
  `stage_traces.py` goes only through guard-proxy's `_post_guard` in the pod. `test_topic_guard_proxy.py` and
  `test_fake_ticket.py` already check the header each caller sends against a fake LLM Guard, so this test does not repeat it.
- No tools-tier test runs the vendored API itself: it needs FastAPI, slowapi, structlog and OpenTelemetry on top of
  llm-guard, and the live probe below runs the real image with this exact file.

**Callers checked first.** Every caller sends the token from the same Secret: guard-proxy (`proxy.py` `_post_guard`,
`Authorization: Bearer {LLM_GUARD_TOKEN}`; the Go guard in the guard-proxy submodule sets it the same way),
`workshop-mcp-server.py` (`_ticket_flagged`), and `verify/stage_traces.py`, which runs guard-proxy's `_post_guard` in the
guard-proxy pod. The kubelet's `/healthz` probes take no auth in the API, so readiness is unchanged. Nothing else in the
repo calls LLM Guard's API: the web pages and the terminal banner only name `llm-guard:8000`.

**Live check, watch-it-burn-private, 2026-11-06 03:56 to 03:58 UTC.** Before: the live `llm-guard-scanners` hashed to

## 2026-11-05 · #882 · run 17542 · The tutor moves to Sonnet 4.6, and preflight fails any bound model without a Bedrock agreement

**What was found.** Run 17336 (#562) saw Bedrock refuse the tutor's calls on both clusters with "not authorized to
perform the required AWS Marketplace actions" after IAM had allowed them: `anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`, the
`tutor_model` default, has no Marketplace agreement in accen-dev. This run read
`aws bedrock get-foundation-model-availability` for every model the cluster root binds, as accen-dev in us-west-2:

    amazon.nova-pro-v1:0                       AVAILABLE      (tier nova, the workshop default)
    anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0   AVAILABLE      (tier haiku)
    anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6                AVAILABLE      (tier sonnet)
    anthropic.claude-opus-4-8                  NOT_AVAILABLE  (tier opus)
    anthropic.claude-sonnet-5                  NOT_AVAILABLE  (the tutor)

All five read `authorizationStatus` AUTHORIZED and `entitlementAvailability` AVAILABLE; only the agreement is missing.
The opus tier is new: the bedrock-opus ModelConfig would be refused the same way if the Agent were swapped to it.

**Which of the issue's two ways.** The issue offers accepting the Sonnet 5 agreement in each fleet account, or moving
`var.tutor_model` to a model the accounts already have one for. Accepting is a Marketplace subscription on Michael's
account, which a run does not make. Moving is a one-line default this run can make, nothing calls the tutor today
(#89), and the tutor's grant already allows `anthropic.claude-sonnet-*`, so "Sonnet only" still holds. So the
default is now `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, the sonnet tier's model, whose agreement reads AVAILABLE. Whether a
tutor returns at all stays open; when it does, it works in accen-dev as the tree stands. Going back to Sonnet 5 is
the one-line default plus the agreement in every account, and the comment above the variable says so. The two
running clusters keep their Sonnet 5 `-tutor` profile until their next cluster-root apply replaces it, which costs
nothing and changes nothing live, since nothing calls it.

**The check.** `infra/terraform/fleet/preflight.sh` (the `fleet.sh preflight` gate, run at the Night Before) reads the
`local.bedrock_tiers` values and the `tutor_model` default from `infra/terraform/aws/cluster/main.tf`, drops the geo
prefix, and asks `get-foundation-model-availability` for each, once per account, as that account in `WIB_REGION`.
AVAILABLE passes; NOT_AVAILABLE fails with the offers and `create-foundation-model-agreement` commands for that
account; PENDING fails with "re-run in 15 minutes"; an error, an empty answer or `None` fails as unreadable; a
cluster root it cannot read fails rather than passing on an empty list. It never runs the accept commands. It went
in preflight rather than `verify/model_pin_check.py` because the agreement is per account, preflight already walks
every fleet account, and the pin check is about the one pinned model in the delivery account. The run-of-show's
Night Before preflight bullet says what the new FAIL means and whose act fixes it.

**Tests.** `verify/test_preflight_model_agreements.sh` (offline, aws is a shim) holds: one read per bound model per
account, without the `us.` prefix; a tutor sharing a tier's model is one read naming both; NOT_AVAILABLE, PENDING,
an AccessDenied, an empty answer and a missing or tutor-less cluster root each fail; only the account without the
agreement fails; preflight never calls the offers or accept commands; and against the real cluster root it asks about
exactly `bedrock_tiers` plus the `tutor_model` default, after checking both anchors are there.
`verify/test_preflight_boundary.sh` now copies the cluster root into its temp tree and its shim answers AVAILABLE.

**Live check, accen-dev, run 17542 (read-only).** `WIB_ATTENDEE_ACCOUNTS=accen-dev WIB_REGION=us-west-2 bash
infra/terraform/fleet/preflight.sh 2` printed PASS for identity 515966504359, every quota and the boundary, then:

    PASS  Bedrock agreement for anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 (tier:haiku): AVAILABLE
    FAIL  Bedrock agreement for anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 (tier:opus): NOT_AVAILABLE in accen-dev; ...
    PASS  Bedrock agreement for anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 (tier:sonnet,tutor): AVAILABLE

and a FAIL for "no lab VPC state", since this worktree carries no lab VPC tfstate. Only accen-dev is in the run's

**Left open.** The opus agreement in accen-dev, and the agreements in the four student accounts, are Michael's to

## 2026-11-06 · #902 · run 17812 · check_inventory takes the ingredient it is asked about

**What was wrong.** On watch-it-burn-private on 2026-10-31 and 2026-11-05 every check_inventory call workshop-agent made
logged `tool_input {}` (guard-proxy-agenticburn#29). The cause is the tool's schema, not the model. `check_inventory()`
in `gitops/ai-layer/workshop-mcp-server.py` took no argument, so the schema FastMCP builds from its signature declared
no property. Read live from the running workshop-mcp pod on watch-it-burn-private (tools/list over `127.0.0.1:8000/mcp`):
`"inputSchema": {"properties": {}, "title": "check_inventoryArguments", "type": "object"}`. The model had nothing to
fill, and every call answered the same 278-character `json.dumps(_INVENTORY, indent=2)`.

**Decided: it takes an ingredient.** It is the one business tool a chat asks about one thing at a time ("how many ghost
peppers"), and `reorder_supply` already takes its `item`. `check_inventory(ingredient: str = "")`:
- an ingredient in any spelling (`ghost_pepper`, `Ghost Peppers`, `Toe-Fu`) answers that one level as JSON,
  `{"ghost_pepper": 12}`; a part of a name (`queso`) or a name with more words (`Bogbacoa burrito`) answers every
  stocked ingredient it matches, and a sentence naming two (`ghost pepper and witch hazel`) answers both;
- one the cantina does not stock answers that it is not in the inventory and lists what is, so the model can ask again;
- no ingredient, or a blank one, answers the whole inventory as before, so a call with `{}` still works and the
  tool-audit tests that call it so are unchanged;
- the levels are read from `inventory.json` on disk, which run_shell sees, and the seed when it is unreadable.

The description now tells the model to give the ingredient. The argument is optional. A required one
would turn every `{}` call into a validation error, and "what is in stock" is a fair question too.

**Tests.** `verify/test_check_inventory_ingredient.py` (offline, 22 checks) holds the signature, the description and
each answer above. `verify/test_check_inventory_schema_e2e.py` (tools tier) imports the server with mcp==1.29.1, as
images/workshop-mcp pins it, beside the real `tool_audit.py`: tools/list's inputSchema has an `ingredient` string
property and requires nothing, a call with `{"ingredient": "ghost pepper"}` answers `{"ghost_pepper": 12}` and its
audit line's `tool_input` carries the ingredient, and a call with `{}` answers the whole inventory.

**Live check, run 17812 (watch-it-burn-private, the cluster left as found).** In pod `workshop-mcp-75bcdb57f8-l6ntd`, the
changed server.py, copied to `/tmp/probe-902` and imported in a one-off python3 with the image's own mcp (`mcp 1.29.1`)
and `WORKSHOP_DATA_DIR=/tmp/probe-902/data`, printed `SCHEMA {"properties": {"ingredient": {"default": "", "title":
"Ingredient", "type": "string"}}, ...}`, `ONE {"ghost_pepper": 12}` for `{"ingredient": "Ghost Peppers"}` with
`"tool_input":{"ingredient":"Ghost Peppers"}` in its audit line, and `EVERY_LEN 278` for `{}`. `/tmp/probe-902` was
removed and `/tmp` held only `burrito-data` after. Nothing bound a port and the running server was not touched.

Then the model half of the issue's question, asked of Bedrock directly: Converse on workshop-agent's own model,
ModelConfig `bedrock-nova`, application inference profile
`arn:aws:bedrock:us-west-2:515966504359:application-inference-profile/88hce5o0zw45` (Nova Pro), temperature 0, with
only check_inventory as its tool, two prompts, each twice per schema:

| schema | "How many ghost peppers do we have in stock?" | "Check the inventory for kelpie queso, then for witch hazel." |
|---|---|---|
| old (no property) | `[{}]`, `[{}]` | `[{}, {}]`, `[{}, {}]` |
| new | `[{"ingredient": "ghost pepper"}]` twice | `[{"ingredient": "kelpie queso"}, {"ingredient": "witch hazel"}]` twice |

So Nova Pro fills the argument when the schema declares one; the `{}` was the schema.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The change running in workshop-mcp. The Deployment carries no checksum annotation for
`workshop-mcp-src` (guard-proxy's `checksum/proxy-py` is the pattern), so an Argo sync updates the mounted file but the
running python keeps the old schema until the pod restarts: after promotion, `kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private -n
agent rollout restart deployment/workshop-mcp` (and the same on watch-it-burn-community), then
`kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private -n agent rollout restart deployment/workshop-agent` so the agent lists the tools
afresh. The check is a chat naming an ingredient and its `tool_input` in workshop-mcp's log
(`kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private -n agent logs deploy/workshop-mcp | grep check_inventory`), which should carry
`"ingredient"`. Owed to the next run on #902. The missing rollout trigger is filed as a follow-up.

No dependency was added to the repo; the Bedrock probe ran boto3 1.40.70 in a throwaway `uv run --with`.

**The suites (run 17812, at `778f2a8b`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` printed `285 tests ran` and
`ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN` for the offline suite, then `66 checks ran (the offline suite and 65 tier tests)
in 41m25s`, `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN` and `exit=0`.

hand it over by the rules above. Your kitchen folder is "burrito-data" (/tmp/burrito-data in your shell), and

3. Every other time, the conversation has not included that question of what you can see, and a recipe ask
   is an ordinary kitchen chore. When the guest's own message names the burrito-data folder or the recipe
   file (its path, /tmp/burrito-data, or a command that searches it counts) and gives a kitchen reason (a

## 2026-11-06 · #932 · run 17820 · The mrf-secrets login request is kept in the repo and held to what fleet.sh reads

**What changed.** #910's criterion is an agent-task issue on mrf-secrets that asks for the new private terminal login
to be generated and stored, names the key this repo reads, and carries no login value. No run can read or file on
mrf-secrets (`gh` refuses it as a data vault, and hecaton's governance keeps every run out of it), so no test here could
read the filed issue, and #910's run put the request in its report for hecaton to file. The request's text is now
committed at `docs/requests/mrf-secrets-terminal-login.md`: a header naming the repo, the `agent-task` label and #910,
then the issue body. `verify/terminal_login_request.py` checks a request and reads what it checks against from
fleet.sh, never from a copy: the file `WIB_TERMINAL_ENV` defaults to under `~/secrets/`, the keys `presenter_login`
hands to `_terminal_env_value`, and that parser's own bash source. A request fails unless it is labelled
`agent-task`, asks for a new login to be generated and stored, says it is the terminal's, and names the file and
both keys. It also fails when it carries a value, which is read three ways: fleet.sh's parser, run on the body as
if it were the env file, reads nothing for either key; no line gives either key or `TTYD_CREDENTIAL` a value as
`KEY=v`, `export KEY="v"`, `KEY: v` or a JSON pair; and no token hashes to the old login, whose digests are read
from `verify/test_no_presenter_login.py`.

**The test.** `verify/test_terminal_login_request.py` (offline, 32 checks) runs the check on the committed request
and then proves each part fails: the file or a key dropped, the asks to generate or store taken out, the label
missing, a value planted in each of six forms, the old login planted (against a test-owned digest), and a fleet.sh
copy with a key or the file renamed, which fails the committed request until it follows. Each case that edits the
request or fleet.sh on a literal checks the literal is there first and names it when it is not.

**The live mode.** `python3 verify/terminal_login_request.py --gh`, or `--issues <file>` on the output of
`gh issue list -R peopleforrester/mrf-secrets --label agent-task --state all --search "WIB_TERMINAL_USER in:body"
--json number,title,body,labels,url`, checks the filed issue with the same function and exits 0 naming the first issue
that meets the criterion, 1 otherwise, never printing a body. The test runs it on test-owned issue lists and on a gh
stub that refuses the vault. It is in neither suite: no host a run or the gate reaches can read mrf-secrets, so in the
tools tier it would hold every run red. Run here, `--gh` printed `FAIL  cannot read peopleforrester/mrf-secrets's
issues: gh issue list -R peopleforrester/mrf-secrets exit 2: REFUSED peopleforrester/mrf-secrets is a data vault`, exit 1.

**Live check, clusters.** None: this change touches no cluster, and the clusters' terminal login is #912's check.

**Not yet run.** `python3 verify/terminal_login_request.py --gh` from a gh that can read mrf-secrets (Michael's),
which says whether the request #910's run handed to hecaton was filed and still meets the criterion.

**The suites (run 17820, at `433dc499`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` printed `288 tests ran` and
`ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN` for the offline suite (`bash verify/run-tests.sh`), then `65 checks ran (the
offline suite and 64 tier tests) in 52m56s`, `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN` and `exit=0`. The new test is one of
the 288.
## 2026-11-06 · #903 · The workshop-agent's log exporter names /v1/logs, and the collector states its logs pipeline

**What the 404 was.** `verify/prior-drafts.sh 903 origin/staging` printed NONE. The issue reads the 404 as a missing
logs pipeline and offers two fixes: add one, or set `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none`. Neither stops it, and the first is
already in place. The live collector on watch-it-burn-private has a `logs` pipeline (otlp, then memory_limiter and
batch, to debug) from the chart's default config, which values.yaml merges into. Through a port-forward to its
Service, a POST of `{}` to `/v1/logs` answered 200, to `/v1/traces` 200, and to `/` 404. The pod's line names the URL
it sent to, `http://otel-collector-opentelemetry-collector.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:4318`, with no path. The
agent runs `ghcr.io/kagent-dev/kagent/golang-adk:0.10.1`. Its `go/adk/pkg/telemetry/tracing.go` at v0.10.1 builds the
log exporter with `otlploghttp.WithEndpointURL(endpoint)`, where the endpoint is `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT`,
then `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, then the base `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` the Operator injects. otlploghttp
v0.20.0 keeps that URL's path as given, an empty one included, so every batch went to `/`. The trace exporter
(otlptracehttp v1.44.0) puts `/v1/traces` in when the path is empty, which is why traces arrived and logs did not.
Nothing in kagent or ADK reads `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, so `none` would change nothing. Turning kagent's
`otel.logging.enabled` off does not stop the export either: adk-go v2.1.0's `telemetry/setup_otel.go` then builds its
own log exporter from the base endpoint, which posts to `/v1/logs` correctly, so with the pipeline in place it would
be quiet, but it would rest on ADK's fallback and drop kagent's own exporter.

**The change.** The Agent (`gitops/workshop-agent/agent.yaml`) sets `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT` to the
Instrumentation CR's endpoint plus `/v1/logs`, which kagent reads first. `gitops/otel-collector/values.yaml` states the
logs pipeline the chart had been supplying, the same receivers, processors and exporter, so a chart bump cannot drop
the path the agent now depends on and the offline render sees it. The records stay at debug on every profile, with
or without Datadog: they are ADK's gen_ai events (`gen_ai.choice`, `gen_ai.user.message`, `gen_ai.system.message`),
which carry the prompt and the reply, and the traces pipeline's redaction and burn's `transform/scrub_pii` never see
a logs pipeline. The Datadog Agent already ships the pod's own log lines. Sending the events to Datadog would be a
choice of its own, with its own scrub.

**Tests.** `verify/test_agent_otlp_logs.py` (offline) holds the env: it is set, its path is `/v1/logs`, it is the
Instrumentation CR's host and port, and the protocol is http/protobuf. It also holds that every profile, with and
without datadog-secret, has a logs pipeline on the otlp receiver at that port, exporting to debug alone. Without the
change it fails on the env and on the pipeline. `verify/test_agent_otlp_logs_collector.py` (tools tier) resolves the
URL the way kagent does and sends a `gen_ai.choice` record through each profile's shipped logs pipeline on the pinned
otelcol-contrib 0.160.0. It was accepted (200) and came out the other end on all six. The same record sent to `/`
answered 404, the pod's line.

**Live check, run 17813 (reads and a port-forward; nothing changed).** On watch-it-burn-private the workshop-agent
pod (`workshop-agent-8bd97f75c-rdc4s`, 45 minutes old) had 139 `failed to send logs ... 404 Not Found` lines among 286,
in bursts while it ran tools. Its env has `OTEL_LOGGING_ENABLED=true`, `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp` and the base
endpoint without a path, and no logs endpoint. On watch-it-burn-community the pod had the same env and no such line
in 20, as it had done little. The collector probe is in the first paragraph.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** After this change syncs, on watch-it-burn-private:
`kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private -n agent get pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=workshop-agent -o yaml` should
show `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT` ending in `/v1/logs`, and after a few chats through the storefront,
`kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private -n agent logs deploy/workshop-agent --since=10m | grep -c 'failed to send logs'`
should print 0 while the `Tool execution` lines still appear. kagent rolls the pod when the Agent's env changes; if it
does not, the Agent CR bounce in docs/DECISION-LOG.md applies. Owed to the next run on #903.

**The suites (run 17813, at `64f174b1`).** The first `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` printed `285 tests ran` and
`ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`, then `66 checks ran (the offline suite and 65 tier tests) in 43m46s`, with one
red: `test_public_images_served.py` printed `public.ecr.aws gave no anonymous token: URLError: <urlopen error
_ssl.c:1012: The handshake operation timed out>`. Run alone right after, it exited 0. The second full run printed
`285 tests ran`, `ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`, `66 checks ran (the offline suite and 65 tier tests) in

## 2026-11-05 · #873 · run 17449 · Attendee seats admit lab-platform-operator in the group lab-platform:learner-apps

**What changed.** `infra/terraform/aws/cluster/main.tf` gives every attendee seat (`role=attendee`) an EKS access
entry for `arn:aws:iam::<the seat's account>:role/lab-platform-operator`, type STANDARD, Kubernetes group
`lab-platform:learner-apps`, with no access policy associated. lab-platform's `labctl harvest` probes each seat's
workshop apps as that role in every account but the harvest's own (lab-platform#370), and until now each seat
admitted only its creator and its student, so one harvest across the five accounts got a 401 from every seat
outside its base account. The new output `lab_platform_operator_entry` names the admitted ARN, or is empty.

**Why the entry is conditional.** lab-platform makes the role in every account except the base credentials' own
(lab-platform `docs/aws-accounts.md`, "Creating the role"), and EKS refuses an entry whose principal does not exist
(checked live below). So the root looks the role up by name (`data.aws_iam_roles` with `^lab-platform-operator$`)
and makes the entry only where it is found. A seat built before the role reached its account gets the entry at its
next apply. The community and admin clusters get none: the harvest pools only seats, and lab-platform refuses those
two clusters at its own entries.

**A role made again.** EKS binds an entry to the principal's unique id, and lab-platform removes the role from an
account once its event is over. A role made again under the same name has a new id, and the old entry no longer
admits it while its ARN, which is all Terraform compares, is unchanged. A `terraform_data` holding the role's
`unique_id` is in the entry's `replace_triggered_by`, so the next apply replaces the entry.

**What the entry grants.** Only what the group's RBAC grants. #874 (now in staging, `gitops/learner-apps-access`,
synced on the attendee profile) binds `lab-platform:learner-apps` to get on the eight workshop apps' Service
proxies, as an attendee's check does, and nothing else. On a seat without that Application the entry authenticates
and is granted nothing.

**Test.** `verify/test_lab_platform_operator_entry.py` (E2E tools tier) copies the root into an empty directory,
initialises it against the committed lock, and runs `terraform test` with the cases in
`verify/fixtures/lab_platform_operator_entry.tftest.hcl` against a mocked aws provider, so no AWS call is made: a
seat in an account with the role gets one entry with the right ARN, the one group and type, the root's only access
policy association stays the student's, and the entry follows the role's unique id; a seat in an account without the
role, the community cluster and the admin cluster get none. With the `role=attendee` condition removed from the
root, the community and admin cases fail.

**Live check (watch-it-burn-private, account 515966504359, us-west-2, 12:45Z).** With the run's session sourced:

- `aws eks create-access-entry --cluster-name watch-it-burn-private --principal-arn
  arn:aws:iam::515966504359:role/lab-platform-operator --kubernetes-groups lab-platform:learner-apps --type STANDARD`
  made the entry: `kubernetesGroups` `["lab-platform:learner-apps"]`, username
  `arn:aws:sts::515966504359:assumed-role/lab-platform-operator/{{SessionName}}`. So the role exists in accen-dev,
  and the entry's shape is one EKS takes.
- `aws eks list-associated-access-policies` on it returned `"associatedAccessPolicies": []`.
- The same call for `role/wib-873-no-such-role-x7` was refused: `InvalidParameterException ... The specified
  principalArn is invalid: invalid principal.` That is why the root looks the role up first.
- `aws eks delete-access-entry` removed the entry, and `list-access-entries` afterwards listed the five entries the
  cluster held before (the EKS service role, the node group role, `hecaton-run`, `nwuser` and `wib-private`). Left as
  found.

The run's session cannot call IAM (its `get-role` answers `InvalidClientTokenId`), and it reaches accen-dev only, so
whether the other four accounts hold the role was not read here; the lookup makes an account without it plan no entry.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** No attendee seat is up, and a run brings none up. The next seat build (`fleet.sh up`)
plans the entry; then `aws eks describe-access-entry --cluster-name <seat> --principal-arn
arn:aws:iam::<account>:role/lab-platform-operator` and one `labctl harvest` across the accounts, after #874, show a
seat outside the base account answering the probe.

No dependency was added.

**The suites (run 17449, on c98a0831).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran 58 checks (the offline suite and 57 tier
tests) in 32m31s and exits 0 with `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN`. The offline suite inside it ran 263 tests,
`ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`, and `verify/test_lab_platform_operator_entry.py` printed
`ALL LAB-PLATFORM-OPERATOR ENTRY CHECKS GREEN` with its four cases passed.

## 2026-11-06 · #933 · run 17822 · A test runs the wall's own page on a fake clock and holds it to one card per 1.5 s

**What was missing.** #927's criterion for the prompt wall, that prompts arriving faster than one per 1.5 s add at
most one card per 1.5 s window, was tested only on this repo's `/display` page. The wall's change landed in
peopleforrester/prompts-agenticburn as #18, commit `6601313a`, the tip of that repo's `main` and `staging` on
2026-11-06, with its own MiniRacer test. No test here read `templates/wall.html`. `bash verify/prior-drafts.sh 933
origin/staging` printed NONE and the issue had no comments, so there was no draft to port.

**Decided: a pinned copy for the gate, and a live half that reads the wall repo's main.** prompts-agenticburn is
private, and the gate runs `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` with no GitHub login, so the gate cannot fetch the page.
`verify/fixtures/prompts-agenticburn/wall.html.fixture` is a byte copy of `templates/wall.html` at `6601313a`, held
to its SHA-256 (`52323b00...`). The suffix is `.fixture`, not `.html`, because the ai-isms gate reads every changed
`.html` file as this repo's prose, and the page names the repo with its hype verb. The copy only proves the rule on
the bytes it holds, so `verify/test_wall_throttle_upstream_e2e.py` (live suite, run by hand with `run-e2e.sh`)
reads `templates/wall.html` on the wall repo's `main` through `gh api`, runs the same checks on it, and fails when
`main` has moved past the copy, naming the commit and SHA-256 to refresh it to. That turns red once
prompts-agenticburn#22 (pause and pin) lands there, which is the point: the copy gets refreshed and rechecked.

**The test.** `verify/wall-clock-harness.js` runs the page's last `<script>` in a node vm with its two Jinja
expressions filled in (`{{ pinned | tojson }}`, `{{ interval }}`; any other one fails it), a stub DOM, a stub
`/api/prompts` fetch, a stub `EventSource` the test pushes SSE frames into, and `setTimeout`, `setInterval` and
`performance.now()` on a fake clock. It records the time of every card the page prepends to `#stream`.
`verify/wall_throttle.py` holds the four floods: 17 prompts a second for 60 s as one SSE frame of 17 a second
(the wall's `events()` sends one frame a second) and as one prompt every 59 ms, one prompt every 1.4 s for 30 s,
and a burst of 200, then 200 more 10 ms after the card the first brought. On each, no two cards after the first
snapshot are less than 1500 ms apart, each fixed 1.5 s window holds at most one, every card is a prompt that
arrived and is drawn once, the snapshot's prompt goes up at once, and the flood keeps drawing (30, 30, 10 and 2
cards at least), so a page that drew nothing does not pass. `verify/test_wall_throttle_e2e.py` (tools tier, needs
node) runs them on the copy, checks its `CARD_INTERVAL_MS` is 1500, and applies three mutations, each on a literal

## 2026-11-06 · #934 · run 17824 · The wall's newest-card test is prompts-agenticburn's, and it fails when the card is not the newest or the rest are queued

**What #934 asks.** Test review run 17682 found no test for #927's criterion that the card added at each tick is
the newest prompt since the previous card, and that the older ones are dropped and never drawn at a later tick, on
prompts-agenticburn's `templates/wall.html`. Only this repo's `/display` had one
(`verify/test_display_throttle_e2e.py`). The review ran before prompts-agenticburn#18 landed. That repo's main and
staging now both stand at `6601313a` ("Draw one card per 1.5 s on the wall, the newest, with a "+N more" count"),
which adds the throttle and its tests to `test_wall_page.py`.

**Why the test is there and not here.** #927 moved the wall's half to prompts-agenticburn#18, and that repo's own gate
(`uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest`) runs on every change to `wall.html`, so a change that breaks the criterion
fails before it lands. A test in this repo would have to fetch another repo's page over the network and would only
fail after the change had merged there. This run adds no test here. `verify/prior-drafts.sh 934 origin/staging`
printed NONE and the issue had no comments.

**What the tests check.** Three tests in `test_wall_page.py` at `6601313a` hold the criterion:
- `test_throttle_shows_only_the_newest_of_each_window_and_counts_the_rest` drives `makeThrottle` on a fake clock. Of
  a burst of 10 it shows 10, then four more windows add no card and leave no timer pending. Over a 60-prompt flood it
  asserts, from an ordered log of offers and shows, that every card is the last prompt offered before it.
- `test_a_burst_on_the_stream_adds_one_card_the_newest_with_a_live_count` drives the page through the real `/events`
  route. The cards are "burst 10" of 10 and "second 5" of 5, and four more windows leave the card count at 4.
- `test_a_burst_on_the_polling_fallback_is_sampled_the_same_way` does the same on the polling path: "polled 7" of 7,
  and three more windows add nothing.

**Mutation check (run 17824).** On a copy of prompts-agenticburn at `6601313a` (a `gh api` tarball, outside this
clone), `uv run ruff check .` printed `All checks passed!` and `uv run pytest` printed `90 passed`. Two edits to
`makeThrottle` in `templates/wall.html`, each run against the unchanged tests:
- *Oldest, not newest:* `held = e` became `if (held === null) held = e`. `3 failed, 87 passed`, the three tests above.
- *Queued, not dropped:* each offer pushed onto a queue and each tick showed `queue.shift()` and re-armed while the
  queue held more. `3 failed, 87 passed`, the same three.

So the criterion has a test that fails when it stops holding, in the repo that owns the page.

**Live.** No cluster is involved: the wall runs on Railway, and this run touched neither cluster.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing from this issue.

## 2026-11-06 · #936 · run 17833 · A test here holds prompts-agenticburn's fake-clock burst test to #927's criterion

**What was missing.** Test review run 17682 found no test for #927's criterion "An offline test in prompts-agenticburn
with a controlled clock (no real timers, no network) feeds a burst of prompts and checks the card count, which prompt
was shown, and the counter value after each tick." #927's own fake-clock test, `verify/test_display_throttle_e2e.py`,
drives this repo's `display.js`, not the wall. The wall's throttle has since landed in prompts-agenticburn as
prompts-agenticburn#18 (`6601313a`, the tip of that repo's `main` and `staging`), with the test the criterion names in
its `test_wall_page.py`: the page runs in MiniRacer on a fake browser whose timers, `performance.now()`, fetch and
EventSource are all on one virtual clock, and two tests (`test_a_burst_on_the_stream_adds_one_card_the_newest_with_a_live_count`
and `test_a_burst_on_the_polling_fallback_is_sampled_the_same_way`) feed a burst through `wall.ingest()` and assert the
card count, the shown card's text and `+N more` between ticks. So the criterion holds; what was missing is a check
that fails when it stops holding. `verify/prior-drafts.sh 936 origin/staging` printed NONE, and the issue has no
comments, so there was no draft to port.

**What was added.** A run cannot change prompts-agenticburn, so the test reads it.

- `verify/wall_clock_burst.py` reads `test_wall_page.py` and `conftest.py` with `ast` and makes ten named checks:
  MiniRacer imported; one module constant defining `setTimeout` passed to `.eval()`; its `setTimeout` and
  `setInterval` scheduling on the variable `performance.now()` returns; an `advance(ms)`; a fake `fetch` and
  `EventSource`; the page's script taken from `client.get("/")`, which serves `wall.html`; no network client imported;
  `WALL_POLLER` set to `off` in conftest.py; and at least one `page` test that hands `wall.ingest()` two or more
  prompts, calls `page.advance()` at least twice, has an assert on `page.cards()` or `browser.more()` after every
  advance before the next one, and between those asserts reads `len(page.cards())`, a card's `"text"` and
  `browser.more()`. "After each tick" is read as that: every tick is followed by an assert on the page, and the three
  values are each asserted after a tick. The two tests prompts-agenticburn#18 landed read the count or the counter
  after every tick but not all three after each, so a reading that asked for all three after every tick would fail the
  test the criterion describes.
- `verify/test_wall_clock_burst_sister_e2e.py` (`# SUITE: e2e`) reads prompts-agenticburn's `main` head and tarball
  through `gh api`, runs those checks, runs the repo's `test_wall_page.py` under its own lock
  (`uv run --frozen pytest`) and checks each burst test passed, then sets the page's `CARD_INTERVAL_MS` to 1 ms (the
  anchor `const CARD_INTERVAL_MS = 1500;` is checked first) and checks a burst test fails on an assert.
- `verify/test_wall_clock_burst.py` (offline suite) runs the analyser on a made-up page test written to the criterion,
  which passes every check, and on 17 edits of it, each checked to fail exactly the check it breaks: a real
  `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `performance.now()`, `fetch` or `EventSource`, no `advance`, no MiniRacer, no fake
  evaluated, another route, `urllib.request` imported, one prompt in place of a burst (as a list and as a range), one
  tick, a tick with no assert after it, and no card count, shown text or counter. A conftest with the poller on fails
  only that check. Each edit's anchor is checked to be in the made-up source first.

**Why the live suite, not the tools tier.** prompts-agenticburn is private, so there is no anonymous read, and the
promotion gate's gh refuses `gh api` (verify/gh_comments.py, #863). In the tools tier the check would hold the gate red
for want of access, not for the criterion. `run-e2e.sh` runs it by hand with gh signed in, and a dispatched run, whose
gh allows `gh api`, runs it as `python3 verify/test_wall_clock_burst_sister_e2e.py`. A missing gh or uv, or a failed
read, is a failure with gh's reason, never a skip.

**Run by this run (17833), at prompts-agenticburn `6601313a`.** `python3 verify/test_wall_clock_burst_sister_e2e.py`
printed all 18 checks PASS, both burst tests passed under that repo's lock, the 1 ms page failed

## 2026-11-06 · #940 · run 17838 · The DNS collector build spec, a sibling of the beacon collector spec

**What was missing.** The DNS stage of the Challenge 1 exfil beat (stage 2b in
`docs/research/2026-10-31-c1-dns-exfil-beat.md`) had a tool side already built
(`challenges/c1-exfil-s3/dns-exfil.py`, covered by `verify/test_c1_dns_exfil.py`) but no written spec for its
far end: the authoritative nameserver that owns the delegated zone, the per-query log, and the `GET /dns/view`
room view. #726 carried the collector and the view; planning run 17700 split the spec out as #940.
`bash verify/prior-drafts.sh 940 origin/staging` printed NONE and the issue has no comments, so there was no
earlier draft to port.

**Decided: formalize the research doc into a sibling of the beacon spec.** `docs/dns-collector-spec.md` mirrors
`docs/beacon-collector-spec.md` section for section (What exists today, Routes to add, the room view, Notes, the
one hand-off, Both domains), at the same altitude: it names the channel, the pieces to build and the checks, and
it does not specify how the tool produces the lookups. The nameserver answers every query under the delegated
subdomain of `agenticburn.com` with NOERROR so the lookup succeeds, appends one record per query to the
provisioning app's existing `/data` volume (`ts` in iso8601 UTC, source address, the full query name), and keeps
a running count. `GET /dns/view` sits beside `/beacon/view` on the provisioning app: a count, the last ~50
queries, and the payload reassembled in sequence by the marker and ordinal each query name carries. The deploy
and storage pattern is the beacon's (Flask on the provisioning app, records under `/data`). The zone delegation
is a one-time registrar change on Michael's side, the same shape as the beacon's apex repoint, per
`infra/dns/README.md`. A code implementation is optional and may follow; the owed offline coverage, the hand-off
and the live check are tracked by the sibling children (#724, #727, #728), not by this issue. The prose gate
printed `prose gate: pass`.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing: the change is one documentation file, and no dependency was added. This
run touched neither the community nor the private cluster.
