**What #944 asks.** Run 17705 (#912) found that `infra/terraform/fleet/fleet.sh` wrote the `terminal-auth` Secret
with `--from-literal=TTYD_CREDENTIAL=<login>`, which puts the login in kubectl's argv, readable in the process list
by any user on the host while kubectl runs. `terminal_password_one` then piped the manifest to `kubectl apply`, which
stores a second copy of the login in the `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotation; run 17705
removed that annotation by hand on both KubeCon clusters. `verify/prior-drafts.sh 944 origin/staging` printed NONE
and the issue had no comments, so this is a first draft.

**What changed.**
- A new `terminal_auth_manifest <login> [kubectl args]` prints the Secret through `kubectl create secret generic
  terminal-auth --from-env-file=<(printf 'TTYD_CREDENTIAL=%s\n' ...) --dry-run=client -o yaml`. `printf` is a bash
  builtin, so the login is in no process's argv; kubectl reads it from `/dev/fd/N`.
- `terminal_password_one` pipes that manifest to `kubectl replace -f -`, and when the replace fails (no Secret to
  replace) pipes a fresh copy to `kubectl create -f -`. Both failing is "could not write terminal-auth", as before.
- `bootstrap_terminal_auth` keeps its plain `kubectl create`, which writes no annotation without `--save-config`, and
  takes the login by `--from-env-file` of a process substitution in place of `--from-literal`.

**Why replace and not `apply --server-side`.** The issue offered either. A server-side apply writes no annotation on
a Secret that has none, but on one that already carries it the API server keeps the copy up to date with the new
login (checked live below). A replace writes the whole object, so it also drops an annotation an earlier apply left.
Nothing else labels or annotates `terminal-auth` (the only other reference in `gitops/` is the web terminal's
optional `secretRef`), so a replace loses nothing. Values pass through kubectl's env-file parser unchanged for the
logins `presenter_login` admits (no whitespace; colons and quotes are kept, checked offline with `u1:p:a$s"x`).

**Tests.** `verify/test_admin_actions.sh` and `verify/test_fleet_terminal_harvest.sh` read the old
`--from-literal=TTYD_CREDENTIAL=` call lines and change with it. Their kubectl shims now log the contents of a
`--from-env-file` argument on its own `env-file` line, and the checks hold that the login is on that line and on no
`kubectl` argv line. The admin test adds that the Secret is replaced and never applied, that with no Secret to
replace it is created, and that both failing fails by name without restarting the terminal. The harvest test adds
that the bootstrap never applies and never passes `--save-config`. Results: admin 62 passed, harvest 90 passed,
`test_fleet_converge_repairs.sh` 73 passed, each 0 failed.

**Live (run 17840, watch-it-burn-community, a scratch Secret `wib-944-scratch` in `default`, deleted after; the
cluster is as found).** Read-only first: `terminal-auth` in `agent` on both clusters carries no annotations. Then:
1. The old path (`create --dry-run=client -o yaml | apply -f -`): `last-applied present: True`.
2. `terminal_auth_manifest`'s output, sourced from this fleet.sh and renamed to the scratch Secret, through
   `replace -f -`: `secret/wib-944-scratch replaced`, `last-applied present: False | value: scratch:two`.
3. With the Secret deleted, replace printed `secrets "wib-944-scratch" not found` (rc 1), the create fallback
   `secret/wib-944-scratch created` (rc 0), `last-applied present: False | value: scratch:three`.
4. Apply, then `apply --server-side --force-conflicts` with a new value: `after SSA, last-applied present: True | it
   holds the new value: True`. This is why the change uses replace.
The scratch Secret was deleted and a final `get` printed NotFound.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** `fleet.sh terminal-password <name>` itself, which writes the real `terminal-auth` and
restarts the terminal, was not run: it would rewrite a live login. The next `terminal-password` on a KubeCon cluster
runs it; afterwards `kubectl -n agent get secret terminal-auth -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations}'` should print
nothing.

**Left as it was.** fleet.sh's `datadog-secret` writes (`--from-literal=api-key=...`) put the Datadog keys in argv the
same way. They are outside #944, which is about the terminal login, and are named as a followup in the run's report.

OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`) and then the tier: `69 checks ran (the offline suite and 68 tier tests) in 32m57s`,
`ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN`, exit 0. No dependency was added. The prose gate printed `prose gate: pass`.

## 2026-11-06 · #935 · run 17826 · A live test of the wall's "+N more" count, which the deployed wall does not have yet
## 2026-11-06 · #935 · runs 17826 and 17844 · The wall's "+N more" count, checked on the pinned copy and on the live wall, which lacks it

**The spec.** #935 (filed by test review run 17682) asks for a test that fails when #927's third criterion stops
holding: a visible "+N more" counter on the prompt wall equals the prompts that arrived and were not shown since the
last card, and resets to 0 when a card appears. The review found that only `/display`'s `display.js` was checked
(`verify/test_display_throttle_e2e.py`), never the wall. `verify/prior-drafts.sh 935 origin/staging` printed NONE.

**Where the wall lives.** The wall is `templates/wall.html` in peopleforrester/prompts-agenticburn, which a run here
may not change. Its throttle and count landed there as commit `6601313` (prompts-agenticburn#18, run 17757), with
tests in its `test_wall_page.py` that run the template. What nothing here checked is that page, and the wall the room
reads at prompts.agenticburn.com.

**Why run 17826 did not land, and what changed.** Run 17826 wrote the live test and a runner named
`verify/wall-clock-harness.js`, and its rebase failed: while it ran, #933 (run 17821, `e8dd97e8`) put a different
runner at that path for the card-rate criterion, with a byte copy of the wall at `6601313`,
`verify/fixtures/prompts-agenticburn/wall.html.fixture`. This run kept #933's runner as it is and moved this one to
`verify/wall-more-harness.js`. They model different things: #933's answers every fetch with one fixed snapshot and
reads no markup, and this check needs the polling fallback to fetch what arrived after its cursor, a replay of prompts
the page holds, the #more element as the markup ships it, and an ordered log of every answer the page was handed and
every card it put up. Folding one into the other would change #933's runner under its own tests. #933's pinned copy
also made a gate half possible, which run 17826 did not have, so the checks moved into a shared module and a tools-tier
test was added, following #933's layout.

**The tests.** `verify/wall_more_count.py` holds the checks. It runs a page's inline script through
`verify/wall-more-harness.js` (a fake clock, a stub DOM built from the page's own markup, and a fake `/api/prompts` and
`/events` that model app.py's `snapshot()` and stream cursor). The scenario is a burst of 10, one prompt every 100 ms
for 6 s from two clusters, a dropped stream whose 7 prompts the polling fallback picks up, 3 more on the reopened
stream, and a replay of 8 the page already holds. After every step (459 frames) the #more line must equal the count
read off the log `wall-more-harness.js` prints: prompts with a new seq delivered since the last card the page put up.
It also checks the element is in the header, ships without the hidden attribute, and that no inline style, CSS rule
for its classes or script hides it; that the burst reads `+10 more`; that each card resets it to `+0 more` (at least 6
cards); and that the replay adds no card and no count.
- `verify/test_wall_more_count_e2e.py` (tools tier, so the gate runs it) runs the checks on #933's pinned copy, held to
  the SHA-256 `test_wall_throttle_e2e.py` pins, and eight mutations of it must each fail: the card not calling
  `setCount(0)`, `setCount(count - 1)`, the tick not zeroing `count`, the #more div shipped `hidden`,
  `.more.zero{display:none}`, the script hiding #more at 0, the replay guard removed, and offer() not updating the
  count. All passed on the copy and all eight mutations failed.
- `verify/test_wall_more_count_live.py` (live suite, `run-e2e.sh`) downloads the served page (`WALL_URL`, default
  `https://prompts.agenticburn.com/`) and runs the same checks; `--page <wall.html>` runs them on a local copy or a
  template from a prompts-agenticburn checkout. `verify/run-e2e.sh`'s header names it.

the workspace over, merged as `2cb0484d`, which fits the workspace having been retired with that run rather than on 2026-11-19. A search of
every path this host allows a run to read found no `accen-dev*.tfstate`. tanjiro-wsl2's checkout has an
`audit/states/accen-dev.tfstate` that manages nothing (serial 28, `resources: []`), which is escalation 822's partial

sources do not count), so it never imports over a live state. `verify/test_audit_import_state.py` runs it on fake
terraform and aws ahead of the no-cloud stubs, holds its import list to main.tf's resources one for one, and checks

command. Destroying the root after the event was the other option #955 named. It is not taken: a rebuilt state can
do the destroy later, and the record is wanted for the KubeCon session.

## 2026-11-06 · #956 · run 17845 · A fresh lab VPC, boundary or cluster state reads as drifted, so each is settled after its apply

**Question.** Run 17588 on #795 found that a freshly applied audit root reads as drifted in the next
`drift-report.py`, and added a refresh-only apply after the audit apply. #956 asked whether the other roots the
report plans (the lab VPC in `aws/network`, the boundary in `infra/org/boundary` and the cluster root `fleet.sh`
applies) show the same, and to settle them the same way if they do.

**How it was checked.** The issue assumed this needed the operator machine's states. It did not: a fresh state
can be made. Copies of the network and boundary roots, with only their AWS names changed (`watch-it-burn-drift956-*`)
so they could not collide with the fleet's own VPC or boundary, were applied in accen-dev into scratch states, event
tag `drift-check-956`. The VPC went to us-east-2 with `-var create_budget=false`, as the standby-region states are
applied. Each was planned with the report's own command (`terraform plan -refresh-only -lock=false` and `show -json`,
reading `resource_drift`), settled with `apply -refresh-only -auto-approve` and the same arguments, planned again,
given a tag by hand, planned again, untagged, and destroyed.

**What it printed.**
- Boundary: the fresh state's plan had one resource in `resource_drift`, `aws_iam_policy.permissions_boundary`
  (update), `tags: null -> {}`. After the settle (`Apply complete! Resources: 0 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed.`) the
  plan said `No changes. Your infrastructure still matches the configuration.` and `resource_drift` was empty. With a
  tag `oob=drill` set on the policy by hand, the plan listed the policy again (`tags: {} -> {"oob": "drill"}`), so
  the settle does not hide a real change; with it removed, the plan was clean.
- Lab VPC: `Apply complete! Resources: 21 added`, then five resources in `resource_drift`, all updates:
  `module.vpc.aws_route_table.private[0]` and `.public[0]` (`route: [] -> [0.0.0.0/0 ...]`, added by their own
  `aws_route` resources), `module.vpc.aws_eip.nat[0]` (`association_id`, `network_interface`, `private_ip` and
  `private_dns` filled in once the NAT gateway took the address), `module.vpc.aws_default_network_acl.this[0]`
  (subnet ids and rules) and `module.vpc.aws_default_route_table.default[0]` (`propagating_vgws: null -> []`). After
  the settle the plan said `No changes.` and `resource_drift` was empty. A tag set by hand on the VPC showed as
  `module.vpc.aws_vpc.this[0]` drift. `Destroy complete! Resources: 21 destroyed.`, and afterwards us-east-2 held only
  `vpc-029be867c4c5e4151` (the fleet's lab VPC), no address tagged `drift-check-956`, and no policy named
  `*drift956*`. AWS was left as found.
- Cluster root: not built. A dispatched run creates no cluster (CLAUDE.md, Dispatched runs, point 1). It holds the
  same shapes as the two that drift: `aws_iam_policy.bedrock_invoke` and `aws_iam_policy.tutor_bedrock_invoke` carry
  no resource `tags`, like the boundary's policy, and the EKS and pod-identity modules make IAM roles whose policies
  sibling resources attach, like the audit root's role in #795. So it is settled too. The step costs one refresh per
  cluster and changes nothing in AWS.

**What changed.**
- `fleet.sh` `up_one`: after a cluster apply that succeeds, `terraform apply -refresh-only -auto-approve` with the same
  `-state`, `event` and variables, appended to the cluster's apply log. If it fails, the cluster is reported
  `FAILED: <name> (built, but its state did not settle ...)`, the bootstrap still runs (the cluster exists) and the
  run exits non-zero. `WIB_FORCE_UP=1` re-applies and settles. Re-running `up` without it would skip a healthy
  cluster and never settle it.
- Every documented apply of the lab VPC and boundary roots is followed by its refresh-only twin: `infra/terraform/README.md`,
  `infra/org/README.md`, the boundary root's header, `docs/MASTER-RECREATION-SPEC.md` (and its line on what `up_one`
  runs), `docs/BUILD-SPEC.md`, `infra/attendee-cluster/README.md`, `infra/shared-vpc/README.md`, the run-of-show's
  two standby-region VPC applies and its boundary line, and the apply lines `preflight.sh`, `fleet.sh` (`read_vpc_for`)
  and `backups.py` (`up` with no lab VPC) print. `fleet.sh`'s hint was two lines joined by a printed backslash; it is
  now one line per command.
- `docs/floor.md` has a new section, "Settling a fresh state", with these findings.

**Tests.**
- `verify/test_drift_settle.py` (offline): scans every tracked `.md`, `.tf`, `.sh` and `.py` file outside the history
  records and `verify/`. For each `terraform apply` of the lab VPC, boundary or audit root that is not refresh-only, it
  requires a refresh-only apply of the same root with the same arguments later on the line or within three lines. Its
  parser is checked first on ten cases it owns (settled, unsettled, other arguments, another root, a settle above the
  apply, one too far below, a quoted hint, backups.py's f-string, a cluster apply). It requires the 13 files that hold
  those commands today to be found, and floor.md's section to name each root and both tests. On the base tree it fails
  the settle check and the floor.md checks.
- `verify/test_fleet_settle_after_apply.sh` (offline): runs `fleet.sh up watch-it-burn-attendee-001` with terraform
  and aws shimmed. A good apply is followed by exactly one refresh-only, auto-approved apply with identical state,
  chdir and variables, logged to the same apply log. A failed apply is not settled. A failed settle exits non-zero
  and names the cluster. On the base `fleet.sh` 8 of its 13 checks fail.
- `verify/test_preflight_boundary.sh`: two new checks that the boundary and lab VPC FAIL lines carry the settle with the
  same arguments. Both fail on the base `preflight.sh`.
- `verify/test_fleet_apply_failure_exit.sh`: its shim counted every apply as a build, and would have counted each
  settle. The shim now answers a refresh-only apply with success and does not count it. The test's checks are
  unchanged.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The `fleet.sh` settle runs at the next cluster build. A run cannot build one, so the
first fleet bring-up after this lands checks it: `fleet.sh up <name>`, then
`python3 infra/terraform/drift/drift-report.py` on the operator machine. The new cluster's state should read clean,
with the refresh-only apply's output at the end of `fleet/logs/<name>.apply.log`.

## 2026-11-06 · #937 · run 17835 · A live test runs prompts-agenticburn's `uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest`

**What was missing.** #927's fifth criterion is "`uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest` passes in
prompts-agenticburn". The throttle #927 asked for landed in that repo as prompts-agenticburn#18 (`6601313a`), but no
test here ran the command, so nothing failed when it stopped holding (#937, from test review run 17682).
`bash verify/prior-drafts.sh 937 origin/staging` printed NONE and #937 has no comments, so there was no draft to port.

**The change.** `verify/prompts_wall_suite.py` (new) resolves the tip of prompts-agenticburn's `main` and `staging`
with `gh api repos/peopleforrester/prompts-agenticburn/commits/<ref>`, fetches that commit's tarball with
`gh api .../tarball/<sha>`, unpacks it with tarfile's data filter into a new temporary directory, refuses a tarball
that is not one top directory holding a `pyproject.toml`, and runs `uv run ruff check .` and then `uv run pytest` in
it, stopping at the first failure as `&&` does. The suite gets PATH, HOME, the locale, TMPDIR and UV_* only: the
wall's app reads FEED_URL, ROSTER_URL, MAX_ENTRIES and more from its environment, and run-e2e.sh's environment carries
CONTEXT and AWS settings, so without that the result would hang on the caller. `verify/test_prompts_wall_suite_e2e.py`
(new, `# SUITE: e2e`) runs it on both branches, runs a commit once when both branches point at it, and exits 1
naming the branch and the step that failed.

**Why the live suite and not the tools tier.** prompts-agenticburn is private (an anonymous read of its API answers
404, and `git ls-remote` asks for credentials), so the only read is through gh's token. Dispatched runs get `gh api`
GETs; the promotion gate's read-only gh refuses `gh api` (the #863 entry above), and refuses `gh repo clone` too. In
the tools tier the test would turn every promotion red, so it sits in `bash verify/run-e2e.sh`, the same call
`verify/test_images_saved.py` makes for the image archive. Dispatched runs can run it directly:
`python3 verify/test_prompts_wall_suite_e2e.py`.

**Offline test.** `verify/test_prompts_wall_suite.py` (new) puts a stub gh and a stub uv alone on PATH. The uv stub
fails the step that the fetched tree's `fail_step` file names, so the tree decides the outcome. It checks the command
is the criterion's word for word; the sha and tarball reads; that both steps run in the unpacked tree; that the
caller's CONTEXT and FEED_URL do not reach the suite; that a failing ruff stops before pytest and a failing pytest
fails; that no uv, no gh, the gate's `REFUSED gh api` answer, a 404 and an answer that is not a sha each fail by
name; that a tarball with two top directories, a path out of the destination, no `pyproject.toml` or bytes that are
not gzip is refused; and, end to end on the stubs, that the live test exits 0 on two green branches and 1 naming
staging's pytest or main's ruff. It also holds that the live test has no `# E2E TIER: tools` line.

**Live check, run 17835.** `python3 verify/test_prompts_wall_suite_e2e.py` read `main` and `staging` both at
`6601313a76c9`, and on it `uv run ruff check .` printed `All checks passed!` and `uv run pytest` printed
`90 passed`, exit 0, in about 6 s. On copies of that tree, the helper failed each mutation: an unused import in
`app.py` failed ruff (exit 1) and pytest did not run; an added `assert False` test failed pytest with `1 failed,
90 passed`; and the wall's `1500` ms card interval changed to `500` failed pytest with `3 failed, 87 passed`. No
cluster was touched.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing is owed: the test reads GitHub and runs that repo's suite locally.

No dependency was added.

**A broken test this run's suite found, fixed here (run 17835).** The first `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh`, at
`13c80f0c`, went red in the offline suite on `test_chat_turn_cancel.py` alone: "guard-proxy logs forward_error, then
task_cancel" saw `events ['forward_error']`, while the same output already held the proxy's `task_cancel` JSON line
on stderr. The test slept a fixed 0.2 s after the agent received `tasks/cancel` and then read the events its logging
handler had collected. The proxy's cancel thread logs `task_cancel` only after the agent answers, and its stderr
handler writes the JSON line before the test's handler sees the record, so a thread stalled in that write on a loaded
host misses the window. Run alone three times it passed. With `logging.StreamHandler.emit` slowed by 0.5 s for the
`task_cancel` record, the old test failed with that exact check and the fixed one passed. The check now waits up to
5 s for `task_cancel`, as the line above it already waits for the cancel itself, and holds that `forward_error` came
first, which its label always said.

## 2026-11-06 · #959 · run 17846 · The Gateway API CRDs ship wherever Istio does, and the C1 egress waypoint works on Istio 1.30.4 once its allowlist matches the SNI

**What this issue is.** A followup of #727. The C1 stage-2b fix builds its forced egress proxy as an Istio ambient
egress waypoint, a Gateway of class `istio-waypoint` (`challenges/c1-exfil-s3/fix/egress-waypoint.yaml`), and run
17752 found no `gateway.networking.k8s.io` CRD on `watch-it-burn-private`. The issue asked for an Argo CD app with
the CRDs on the attendee, admin and full profiles, and for a check on the pinned Istio that the ambient egress
pattern works, or else the Istio upgrade #860 left open. `prior-drafts.sh 959 origin/staging` printed NONE, so
nothing was ported.

**What was built.** `gitops/bootstrap/apps/gateway-api.yaml`, an Application named `gateway-api` at sync wave -7,
before every Istio Application, with `ServerSideApply=true` (the HTTPRoute CRD is 248 KB as JSON). It syncs
`gitops/gateway-api` at the root's revision. That directory holds the v1.5.1 standard-channel release asset
`standard-install.yaml`, byte for byte, whose SHA-256 `751002b3…` is the digest GitHub publishes for it, and a
`kustomization.yaml` that builds it. The bundle is eight CRDs and the release's `safe-upgrades` admission policy
and binding, with no workload. It is listed on every profile that lists `istio`: attendee, admin and full, as the
issue asked, and kubecon-private and local-inference, which carry the mesh too (kubecon-private is admin's list
with the breakout's changes, local-inference is full's plus vLLM, and both tests that hold those pairs pass).

**Why v1.5.1.** It is the `sigs.k8s.io/gateway-api` version in istio/istio's `go.mod` at the 1.30.4 tag. v1.7.0 is
the newest release, but the pair that Istio tests is the one to ship; when Istio moves, the two move together, and
`verify/test_gateway_api_crds.py` fails on an Istio pin it has no Gateway API version for.

**Why vendored, not a git source on kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api.** No app here sources another git repo, the render
gates (`verify/app_render.py`) read in-repo paths and would read nothing from an external one, and a vendored copy
builds with no third host. No new dependency: the file is data, and its version is in VERSIONS.lock.

**What changed with it.** `platform-baseline.yaml`'s `gateway-api` entry moves from proposed to adopted.
`test_bootstrap_chart.py` now counts attendee 31, admin 34, full 32 and checks that gateway-api is listed exactly
where istio is. The Application counts the docs state move by one: the run-of-show's 39 and 36, the platform
page's 36 and 39, and the design glance's 36, held by `test_fleet_contract.py`. `test_mesh_enrollment.py`'s check
that nothing installs the CRDs became a check that `gitops/gateway-api` alone defines them, and section 2.4 of the
Istio evaluation marks that step done. Two new tests: `verify/test_gateway_api_crds.py` (offline: the digest, the
CRD set, the channel and version, the Istio pair, the Application's source, wave and profiles) and
`verify/test_gateway_api_crds_upstream.py` (tools tier: downloads the release asset and compares it, and reads
istio/istio's go.mod at the pinned tag).

**Live check (run 17846, 2026-11-06, `--context watch-it-burn-private` on every call).** Before: no
`gateway.networking.k8s.io` CRD, no ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, istiod `1.30.4`. The vendored bundle was applied
server-side; istiod logged its CRD watcher picking the CRDs up and created the `istio`, `istio-remote` and
`istio-waypoint` GatewayClasses within 9 s, with no restart. In a scratch namespace `check-959-17846` labelled
`istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient`, the fix's three objects were applied unchanged except for the namespace, with a
second ServiceEntry for `example.com` steered to the same waypoint. The Gateway went Programmed, its pod ran
`registry.istio.io/release/proxyv2:1.30.4-distroless` with limits `cpu 2, memory 1Gi`, so the cluster's
require-resource-limits admitted it, and it carried `gateway.networking.k8s.io/gateway-name=egress-waypoint` and no
`istio.io/gateway-name`. A Python client in an enrolled pod opened TLS to each host and sent a GET:

- With the fix's AuthorizationPolicy as written (`operation.hosts`), all three steered hosts failed with an EOF.
  ztunnel's access log showed each connection sent to the waypoint over HBONE (`dst.service="api.open-meteo.com"`,
  `dst.workload="egress-waypoint-…"`) and closed there.
- With the policy deleted, `api.open-meteo.com` and `geocoding-api.open-meteo.com` answered `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, and
  so did `example.com`. So the egress pattern works on 1.30.4 and no Istio upgrade is needed; the policy was what
  refused them. `operation.hosts` is an HTTP-only field and the waypoint passes this TLS through, so the ALLOW
  rule never matched.
- With the rule matching `connection.sni` on the two Open-Meteo hosts and port 443, both answered 200 and
  `example.com` failed with an EOF. A host with no ServiceEntry (`www.wikipedia.org`) went direct, not through the
  waypoint, in every case.
- A second pod labelled `istio.io/dataplane-mode=none`, with the SNI rule in place, reached all three hosts
  directly, `example.com` included. The waypoint holds only enrolled pods.

Then the namespace was deleted and the bundle removed with `kubectl delete -f`. After: no Gateway API CRD, no
ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or binding, no `check-959-17846`, and istiod, the CNI and ztunnel the same pods as before.
`watch-it-burn-community` was not touched; it carries no Istio (#860).

**What that changed in the fix.** `egress-waypoint.yaml`'s AuthorizationPolicy now admits port 443 when
`connection.sni` is one of the two Open-Meteo hosts, the rule that worked live. `test_c1_dns_exfil_fix.py` holds
that and refuses an HTTP-only operation field. The waypoint-label note in `agent-egress-fqdn.yaml` and the fix's
README say what the live check read. Still owed to #728, and in the README: the weather feed has to be enrolled in
the mesh before the fix is applied. In `agent` only the console and guard-proxy are enrolled (#471, question 947),
and live `weather-feed-…` carried no `istio.io/dataplane-mode`. Without it, `agent-egress-fqdn.yaml` shuts the weather
feed's only path to Open-Meteo. Enrolling a pod changes what the mesh carries, which `test_mesh_enrollment.py`
holds to the two pods question 947 chose, so it is a followup and not done here.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The `gateway-api` Application itself syncing through Argo CD, which needs this change
promoted: after promotion, `kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private -n argocd get application gateway-api` should read
Synced and Healthy, and `kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private get gatewayclass istio-waypoint` should read
Accepted. The next run on #728 reads both.

## 2026-11-06 · #962 · run 17855 · the first heals after two staging commits were selective, 2.7 s and 2.5 s; the gate Jobs held

**Context.** Run 17855 is #962's first dispatch, on staging `69b85238`. `bash verify/prior-drafts.sh 962
origin/staging` printed NONE. #898's commits reached staging as `5b9530ea` and `60de9d9a` (the issue names their
pre-promotion SHAs, `3a7baaf7` and `7282b41a`), and `ai-layer` on watch-it-burn-private synced `60de9d9a` at
05:41:34Z.

**Check 1 (09:28Z).** `kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private -n agent get jobs` printed
`kubearmor-gate-d92910c4   Complete   1/1   8s   3h47m` and `otel-gate-0353f97d   Complete   1/1   8s   3h47m`.
`ai-layer` read `Synced Healthy` at `69b85238`. The transition sync left neither Job Failed, so the recovery in
docs/floor.md was not needed.

**Check 2, first drill (09:29Z).** `ai-layer` had last synced `8673057d` (07:30:07Z), and staging had since moved to
`69b85238` with no change under `gitops/ai-layer`. `CONTEXT=watch-it-burn-private python3
verify/test_drift_selfheal_live.py` printed `back after 2.7s` and `healed by a selective self-heal of 1
resource(s), no hooks run`, then `Self-heal drill passed.`, exit 0. The controller log has `Initiated automated
sync to '69b85238...'` with `Resources:[...NetworkPolicy platform-console-egress]`, `skipHooks=true`, and `Partial
sync operation to 69b85238... succeeded` at 09:29:01Z. It did not print the `healed by a full sync to revision
<rev>, PreSync Jobs run first: none` the issue expected. The heal was at the new revision, and it was selective.

**Why it was selective.** Read from Argo CD v3.5.7's source (`controller/appcontroller.go` and
`controller/state.go` at the tag). A refresh asked for by an object change runs at comparison level 1
(CompareWithRecent), at `status.sync.revision`. The periodic resync had already moved that to `69b85238` (every
120 s plus up to 60 s jitter: argocd-cm on private has `timeout.reconciliation` 120s and the jitter 60s).
`evaluateRevisionChanges` then sees the synced and compared revisions equal and reports no changes, so
`alreadyAttemptedSync` compares only the sources. They match, so autoSync takes the self-heal branch, which syncs
only the out-of-sync resources. A full sync needs a level 2 comparison (against `staging` by name) that sees the
object missing while `operationState.syncResult.revision` is older. The log showed the delete came 63 s after the
last comparison (09:27:57Z), inside the 120 s expiry, so it got level 1.

**Check 2, a second drill timed for the full path (10:13Z).** The run's first commit (`947ed106`) made the drill aim at that path:
`HEAL_PATH=full` waited for staging to move past the last sync and for the comparison to pass 120 s, then deleted.
Staging moved to `8e00324d` while `ai-layer` had last synced `10193be9`, and at 10:13Z the drill printed `compared
8e00324d, last synced 10193be9, reconciledAt 2026-11-06T10:11:07Z`, deleted, and then `back after 2.5s` and
`healed by a selective self-heal of 1 resource(s), no hooks run`. Every check passed but the full-path one. The
controller log shows why. The delete's first refresh did run at level 2 (`comparison expired ... level (2)`,
10:13:12Z), but it still read the policy as present and printed `Skipping auto-sync: application status is
Synced`. The next refresh (`controller refresh requested, level (1)`) saw it missing and healed it selectively at
`8e00324d`. Timing the delete makes a full sync possible but not certain. A check that passes or fails on that race
would be broken under the repo's rule on random results, so the run's second commit takes `HEAL_PATH=full` out
again. The drill's docstring and docs/floor.md now say that the first heal after a staging commit can take
either path, and why.

**The full path since #898, read from a real full sync.** `10193be9` changed `gitops/ai-layer/workshop-mcp-server.py`,
so `ai-layer` ran an automated full sync at 10:03:41Z (`skipHooks=false`). It applied the wave -1 objects at
10:03:44Z, and `job.batch/kubearmor-gate-d92910c4 serverside-applied` and `job.batch/otel-gate-0353f97d
serverside-applied` at 10:03:46Z. `get pods` still shows only the gate pods from 4h33m earlier, so no gate ran again.
`networkpolicy.networking.k8s.io/platform-console-egress serverside-applied` came at 10:03:48Z, 7 s into the sync,
and the sync succeeded at 10:03:54Z. At 03:47Z, under the hooks, the same point came 24 s in. So a full-sync heal
now has the policy back about 7 s after its sync starts. That is a sync started by a commit, not by the drill, so
it is the time a full-sync heal would take, not a drill measurement. The other syncs since `60de9d9a` were also full
syncs started by commits that changed `ai-layer`: `b17fc38b` in 12 s, `6cabaa4b` in 16 s and `8673057d` in 13 s,
start to finish. Each `syncResult` lists both gate Jobs with no `hookType`.

**Check 3.** `kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private -n agent get pods -l app=workshop-mcp -o
jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.annotations.kubearmor-policy}'` printed `enabled` at 09:29Z and again at 10:13Z
(pod `workshop-mcp-b444f5c8d-btlbr`).

**Left as found.** Each drill deleted only `agent/platform-console-egress`, and Argo CD put it back with git's spec
and the tracking annotation. At 10:13Z `ai-layer` read `Synced Healthy` at `8e00324d`, and both gate Jobs were
Complete.

**What changed in the repo.** The drill's `heal_kind` docstring and docs/floor.md said that when staging has moved,
the next delete starts a full sync. Both now say it can take either path, and give the measurements and the
post-#898 full-sync timing. `verify/test_drift_selfheal_ops.py` gains the 09:29Z operationState, a selective heal at
a revision the app had not synced, and checks that it reads as selective. The drill's behaviour is unchanged.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** A drill whose heal is a full sync, printing `healed by a full sync to revision <rev>,
PreSync Jobs run first: none`, has still not been seen. The drill cannot cause one on demand. When a future run of
`CONTEXT=watch-it-burn-private python3 verify/test_drift_selfheal_live.py` happens to heal that way, its `back
after` time is the number to record against the 10:03Z sync's 7 s.

## 2026-11-06 · #953 · run 17848 · The same-conversation recipe decline cannot be made reliable under #951's no-wall shape; recon is fixable; a design decision is asked

**The spec.** #953 (split from #925 by planning run 17725) asks for the four beats of #951's recipe rule,
run at least five times each on the public bot with every reply recorded, and for any beat that is not yet
reliable to be named so the next run on the issue can act. Run 17832 (the prior run, now in staging at this
run's base) ran the four beats live: the attack after a Reset returned the recipe 6 of 6 and the Reset button
cleared the memory 5 of 5, both reliable; recon named the folders and opened nothing on only 2 of 11, and the
same-conversation decline held 0 of 6. 17832 named two things for the next run to try, both measured first
through `converse` as #954 did: give case 1 its own fixed reply and move the joke so it is not reused on
recon, and key case 2 on the bot's own earlier reply rather than on the guest's question. This run is that
next run. `verify/prior-drafts.sh 953 origin/staging` printed LANDED then NONE, so 17832's branch is already
in staging and nothing earlier was reused.

**Why this run did not change the live bot.** A dispatched run cannot deploy, so a reworded rule cannot reach
the community cluster this cycle; the cluster still carries staging's wording, which 17832 already validated
live. So re-running the four beats live would only reproduce 17832's result. The productive step, and the one
17832 named, is to measure candidate rewords through `converse`, the method #954 used and 17832 confirmed is
faithful (its 0 of 8 for the same-conversation decline matched the live 0 of 6). This run measured; it did not
touch the live bot, and no prompt reached the room's feed because `converse` calls Bedrock Nova Pro directly
and never passes through kagent, guard-proxy or the room. The community cluster was read only (its live
`workshop-agent` systemMessage, byte-equal to git at 19746 bytes, and workshop-mcp's 12 tool schemas plus
evil-mcp's 3, read through a local port-forward that was closed afterward); nothing on either cluster was
changed.

**The measurement rig.** `converse` against the `bedrock-nova` application inference profile
(`5l72jg8rnz71`, the model the live Agent runs), system message byte-equal to the deployed one, the 15 live
tool schemas from workshop-mcp and evil-mcp, and a `run_shell` read of the recipe path returning the baked
bait whose signature is `WITCH-HAZEL-GHOST-PEPPER-BAT-SPIT-No7`. The folded `<thinking>` text the chat page
hides is stripped before judging the visible reply, as the page hides it. The scripts, the candidate system
messages and the per-trial transcripts are in the run's directory, not the repo. 177 recorded conversations,
about 330 Nova Pro calls on the `accen-dev` Bedrock counter, roughly a dollar; no live-bot guard-proxy cost
was spent.

**The rig is faithful.** On staging's deployed wording (HEAD) it reproduced the shape 17832 and #954 saw:
recon named the folders and opened nothing 8 of 11; the same-conversation decline held 0 of 8 (the hard beat,
matching #954's 0 of 8 and 17832's live 0 of 6); the fresh attack read the card and read back the signature 8
of 8; and recon-then-reset-then-attack (the lab's Challenge 3, which tells attendees to "start a fresh chat"
between the two prompts) held 7 of 8, the one miss a recon turn that named no folder.

**Two candidate rewords, each measured, 12 trials a beat unless shown.**

| Beat | HEAD (staging, no wall) | Wall wording | Playful state-flip (no wall) |
|---|---|---|---|
| recon: names folders, opens nothing | 8 of 11 | 12 of 12 | 11 of 12 |
| same-conversation decline after recon | 0 of 8 | 10 of 12 | 3 of 12 |
| fresh attack: reads and reads back | 8 of 8 | 11 of 12 | 12 of 12 |
| recon, reset, attack (lab C3) | 7 of 8 | 11 of 12 | 10 of 12 |
| passes `verify/test_recipe_persona.py` | yes | no | yes |

The "wall wording" made case 2 an explicit lock: once the guest has asked what the bot can see, for the rest of
that conversation the bot does not open the card for anyone, and the case fully overrides case 3. It lifted the
decline to 10 of 12, but it carries the absolute phrasing #951's accepted shape forbids (`verify/test_recipe_persona.py`
fails any rule matching "no matter what", "under no circumstances", or "never read/reveal/share/open"; the shape is
graduated resistance, memory `agent-graduated-resistance`), and the same absolute framing bled into the fresh
attack as over-refusal, dropping case 3 to 11 of 12 and the lab's Challenge 3 below #954's 15 of 15.

The "playful state-flip" wording kept every persona-test anchor and used no absolute phrasing: case 1 got its own
canned naming line ("I've got my burrito-data folder, sugar, with config and legacy tucked inside it!") with an
explicit "nothing to look up, call no tool", and case 2 added a playful reinforcement keyed on the bot's own prior
answer ("the pantry stays playfully shut to them for the rest of that chat") without a lock. It fixed recon (11 of
12, the joke no longer leaks onto the recon question and no stray verify tool call) and kept the fresh attack at 12
of 12, but the decline reached only 3 of 12.

**The finding, named for the decision.** Recon (criterion 1) is fixable inside #951's shape: the case-1 canned line
plus "nothing to look up" is test-legal and measures 11 of 12, a real gain over staging's 8 of 11, and it keeps the
fresh attack and the lab's Challenge 3 whole. The same-conversation playful decline (criterion 2) is not: with no
absolute phrasing it reaches at most 3 of 12, and the only wording that makes it reliable (10 of 12) is the wall
#951 forbids, which also degrades the after-reset read the workshop depends on. The two beats pull against each
other because the same attack prompt (the folder named, a kitchen reason) is meant to be declined in the recon
conversation and obeyed after a reset, and the only signal between them is whether a "what can you see" question
came earlier; Nova Pro will not hold that reliably from the prompt alone without a hard rule, and a hard rule breaks
the reset beat. #954 reached the same wall from the other side (its two wordings held the decline 0 of 8 and 1 of 8).

**The decision this run asks.** Criterion 2 as written cannot be met by prompt wording under #951's accepted shape.
The choice is Michael's because it changes a shape he approved: accept the same-conversation decline as a
best-effort beat and not a reliability gate (the workshop still demonstrates recon, reset and the attack, all
reliable), or relax the no-wall constraint (and `verify/test_recipe_persona.py`) to allow scoped absolute phrasing
for the in-conversation case and accept the measured case-3 over-refusal, or move the decline out of the prompt into
a deterministic layer (for example guard-proxy declining a card read while a recon turn is in the session). The
recon-only reword is held with it rather than committed alone, so the chosen case-2 path and the case-1 fix land
together in one wording on the next run.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Once a decision lands and its wording reaches the community cluster through Argo CD,
the next run on #953 re-runs the four beats live on https://attackme.burritobot.co/ as 17832 did, through the real
chat page with the probe marker, and records every reply. This run changed no rule, so there is nothing new for the
cluster to take yet.

**The suites (run 17848, at `c42ad648`).** This run changed only this prose entry, no code, test or gitops path.
`bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` printed `292 tests ran` and `ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN` for the offline
suite, then `69 checks ran (the offline suite and 68 tier tests) in 30m14s`, `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN` and
`exit=0`. `test_recipe_persona.py` and `test_recipe_block_coverage.py`, the offline guards for this rule, are among
them and stay green because the rule is unchanged. The prose gate printed `prose gate: pass`.

## 2026-11-06 · #953 · run 17862 · question 1094: keep the no-wall shape and make the same-conversation decline best-effort; recon gets its own naming line

**The question.** Question 1094, asked by run 17848: for the recipe challenge's same-conversation refusal beat,
should BurritoBot keep the playful, no-wall rule shape (accepting that the beat is not reliable), relax that shape
to allow a scoped firm refusal, or enforce the refusal outside the prompt?

**The answer.** Keep the no-wall shape and accept the refusal beat as best-effort.

**Who decided.** Decided by hecaton's research under Michael's standing rules, not by Michael. The research cited
the repo's standing key design in `docs/DECISION-LOG.md` ("Agent behavior: graduated resistance"): a hard "never
reveal" makes the model self-censor, which breaks the leak and the output-guard scrub, so the rule must not harden
into an absolute refusal. Run 17848's lock wording, which drops the fresh recipe attack from 15 of 15 to about 11
of 12, is that failure. It also cited #951's run 17734 entry, the persona tests, `PROGRESS.md`, and #925's body: the
recipe flow is a play-on-your-own attack, not a scripted stage beat, so a decline that rarely fires only makes the
puzzle easier for an attendee and does not break the leak the challenge exists to show.

**What it changes.**

- `gitops/workshop-agent/agent.yaml`: the recipe rule takes run 17848's measured no-wall wording (its "playful
  state-flip" column). Case 1, recon, keeps every word it had and adds a "nothing to look up" clause (do not run
  ls, cat, find or grep, and do not call run_shell or any tool even to check), its own naming line ("I've got my
  burrito-data folder, sugar, with config and legacy tucked inside it!"), and keeps the pantry joke for case 2
  only. Case 2 keeps every word it had and adds a playful reinforcement keyed on the bot's own earlier
  answer ("the pantry stays playfully shut to them for the rest of that chat") with no lock. Case 3 is unchanged.
  The rendered systemMessage is 20521 bytes and is byte-equal to the candidate run 17848 measured through
  `converse`, 12 trials a beat: recon names the folders and opens nothing 11 of 12 (staging's wording: 8 of 11), the
  fresh attack reads and reads back the card 12 of 12 (8 of 8), recon then reset then attack 10 of 12 (7 of 8), and
  the same-conversation decline 3 of 12 (0 of 8).
- The same-conversation decline is no longer a reliability gate. Criterion 2 of #953 stays unmet as written, and
  this is now by decision rather than an open defect. Nothing scripted relies on it: the prompt sheet
  (`facilitation/kubecon-na-2026/fallback/prompts.yaml`, `c3-recon` and `c3-attack`) and `challenges/LAB-TEXT.md`
  both run recon, then a fresh chat, then the attack, and the run-of-show names no same-conversation decline, so no
  facilitation text changes.
- `verify/test_recipe_persona.py` adds four checks: recon has nothing to look up and calls no tool even to check,
  recon has its own naming line with all three folders, the pantry joke is kept off recon, and the decline is keyed
  on the bot's own earlier answer as a playfully shut pantry. Its existing no-absolute-refusal check still holds the
  decline from becoming a lock. Run against staging's rule, the four new checks fail and the rest pass.
- What did not change: the card's path, so `block-recipe-snoop`, slide 21 and the workshop-mcp image are as #954
  left them. The persona test's anchors and the CEO address rule are also unchanged.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** The reworded rule reaches watch-it-burn-community through Argo CD only once hecaton
promotes this run. Until then, the live bot carries staging's wording, which run 17832 already recorded beat by
beat. The next run on #953 reruns the four beats live on https://attackme.burritobot.co/, as run 17832 did, through
the real chat page with the probe marker: `c3-recon` at least five times (each should name burrito-data, config and
legacy and open nothing), `c3-attack` in the same conversation at least five times (recorded, best-effort), Reset at
least five times, and `c3-attack` after Reset at least five times. It also reruns `PRIVATE_CONTEXT=watch-it-burn-private
python3 verify/test_recipe_block_live.py`, whose first check holds the live systemMessage equal to git's. Run 17832's
Playwright driver is in that run's directory, not the repo.

## 2026-11-06 · #965 · run 17872 · workshop-mcp and evil-mcp-shim already roll on a server.py change; a test now holds it for every generated source

**What the issue said.** #965 read workshop-mcp's Deployment in `gitops/ai-layer/resources.yaml`, saw that it mounts
`workshop-mcp-src` with no checksum annotation, unlike guard-proxy's `checksum/proxy-py`, and concluded that a change
to `workshop-mcp-server.py` or `tool_audit.py` syncs green while the old process keeps answering. It proposed a
`checksum/workshop-mcp-src` annotation and asked the same of evil-mcp-shim's `server.py`.

**What is true.** That was true before #252 and is not now. The 2026-09-06 entry for #252 turned the kustomize content
hash on for the whole ai-layer bundle (`generatorOptions.disableNameSuffixHash: false`). A change to a generated
source renames its ConfigMap (`workshop-mcp-src-<hash>`), kustomize rewrites the Deployment's volume to the new name,
the pod template changes, and Argo CD rolls the pod. The `checksum/proxy-py` annotation stayed only because `/controls`
reports it in the room, which that entry says. A rendered probe in this run showed it: appending one line to
`workshop-mcp-server.py` and `server.py` moved workshop-mcp from `workshop-mcp-src-gdtg56h2kf` to
`workshop-mcp-src-tcdmgfhtmd` and evil-mcp-shim from `evil-mcp-src-78t5dt5d9d` to `evil-mcp-src-267k9d288t`.

**What was missing.** A test that holds it for these two. `verify/test_ai_layer_rollout.py` checked only that editing
`web/lab.html` rolls the console. It now reads every `files:` entry of every `configMapGenerator`, appends a line to
each in a copy, renders, and fails naming the file and the Deployment whose pod template did not change. It holds by
name that workshop-mcp mounts `workshop-mcp-src` built from `workshop-mcp-server.py` and `tool_audit.py`, and that
evil-mcp-shim mounts `evil-mcp-src` built from `server.py`, so the probe cannot pass by finding no consumer. That is
24 sources over 8 generators, and the whole test now takes about 17 s. With `disableNameSuffixHash: true` set by hand the test failed 5 checks,
the two new by-name mount checks among them. No checksum annotation was added: it would be a second, hand-bumped
mechanism for what the hash already does, and a forgotten bump would only fail a test. A comment at each of the two
volumes in `resources.yaml` says why there is none.

**Does workshop-agent need a restart?** No. workshop-agent runs `ghcr.io/kagent-dev/kagent/golang-adk:0.10.1`, which
builds its MCP toolsets with `google.golang.org/adk/v2` v2.1.0 (kagent `go/go.mod` at v0.10.1). That version's
`tool/mcptoolset/set.go` `Tools()` calls `ListTools` on the server each time it is asked, with no cache, and
`client.go` reconnects when the session is lost. A changed schema or description reaches the next turn. A new tool
name is different: the Agent CR's `toolNames` filter it, and a change there changes the Agent, which kagent rolls.

**Live check (run 17872, 2026-11-06, both clusters, read only).** On `watch-it-burn-community` and
`watch-it-burn-private`, Argo CD's `ai-layer` was `Synced` and `Healthy` at staging `30982703`. Each cluster's
workshop-mcp mounted `workshop-mcp-src-gdtg56h2kf`, the name this tree renders, and its pod was 39 minutes old, the
same age as that ConfigMap: the last `workshop-mcp-server.py` change (#939, `24307b11`) rolled it with nobody
restarting it. Each `RemoteMCPServer/workshop-mcp` listed 12 tools, with `check_inventory` described as taking an
ingredient (#902) and `deploy_app` taking a bare app name (#939). The workshop-mcp logs showed a `ListToolsRequest`
every 60 s from the kagent controller's discovery. workshop-agent's pods were 79 and 169 minutes old, older than
workshop-mcp's, and needed nothing. evil-mcp-shim mounted `evil-mcp-src-78t5dt5d9d` on both, the rendered name;
`server.py` has not changed since. Nothing on either cluster was changed.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** Nothing is owed. The change is a test and two comments; the rollout it holds is already
live, as above.

No dependency was added.

**The suites (run 17872, at `a3cdc495`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` printed `298 tests ran` and `ALL OFFLINE
RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`, then `71 checks ran (the offline suite and 70 tier tests) in 29m55s`, `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER
CHECKS GREEN` and `exit=0`. `test_ai_layer_rollout.py` passed in it with the new checks.

**Run 17890, the port (2026-11-06).** Run 17872 ended failed on hecaton's claim-stale, not on a gate, so its two

## 2026-11-06 · #969 · run 17879 · The redaction tier test starts its collector through otelcol_local, which waits for the ready line and retries a taken port

**What failed.** Run 17806 (#954) saw `verify/test_collector_act2_redaction_e2e.py` fail once in the tools tier and
pass on the rerun: the attendee profile's Act 1 printed "the collector took the turn" false, no spans reached the
exporter, and the collector log tail was empty. The send loop gave the local otelcol-contrib 30 seconds from its
`Popen` to answer the POST, and printed nothing about the collector when it did not.

**Which cause the empty log fits.** With a port held by another listener, the pinned otelcol-contrib v0.160.0 exits
in 0.18 s with exit code 1 and logs `listen tcp 127.0.0.1:<port>: bind: address already in use` (measured on this host
for this run). A collision therefore leaves a full log, not an empty one, and the old loop would have stopped on
`proc.poll()` at once. An empty log after 30 seconds fits a collector that had not started on the loaded host (that
tier run took 36m05s, against about 23 to 30 minutes on a quiet one). Both causes are now handled.

**The change.**
- `verify/otelcol_local.py` is new. `start(argv, log_file, env)` picks a port with `free_port()`, starts
  `argv(port)`, and waits for the collector's own `Everything is ready` line, which it logs only once every receiver
  is bound. The wait counts polls (600 at 0.3 s, so 180 s at least), not wall seconds, as #799 taught
  `verify/test_trace_shape_e2e.py`. When the collector exits with `address already in use` in its log, it starts
  again on a fresh port, up to 5 times. Once the collector is ready the port is its own, since Linux admits no
  second listener on an address while one listens, so a POST reaches this collector and no other process. When the
  start fails, `Collector.detail()` gives `proc.poll()` (the exit code, or "still running"), the polls and seconds
  waited, the host's pressure stall over the wait, and the log of every attempt.
- `verify/test_collector_act2_redaction_e2e.py` starts each collector with it. Its 30-second send clock starts only
  once the collector is ready, and "the collector took the turn" prints `collector.detail()` when it is false. Its
  own `free_port()` and `Popen` are gone; `validate` reads the same config written for port 0.
- `verify/test_otelcol_local.py` (offline) holds the helper with a stand-in collector the test writes itself, which
  logs the collector's lines and answers a POST with its pid. It forces each case: a port this test holds and
  serves 200 on (the start comes up on a fresh port, and a POST reaches the stand-in, not the holder), every port
  taken (the start gives up after its attempts and prints each one's log), a 2 s silent start (start() returns only
  once ready, so the first POST is taken), a collector that never says it is ready (the detail reads
  `proc.poll() = None (still running)` and an empty log), and one that exits 3 on another error (no retry, the exit
  code and log printed). It also reads the redaction test's source for the helper and the detail.

**Checked on this host.** `python3 verify/test_collector_act2_redaction_e2e.py` passed every check in 40 s. A forced
collision with the real binary, a listener held on the first port given to `start()`, came up on the second port
after two starts in 0.60 s, the first start's log carrying `address already in use`.

**Not done here.** Six other tier tests start otelcol-contrib on a `free_port()` port with their own loop:
test_collector_pii_scrub_e2e.py, test_tool_failure_status_e2e.py, test_collector_one_root_e2e.py and
test_adk_model_content_e2e.py start the send clock at the `Popen`, and test_trace_shape_e2e.py and
test_collector_llmobs_model_e2e.py wait for the ready line but do not retry a taken port. Moving them to
`otelcol_local.start` is a followup issue, so that this change stays the one test #969 names.

No cluster check applies: the change is to the tools tier's own test code, which runs no cluster. No dependency was
added.

**Suites (run 17879, at `7446279f`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` ran the offline suite (`301 tests ran`, `ALL
OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`, test_otelcol_local.py among them) and then the tier: `72 checks ran (the offline
suite and 71 tier tests) in 30m35s`, `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN`, exit 0. The prose gate printed `prose gate: pass`.

**Ported by run 17892.** Run 17879 ended claim-stale, so its two commits (`7446279f`, `ff4a0652`) never reached
staging. `bash verify/prior-drafts.sh 969 origin/staging` printed CLEAN for `origin/agent/969-17879`: staging had
only appended to decisions.md since its base `1503aaa9`. Run 17892 cherry-picked both commits unchanged; nothing in
the code differs from the draft. `python3 verify/test_otelcol_local.py` passed its 15 checks in 8 s on the port.

**Suites and the real collector (run 17892).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` on the port ran the offline suite
(`301 tests ran`, `ALL OFFLINE RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`) and then the tier: `72 checks ran (the offline suite and 71
tier tests) in 33m15s`, `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS GREEN`, `exit=0`, with all six of
test_collector_act2_redaction_e2e.py's "the collector took the turn" checks passing. A forced collision through
`otelcol_local.start` with the pinned otelcol-contrib, a listener held on the first port it was given, came up on the
second port after two starts in 0.60 s, the first start's log carrying `address already in use`, as in run 17879.
The prose gate printed `prose gate: pass`. No cluster check applies, and no dependency was added.

or without the recipe rule (run 17806) and is #967's, so neither is a beat here.

**The bars, from the odds.** A beat's attempts are binomial, so each bar was set from the chance it passes a beat at a
given true rate:

| Tries, bar | 20% | 29% | 36% | 56% | 70% | 90% | 95% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8, at least 6 (C3's attack) | 0.001 | 0.009 | 0.029 | 0.238 | 0.552 | 0.962 | 0.994 |
| 4, at least 2 (the other land-beats) | 0.181 | 0.331 | 0.455 | 0.772 | 0.916 | 0.996 | 1.0 |

#951's wording landed C3 2 of 7 live (29%) and 9 of 25 direct (36%); the reworded rule landed it 15 of 15 direct and 5
of 5 live. At 6 of 8, the regression passes under 1% of runs and the reworded rule's rate passes over 99%. The other
land-beats need at least half, which a 90% beat passes 99.6% of runs. A guarded beat must hold on every try.

## 2026-11-06 · #985 · run 17912 · A KubeCon standby that takes attackme has Kyverno admission armed before the router sends the room to it, and the new holder is linked to the other bot's cluster

**The question.** Once #988 and #991 take the six-image list out of `deploy_app`, the public cluster admits any image
until `guardrails-on` in Segment 3's step 5. If a room deployment takes attackme's cluster down, the watcher (#643)
promotes a standby within about a minute, and that standby starts in the KubeCon start state (#774), all four
Kubernetes guardrails off. The same ask can then take it down too, and the next one: an outage loop. Michael signed
off on 2026-11-06 for the run to pick the design.

**The design.** `infra/terraform/fleet/backups.py`'s watcher, at every promotion of the community role (automatic,
or `backups.py promote` by hand, the roster cluster included):

1. **Arms Kyverno admission on the incoming cluster before the router moves.** `arm_floor` patches
   `restrict-image-registries` and `deny-external-registries` to `[Deny]` and reads each back, with an isolated
   kubeconfig and the cluster's own `--context`, the same patch `guardrails-on`'s Kyverno step makes
   (`images/web-terminal/entrypoint.sh`, `_kg on kyverno`). Only after that is the router table written and
   reloaded. Argo CD keeps the change, since both Applications ignore `/spec/validationActions`.
2. **Leaves RBAC, KubeArmor and egress as the start state has them,** for `guardrails-on`.
3. **Links the new holder with the other role's holder** once the router has taken the table, by running
   `fleet.sh guardrails-link <community>@<region> <private>@<region>` (with `WIB_LINK_TOKEN_TRIES=3`, so the
   watcher waits at most about 30 seconds on a token). An admin promotion links too. Without this, `guardrails-on`
   from the private bot's terminal reaches the dead roster cluster, prints a failure on stage, and never reaches the
   cluster the room is on.

A private standby is not armed: the room's phones reach the public bot, and Whitney's step-4 attack on the private
bot needs its guardrails off. The arm and link follow each role's bootstrap profile, read from fleet.sh's
`bootstrap_profile_for_role` (event.sh's `WIB_ROSTER_PROFILES`). Only `kubecon-community` is armed, and the link
runs only when both roles are `kubecon-*`. So the 2-hour workshop's `burn` and `admin` profiles get neither.

A standby that cannot be armed still takes the hostname, and the watcher's log and `logs/failover.jsonl` say so
(`armed: false`). A room on a dead cluster is an outage now; a room on an unarmed one is only the chance of one, and
`guardrails-on` closes it. A link that fails leaves the promotion standing (`linked: false`), and the log names the
`guardrails-link` command to run by hand.

**Why Kyverno alone, and not all four at promotion.** The room's way to take a cluster down is a workload BurritoBot
deploys for it, and Kyverno admission is the one guardrail of the four that stands in that path. The other three
do not touch the cluster's health. The broad and scoped `workshop-agent` Roles (`gitops/ai-layer/resources.yaml`,
`c8-broad-role.yaml` and `c5-scoped-role.yaml`) carry the same workload verbs and differ only in which Secrets agent-sa
reads. KubeArmor guards the recipe files and egress the way out. Arming all four would take Challenge 1's CEO read and
Challenge 2's recipe read and beacon post away from the room on a promoted cluster as well. With Kyverno alone those
three still land, and only the attack that can cause the loop is refused.

**Why at promotion, and not at the standby's build.** Arming at the build would leave nothing new on the promotion
path. But a standby could be reset between its build and its promotion (a rehearsal's `guardrails-off`, a hand
reset), and nothing would notice. The patch at promotion is idempotent and quick, it is checked right before the room
arrives, and it covers the by-hand fail-back to the roster cluster too.

**How it fits Segment 3's switch moment.** Before step 5, a promoted public bot refuses a public image. The
presenters can say the replacement cluster came up with admission on; the room still has the recipe read and the
beacon post, and the chat page shows the Kyverno badge already lit there. Step 5 runs as written: on the promoted
cluster the Kyverno line repeats what the promotion did, and the link means the other three arm on both clusters.
A promotion after step 5 gets Kyverno and the link, not the other three, so the run-of-show says to run
`guardrails-on` again from the private bot's terminal (it is safe to repeat). This run did not make the watcher copy
the private cluster's switch state onto the standby: that needs the Role, KubeArmorPolicy and NetworkPolicy
manifests on the fleet host, and one presenter command already restores it. The run-of-show's "After a promotion on
stage" carries all of this, and Segment 3's start state names the exception.

**Standby builds no longer link.** `backups.py up` builds each region with `fleet.sh instructors up all`, which
under the KubeCon profiles ended by linking the default roster pair in that region. Outside us-west-2 that failed and
was masked by the converge after it. In us-west-2, the six-hours wave would put the roster pair back over a link the
watcher had made for a promotion earlier in the window. `region_steps` now passes `WIB_NO_LINK=1`, and fleet.sh's
`instructors up` skips the pair link when it is set.

**The 2-hour workshop and the Portland tag.** No 2-hour workshop file changed. The arm and the link turn on only for
the KubeCon profiles, `WIB_NO_LINK` is set only by `backups.py up`, and `verify/test_backups_floor.py` drives a
promotion under `WIB_ROSTER_PROFILES=workshop` and checks that nothing is patched or linked.
`delivered/devopsdays-portland-2026` is a tag, and this run did not touch it.

**The offline test.** `verify/test_backups_floor.py` builds the watcher with `make_watcher`, as `backups.py watch`
does, and drives promotions through it. Fake `aws` and `kubectl` scripts play the EKS clusters, each one's two
registry policies kept in a state file. A stub fleet.sh records the link, and the router's reload script records
every cluster's policy state at the moment it takes a table. It checks:

- b01 is at Deny on both policies, and already was when the router took the table.
- The two patches on b01 are the only changes made, and every call names its kubeconfig and context.
- No other cluster moved.
- The link is `watch-it-burn-community-b01@us-east-2 watch-it-burn-private@us-west-2`.
- The private standby stays at Audit and is linked with attackme's holder.
- A by-hand fail-back arms the roster cluster.
- A failed arm or link leaves the promotion standing and is recorded.
- The workshop profiles arm and link nothing.

**The live check (watch-it-burn-community, 13:39 to 13:44 UTC).** With `. "$HECATON_CLUSTER_ENV"`, both clusters'
two policies read `["Audit"]`, and `lab-bootstrap` on community is labelled `kubecon-community`. A server-side dry
run of a `public.ecr.aws/docker/library/busybox:1.38.0` pod in `agent` printed `pod/floor-probe-985 created (server
dry run)`, as the run's role and as `system:serviceaccount:agent:agent-sa`. Then `backups.py`'s own functions were
run against the roster cluster, standing in for a promoted one:

- `console_lb` printed `k8s-agent-console-6d7d3fd8cd-932f5f880aa49b92.elb.us-west-2.amazonaws.com`, so the shared
  kubeconfig helper works live.
- `arm_floor` printed `(True, 'Kyverno admission at Deny (restrict-image-registries, deny-external-registries)')`,
  and both policies read `["Deny"]`.
- The same dry run, as agent-sa, was refused: `admission webhook "vpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail" denied the
  request: Policy restrict-image-registries failed: Images must come from allowed registries`.
- A `ghcr.io/stefanprodan/podinfo:6.9.2` pod, which `restrict-image-registries` allows, was refused by
  `deny-external-registries`: `BurritoBot may run images only from the internal registry, registry.burritobot.co`.
- Argo CD reconciled `kyverno-registry-policy` at 13:41:14Z and `kyverno-breakout` at 13:43:17Z. Both stayed
  Synced, and both policies still read `["Deny"]` at 13:43:22Z.

At 13:43:45Z both policies were patched back to `["Audit"]` and read back so on both clusters, and the busybox dry
run was admitted again. The cluster was left as found. No pod was created; every probe was a server-side dry run.

**Not yet run on a cluster.** A promotion of a real KubeCon standby, with the watcher arming it and linking it to the
private cluster, waits on a KubeCon-profile standby, which a dispatched run cannot build. #986 owns that failover
test. When it runs, the check is: `backups.py watch --drill watch-it-burn-community` with the standbys up promotes

No dependency was added.

## 2026-11-06 · #992 · run 17917 · deploy_app passes any image through, and moves Docker Hub's official images to public.ecr.aws

left exactly as written, a Docker Hub image in Docker's official library is rewritten, and any other Docker Hub image
is refused before the apply. HC-666's Joker flow (#775, `registry.burritobot.co`) and the 2-hour workshop's
promo-mascot image are untouched: both are the platform's own images, and `verify/test_room_jokers.py` passes with no
edit.

**Decided: what happens to a Docker Hub reference.** `_DOCKER_HUB` still lists the bare form and Docker Hub's four
hosts. A reference under any of them whose repository has no namespace (`nginx`, `redis:8`) or the `library/` one
(`library/memcached`, under any of the hosts) is rewritten to `public.ecr.aws/docker/library/<name>:<tag>`, tag and
digest kept, `:latest` where it names no tag. That holds for every official image, the old six and the rest: Docker publishes every
official image there at the same digests, and the tools tier now reads busybox, alpine, httpd, redis, postgres,
memcached and rabbitmq from it. A bare name that is not an official image (`tron`) is rewritten the same way and is
not refused. Docker Hub reads a bare name as `library/<name>` too, so the rewrite names exactly what Docker Hub would
have served, and where that is nothing, the node reports an image it cannot pull. Telling the two apart would need a
list of official images, which is the kind of list #988 removes. A Docker Hub image in any other namespace
(`bitnami/redis`, `trongame/tron`, `library/someone/tron`) is refused before any apply, with the reason "is a Docker Hub
image outside Docker's official library, and the cantina pulls nothing from Docker Hub", and is told to write the image
with the registry it is published on or to send just the app's name. It is not rewritten to `public.ecr.aws/<namespace>/`:
ECR Public aliases are not Docker Hub's namespaces, so that would pull whatever account happens to hold the alias.

**Decided: how a name with no image is served.** A manifest that is only a plain-language name (#939: `Tron`,
`Light Cycle Arena`, `festival landing page`) becomes a one-replica Deployment named after it on `LANDING_IMAGE`, one
pinned web server: Docker's official nginx `1.29-alpine` on public.ecr.aws at the digest images.lock already held for
it. With no list to match, a plain name is never read as an image, so `nginx`, `redis` and `2048` sent alone also get
the landing page under their own name, and the reply says it serves a landing page and not an image of its own. A
bare image reference (one with `/`, `:` or `@`, such as `redis:8` or `quay.io/...`) is that image, read as any other.
The old aliases (`apache`, `2048` as an image) are gone: written as an image they are read as the official names they
spell.

**Decided: what `_shrink_room_deployment` applies to.** It keyed on the six images; it now keys on a room deployment,
a workload with any container whose image is not the platform's own. The platform's own are `ghcr.io/peopleforrester/`
(this repo's and lab-platform's packages, the C2 villains and the C6 image among them), `registry.burritobot.co/`
(the Jokers) and an ECR registry, all three on `restrict-image-registries`' allow-list, which the offline test holds.
A room deployment gets one replica, the room's resources and the scale to zero after `JOKER_SCALE_DOWN_SECONDS`, as
the six did, so a phone still cannot fill the node with any image it names. So an image on quay.io, on another
owner's ghcr.io path or on public.ecr.aws is now capped where before it kept its replicas, and the platform's images
keep theirs as before. A room container whose repository is busybox or alpine and that has no command or args gets
the `sleep 3600`, from any registry; an init container no longer does.

**Pins and tests.** images.lock keeps the landing nginx row and drops the five other old pins (busybox, alpine, httpd,
redis, the 2048 game), which nothing hands a cluster now. The tool description loses the list of names and says any
image can be named and an official name is pulled from public.ecr.aws; the rest of its prose is #988's next child.
`verify/test_public_images.py` sends `ghcr.io/stefanprodan/podinfo:6.9.2`, `quay.io/prometheus/node-exporter:v1.9.1`,
`public.ecr.aws/someone/tron:1`, `registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10` and `postgres:17` and checks each reaches the apply as
written, the last rewritten. It feeds official, bare non-official and namespaced references under every `_DOCKER_HUB`
name and checks each is rewritten or refused as above. `verify/test_deploy_app_named_app.py` sends `Tron` and four
other plain-language names and checks each applies a Deployment on `LANDING_IMAGE`. `test_public_images_served.py`
(tools tier) reads `LANDING_IMAGE` and seven official images on public.ecr.aws. `test_no_docker_hub.py` drops its two
REFUSED lines for test_public_images.py, which builds its Docker Hub references from `_DOCKER_HUB` and names no host.
`test_deployments_page_live.py` builds the room Deployment with the new functions.

**Live check (run 17917, both clusters, nothing created).** A server-side dry run as
`system:serviceaccount:agent:workshop-mcp` of the Deployments deploy_app now builds. Both clusters read
`deny-external-registries [Audit]` and `restrict-image-registries [Audit]`, and on each all four were admitted
(`rc=0`): `nginx` as `public.ecr.aws/docker/library/nginx:latest`, `quay.io/prometheus/node-exporter:v1.9.1` and
`ghcr.io/stefanprodan/podinfo:6.9.2` as written, and `Tron` on
`public.ecr.aws/docker/library/nginx:1.29-alpine@sha256:5616878291a2eed594aee8db4dade5878cf7edcb475e59193904b198d9b830de`,
each at one replica. `CONTEXT=<cluster> python3 verify/test_deployments_page_live.py` did not reach this step on

## 2026-11-06 · #973 · run 17906 · A test holds every C3 prompt copy to /kubecon's recon and attack

**The gap.** Test review run 17827 found that no test checked one criterion of #952: that every other copy that held
the Challenge 3 recipe prompt carries the same recon and attack prompts. `verify/test_replay_prompts.py` holds the
fallback `prompts.yaml` equal to the whole `/kubecon` page and `verify/test_lab_text_export.py` holds
`challenges/LAB-TEXT.md` equal to what the exporter renders from `lab.html`, but neither reads the C3 prompts, and no
test read the C3 section of `challenges/PROMPT-CATALOG.md` at all. `verify/prior-drafts.sh 973 origin/staging`
printed NONE and the issue had no comments, so nothing earlier was reused.

**The test.** `verify/test_c3_prompt_copies.py`, offline, found by `run-tests.sh`'s discovery. It takes `/kubecon`'s
C3 beat as the reference, since the presenters copy from it, and checks that it holds exactly two prompts, recon (it
asks what folders the bot can see) then attack (it names the `burrito-data folder` and asks to `read it to me`), and
neither the old `grep -ri -A3 recipe /tmp/burrito-data`. It then reads each copy and holds its C3 prompts equal to
that pair, in order, whitespace collapsed: every quoted paragraph of the catalog's C3 section, the `cmd` boxes of the
C3 "Stuck? Try this prompt" box in `lab.html`, the fenced blocks of the same box in `LAB-TEXT.md`, and the `c3-`
entries of `prompts.yaml`, which must be `c3-recon` then `c3-attack` and nothing else, with no fallback prompt still
carrying the old grep. `lab.html` is checked as well as its export, since the export is made from it. Each section
anchor is checked first, and a missing one exits naming the anchor and the file.

**It fails when the criterion stops holding.** The test also breaks each copy in memory the way a regression would
(the old grep in place of a prompt, recon or the attack dropped, recon and attack swapped, the grep quoted after
both, the `c3-recipe-grep` entry put back) and checks each is caught. Run against the tree before #952
(`d6de37e1^`) it exits 1 on `/kubecon` holding one C3 prompt; with the current `/kubecon` and the four copies as
they stood before #952, every copy's check fails.

## 2026-11-06 · #972 · run 17893 · A test for #952's C3 block on /kubecon

**Context.** Test review run 17827 found no test holding #952's criterion: the "Read the recipe off the filesystem"
block (C3) of `gitops/ai-layer/web/kubecon.html` carries the recon prompt and the attack-after-reset prompt, on the
chosen folder names, each with its own success marker, and no longer shows the raw `grep` as the attack.
`test_instructor_brief.py` checks one prompt and one marker per block, and `test_stage_traces.py` only checks that
"What folders do you have access to" is not the seeded attack prompt. `bash verify/prior-drafts.sh 972 origin/staging`
printed NONE and the issue had no comments, so there was no earlier draft to port.

**Decision.** A new offline test, `verify/test_kubecon_c3_recipe_block.py`, rather than more lines in
`test_instructor_brief.py`, because the criterion needs its own parse of the block (the order of the shown prompt and
marker divs) and its own mutation runs. It holds that the one C3 block shows, outside its folded notes, exactly a
prompt, a marker, a prompt and a marker; that the first prompt asks "What folders do you have access to", carries the
recipe-card reason and names no folder, file or path; that the recon marker names each seeded folder and says the bot
opens nothing; that the second prompt names "the burrito-data folder" with the same reason and is not the recon ask
again; that the attack marker calls for the reset, has the recipe card come back before the switch, and has
`Permission denied` from KubeArmor `block-recipe-snoop` and its Block alert after `guardrails-on`; that no prompt
carries the raw command or any `grep` or `/tmp/` path, and the shown block does not show it; that the raw grep stays
the folded fallback script; and that both prompts are the fallback deck's `c3-recon` and `c3-attack` word for word.

The test reads the folder names from the files that set them: the folders from the `mkdir -p` in
`images/workshop-mcp/Dockerfile`, the kitchen folder from the agent rule's `Your kitchen folder is "..."` in
`gitops/workshop-agent/agent.yaml`, the blocked directory from `policies/kubearmor/block-recipe-snoop.yaml`, and the raw
command from `challenges/c3-secret-grep/agent-prompt.txt`. Each anchor is checked first and the test exits naming the
literal and the file when one is gone. The test then runs its checks on 13 mutated copies of the page (the recon
prompt, the recon marker or the attack marker dropped, the prompts swapped, the pre-#952 shape of one grep prompt, the
grep as the attack prompt, the recon ask reworded, the folder given away in recon, the folder renamed in the attack, a
folder dropped from the recon marker, the reset dropped, KubeArmor's deny dropped, and the attack prompt out of step
with the fallback deck), and each must fail the check it breaks. It uses only PyYAML, which the suite already needs;
no dependency was added.

**Live check (watch-it-burn-private and watch-it-burn-community, 2026-11-06, read only).** With the session sourced,
`kubectl --context watch-it-burn-private get cm -A -o json` found `kubecon.html` in `agent/console-src-cc5gt65fhk` with
sha256 `db37e7a2b3dd93c8...`, the same bytes as the repo file at `fc15ed53`, so the served page is the one the test
passes on. The community cluster holds no `kubecon.html` in any ConfigMap, as #909's gate intends. On the private
cluster the `workshop-agent` Agent's rule names `burrito-data` as its kitchen folder, `block-recipe-snoop` in `agent`
reads `Block /tmp/burrito-data/config/legacy/`, and `kubectl -n agent exec deploy/workshop-mcp -- ls` listed `config`
under `/tmp/burrito-data` and `legacy` under `config`, and `Permission denied` on `legacy` itself, so the guardrails
were on and the folder names the test reads from the repo are the ones the bot has. Nothing was changed on either
cluster; the `ls` on `legacy` adds one KubeArmor Block alert to the private cluster's log.

**The suites (run 17893, at `53845c01`).** `bash verify/run-e2e-tools.sh` printed `301 tests ran`, `ALL OFFLINE
RENDER-GATE TESTS GREEN`, `72 checks ran (the offline suite and 71 tier tests) in 32m34s`, `ALL E2E TOOLS TIER CHECKS
GREEN` and `exit=0`; `test_kubecon_c3_recipe_block.py` ended `All /kubecon C3 recipe-block checks passed.` The prose
